articles.title: Jours Flash Prime : on a déniché 5 offres en or pour rayer définitivement le ménage de votre to-do list
articles.text:
Jours Flash Prime : on a déniché 5 offres en or pour rayer définitivement le ménage de votre to-do list
Fini la corvée de la serpillière ! Pendant les Jours Flash Amazon Prime, les nettoyeurs de sol et aspirateurs-robots les plus performants de notre comparatif voient leurs prix fondre. Roborock, Dreame, Dyson ou Mova : voici 5 solutions de nettoyage incontournables, tous notés 5 étoiles lors de nos tests, pour déléguer votre ménage à prix cassé.
C'est un marronnier dont on ne se plaint pas : les Jours Flash Amazon Prime sont de retour, et avec eux, l'opportunité de s'équiper lourdement pour ne plus jamais avoir à passer la serpillière le dimanche matin. Sur le front de l'entretien des sols, la bataille fait rage entre les cadors du secteur. Résultat ? Leurs fleurons respectifs, tous salués par d'excellentes notes dans les labos des Numériques, voient leurs prix fondre. Que vous cherchiez l'automatisation totale d'un robot ou la polyvalence d'un balai-laveur, voici les vraies affaires de ce Prime Day.
Les balais-laveurs : l'huile de coude en moins, la technologie en plus
Mova M10 : L'outsider qui met des claques aux ténors
Mova M10
On commence par l'entrée de gamme qui n'en a que le nom. À 158 €, le Mova M10 est tout simplement l'un des meilleurs laveurs de sol du moment. Sur le terrain, ce nettoyeur frôle le sans-faute : son articulation lui permet de se coucher complètement à plat (180°) pour traquer la poussière sous les canapés et les meubles bas sans lever la brosse du sol.
Mais ce qui bluffe à ce tarif, c'est son système d'auto-entretien. Le M10 lave son rouleau à l'eau chaude et intègre un dispositif pour couper automatiquement les cheveux et poils d'animaux qui s'y emmêlent. Léger sur le bras et doté d'une excellente gestion de ses réservoirs d'eau pour éviter les allers-retours à l'évier, il a tout d'un grand, le prix en moins.
Dreame H15 Mix : L'hybride ultime pour sols et tissus
Si votre credo est de limiter les appareils dans les placards, c'est vers le Dreame H15 Mix qu'il faut se tourner. Affiché à 455 €, ce modèle ne se contente pas de laver le carrelage.
Dreame H15 Mix
Son secret ? Un bloc-moteur et une batterie amovibles que l'on clipse d'un accessoire à l'autre. Il se transforme ainsi en aspirateur-balai classique ou en shampouineuse redoutable pour détacher vos canapés, matelas ou sièges de voiture.
En mode laveur de sol, sa raclette est pensée pour piéger la poussière au millimètre près le long des plinthes. Revers de la médaille de cette polyvalence extrême : l'appareil est un peu lourd et demande un certain coup de main dans les virages serrés. Mais son autonomie redoutable et la taille généreuse de ses bacs à eau en font un véritable char d'assaut contre la saleté de toute la maison.
Les robots : l'automatisation totale pour ne plus lever le petit doigt
Dreame L40s Pro Ultra : Le franchisseur de l'extrême
Faire passer un robot ultra-premium sous la barre symbolique des 500 €, c'est la promesse du Dreame L40s Pro Ultra, sacrifié à 474 €.
Dreame L40s Pro Ultra
Évolution musclée du L40 Ultra, ce modèle impressionne par sa capacité de franchissement : il peut enjamber des seuils de portes ou des pieds de chaises tubulaires mesurant jusqu'à 4 centimètres de haut. Fini le robot qui reste bloqué sur la barre du séchoir à linge.
Côté nettoyage, il ne fait pas dans la dentelle avec sa double brosse anti-nœuds (idéale si vous avez des animaux) et sa capacité à installer et retirer ses serpillières de manière totalement autonome depuis sa base. S'il concède une légère baisse d'autonomie par rapport à son prédécesseur, sa charge rapide et son traitement impeccable des coins et bordures compensent largement. Un vrai monstre d'indépendance.
Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro : La stérilisation à 100 °C
Un cran au-dessus dans la hiérarchie de l'automatisation, le Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro tombe à 649 €.
Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro
Son argument massue ? Une station d'accueil ultra-complète qui ne se contente pas de vider la poussière, mais lave les patins de nettoyage à l'eau bouillante (100 °C). Autant dire que les taches de gras incrustées dans la cuisine et les mauvaises odeurs ne feront pas un pli.
Plus fin que la première génération, il se glisse plus facilement sous le mobilier. Ses performances d'aspiration pures sur sols durs comme sur moquettes sont parmi les meilleures mesurées en laboratoire. Seul petit bémol à garder en tête : sa navigation prudente lui fait parfois éviter les petits objets avec un peu trop de marge, et sa brossette latérale tourne si vite qu'elle peut projeter quelques miettes au loin. Rien de rédhibitoire face au niveau d'hygiène globale délivré.
Dyson Spot+Scrub AI : La fin de l'esclavage des sacs
L'innovation de rupture nous vient du Royaume-Uni. Dyson a enfin trouvé la formule magique pour son aspirateur-robot avec son Spot+Scrub AI, proposé à 849 €.
Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai
Son coup de génie ne réside pas seulement dans son intelligence artificielle qui cartographie et navigue avec une précision chirurgicale, mais dans sa station d'accueil. C'est l'un des très rares modèles premium du marché à proposer un collecteur totalement dépourvu de sac.
Un vrai soulagement pour le porte-monnaie sur le long terme (et pour la planète), couplé à un filtre HEPA qui ne s'encrasse pas grâce à la technologie cyclonique typique de la marque. Si l'application MyDyson manque encore d'un peu de folie (pas de retour vidéo en direct, par exemple) et qu'il faut parfois l'aider sur les taches liquides très collantes, ses opérations d'entretien réduites à néant et son aspiration monumentale en font un investissement d'une durabilité redoutable.
Pour profiter de ces baisses de prix éphémères, il faut impérativement posséder un compte Amazon Prime. Si vous n'êtes pas abonné,la période d'essai gratuite de 30 jours permet de rafler la mise aujourd'hui sans débourser un centime de plus.

articles.title: CD players are back with modern, interesting features, starting as low as $89 — here are some of the best and most interesting new models
articles.text:
CD players are back with modern, interesting features, starting as low as $89 — here are some of the best and most interesting new models
Bluetooth, MagSafe, wild form factors, and more
In case you didn’t get the memo, CD sales are surging, up a whopping 58.6% in the U.S. this year, according to the RIAA. And whether you’re looking to break your old disc collection out of the attic or closet, or you’re considering starting a new CD collection and ditching that algorithmically driven streaming service, there are plenty of options to choose from. Some can offer as good or arguably even better audio quality than a 90s-era Discman or hi-fi player, while others prioritize modern features, like Bluetooth, showcasing your spinning disc, novel form factors, or RGB lighting.
There are solid, affordable, sub-$150 options that deliver the best of old and new, though. Below is a list of some of the best and most interesting new CD players, starting with a couple that I own and enjoy myself.
Most of my old CDs are housed semi-permanently in a large Sony CX555ES 300-disc CD changer I picked up, refurbished and serviced, from eBay in early 2025. But my whole collection (roughly 450 discs at this point) doesn’t fit in that machine, and I often want to listen to my more recent purchases someplace other than my living room.
That led me to buy the Fiio DM13 last year, around the Black Friday deals season. If you haven’t heard of Fiio, it’s a Chinese consumer electronics company that has made a name for itself over the last decade-plus, churning out all manner of audio gear that typically sounds and performs well for its price bracket.
This CD player features dual CS43198 DACs for solid sound, a nice metal frame, an ample 3750mAh battery, and Bluetooth 5.2 (although pairing is kinda clunky).
Read moreRead less▼
The DM13 has a nice metal frame and sounds great, thanks to dual CS43198 DACs and a SGM8262 op-amp, and sports a USB-C rechargeable 3750mAh battery that lasts a solid 7-8 hours. It also supports Bluetooth 5.2 (SBC, aptX, aptX Low Latency, and aptX HD) for wireless connectivity, and has a balanced input for high-end headphones.
I briefly considered the more premium FiiO DM15 R2R (better DAC and Bluetooth chip, and a better screen, plus a disc window — but it didn’t feel different enough, and I didn’t really want to spend $250-plus on a (second) portable CD player. That’s when I heard about the recently announced Fosi Audio DISC Nano CD player. And mere moments after seeing it (and reading that it was priced at $99), I knew I wanted one.
Yes, it’s a CD player that’s smaller than a CD, with two edges of the disc exposed while it’s playing. Yes, Sony did this with its D-88 Discman in 1988. Yes, it’s mostly a gimmick. But yes, I still bought one and (mostly) love it.
Fosi Audio is a newer company (founded in 2017, also in China) that typically makes budget-focused gear. I’ve been using the company’s $89 Audio Box X4 Phono Preamp for going on four years, and it’s performed flawlessly.
The Nano’s display is a simple two-digit design, and the battery life is short, at around two hours of listening between charges (via USB-C). But it also has a magnetic back for attaching to accessories. And so far (I’ve only had it for a few days), I’ve enjoyed popping it onto my fridge while listening through my various Bluetooth speakers, and have no complaints about the sound output or pairing.
It does have an old-school slide switch for turning the player on and off (there is no auto-off), which feels a bit crude. But for me at least, the unique design and magnetic back make it fun to use.
There are, of course, several other modern desk, desktop, and portable CD players on the market. And several are on sale for Prime Day. Below are some of the more interesting and affordable options we could find.
Yes, this is a no-name CD player with questionable sound output. But if you're looking for something that stands out, it's hard to beat a player that looks like a mini arcade cabinet, plays CDs vertically behind a translucent door, and even sports RGB lighting. The CD211 makes do with Bluetooth 5.1 if you don't want to use the built-in speakers, and there's even an FM radio for more retro audio vibes.
Read moreRead less▼
The CP1 from Japan's KM5 is a fairly standard portable CD player in terms of features, although you do get Bluetooth connectivity. But the main draw with this model is its transparent "Neonyellow" shell. Few things scream retro 90s nostalgia meets cyberpunk harder than this player, and I love it.
Read moreRead less▼
If you like showing off your hardware and music and want a CD player that's designed to be a functional piece of art, look no further. The M1 is a transparent frame with a floating CD player inside. You'll need to slide the front cover off to swap CDs, but you can connect to speakers via Bluetooth 5.0 or aux, and the battery is rated for up to 8 hours of playback.
Read moreRead less▼
Looking for something more traditional that won't force you to get up and swap discs every 74 minutes or less? This six-disc changer from Onkyo is one of the very few of these old-school-type carousel players still being manufactured. It doesn't have Bluetooth, and it isn't portable, but I do like the retro green display and the idea of creating a "playlist" of my six favorite CDs.
Read moreRead less▼
This 80W complete stereo system is a nice mix of old and new. Aside from the pair of speakers, you get FM radio, USB/MP3 playback, and Bluetooth 5.4 Auracast for simple device pairing. Sure, it will take up a fair amount of shelf space, but this is a dead-simple way to breathe new life into your old CD collection, or start a new one.

articles.title: Google proche d’un accord d’1 milliard de dollars pour l’énergie nucléaire
articles.text:
Google est sur le point de signer un contrat nucléaire d’au moins 1 milliard de dollars avec Constellation Energy. Après Amazon, Microsoft et Meta, ce géant discret de l’atome devient le fournisseur de toute la tech.
Car l’intelligence artificielle (IA) a un appétit colossal en énergie. Les data centers tournent jour et nuit, et nécessitent une alimentation stable que l’éolien et le solaire ne garantissent pas à eux seuls. Mais le nucléaire, lui, coche toutes les cases : une production continue sans émission de CO2.
Problème, construire de nouveaux réacteurs peut prendre plus de dix ans. Et les géants de la tech sont dans l’urgence, ils se rabattent donc sur les infrastructures qui existent déjà. Un nom revient sans cesse dans cette ruée : Constellation Energy.
Les contrats s’enchaînent
Cette entreprise, méconnue chez nous, exploite plus de réacteurs nucléaires que n’importe quelle autre aux États-Unis. En 2024, elle a signé un contrat avec Microsoft s’étendant sur 20 ans pour relancer un réacteur de Three Mile Island, en Pennsylvanie. Meta s’est, pour sa part, assuré toute la production de la centrale de Clinton, dans l’Illinois, à partir de 2027.
Et la semaine dernière, Amazon lui a acheté pour 690 mégawatts, dont une partie provient de la modernisation de la centrale de Calvert Cliffs, dans le Maryland. Google devrait leur emboîter le pas dès cette semaine, révèle Bloomberg avec un contrat portant sur plusieurs années. Reste à savoir quelle centrale fournirait l’électricité, et en quelle quantité, car l’information n’a, pour l’instant, pas filtré.
Le retour en force de l’atome
Ce n’est pas une première pour la firme de Mountain View. Elle multiplie les initiatives similaires depuis plus d’un an, et va même ressusciter une centrale nucléaire à l’arrêt depuis six ans dans l’Iowa. Le mois dernier, Google a aussi accepté de participer aux frais de modernisation de deux centrales en Géorgie, bien que l’accord doive encore être validé par les autorités.
C’est un retour en force de l’atome. Au début des années 2010 pourtant, le monde semblait doucement s’en détourner en raison des risques sécuritaires, illustrés par la catastrophe de Fukushima, mais aussi des coûts de maintenance extrêmement élevés. Mais l’IA a totalement redistribué les cartes, et les géants du cloud foncent sur cette technologie pour alimenter leurs ogres de data centers. Sans oublier le recours au gaz naturel, de plus en plus convoité par ces mêmes entreprises.

articles.title: Dell Servers are Exposed to Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 6th 2026
Dell Servers are Exposed to Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
Dell has released a patch for its Dell System Update (DSU) software, version 2.3.0.0, to address a critical vulnerability affecting the tool. According to the latest DSU update information, several CVEs are present that impact the DSU command-line tool. The highest-rated CVE-2026-86360 involves a full system privilege escalation in DSU versions prior to the latest 2.3.0.0. This issue arises from an improper limitation of a pathname leading to a restricted directory, allowing potential attackers to execute code with root privileges. This vulnerability compromises the underlying operating system's security and becomes a significant concern.
DellDell System Update, versions prior to 2.3.0.0, contains an Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Filesystem access for attacker. This vulnerability is considered critical because it can be leveraged by an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges. Successful exploitation may allow complete compromise of the vulnerable application and underlying operating system. Dell recommends customers upgrade at the earliest opportunity.
Regular software updates are essential for server infrastructure management and the overall organization security. For IT administrators running DSU on Dell PowerEdge systems, an immediate update is necessary, as any internet-connected equipment is now vulnerable to attacks. In an era where AI assists in writing code and creating features, it also aids in identifying potential execution privileges like these. Therefore, we can expect more timely updates for critical server infrastructure components as exploits could accumulate. Meanwhile, check Dell's website for more details about the remaining vulnerabilities that have been patched.

articles.title: Agentic era: Dell extends AI Data Platform with semantic layer - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Transforming the data path: Dell’s new releases move enterprises closer to the agentic data center
AI is taking shape, moving from models that answer questions to models that can reason. Now models are powering the agentic era, and Dell Technologies Inc. has announced several extensions to its AI Data Platform designed to manage this new paradigm.
These include extending the Dell Data Orchestration Engine with three new capabilities: the Unified Semantic Layer, the Enterprise Knowledge Graph and Knowledge Agents. Dell also added a new capability in the Data Processing Engine designed to accelerate the enterprise data prep for AI. The engine will run on graphics processing units using Nvidia Corp.’s cuDF library.
The intent, as explained on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio, by Arthur Lewis (pictured), president of the Infrastructure Solutions Group at Dell, is to bring the Data Processing Engine and Dell’s storage engines closer together, reducing unnecessary data movement with capabilities such as zero-copy data access, memory-to-memory transfer and distributed processing. Dell is creating a more efficient data path from raw enterprise information to AI-ready context, key elements of the AI Data Platform and the Dell AI Factory.
“In many cases, the model is not the next constraint, the data is,” Lewis said. “That is the problem that the AI Data Platform was built to solve. Within the Dell AI Factory, it is the data foundation that curates, connects and serves enterprise data to fuel the AI, and especially agentic AI.”
This feature is part of SiliconANGLE Media’s exploration of the architectural shifts powering continuous, production-grade AI. Be sure to check out theCUBE’s “Dell AI Data Platform Event: From Ambition to AI at Scale.” (* Disclosure below.)
Storage solutions for the agentic era
Dell’s announcements underscore the importance of storage in different stages of the AI lifecycle. In bringing the Data Processing Engine closer to Dell’s storage architecture, the company is leveraging the capabilities of PowerScale, ObjectScale and Lightning File System to target different performance, capacity and workload requirements.
PowerScale is the foundation for enterprise AI at scale, with support capabilities for up to 16,000 GPUs. ObjectScale provides customers with the object foundation for enterprise data, delivering up to 40 gigabytes per second per node. According to Dell’s AI Storage Product Management team, Lightning is the world’s fastest parallel file system, handling workloads that push into extreme throughput, large-scale training, checkpointing and the most demanding inference paths.
At AI cloud scale, storage becomes part of the underlying business model, with its performance affecting revenue per GPU, infrastructure utilization and how quickly customers can move into billable production.
Dell is positioning its AI Data Platform as the connective layer between enterprise data and production AI, bringing together storage, data processing, orchestration, search, governance and GPU acceleration. Today’s announcements essentially connect the data orchestration engine, storage semantic layer, knowledge graph at scale and cyber resilience into one AI data architecture.
“They’re focusing on helping customers get AI right,” said theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante. “Everybody wants to get AI right. That means getting to the right information, making sure that information is harmonized and ready, and then delivering it efficiently at a low cost with low operational complexity. Those are the big things. Two years ago, we said, look, the enterprise needs solutions. And what Dell is doing is they’re bringing a solution.”
Extensions for semantic layers and knowledge graphs
A key part of Dell’s solution moving forward will involve newly announced extensions to the Dell Data Orchestration Engine with a Unified Semantic Layer, Enterprise Knowledge Graph and Knowledge Agents.
The Unified Semantic Layer offers an enterprise-wide knowledge graph native to the Data Orchestration Engine. Dell is seeking to address frustration on the part of customers who have worked with other semantic tools that reach only structured data sources, leaving unstructured information behind. Another source of friction is that other offerings build context once and rely on users to keep it updated as the underlying data evolves.
“We’re doing it differently,” said Vrashank Jain, lead product manager, AI Data Platform at Dell, during an interview on theCUBE. “The semantic layer gives structured and unstructured information consistent business meaning, so a term means the same thing everywhere it appears. It uses open models to fix the hardest part of building semantic layers: generating entities, definitions and finding meaning at-scale with human-in-the-loop for verification. No more standardized ontologies. Each organization is unique. Their semantic layer should reflect that.”
Dell’s Knowledge Graph connects entities and relationships so an application or agent can understand how data is related. It uses metadata from structured and unstructured sources, lineage, storage metadata and query history to continuously tune the graph. Once an agent asks a question, the platform augments the context surrounding the query with related entities such as tables, images, vector indexes and logs, according to Jain.
Dell’s Knowledge Agent is a new way of interacting with the AI Data Platform, powered by the Unified Semantic Layer and Knowledge Graph. After building the graph and semantic layers, users will be able to develop Knowledge Agents focused on a part of the Knowledge Graph that is curated with a specific expertise. Users can give the agents prompt-based guidance, data access permissions, quality guardrails, token cost thresholds, all while remaining model agnostic.
“A Knowledge Agent is like a trusted advisor on your team who is an expert on any given topic,” Jain told theCUBE. “It brings trust and accuracy to agentic retrieval.”
Enhancing the Dell AI Data Platform
The announcements from Dell reflect several key transformations currently taking place in the world of enterprise compute.
One involves an evolution of the AI stack itself, brought on by the rapidly expanding influence of agents. Enterprises now want to get to agent outcomes as fast as possible. This will involve connecting the underlying enterprise data and converting it into context that can then be served to agents.
“We should step back and look at how we are moving from these so-called AI factories or intelligence producing factories, which they were originally conceived as, to what we are now calling agentic data centers,” said Gaurav Chawla, vice president and Dell fellow, Infrastructure Solutions Group, at Dell, in conversation with theCUBE. “And when you look at an agentic data center, it’s not just the model, it’s not just the storage, but you need a combination of models, the storage and the data stack.”
Dell is also retooling how it ultimately serves enterprise customers, transforming its business to operate at the speed and agility of an AI-native company. This is a major shift from what we have seen so far, according to Chawla, because AI is becoming much more than just a copilot for its human operator.
“This is a shift now evolving from human as the operator [to] where you want the agent to be the operator and agents bring humans back in the loop when they need them to review or to approve something,” Chawla said. “If architected and deployed correctly, this means agents not only execute business processes, but they also learn and get better over time. So that’s what we are building at Dell AI Data Platform.”
The various elements of this transformation point toward an important shift in the role of the AI Factory. As theCUBE Research’s John Furrier has noted, the data center is becoming an industrial system in its own right, and the AI infrastructure race is no longer just about compute; it’s about data movement.
“My big takeaway is that the most important thing that’s happening here is two things: Dell has a new data architecture that’s unified and two, the industry itself is moving to this phase where … data centers are going to become industrial centers, multiple data centers working together,” Furrier said. “The story here is that the data path is the new architecture.”
Stay tuned for the complete video interview, part of SiliconANGLE’s and theCUBE’s coverage of the Dell AI Data Platform Event.

articles.title: Gemini ya puede entender lo que muestra la cámara del celular: así funciona Guided Visión
articles.text:
Google incorporó Guided Vision a Gemini Live, una función que permite utilizar la cámara del celular para que la inteligencia artificial describa lo que está frente al usuario en tiempo real. La herramienta responde mediante voz y permite hacer preguntas sobre objetos, colores, formas y espacios, además de realizar consultas de seguimiento durante la conversación.
La función está especialmente orientada a personas ciegas o con baja visión, aunque también puede resultar útil para cualquier usuario que necesite asistencia visual en determinadas situaciones. Guided Vision forma parte de las herramientas de accesibilidad de Gemini y busca facilitar tareas cotidianas mediante instrucciones de audio.
Gemini puede describir lo que muestra la cámara
Guided Vision funciona mientras el usuario mantiene una conversación con Gemini Live y comparte la cámara del dispositivo. A partir de las imágenes que recibe, el asistente puede describir diferentes elementos del entorno y responder preguntas específicas.
Por ejemplo, una persona puede apuntar el teléfono hacia una mesa y preguntar qué objetos hay sobre ella. También puede consultar el color de una prenda, identificar determinadas formas o pedir información sobre un objeto que aparece frente a la cámara.
Una de sus aplicaciones más prácticas está relacionada con la lectura. La herramienta puede ayudar a interpretar letras pequeñas en envases, etiquetas o información nutricional que puede resultar difícil de distinguir a simple vista.
También puede servir para localizar objetos que se hayan caído al suelo o que no estén a simple vista. En estos casos, el usuario puede realizar varias preguntas de seguimiento para obtener más información sin necesidad de iniciar nuevamente la consulta.
También ayuda a colocar correctamente el celular
Una de las particularidades de Guided Vision es que no solamente analiza aquello que aparece en la imagen. La función también puede orientar al usuario cuando la cámara no está correctamente posicionada.
Si el teléfono apunta demasiado arriba, demasiado cerca o ligeramente hacia un lado, Gemini puede indicar mediante la voz cómo modificar el encuadre para obtener una imagen más útil. Esto puede facilitar la interacción para personas que dependen principalmente de las indicaciones auditivas.
De esta manera, la función combina reconocimiento visual y conversación por voz para ofrecer una experiencia más intuitiva. El usuario no necesita describir manualmente qué está observando: puede apuntar la cámara y formular preguntas directamente al asistente.
Google advierte que no reemplaza las ayudas de movilidad
Aunque Guided Vision puede ser útil para numerosas tareas diarias, Google establece límites importantes sobre su utilización. La compañía advierte que no debe emplearse como herramienta para navegar por espacios, viajar de forma segura o detectar obstáculos.
Por ese motivo, la función no debe sustituir un bastón, un perro guía u otras ayudas destinadas a la movilidad. La inteligencia artificial puede cometer errores al interpretar una imagen y sus respuestas no deben considerarse un sistema de seguridad.
Su principal utilidad está en ofrecer información visual complementaria para actividades concretas, como leer una etiqueta, reconocer un color o saber qué hay en determinado espacio.
Cómo activar Guided Vision en Gemini
Para utilizar la función es necesario abrir la aplicación de Gemini, acceder a la configuración del perfil y activar la opción “Usar visión guiada en directo”. Después, el usuario puede iniciar Gemini Live y compartir la cámara del teléfono.
También existe la posibilidad de configurar un acceso directo desde Ajustes > Accesibilidad > Asistencia visual > Guided Vision.
La función está disponible en dispositivos Android con Android 9 o versiones posteriores, siempre que Gemini Live sea compatible con la región y el idioma utilizado. Además, es necesario mantener actualizadas tanto la aplicación de Gemini como la versión del sistema operativo.
Guided Vision también funciona con Google TalkBack, el lector de pantalla de Android que permite a personas con discapacidad visual interactuar con el teléfono mediante indicaciones habladas. Con esta incorporación, Google amplía el uso de Gemini más allá de las consultas tradicionales y lo convierte en una herramienta capaz de interpretar el entorno mediante la cámara del celular.

articles.title: Proibição das bets começa a valer e R$ 1,32 bilhão ainda não foi devolvido • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Proibição das bets começa a valer e R$ 1,32 bilhão ainda não foi devolvido
Serviços de apostas online estão proibidos de operar em todo o Brasil a partir desta terça-feira (06/10). Ainda há valores em aberto a serem devolvidos aos apostadores.
A partir desta terça-feira (06/10), os serviços de apostas e jogos online conhecidos como “bets” estão proibidos de operar no Brasil. Como consequência, os valores em aberto nessas plataformas devem ser restituídos aos usuários. O governo estima que a soma de devoluções pendentes é de R$ 1,32 bilhão.
Desde o fim de setembro, as plataformas de apostas não podiam mais aceitar novos depósitos. Hoje, seus aplicativos e sites devem ficar totalmente indisponíveis. Oficialmente, a decisão faz parte da Medida Provisória N° 1.394, de 25 de setembro de 2026, que determina:
Ficam proibidas, no território nacional, a exploração, a oferta, a intermediação e a publicidade de loterias de aposta de quota fixa, em meio físico ou virtual, inclusive quando realizadas por agente sediado no exterior que as ofereça a pessoa localizada no território nacional.
A MP também estabelece que as casas de apostas devolvam aos clientes todos os valores que estiverem nos saldos das contas ou foram direcionados a apostas não finalizadas.
O prazo para resgate direto desses valores terminou na última segunda-feira (05/10). Mas, de acordo com o Ministério da Fazenda, R$ 1,32 bilhão ainda estava em posse das “bets” nesta terça-feira, montante associado a 26,5 milhões de CPFs.
Provavelmente, parte desse dinheiro está em contas de usuários que esqueceram de fazer o resgate, desconhecem ter direito à restituição ou não souberam como realizar a solicitação.
Mas o próprio governo dá a entender que outra causa, ainda que em escala menor, é o desinteresse, visto que 86,2 milhões de contas registram saldos entre R$ 0,02 e R$ 0,99.
Apesar disso, esses valores não estão perdidos. Entre 7 e 8 de outubro, as casas de apostas deverão informar aos bancos os saldos remanescentes, identificados por CPF. Já entre 9 e 14 de outubro, as instituições financeiras terão que depositar os valores nas contas dos apostadores. Após esse prazo, a Caixa Econômica Federal poderá intermediar os pagamentos que não puderam ser realizados.
O governo justificou a medida sob os argumentos de que a atuação de “bets” estava causando alto nível de endividamento entre jogadores, problemas de saúde ligados à compulsão por apostas ou jogos, e possível uso das plataformas para lavagem de dinheiro.
Mas entidades que representam os serviços de apostas e jogos discordam. Duas delas, o Instituto Brasileiro de Jogo Responsável (IBJR) e a Associação Nacional de Jogos e Loterias (ANJL), recorreram ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) para pedir a suspensão da medida provisória:
As preocupações com os impactos das apostas são legítimas. O IBJR sempre defendeu que elas sejam enfrentadas com fiscalização, responsabilidade dos operadores e respeito à lei. Na avaliação do Instituto, a medida provisória desconsidera o marco legal vigente e enfraquece os mecanismos de controle e proteção criados pelo próprio Estado.
A decisão é precipitada e causa grave insegurança jurídica. Empresas receberam autorização do poder público, cumpriram as exigências regulatórias e investiram para operar segundo as regras estabelecidas pelo Brasil. Mudar essas regras de forma abrupta abala a confiança no país, independentemente da opinião de cada um sobre as apostas. É essa questão que o IBJR leva ao Judiciário.

articles.title: El mercado del petróleo necesitará hasta dos años para recuperar sus reservas aunque Ormuz reabra hoy mismo
articles.text:
Hace ya siete meses que Irán decidió cerrar el estrecho de Ormuz, en respuesta a la ofensiva estadounidense e israelí del 28 de febrero. Las consecuencias se han dejado notar en el transporte marítimo, el suministro de crudo y el notorio aumento del precio de los combustibles a nivel global.
Aunque no sabemos cuánto más se prolongará este pulso entre Washington y Teherán ni cómo evolucionará un conflicto que, a día de hoy, sigue en punto muerto, sí tenemos ya una estimación de cuánto podría tardar el mercado en recuperar la normalidad una vez el estrecho vuelva a funcionar a total capacidad. Y no invita precisamente al optimismo.
Será peor cuanto más tarde en reanudarse el tránsito. El presidente y consejero delegado de la petrolera Saudi Aramco, Amin H. Nasser, ha declarado durante el Energy Intelligence Forum en Londres que reponer existencias y mantener la demanda en niveles habituales podría llevar hasta dos años, según recoge El Periódico de la Energía. Este tiempo podría aumentar, según él, cuanto más se prolongue la interrupción del transporte por la zona: cuanto más dure la interrupción, mayor será el agujero que haya que recuperar.
Y de momento no se ve el final: según la agencia Reuters, el presidente del Parlamento iraní Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf informó a los medios estatales que el estrecho no se reabriría hasta que no se cumplan las siete condiciones del acuerdo provisional que firmó en junio con Estados Unidos. La incertidumbre se mantiene y deja cada vez menos margen de seguridad al sistema energético mundial.
Mientras tanto, en el resto del mundo... Hace solo unos días, Donald Trump coqueteó con la idea de limitar sus exportaciones de diésel y, así, tratar de controlar la escala de precios interna que está viviendo Estados Unidos. La amenaza contribuyó a que el G7 (Estados Unidos, Japón, Alemania, Reino Unido, Francia, Italia y Canadá) tomara cartas en el asunto y hace unos días el grupo anunció que se liberarían 100 millones de barriles de petróleo y diésel de sus reservas de emergencia durante cuatro meses, según la BBC. La acción se realizará bajo la coordinación de la Agencia Internacional de la Energía (AIE), aunque todavía no se conoce qué países socios liberarán existencias ni con qué ritmo.
España diversifica sus proveedores. Según datos de la Corporación de Reservas Estratégicas de Productos Petrolíferos (Cores) que recopila El Periódico de la Energía, las importaciones de crudo a España en el mes de agosto alcanzaron los 5.705 millones de toneladas, un 11% más que el mismo mes de 2025.
En este caso, y con la situación internacional tal y como está, el principal proveedor ha sido Nigeria, con 1.035 millones de toneladas y el 18,1% del total de lo que recibió nuestro país, seguido por México (648.000 toneladas y 11,4% del total), Venezuela (641.000 toneladas y 11,2% del total) y Estados Unidos (632.000 toneladas y 11,1% del total). Desde Oriente Medio, España también recibió 378.000 toneladas (un 6,6% del total), principalmente de Arabia Saudí y Emiratos Árabes Unidos, aunque nada de Irak, otro de los suministradores habituales.
El principio del fin, pero no el fin. La reapertura de Ormuz, cuando algún día llegue, será el principio de la vuelta a la normalidad, pero no necesariamente la normalidad en sí: el mercado tendrá que recuperar la confianza, reconstruir los flujos comerciales habituales y reponer las reservas que se consuman mientras dure la crisis. Todo, mientras se restablece la respuesta a la demanda mundial. De ahí que palabras como las de Nasser sean tan relevantes: que los petroleros vuelvan a atravesar Ormuz no significa que el mercado vaya a volver a su punto de partida.

articles.title: Mistral lance Le Chonk, la nouvelle IA française qui réduit l'écart avec ChatGPT et Claude
articles.text:
Mistral AI sort l’artillerie lourde. Ce mardi 6 octobre, la start-up française a levé le voile sur Mistral Large 4, un nouveau modèle d’intelligence artificielle surnommé « Le Chonk ». Mistral Large 4 est décrit comme une IA multimodale, c’est-à-dire qu’elle est capable de traiter plusieurs types de contenus, comme des images, du texte ou des contenus audio. Dans trois semaines, des entreprises et des chercheurs pourront télécharger et utiliser le modèle en toute liberté. Pour le moment, l’IA est néanmoins accessible en ligne à tous les internautes.
 Meet Mistral Large 4, aka Le Chonk.
• 1T parameters, natively multimodal. 49B active.
It is the best open weights model from US or Europe on aggregated benchmarks.
• State-of-the-art on critical workloads, including cyber defense, manufacturing and finance and it surpasses closed frontier models on visual grounding.
• Forged in Europe end-to-end and is deployable from Europe via our own Mistral Cloud infrastructure.
• Available to all via API today. Working with cybersecurity partners privately.
Open weights release end of October.
— Mistral AI (@MistralAI) October 6, 2026
Une IA qui « ne comble pas complètement l’écart »
Interrogé par le Figaro, le cofondateur de Mistral, Guillaume Lample, reconnaît que « Le Chonk » n’est pas encore capable de rivaliser avec les autres IA sur le marché, dont les incontournables ChatGPT et Claude. Il admet que c’est « un modèle qui ne comble pas complètement l’écart avec les modèles frontières, mais le réduit significativement ».
Le PDG de la start-up, Arthur Mensch, précise quant à lui que le modèle dépasse par contre les IA chinoises sur certains points, comme la cybersécurité. Pierre Stock, vice-président en charge de la science chez Mistral, vante par ailleurs « des performances de pointe » dans la cybersécurité, les processus industriels et la finance. Le modèle se classe selon lui « parmi les meilleurs modèles open source du monde sur des métriques agrégées ».
À lire aussi : Le Chat devient Vibe – Mistral mise tout sur les agents IA
Moins de puces et plus de libertés
Mistral insiste aussi sur la sobriété de son modèle d’intelligence artificielle, qui a été entraîné avec seulement 4 000 puces Nvidia, soit « deux à trois fois moins » que les concurrents chinois. C’est aussi « nettement moins que les concurrents de l’IA fermée », comme ChatGPT. Pour rappel, un modèle fermé, comme ceux d’OpenAI ou d’Anthropic, reste sur les serveurs de son créateur.
Par contre modèle ouvert peut être téléchargé, installé et personnalisé par autrui. En clair, un modèle public peut être utilisé par tout le monde… y compris par des pirates. En marge de l’annonce, Pierre Stock assure que Mistral travaillera avec des partenaires de confiance et des gouvernements pour que le modèle serve « à défendre, et non à mener des attaques malveillantes ».
À lire aussi : ChatGPT vs Claude – OpenAI et Anthropic dégainent des IA moins chers et plus efficaces… au lieu de ralentir
Avec ce nouveau modèle, Mistral cherche surtout à montrer que l’Europe, et en particulier la France, est toujours bien placée dans la course à l’IA, toujours marquée par domination des géants américains.

articles.title: Mistral launches open-source Mistral Large 4, details AI roadmap - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Mistral launches open-source Mistral Large 4, details AI roadmap
Mistral AI SAS today opened access to Mistral Large 4, its most capable large language model to date.
On launch, the LLM is available in public preview through the company’s cloud platform. Mistral plans to release the model’s weights later this month.
Mistral Large 4 features a mixture of experts architecture with 1 trillion parameters. It only uses 49 billion parameters at a time, which is more hardware-efficient than activating the entire model when a user enters a prompt. Mistral says that the LLM can answer questions across more than 160 languages.
The new model earned a top five score on the AA Cyber Index, a collection of benchmarks that measures LLMs’ ability to find and fix software vulnerabilities. The model proved particularly adept at patching open-source projects. Mistral Large 4 earned an AA Cyber Index score of 82% in that department, which put it ahead of open-source rivals.
Mistral says computer vision is another strong suit of its LLM. It outperformed GPT-6 Astra by 1% on Dense200, a benchmark that measures models’ ability to find objects of interest in images.
Mistral Large 4 falls well behind frontier models such as Astra on the AI industry’s most popular coding benchmarks. However, it outperforms several leading open-source LLMs including Qwen3.8 Max and DeepSeek V4 Pro. It also scored higher than the latter model on the AutomationBench and AA-Briefcase knowledge work benchmarks. The former test comprises relatively simple tasks, while the latter includes assignments that would take a human weeks to complete.
Mistral trained Large 4 on 3,800 Grace Blackwell chips. Each accelerator combines two of Nvidia Corp.’s Blackwell graphics cards with one central processing unit. The company didn’t specify how long the training run took. It did, however, share other details about the project.
Advanced LLMs are trained through trial and error. The model being developed receives a task and attempts to complete it without human guidance. Each such exercise is known as a rollout. At the end of a rollout, a specialized AI model analyzes the results and uses them to refine the LLM.
According to Mistral, its engineers developed a software stack that can run tens of thousands of rollouts in parallel. It assembles rollouts from a library of AI building blocks. Those modules include sandboxes in which LLMs can run code, a search engine that facilitates web access and tests for checking rollout results. The software stack was used to develop Mistral Large 4.
The model’s rollouts produced 33 billion tokens per day. Mistral used just under half of those tokens to power the training workflow that was responsible for refining Large 4. The rollouts and training workflow were asynchronous, which means that a delay in one workload doesn’t slow down the other. That helped Mistral speed up processing.
Notably, the company didn’t pause the training run that produced Large 4 after creating the current iteration of the model. Mistral expects the workflow to produce larger, more capable versions of the LLM in the coming months. In the longer term, the company will use Mistral Large 4 to build an entire series of models optimized for specific use cases.

articles.title: SEGA Exec Says AI Already in Use at Studio but Not for Creative Tasks
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 6th 2026
SEGA Exec Says AI Already in Use at Studio but Not for Creative Tasks
The use of AI-generated art to accelerate video game development is becoming more and more common, with massive game studios like EA and Capcom openly acknowledging that they will be using AI to streamline their game development workflows, despite public outcry about quality and concern for the human cost in an industry already rife with layoffs. 
Addressing a question in a recent interview with Nikkei regarding how game production will change in the face of AI, SEGA's senior executive officer and deputy chief business officer, Tsuyoshi Saito, said that the company is already using AI to improve efficiencies at the company, specifically when it comes to business idea generation and publishing processes, but that it will not be using AI for creative aspects of game development.
Tsuyoshi Saito, (machine translation)As for AI, we are using it to improve the efficiency of publishing departments and corporate departments, as well as to generate business ideas. However, we are very careful in the development process of the game, and we do not leave the creativity of the game to AI.
As far as AI use in game development goes, this is a fairly tame example, even if it doesn't completely rule out that we may, at some point sooner or later, see SEGA use AI-generated assets or placeholders in games, as we have seen a number of times from studios like Pearl Abyss, Panache Games, and Sandbox Interactive.

articles.title: Gigaphoton debuts neon recycling system with claimed 50% recovery rate — systems throw a lifeline to chipmakers that utilize 70% of global neon supply in DUV lithography
articles.text:
Gigaphoton debuts neon recycling system with claimed 50% recovery rate — systems throw a lifeline to chipmakers that utilize 70% of global neon supply in DUV lithography
The recycling rate is only 50% for now, but this could be improved in time.
Japanese semiconductor lithography tool maker Gigaphoton has developed a novel neon gas recycling system named hTGM for its argon fluoride (ArF) excimer lasers. The method has demonstrated a 50% recycling rate, with hopes that it can be improved dramatically with adjusted configurations, Business Wire reports. This could help fill a gap in the chip supply chain caused by the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Before 2022, Ukraine shipped up to 50% of the neon gas used in the semiconductor industry, but its major producers had to stop exports, raising concerns over chip supply. 70% of global neon production is used in semiconductor manufacturing, particularly in advanced DUV processes.
In the aftermath, China, Taiwan, and South Korea all increased their own domestic Neon production efforts, but various chip manufacturers also integrated recycling systems at various points during the fabrication process. Gigaphoton's more efficient ArF lasers with neon recycling could further help close those loops, reducing material costs and further reducing reliance on global supply chains.
It's not the only company pushing this technology forward, either. At the start of September, Japanese environmental protection company Kanken Techno demonstrated its own Neon gas recycling system for excimer lasers at SemiCon Taiwan. It demonstrated a recycling rate of over 90%, suggesting there is considerable headroom to improve this process in the future.
What makes Neon so scarce?
Neon is one of a handful of noble gases, making it inert under standard conditions and easy to handle. However, the ease with which it vaporizes and its limited bonding ability mean it is relatively scarce in Earth's atmosphere, making it scarce. It is most efficiently obtained through fractional distillation of super-cooled air, making it most affordable to obtain as a byproduct of other processes. For decades, Ukrainian steel-mill air-separation units produced crude neon from large-scale air-separation units (ASUs), and then refined it in-country via a pair of key companies.
That meant that when Russia escalated its war against Ukraine into a full-scale invasion in 2022 and Ukrainian neon refiners shut down production, there was an immediate global response.
As SFA Oxford explains, South Korea accelerated domestic production and implemented a large-scale, national neon recycling initiative focused on in-fab recovery. Taiwan installed purification systems in existing blast-furnace ASUs, developing its own domestic supply chain. By utilizing its national infrastructure, it targeted complete self-sufficiency in neon gas production within a few years.
China integrated neon gas purification into many elements of its industrial base, twinning it with steel and petrochemical production facilities. The U.S. also responded with the development of new ASUs at Gulf-coast petrochemical hubs, but those aren't expected to meaningfully improve American neon supplies until near the end of the decade.
Lithography accounts for around 70% of global neon use, particularly in more advanced DUV processes — though crucially, not in EUV lithography, which uses a tin-plasma laser instead. With global DUV-produced semiconductor supply rapidly advancing in the wake of the AI buildout, neon supply is an important component in the chip supply chain, which has rapidly evolved to become a key asset within strategic defence and global trade.
Working with what you've got
For individual companies that can't directly control their supply chains, recycling has been a much more immediate focus. The first neon gas recycling systems were qualified for use with Cymer excimer ArF lasers at the end of 2023, and Samsung and SK Hynix became the first of the major memory makers to implement neon gas recycling in 2024.
Gigaphoton previously offered neon recycling with KrF (krypton fluoride) lasers, but has now extended that recycling capability to ArF lasers as well. It claims a single hTGM for ArF unit can reduce neon gas consumption by up to 470 kilotres per year, representing substantial material cost savings, as well as reducing company reliance on a global supply chain that has been sufficiently unstable in recent years.
However, its claims of a 50% recycling rate aren't exactly groundbreaking. Cymer's excimer laser neon recovery system demonstrated that same level of efficiency in 2015, and Gigaphoton's own testing suggested a potential peak for ArF recovery of over 90% in 2017.
That suggests it should be able to ramp up its efforts to a higher percentage quite swiftly. Especially since fellow Japanese firm Kanken Techno recently unveiled a neon recycling system with over 90% efficiency. Kanken works with both major ArF laser developers and is currently going through the certification process, with expected approval in the near future.
A temporary fix?
With neon gas recycling during chip production effectively solved, it may be that the supply of neon for the chip industry has proved to be a temporary problem. But it may be a temporary solution too, as the use of neon within the industry may be set to shrink dramatically in the years to come.
EUV lithography can build far more complex chips than DUV, and offers a future path beyond the need for neon gas usage in excimer lasers as newer electronics adopt the more capable chip designs. On top of that, alternative technologies to DUV are being developed which could produce the same DUV light to generate advanced semiconductors, but without the need for noble or toxic gases.
Solid-state laser technologies have been rapidly developing in recent years, though last year's Chinese efforts are still below required industrial power thresholds. Nanoimprint lithography also holds promise as a DUV alternative, as well as cutting costs by a comparative 90%.
There are still huge hurdles in performance and certification, as well as integration with existing fabrication plans and supply chains. But the potential to move beyond the need for neon gas within semiconductor lithography is there. Over the coming years, the combination of laser neon recycling systems and alternative manufacturing techniques could reduce the need for international neon sources to a fraction of existing levels.
Jon Martindale is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. For the past 20 years, he's been writing about PC components, emerging technologies, and the latest software advances. His deep and broad journalistic experience gives him unique insights into the most exciting technology trends of today and tomorrow.

articles.title: Apple refuerza macOS: agentes de IA no podrán acceder a archivos sin permiso explícito
articles.text:
Apple anunció controles más estrictos en macOS para el permiso especial Full Disk Access, una modificación que exigirá autorizaciones explícitas e informadas antes de que aplicaciones de terceros o agentes de inteligencia artificial (IA) puedan ingresar a archivos, correos, mensajes e historial de navegación.
El permiso concede a una aplicación acceso prácticamente ilimitado a los archivos y datos almacenados en una computadora, así que la medida busca reducir las fugas de información sensible derivadas de un uso malicioso de ese nivel de acceso.
Apple advirtió que algunos desarrolladores lo emplean de formas que pueden exponer el contenido completo de los sistemas, sin que los usuarios comprendan plenamente las consecuencias.
La compañía liderada por John Ternus advirtió: “A medida que los agentes de IA se vuelven cada vez más capaces y autónomos, los riesgos asociados a este nivel de acceso aumentarán sustancialmente”.
Cómo cambiarán los permisos en los dispositivos Mac de Apple
Los nuevos controles obligarán a los usuarios a realizar acciones específicas antes de otorgar acceso total al disco. El objetivo es que puedan decidir con mayor información sobre sus datos y su privacidad antes de habilitar un permiso que alcanza contenidos personales y registros de actividad.
Apple explicó que el problema no se limita a los documentos guardados en el dispositivo. El acceso puede abarcar correos, conversaciones, archivos y el historial de navegación, una combinación de datos que permite reconstruir aspectos sensibles de la vida digital de una persona.
Asimismo, la preocupación por el alcance de los agentes de inteligencia artificial fue expuesta recientemente por un columnista de Inc., quien relató que Muse, el agente de IA de Meta, pudo leer todos sus mensajes privados. Según su testimonio, no había autorizado esa acción y tenía desactivado el acceso total al disco.
Por qué crece las dudas sobre los riesgos de los agentes de inteligencia artificial
La discusión sobre los permisos en dispositivos personales coincide con advertencias más amplias sobre la capacidad de los sistemas autónomos. OpenAI publicó en julio de 2026 los resultados de una auditoría sobre un hackeo contra Hugging Face, una plataforma utilizada para compartir modelos y herramientas de inteligencia artificial.
La investigación, acompañada por análisis de dos organizaciones independientes especializadas en sistemas de IA, concluyó que al menos 1.200 agentes de IA lograron comunicarse y coordinarse en secreto durante una evaluación interna.
Los programas habrían engañado al mecanismo que los examinaba y cerca de 700 participaron finalmente en el ataque contra la plataforma. El episodio tuvo repercusión mundial por tratarse de un hackeo sin intervención humana y reavivó las alertas sobre la supervisión y el control de los modelos avanzados.
Cuáles son los peligros que puede ocasionar el avance de la IA, según la ONU
En septiembre de 2026, el alto comisionado de las Naciones Unidas para los Derechos Humanos (ONU), Volker Türk, alertó que el desarrollo acelerado de la inteligencia artificial puede amenazar derechos como la vida, la alimentación, la privacidad, la salud y la seguridad.
El funcionario advirtió sobre efectos en el suministro de agua y en las barreras contra el empleo de armas de destrucción masiva. Türk incluyó en su advertencia a la IA agéntica, capaz de tomar decisiones propias que exceden las funciones de los sistemas convencionales.
A su juicio, los fallos de esta tecnología podrían paralizar servicios esenciales, interrumpir comunicaciones, desestabilizar infraestructuras críticas y afectar a las instituciones democráticas.
Agregó que “poblaciones enteras podrían perder el acceso a agua, calefacción o servicios financieros si esos sistemas fallaran o fueran utilizados sin controles adecuados”. El funcionario pidió que Estados y empresas actúen con urgencia en foros multilaterales bajo las normas del derecho internacional y los derechos humanos.

articles.title: Teen founder reveals 'personal AI computer' — $3,499 Mac mini rival wants to do local AI better than Apple, majoring in ease of use, privacy and security
articles.text:
Teen founder reveals 'personal AI computer' for running local agents — $3,499 Mac mini rival runs on Nvidia RTX Pro 4000 GPU and promises to be a subscription-free 'brain in a box'
A pricey niche product — but an intriguing one
- A new startup has built an AI PC which has sold out of its first batch
- Ghost's Core is a 'personal AI computer that runs models entirely on device'
- It connects to your apps, services and devices, so it 'builds context on your life over time, and works continuously to help you'
Ghost is a startup in the AI field that wants to capitalize on the desire to have agents running locally rather than using AI in the cloud — and to get this done with a minimum of fuss.
TechCrunch reports that Ghost's first product is a PC for using local AI agents which runs those LLMs (Large Language Models) exclusively on-device, ensuring your data stays private (I'll come back to that point later).
The device is called Core, and Ghost explains on the product's site: "Core is a personal AI computer that runs models entirely on device. It connects to your apps, files, and devices, builds context on your life over time, and works continuously to help you, not just when you ask."
It is, if you will, a personal AI assistant on your desk at home, or as Zain Javaid, the founder and CEO of Ghost — which just raised $11 million in funding — put it, a "brain in a box".
Core is a PC which is an unassuming black box built around an Nvidia RTX Pro 4000 (Blackwell) graphics card with 24GB of video RAM, the central muscle for driving the AI, along with 64GB of DDR5 system RAM. The rated AI performance is 770 TOPS.
The PC comes with three AI models pre-installed: Qwen-3.8-Next, Qwen-3.8-27B, and Gemma-4-31B.
You can use your own model on the device, as you might expect, or any alternative for that matter, but the real selling point of Core is that it's an easy way to get yourself a fully primed AI box which requires no effort or setup.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This is for the AI enthusiast who doesn't want to buy a Mac mini (or Mac Studio) with maxed-out memory (required for larger AI models), and then have to mess around setting up everything themselves.
Javaid stresses that the PC comes with software built specifically for running those pre-installed AIs, avoiding all the fuss of model configuration. The CEO observes: "You can run [AI] models on existing hardware, but it's a terrible experience on many levels."
Core updates its models automatically as new upgrades emerge (unless you don't want that to happen), and the idea is that it's a seamless system and "similar to how Tesla works" with over-the-air updates.
You interact with the PC using an app (on your phone or laptop) with which you can issue voice commands should you wish.
Privacy and security
As well as the ease of use, privacy is the other big selling point for Core. It's tapping into a market of the increasing number of people realizing the potential of AI for helping with their life or work, who are concerned about sending their thoughts or data into the cloud, when they have no real idea where those queries or uploads will end up.
Core will run your AI agents continuously taking on whatever tasks you require while keeping all your data on the device, with Ghost promising that it's not going anywhere else. The personal data on the PC is encrypted to keep it safe — even Ghost can't access the data — and the device is specifically designed to keep running even if Ghost were to shut down (there's no subscription fee here).
The CEO assures us: "All of the source code, logic, and model weights live on the device, not the services. We build this device to not be dependent on having an outside entity maintaining the service."
Security is further bolstered by a firewall that limits how any agent can use credentials such as passwords, and you can dictate how much autonomy the Core agents are allowed, heavily restricting the AI should you prefer.
Javaid tells us that the firewall monitors all outgoing requests and "if it sees the agent performing a sanctioned action or exfiltrating data it shouldn't, it rejects the request and flags it for user review".
Core is priced at $3,499 in the US (around £2,600 / AU$5,000), and pre-orders for the first batch of PCs sold out on the first day that they were offered (yesterday). Those devices ship at the end of this month, and you can now register your interest in a second batch of PCs which are coming off the production line.
Analysis: a question of worth
Core can be hooked into all aspects of your life — or that's certainly the idea, and part of the reason why there's such an emphasis on privacy. It needs to be watertight for security given that Core connects to your existing devices and services, smart-home gadgets, fitness watches — or personal health data — and learns over time about how you live your life, imparting advice based on that knowledge.
Exactly how useful the system will be, well, that remains to be seen — and it may also depend on how 'smart' you've gone in terms of your array of gadgets and tech. There could be a lot of scope beyond life monitoring for Core's AI agents, of course, and there will presumably be the flexibility to get them doing whatever you want.
The other potential sticking point is that price. Is $3,499 a lot to pay for a dedicated AI PC? Well, it's undeniably a hefty sum of money, but there are some heavyweight components under the hood here (and the RAM crisis remains in full force). Indeed, the current price of the Nvidia GPU actually makes the PC a bargain as it stands (the company bought its stock of those graphics cards when they were much cheaper — so the next batch will be pricier).
If you configure a Mac mini as a top-of-the-line device for AI, you're looking at $3,199 in the US at the time of writing — and it doesn't come with the aforementioned strengths of software specifically designed for running local AI easily, and the privacy and security elements mentioned.
I've a feeling Ghost might be onto something here, at least in terms of pushing the concept of a user-friendly and straightforward AI box that does everything locally. I doubt this will be the last take on this kind of idea, and the price tag involved may eventually become a bit more realistic in the future. Although that depends on how the RAM crisis shakes out — and the latest signs are far from positive, sadly.

articles.title: Esta semana en Lidl, descuento en toda su web sin mínimo de compra: estos son nuestros dispositivos favoritos
articles.text:
Entrar en la web de Lidl es perderse por un catálogo donde podemos encontrar todo tipo de dispositivos y gadgets. Los podemos encontrar en muchas ocasiones con descuento, pero lo de hoy va un pasito más allá. Lidl tiene activos sus Happy Days hasta el próximo 9 de octubre, pero ¿y eso qué implica? Que podemos beneficiarnos de un descuento del 10 % en toda su página web sin mínimo de compra (hasta un máximo de 10 euros).
Los productos de Lidl ya tienen una gran relación calidad-precio, pero si a eso le podemos añadir un descuento extra, mejor que mejor. Además, hay que tener en cuenta que los gastos de envío son gratis a partir de 70 euros de compra, con la excepción de artículos pesados, que pueden llevar un pequeño suplemento.
Hidrolimpiadora flexible
Como hay mucho donde elegir, nosotros hemos hecho una selección de cinco de nuestros productos favoritos de Lidl.
- Hidrolimpiadora flexible por 66,99 euros, ideal para limpiar el jardín o el coche en casa.
- Ronda de enchufe por 10,99 euros, una solución para aprovechar un enchufe con más conexiones.
- Freidora de aire de cristal por 74,99 euros, un modelo que permite cocinar en unos recipientes de cristal que también sirven para el frigorífico.
- Monsieur Cuisine smart por 499,99 euros, uno de los mejores robots de cocina que hay.
- Cafetera espresso por 54,99 euros, con diseño retro y un color crema muy vistoso.
Hidrolimpiadora flexible
Uno de los productos más populares de Lidl es esta hidrolimpiadora flexible de la marca Silvercrest. Tiene una potencia de 2000 W y una presión máxima de hasta 150 bares, suficiente para poder despegar suciedad incrustada que tengamos en el patio, la terraza o incluso en el coche. Su precio normalmente es de 80,99 euros, pero está rebajada hasta los 66,99 euros.
Si buscas una alternativa, tienes esta hidrolimpiadora Bosch por 94,99 euros en Amazon. Tiene una presión de 125 bares y viene con una boquilla que es 3 en 1.
Hidrolimpiadora flexible
Ronda de enchufe
Es muy probable que tengas una zona de casa con un solo enchufe y quieras conectar más dispositivos. Esta ronda de enchufe es una solución muy económica (cuesta 10,99 euros) y te permitirá conectar hasta cuatro cosas. Además, podemos recoger su cable de forma cómoda. Sí, por otro lado, solo quieres conectar dos dispositivos y quieres algo más económico, también tienes esta alternativa de doble enchufe en Amazon por 4,25 euros.
Ronda de enchufe
Freidora de aire de cristal
Las freidoras de aire con recipientes de cristal se han puesto muy de moda y Lidl tiene la suya. Esta viene con dos recipientes diferentes (uno de dos y otro de cuatro litros), alcanza los 200 grados y tiene cuatro programas diferentes. Lo más destacable de la misma está en sus recipientes, puesto que sirven para llevar la comida a la mesa o incluso para guardar lo que sobre en el frigorífico.
Su precio es de 74,99 euros, aunque ahora mismo indica en la página web de Lidl que estará disponible en un plazo de dos a cuatro días. Si prefieres una alternativa, tienes ahora mismo rebajada la freidora de este tipo más popular: se trata de la Ninja Crispi y cuesta 109,99 euros.
Freidora de aire de cristal
Monsieur Cuisine smart
Aunque ahora mismo no está a su mejor precio, sigue mereciendo destacar el Monsieur Cuisine, uno de los mejores robots de cocina que hay. Es un dispositivo que no solo sirve para mezclar o remover, sino que lo podemos usar para cocer, dorar o cocinar al vapor, entre otras cosas. Además, tiene balanza incluida y una pantalla táctil que hace que su manejo sea muy intuitivo. Cuesta 499,99 euros.
Una alternativa más económica es la Mambo Touch de Cecotec, que cuesta actualmente 340,34 euros. Tiene 37 funciones, una pantalla táctil de 5 pulgadas y también incorpora báscula.
Monsieur Cuisine
Cafetera espresso
Y terminamos con esta cafetera espresso, disponible por 54,99 euros. Es ideal para preparar un buen café en casa (aunque, de hecho, puede preparar dos tazas a la vez). Además, cuenta con sistema de desconexión automática y un vaporizador manual para crear una espuma cremosa en la leche. Todo redondeado por un diseño retro con un color crema que la hace muy vistosa.
Una de sus mejores alternativas la tenemos con la Thera Retro de Create, que cuesta actualmente 85,95 euros. Tiene un diseño en la misma línea que la de Lidl (de hecho, su color es muy parecido), aunque cuenta con una bomba de extracción de 20 bares y es muy fácil de limpiar.

articles.title: Jours Flash Prime : l’aspirateur-robot Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 Set passe à 549,99 € chez Amazon
articles.text:
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 aspire et lave les sols. Grâce à sa hauteur de moins de 8 cm, c’est le parfait candidat pour passer sous les meubles. Cet aspirateur-robot laveur passe de 899,99 € à 549,99 € durant les Jours Flash Prime d’Amazon.
Quitte à investir dans un aspirateur-robot laveur, autant choisir un modèle capable de passer sous un maximum de meubles et de s’autonettoyer. C’est ce que propose le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 Set, proposé à 549,99 € chez Amazon durant les Jours Flash Prime. Ce modèle combine deux serpillières rotatives, une navigation avec capteur rétractable et une puissance d’aspiration de 25 000 Pa.
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 Set est disponible à 549,99 € sur Amazon pour les membres Prime.
Pour profiter des Jours Flash Prime n’oubliez pas de devenir membre Amazon Prime. Vous bénéficiez d’un essai gratuit de 30 jours, c’est donc le bon moment pour tester.
Pourquoi choisir le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 ?
- Pour son format fin : une fois son capteur rétracté, sa hauteur de 7,98 cm lui permet de passer sous un grand nombre de meubles bas.
- Pour sa station complète : elle vide le bac à poussière, lave les serpillières à l’eau chaude à 80 °C et les sèche à l’air chaud.
- Pour ses brosses anti-enchevêtrement : si vous avez des animaux de compagnie, leurs poils ne risquent pas de bloquer le robot.
Un robot qui s’invite là où les autres aspirateurs ne vont pas
L’aspirateur-robot laveur Qrevo Edge 2 dispose d’une puissance d’aspiration maximale de 25 000 Pa, associée à une brosse latérale extensible FlexiArm qui se rapproche des plinthes et des angles pour récupérer les poussières en bordure. Si l’on ajoute à cela sa capacité à se glisser facilement sous les meubles, on obtient un aspirateur qui traque la saleté partout. Sa partie dédiée au lavage utilise deux serpillières rotatives. Et pour circuler tout en évitant les obstacles, il combine une caméra, un éclairage structuré et une IA capable d’identifier plus de 280 types d’objets.
Un aspirateur autonome, mais qui demande de la place
Quant à sa station d’accueil, si elle s’assure de minimiser les besoins de maintenance manuelle entre deux utilisations, elle prend néanmoins de la place au sol : ses dimensions sont de 34 cm de largeur, 48,7 cm de profondeur et 52,1 cm de hauteur. Avant de commander, assurez-vous d’avoir assez d’espace pour l’installer chez vous.
✅ Les points forts
- Capteur de navigation rétractable et hauteur de 7,98 cm.
- Vidage automatique et lavage des serpillières à chaud.
- Brosse latérale extensible pour les bordures.
❌ Les limites
- Station encombrante dans un petit logement.
- Connexion Wi-Fi limitée à la bande 2,4 GHz.
À 549,99 € pour les membres Prime, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 Set est un bon plan des Jours Flash Prime d’Amazon.
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est un aspirateur-robot laveur adapté aux foyers où se trouvent des meubles bas et des animaux. Il peut passer tous les jours avec une bonne autonomie.
Cependant, dans les petits logements, sa station d’accueil peut s’avérer encombrante, et c’est un point à ne pas négliger avant de craquer pour ce bon plan des Jours Flash Prime.

articles.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra : Samsung aurait une batterie de folie dans les cartons
articles.text:
Nous vous en parlions récemment, un document provenant d’un organisme chinois de certification a révélé que le Galaxy S27 Ultra disposera d’une batterie de 5 700 mAh. Le S26 Ultra étant équipé d’une batterie de 5 000 mAh, nous serions face à une amélioration notable (+14 %), si cette information est confirmée. Mais Samsung ne se contenterait pas seulement d’intégrer une batterie plus importante dans le S27 Ultra : la vitesse de recharge devrait également être améliorée.
Samsung aurait optimisé la vitesse de recharge du S27 Ultra
Selon plusieurs rumeurs, le S27 Ultra serait compatible avec une charge filaire de 60 W (20 V/3 A). Exactement comme le S26 Ultra donc. En revanche, Samsung aurait travaillé sur la vitesse de recharge de son nouveau téléphone haut de gamme, selon le leaker WalleGalaxy. Pour être plus précis, le S27 Ultra parviendrait à maintenir une charge élevée plus longtemps au début de la recharge.
Le leaker explique que le téléphone serait capable de maintenir une puissance de 55 à 56 W plus longtemps au début de la recharge. Ce changement permettrait de bénéficier d’une recharge légèrement plus rapide (2 à 3 %) par rapport à celle du S26 Ultra, et ce, même si la batterie du S27 Ultra est plus grande. Au passage, rappelons que le prix du S27 Ultra devrait lui aussi être plus grand. Quoi qu’il en soit, il n’est donc pas ici question d’une recharge plus puissante, mais d’une optimisation de la courbe de charge.
Enfin une batterie en silicium-carbone pour le S27 Ultra ?
Cette information est à prendre avec davantage de pincettes, mais le leaker coréen Lanzuk affirme que Samsung teste des batteries silicium-carbone pour le Galaxy S27 Ultra, une technologie qui pourrait expliquer sa batterie de 5 700 mAh. Pour rappel, le constructeur sud-coréen a intégré une batterie équipée d’une anode en silicium-carbone dans ses derniers smartphones pliants, comme le Galaxy Z Fold8. Il serait logique que son nouveau smartphone haut de gamme bénéficie également de cette technologie.
Lors de notre test du S26 Ultra, nous avions rangé l’absence de batterie silicium-carbone dans les points négatifs de l’appareil. Espérons que cela ne soit pas aussi le cas pour le S27 Ultra. Rendez-vous début 2027 pour le savoir.

articles.title: GPU utilization in post-training shapes better AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
CoreWeave targets GPU utilization in continuous AI post-training
GPU utilization during post-training depends partly on how efficiently infrastructure moves data and loads updated models. As enterprises continually refine AI agents, reducing delays between training rounds can help keep that process moving.
The need for continual improvement is pushing CoreWeave Inc. to build a full-stack AI cloud for the agent lifecycle. You.com Inc. provides web search tools for those agents, according to Saurabh Sharma (pictured, right), chief product officer of You.com.
“What we’re seeing is that the ceiling is no longer model intelligence,” Sharma said. “The models are getting more intelligent, but it’s their ability to use the tools that dictates the agent’s success.”
Sharma and Corey Sanders (left), senior vice president of product at CoreWeave, spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and John Furrier at the Fully Connected event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed tool skills, graphics processing unit utilization and continuous model improvement. (* Disclosure below.)
Post-training puts GPU utilization at the heart of the AI loop
CoreWeave has announced CoreWeave Forge, which connects model deployment, evaluation and improvement. Its reinforcement learning Rollouts capability, currently in preview, supports repeated cycles of generating training responses and updating models, Sanders explained.
“For the weight synchronization, this is an area that we’ve done a bunch of work to be able to bring the weights in sort of a hot start versus starting cold every time,” Sanders said. “Instead of the weight always coming from object storage, we now get weights from other peers nearby.”
Data movement also matters when the goal is keeping GPU utilization high between training rounds. CoreWeave AI Object Storage now supports cross-region writes, letting post-training jobs write results back for others to use, according to Sanders.
“There actually is core infrastructure like our object storage, which we’ve built around trying to get data into the GPU as fast and as easy as possible,” Sanders said. “You write like it’s a local machine. We treat it like it’s a global system.”
You.com, which runs its own web index, has joined CoreWeave’s partner network to give agents a search layer. Working with Nvidia, the companies used RL Rollouts to post-train Nemotron 3.5 Lightning in eight hours with You.com’s web search tools.
“What our customers are seeing is that … they are able to run their workloads with higher accuracy and lower total cost of ownership,” Sharma said. “If you can do this in eight hours, this is no longer something that only the frontier labs can do.”
