articles.title: EV charging company plans to deploy 100,000 Nvidia GPUs in pods at its roadside sites across the US — aims to offer ‘world’s first edge inference compute network using idle EV charging capacity’
articles.text:
EV charging company plans to deploy 100,000 Nvidia GPUs in pods at its roadside sites across the US — aims to offer ‘world’s first edge inference compute network using idle EV charging capacity’
We hope charging location security will be adequate with up to 48 Nvidia Hopper or Blackwell Ultra GPUs worth roughly $2M+ in each pod.
EV charging firm Xeal plans to use its existing U.S. network to deploy the “world’s first edge inference compute network using idle EV charging capacity.” The big idea is that it already has 1,600+ locations and 200MW of permitted, installed electrical infrastructure, so it aims to “deploy over 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs” at these sites. Thus it has developed Latient Pods (pictured), with each containing up to 48 Nvidia Hopper or Blackwell Ultra GPUs. We hope charging location security will be adequate to keep thieves away from these cabinets, as they are probably worth $2M+ each.
Nikhil Bharadwaj, co-founder and CEO of Xeal, explained that Latient Pods can deliver inference compute today while new data centers are still being built. “Latient is the fastest way to bring new compute online, tapping already permitted and grid-connected, yet idle energy capacity, located right where it's needed for ultra-low latency, with no water hookup requirements,” highlighted the exec. Grid interconnect is said to be one of the trickiest things for those looking to bring new compute online, but Xeal’s EV charging sites, which “typically operate at less than 10% of permitted capacity,” can deliver processing power via a distributed network across a metropolitan area.
An Nvidia rep also praised the upcoming Latient Pod network for being an innovative way to bring low-latency inference closer to users while making better use of infrastructure that has already been built.
In the rendered image from Xeal, a Latient Pod looks quite a lot like a broadband fiber cabinet that you might have on your street. A pod will boast the following specs/features:
- Powered by idle EV charging capacity
- Up to 48 Nvidia Hopper or Blackwell Ultra GPUs
- Self-contained independent cooling, no water hookup required
- Quiet operation at less than 65 dBs (comparable to a washing machine)
- Fixed rental or ancillary revenue for site owner
- Adds up to $1 million in property value for little-to-no investment
- All power bills covered as a tenant pass-through
- Potential savings for EV charging customers
- Built to withstand the outdoors, NEMA 4 enclosure
- Installed and running in hours
If Xeal has 1,600+ locations, and one Latient Pod has up to 48 GPUs, its touted purchasing target of 100,000 Nvidia GPUs suggests some sites will have more than a single pod at the location. Or perhaps it intends to build more EV sites, up to nearly 2,100 in total.
It claims that the location of its pods around metro areas, a feature dubbed Metro Edge, offers sub-20ms latency, a significant speedup over inference located in a distant data center.
We’ve previously reported on EVs and distributed computing, but in a slightly different context. Last year we discussed Elon Musk’s proposal to make use of the untapped asset of the millions of Tesla cars out there. He called it “100 gigawatts of inference” that could be used when the vehicles are “bored.”
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Meanwhile, we must remember that EV charging stations are already being targeted by thieves. We reported about a ‘plague’ of electric car charger cable thefts driven simply by the copper scrap value of the hefty cables used at the sites. Imagine the security that would be required if/when Latient Pods are deployed, stuffed with extremely expensive GPUs. 48 Blackwell GPUs would be worth around $2,000,000 according to 2024 figures – so surely much more by now.
The first Latient Pod will be online by the end of the year, says Xeal.

Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Spurred on by AI usage, Google Docs and Drive now support markdown files natively
articles.text:
Spurred on by AI usage, Google Docs and Drive now support markdown files natively
Google now supports .md on a deeper level
- Google highlights significance of .md files given the rise in AI agents, including its own Gemini
- Markdown files can now be previewed as they're intended to be seen
- All Google Workspace accounts will be getting the update
Despite having its own file formats, Google has confirmed it will be supporting markdown (.md) files natively amid their ongoing popularity thanks to - you guessed it - AI.
It means users will be able to view and edit markdown files directly in Google Workspace without having to convert them to a Docs format first.
Better still, they won't be shown in plain text format, because the update also allows them to be rendered as they're intended to be viewed, including formats like links and tables.
Google Drive finally supports .md files
"Editing Markdown files in Docs also enables both users and agents to collaborate without forcing anyone to write raw syntax, handle manual file conversions, or give up Docs' real-time editing and commenting tools," the company explained, and there's one word that stands out in that explanation – "agents."
The company knows that markdown has become more important recently because it's widely used by AI agents and other coding tools. "Markdown has become the common language between humans and AI agents," Engineering VP Chandu Thota explained in an X post.
By rendering .md files visually for human users but retaining the formatting simplicity of markdown syntaxes, it means users won't need to keep changing between file types in Google Drive.
It's also especially relevant to Google's broader strategy, because the company announced in April 2026 that Gemini would be able to generate multiple file types, including markdown.

All Google Workspace customers are set to get the change, so it's not limited to just business users, but it could take up to 15 days from the initial launch (October 5) for some users to finally see the changes.

articles.title: TCL P80 Ultra : nous avons testé son écran Amoled NxtPaper, et les reflets prennent une claque
articles.text:
TCL P80 Ultra : nous avons testé son écran Amoled NxtPaper, et les reflets prennent une claque
Test labo // TCL marie enfin sa technologie d’écran mat NxtPaper à l’Amoled sur un smartphone, le P80 Ultra. Une association prometteuse sur le papier, que nous avons passée sous nos sondes.
Après plusieurs générations cantonnées aux dalles LCD, la technologie NxtPaper passe à l'Oled. Présentée au MWC 2026, cette déclinaison trouve pour la première fois sa place dans un smartphone disponible dans le commerce avec le TCL P80 Ultra. L’idée reste la même : réduire les reflets et ménager les yeux, sans renoncer cette fois aux noirs profonds et au contraste de l’Oled. Et sur ce point, le résultat est loin d’être surestimé.
TCL P80 Ultra
Un écran qui ne joue pas au miroir
Le P80 Ultra dispose d'une dalle de 6,83 pouces affichant 2772 x 1280 pixels, soit 447 ppp, avec un taux de rafraîchissement maximal de 120 Hz. Pas de LTPO ici : TCL mise sur un rafraîchissement variable et non adaptatif. Le constructeur chinois promet aussi un pic lumineux à 3200 cd/m² et une couverture complète du DCI-P3.
Notre exemplaire de test tient presque cette promesse, puisqu'il grimpe à 3142 cd/m², un excellent niveau pour conserver une image lisible en extérieur. À l’autre extrême, la luminosité descend à 2,94 cd/m², de quoi éviter de se brûler la rétine au fond du lit.
Côté calibration, si le réglage par défaut en fait un peu trop, on s'attendait à pire. Nous relevons un Delta E de 3,88, au-dessus du seuil de 3 à partir duquel les écarts deviennent perceptibles à l'œil nu, ainsi qu’une température des couleurs un peu trop froide (7015 K). Un passage par les réglages change nettement la donne : en sélectionnant le mode Naturel, le Delta E tombe alors à 1,90 et la température atteint 6389 K, plus proche des 6500 K de la norme vidéo de référence.
8,29 % de réflectance : notre record sur smartphone
Le clou du spectacle reste toutefois le revêtement de l’écran. TCL applique une nano-gravure antireflet sous son verre Nano Crystal Shield, avec un rendu mat immédiatement perceptible. Sous le doigt, la sensation est douce, presque comme si un film protecteur avait déjà été posé. Ce n’est pourtant pas le cas, mieux vaut donc rester prudent face aux rayures.
Cette finition n’est pas qu’un effet de style. Notre mesure de réflectance s’établit à seulement 8,29 %, soit la plus faible valeur de notre comparatif. À titre de repère, nous avons relevé 44,62 % sur le Google Pixel 11, 44,68 % sur le Samsung Galaxy S26 et 35,30 % sur l’iPhone 18 Pro. L’écart est donc énorme : sous une lampe ou en plein jour, l’écran renvoie beaucoup moins l’environnement et reste nettement plus confortable à consulter.
La firme chinoise complète le dispositif par une polarisation circulaire pouvant atteindre 95 %, une réduction matérielle de la lumière bleue, ainsi que des modes Papier et Max Ink accessibles via la touche NxtPaper. Des fonctions déjà familières aux utilisateurs des tablettes de la marque, mais qui profitent ici enfin des qualités intrinsèques de l’Amoled.
Le pari est donc réussi : NxtPaper conserve son identité "papier", tout en se débarrassant du principal compromis de ses versions LCD. La luminosité mesurée reste en retrait de la promesse constructeur et l'affichage par défaut mérite une correction, mais avec une réflectance aussi basse, le TCL P80 Ultra signe surtout l’un des écrans de smartphone les plus atypiques — et les moins brillants — passés dans nos labos.

articles.title: From Billions to Watts: Unpacking AI Infrastructure Bottlenecks - EE Times
articles.text:
Broadcom can lend Anthropic up to $42 billion to help finance computing infrastructure. Nvidia says it intends to invest as much as $100 billion in OpenAI as Nvidia systems are deployed. AMD has issued warrants to major customers whose vesting is tied partly to gigawatt-scale GPU purchases.
Capital is clearly available for AI infrastructure. The harder question is what those commitments will produce in the physical world.
The industry increasingly describes AI infrastructure in gigawatts. OpenAI and Nvidia have announced plans for at least 10 GW of Nvidia systems. OpenAI has a separate definitive agreement with AMD covering 6 GW of GPUs and another collaboration with Broadcom covering 10 GW of OpenAI-designed accelerators and networking systems. Those figures look comparable, but they describe different things.
A gigawatt of contracted GPUs is not necessarily a gigawatt of data center capacity. Contracted cloud compute is not the same as installed hardware, and infrastructure described as secured is not necessarily infrastructure that has memory, networking, cooling, and power available to operate.
That distinction matters because AI infrastructure is becoming a systems problem, not simply a semiconductor capacity problem.
I have followed semiconductor capacity cycles for more than two decades, including during my years at Intel. Purchase orders are only one part of the capacity equation. Manufacturing, packaging, memory, and the infrastructure around the chip determine how quickly demand turns into usable systems.
Nvidia’s Vera Rubin reference design illustrates the scale involved. Its published configuration for a 100 MW AI factory includes 40,000 Rubin GPUs and 12 petabytes of HBM4. A simple linear scaling of that reference design would imply roughly 400,000 GPUs and 120 petabytes of HBM4 per gigawatt. That is an illustration, not a universal conversion factor for AI capacity.
The memory requirement alone is significant. Samsung expects HBM to account for nearly 30% of industry DRAM wafer capacity in 2027, up from about 20% currently. Samsung also notes that HBM and standard DRAM share wafer production capacity, so growth in one affects the capacity available for the other.
The next challenge is connecting the processors. Large AI clusters require switches, network-interface cards and large volumes of high-speed optical links. At rack level, rising power density adds liquid cooling, coolant distribution, large power systems, and more complex commissioning.
The GPU is therefore only one component in a much larger industrial system. The supply chain extends from semiconductor manufacturers and memory producers to cooling suppliers, electrical contractors, utilities, and power generation companies.
That becomes clear when construction starts.
JLL estimates that a 50 MW data center takes about 18 months to build globally. Developers are ordering some equipment as much as two years in advance, yet 57% of projects experienced construction delays of at least three months in 2025. In the U.S., JLL puts average equipment lead times at roughly 42 weeks, 83% above 2019 levels. Transformers and switchgear average about 43 weeks, while generators average roughly 51 weeks. A contracted gigawatt can therefore exist long before it becomes usable compute.
The difference also becomes more important closer to the power grid. Semiconductor capacity is relatively fungible. Wafers can be reallocated between customers, and some production steps can be moved between suppliers. A substation, transmission connection, or gas pipeline belongs to a specific location.
That makes power increasingly central to AI deployment. Enverus forecasts that 22.5 GW of new U.S. data center demand between 2026 and 2030 will be served by behind-the-meter generation, equivalent to about 36% of projected U.S. data center capacity additions during that period. Its forecast includes 29.6 GW of gas-fired generation.
Developers are effectively considering power generation as part of the data center project rather than waiting for conventional grid expansion. That can shorten some timelines, but it creates another set of constraints around turbines, engines, transformers, pipelines, and permits. Enverus itself cautions that access to a theoretical power source does not automatically make a site ready for construction.
The financing structures now emerging around AI make these physical constraints more relevant.
OpenAI and Nvidia’s announced partnership calls for at least 10 GW of Nvidia systems, representing millions of GPUs. Nvidia says it intends to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI as the systems are deployed. The first gigawatt is targeted for the second half of 2026 using Vera Rubin. Importantly, the arrangement was announced as a letter of intent rather than a completed purchase obligation.
OpenAI separately entered a definitive agreement with AMD covering 6 GW of GPUs across multiple generations. The first 1 GW deployment using MI450-series products is scheduled to begin in the second half of 2026. AMD also issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares, with vesting linked in part to GPU-purchase milestones.
A separate OpenAI collaboration with Broadcom covers 10 GW of OpenAI-designed accelerators and networking systems, with deployment targeted to begin in the second half of 2026 and finish by the end of 2029.
Those announcements cannot simply be added together and treated as separate data center capacity. They describe different layers of the same infrastructure buildout.
The Meta-AMD agreement shows why that distinction matters. AMD describes the broader relationship as covering up to 6 GW, but its SEC filing says Meta made a binding commitment for the initial 1 GW. Full vesting of Meta’s warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares depends on purchases eventually reaching 6 GW. The headline number and the current binding obligation are not identical.
Anthropic provides another example of how financing and hardware are becoming intertwined.
According to Anthropic’s IPO prospectus, as reported by Reuters, Broadcom agreed to lend the company up to $42 billion to help finance infrastructure. Reuters reported that the facility could cover roughly one-third of a five-year, $125.2 billion commitment for TPU computing capacity. Anthropic is also expected to become Broadcom’s largest chip design customer in 2027.
This does not mean the underlying demand is artificial. It does mean that the roles of supplier, customer, investor, and financier are becoming increasingly difficult to separate.
The same future unit of compute can now appear in several places: as a semiconductor order, a cloud compute commitment, a data center project, a financing obligation, and eventually as capacity described by an AI company as secured.
Each disclosure may be accurate on its own. Problems arise when they are added together as though each represents separate physical capacity. That is the accounting issue behind the industry’s growing use of gigawatts. A gigawatt is a precise unit of electrical power. It is much less precise as a measure of AI capacity.
None of this means the AI infrastructure boom cannot be built. Semiconductor manufacturers are expanding production, memory suppliers are adding HBM capacity, and data center developers are ordering equipment earlier and looking for alternatives to conventional grid connections.
The more important constraint may be timing. Capital can be committed quickly. A GPU agreement can be signed years before delivery, and a cloud customer can contract for compute before the underlying facility exists. Usable compute becomes available only when the semiconductor, memory, network, rack, cooling, and power layers are ready in the same place.
A one-year delay does more than move a construction schedule. It affects utilization, financing costs, depreciation assumptions, and the timing of revenue throughout the infrastructure supply chain.
For that reason, announced gigawatts may become less useful as the AI buildout matures. A better measure may be time to energized compute: How long it takes a financial commitment to become a functioning system that can actually run workloads.
The AI industry has shown that it can finance enormous amounts of future capacity. The next test is how quickly the physical infrastructure can catch up.

The Energy Barrier Reshaping AI Hardware

articles.title: Uber amplía su negocio más allá de los viajes y compra una plataforma de catering por 2.300 millones de dólares
articles.text:
Uber acordó adquirir ezCater, una plataforma estadounidense especializada en catering y servicios de comida para empresas, por 2.300 millones de dólares en efectivo. La operación permitirá a la compañía ampliar Uber Eats hacia un segmento diferente al de los pedidos individuales y reforzar su presencia entre clientes corporativos.
El acuerdo combina la plataforma de catering de ezCater con la amplia red de restaurantes de Uber Eats y las relaciones que Uber for Business mantiene con empresas. La operación todavía debe recibir las aprobaciones regulatorias correspondientes y se espera que quede cerrada durante los próximos meses.
Una plataforma con miles de restaurantes
ezCater cuenta con una red de más de 140.000 restaurantes en Estados Unidos y permite a las empresas solicitar comida para diferentes tipos de actividades, desde reuniones pequeñas hasta programas de alimentación de gran escala y servicios recurrentes.
La plataforma también ofrece atención al cliente durante las 24 horas, un elemento especialmente relevante para compañías que necesitan coordinar pedidos para empleados, reuniones o eventos. A diferencia de las entregas individuales habituales de Uber Eats, este negocio maneja pedidos de mayor volumen y valor.
Durante los últimos 12 meses, ezCater registró más de 2.500 millones de dólares en reservas brutas, con un crecimiento anual de dos dígitos. La compañía también es rentable si se consideran sus ingresos operativos bajo criterios no GAAP y, según Uber, se espera que la adquisición contribuya a mejorar el margen de la compañía.
Otro dato que explica el interés de Uber está en el tamaño de los pedidos. El valor promedio de una orden realizada a través de ezCater supera los 400 dólares, una cifra considerablemente superior a la de un pedido convencional de comida.
Uber busca crecer más allá de los pedidos individuales
La adquisición forma parte de una estrategia más amplia de Uber para encontrar nuevas fuentes de crecimiento en su negocio de entregas. La compañía busca aprovechar su infraestructura, sus restaurantes asociados y su base de clientes para atender pedidos de mayor tamaño.
“El catering es un gran negocio y puede ser una enorme fuente de ingresos para los restaurantes”, señaló Dara Khosrowshahi, director ejecutivo de Uber, al anunciar la operación.
Por su parte, Nihad Rahman, CEO de ezCater, destacó que la compañía busca integrar su experiencia en catering y servicios B2B —es decir, negocios que venden servicios a otras empresas— con el ecosistema de clientes, comercios y repartidores de Uber.
La estrategia también responde al crecimiento que Uber Eats ha registrado recientemente. En el trimestre finalizado el 30 de junio, el negocio de entregas aumentó 25% sus reservas brutas, impulsado por un mayor volumen de pedidos y un incremento en el número de usuarios activos.
Durante la presentación de resultados, Khosrowshahi señaló que los pedidos para grupos grandes y la recogida de comida directamente en los establecimientos representan nuevas oportunidades para continuar expandiendo el negocio.
Una nueva apuesta por la entrega de alimentos
La compra de ezCater llega poco después de otro movimiento importante de Uber en el sector de la alimentación. En julio, la compañía acordó adquirir Delivery Hero mediante una oferta pública de adquisición valorada en 14.800 millones de dólares.
Esa operación, que todavía está pendiente de aprobaciones regulatorias y se espera que concluya durante la segunda mitad de 2027, permitiría ampliar las operaciones combinadas de movilidad y entrega de Uber de 79 a 99 mercados.
Con ezCater, Uber apunta ahora a otro tipo de consumidor: las empresas que necesitan organizar comidas para empleados, reuniones y eventos. La compañía podrá combinar la infraestructura de Uber Eats con una plataforma especializada en pedidos grandes, un segmento en el que cada transacción puede representar cientos o miles de dólares.
La operación será completamente en efectivo. J.P. Morgan Securities asesora a Uber, mientras que Evercore trabaja como asesor financiero de ezCater. El cierre dependerá de las condiciones habituales de la transacción y de las autorizaciones regulatorias necesarias.

articles.title: Skydance nasce após fusão de Paramount e Warner • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Skydance nasce após fusão de Paramount e Warner
Acordo de R$ 552 bilhões coloca sob o mesmo teto grandes estúdios, canais de TV e serviços de streaming.
Os famosos estúdios de cinema Paramount e Warner agora estão sob o mesmo teto. Após meses de negociações e decisões judiciais, o acordo de fusão foi aprovado nos Estados Unidos, criando a nova empresa Skydance Corporation. A companhia concluiu nesta terça-feira (06/10) a aquisição da Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) por US$ 111 bilhões (cerca de R$ 552 bilhões).
A união concentra um portfólio com estúdios e canais conhecidos em Hollywood. No cinema, se juntam a Warner Bros. Pictures e a Paramount Pictures, enquanto o streaming reúne a HBO Max, Paramount+ e Pluto TV.
David Ellison segue à frente do conglomerado como presidente e co-CEO, ao lado de Ynon Kreiz, ex-chefe da Mattel. Entre as figuras com grande poder na companhia também está o pai de David, Larry Ellison, fundador da Oracle.
A disputa judicial chegou a interromper temporariamente o negócio. Em julho, a Justiça dos Estados Unidos suspendeu a operação após procuradores-gerais de 12 estados, liderados pela Califórnia, entrarem com uma ação contra o acordo. Com as fusões Warner/Paramount e Disney/Fox, Hollywood deixa de ter seis grandes estúdios e passa a ter quatro.
A Skydance também passa a controlar CBS, CBS News, CNN, HBO, MTV, TBS, TNT, Cartoon Network, Nickelodeon, Comedy Central e Food Network, além das divisões CBS Sports e TNT Sports. O catálogo de franquias inclui algumas das principais marcas do entretenimento, como DC, Harry Potter, Senhor dos Anéis, Game of Thrones, Top Gun, Missão: Impossível e Bob Esponja.
A divisão de cinema manterá Paramount e Warner como marcas separadas. O streaming, por outro lado, deve fundir os serviços HBO Max e Paramount+ em algum momento, segundo a Variety. Tudo fica sob controle de Casey Bloys, atual chefe do canal HBO e da HBO Max.
Apesar de ter sido aprovada nos principais órgãos antitruste pelo mundo, incluindo no Brasil, sem grandes restrições, a empresa se comprometeu a cumprir diversas obrigações nos próximos anos para fechar o acordo com os estados. Entre eles:
O descumprimento das regras de lançamentos e distribuição de filmes pode levar à venda da participação da empresa na produtora Miramax e no pagamento de até US$ 30 milhões (R$ 149 milhões) por filme não lançado. Nos negócios de TV, a Skydance pode ser obrigada a vender canais como Comedy Central e VH1.

articles.title: Oliver Blume, CEO de Volkswagen: "Es el momento de fijar el rumbo correcto sobre el CO₂ y el comercio con China"
articles.text:
La industria europea del automóvil se acerca a uno de sus años decisivos para definir cómo quiere que sea su mercado en los próximos años. En 2027 se contabilizarán las emisiones medias de los fabricantes y se echarán cuentas. El que se pase, tendrá que pagar. Todo ello mientras los reguladores presionan por el made in Europe y dejan la puerta abierta a los coches chinos con motores de combustión.
Por eso Volkswagen ya presiona.
"El momento". "Ahora es el momento de fijar el rumbo correcto para el ‘Made in Europe’, la normativa de CO₂ y el comercio con China". Son las palabras de Oliver Blume, CEO de Volkswagen en un anuncio publicado justo antes del Salón del Automóvil de París que abrirá sus puertas la próxima semana.
Estos días, los fabricantes están haciendo las presentaciones de sus coches o prototipos más llamativos pero el grueso de las novedades llegará durante el fin de semana o los días posteriores. En este caso, Volkswagen ha aprovechado para compartir el anuncio de que contará con diversas mesas redondas y ponencias para charlar sobre el futuro de la industria.
Arraigo. Ya en el anuncio de estas charlas, Oliver Blume ha querido dejar claro por dónde transcurrirán las mismas. Y es que en el texto asegura que "Europa tiene todo lo que necesita para seguir siendo económicamente exitosa en el futuro: fortaleza industrial, conocimiento tecnológico y una enorme capacidad de innovación".
Pero, sobre todo, se señala que "el Grupo Volkswagen sigue firmemente arraigado en Europa. Como nuestro hogar, centro de innovación y pilar de la fortaleza industrial, Europa es fundamental para nuestra ambición a largo plazo de convertirnos en el Global Automotive Tech Driver. Queremos impulsar una estrecha colaboración entre empresas y política".
No es casual. Estas declaraciones en las que se recalca el arraigo europeo de Volkswagen no son casuales. Llegan justo cuando la compañía está en mitad de un proceso de ahorro de costes que supondrá el despido de hasta 100.000 trabajadores y haya dejado en el aire el futuro de hasta cuatro plantas alemanas. Tampoco se sabe qué sucederá con Seat, compañía que ha sido señalada para sufrir un apagado silencioso en menos de cuatro años.
Volkswagen ha achacado esta reestructuración a las presiones europeas por saltar al coche eléctrico y cuánto está apretando la competencia china en nuestro suelo. Hay que tener en cuenta que los coches eléctricos que llegan desde China sí pagan aranceles pero no lo hacen los que cuentan con motor de combustión.
Esto ha provocado situaciones llamativas como fabricantes chinos peleando a precio dentro de los coches eléctricos, abriendo brecha entre los híbridos enchufables (y no enchufables) y, sin embargo, coches del Grupo Volkswagen como el Cupra Tavascan que tiene que pagar aranceles por venir desde China.
Competencia. Uno de lo problemas de Volkswagen es que se ha visto inmerso en una tormenta perfecta. Sus coches en China han dejado de interesar (como casi todos los fabricantes europeos allí) hasta el punto de que Audi ha tenido que cambiar su imagen de marca y, de hecho, los productos que vende no son suyos. Esto es un problema mayor cuanto más caro era el coche y más rendimiento sacaban por unidad, por eso Porsche se ha desplomado.
UN VISTAZO A...
Al mismo tiempo, en Europa la competencia china está apretando con coches híbridos que, como decíamos, no pagan aranceles. Eso ha llevado a Volkswagen a presionar para que les imponga nuevas barreras comerciales. Esto último es algo que lleva tiempo rumoreándose pero que sigue estando en el aire. Parece que, sobre todo, por las posibles repercusiones económicas que podría tomar China frente a este movimiento europeo.
Emisiones. En esa tormenta perfecta no solo juega un papel relevante la caída en China y el aterrizaje de estos fabricantes en Europa. La propia Unión Europea está presionando mucho para que los fabricantes cumplan con unos niveles de emisiones que en 2025 consideraron irreales. O, al menos, imposibles de cumplir.
A finales del año pasado, la industria del automóvil consiguió un balón de oxígeno. La idea es que todo fabricante cuyas emisiones medias por coche vendido superaran los 95,6 gr/km de CO2, pagaría una multa de 95 euros por cada gramo superado y coche vendido. Es decir, excederse en 10 gramos y vender 1 millón de coches supondría una multa de 950 millones de euros. Volkswagen vendió en 2025 casi cuatro millones de coches en Europa por lo que las multas hubieran sido disparatadas.
Como consecuencia de esa presión, los reguladores aceptaron que puedan seguir vendiéndose coches con motores de combustión (en un número muy limitado de unidades y en condiciones muy exigentes) a partir de 2035. Pero, sobre todo, aceptaron que esa media se haga con las ventas totales del periodo 2025-2027. El año que viene se entra en un año clave porque se intentará compensar los excesos de 2025 y 2026.
A la carrera. Volkswagen llega al final de esta carrera al sprint apretando todo lo que puede. La compañía está lanzando los Volkswagen ID.Polo, el Cupra Raval y el Skoda Epiq. Son sus tres propuestas más accesibles para dar un empujón a las ventas, reducir volumen de emisiones y reducir la posible (y muy probable) multa.
Sin embargo, en mitad de esa carrera ha tenido que vender la mitad de la empresa con la que quería fabricar baterías en Sagunto (Valencia) a una empresa china. Este movimiento deja claro que la compañía pretendía desligarse de sus dependencias chinas pero que, ahora mismo, Volkswagen necesita dinero y los conocimientos necesarios para fabricar lo más rápido posible con la mayor fiabilidad posible.
Made in Europe. Eso nos lleva a la última pata de la mesa, al último nubarrón en la tormenta. Al mismo tiempo que en la Unión Europea presionan para imponer soluciones neutras en carbono también están presionando para que la fabricación de los nuevos productos se quede en Europa.
Por eso Volkswagen pide más proteccionismo, ya que está más que demostrado que producir en suelo europeo conlleva unos costes laborales y energéticos mucho más altos que sacar las propuestas a terceros países. La Unión Europea, a través de fondos como los del Plan Auto+, está premiando a quienes fabrican en nuestro suelo con descuentos para las compras.
Sin embargo, empresas como Renault han dejado claro que, incluso produciendo en Europa, la dependencia de China es enorme.

Zalman has launched two new mid-tower cases, the S6 Black and S6 V2 Black, with identical dimensions of 412 x 215 x 486 mm and the same core specifications. articles.title: AI storage strategy: Three insights from Supermicro’s summit- SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Three key insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the Supermicro Open Storage Summit interview series
AI storage strategy is taking on a larger role as enterprises move from successful experiments to systems that must deliver dependable business results. How organizations store, serve and manage data increasingly shapes the performance, cost and practicality of artificial intelligence deployments.
The challenge extends beyond choosing faster hardware. Evolving workloads require enterprises to rethink how their infrastructure supports data-intensive applications. Turning that infrastructure into a production foundation requires coordination across the organization, according to theCUBE Research’s Rob Strechay.
“The organizations succeeding today are focusing less on models and more on operationalization,” Strechay said. “They’re aligning data teams, infrastructure teams and business stakeholders around measurable outcomes and repeatable deployment strategies.”
During the Supermicro Open Storage Summit interview series, industry leaders examined the evolution of storage architectures to meet those production demands. Their discussions explored what it takes to build an efficient, adaptable foundation for enterprise AI. (* Disclosure below.)
Here are three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the event:
Insight #1: AI storage strategy changes the economics of inference.
Keeping graphics processing units productive requires storage that can serve active workloads quickly while accommodating growing volumes of less frequently accessed data. An effective AI storage strategy balances those demands across performance and capacity tiers, pointed out Greg DiFraia, senior vice president of AI and alliance partnerships at Scality Inc.
“We need to drive utilization up as high as it can go, and in order to do that, you’ve got to really think about things differently,” he said. “Because when we look at the topology for customers, it’s that the life cycle, when you’re talking about tens or hundreds of petabytes or even exabytes, it’s not all going to live in flash.”
Expanding agent contexts are also creating demand for storage that stores intermediate calculations used during inference. When those key-value caches outgrow GPU memory, additional tiers must balance capacity with fast access. Solidigm Inc.’s flash drives, Super Micro Computer Inc.’s integrated systems and Vast Data Inc.’s data platform support this evolving hierarchy, emphasized Anat Heilper, director of AI architecture at Vast Data.
“When we talk about [key-value] cache, which is a very significant optimization that can be done in AI inferencing … in essence, it’s the ability to replace compute with storage,” she told theCUBE. “When you have very high KV cache hit rates, we both save on compute and reduce the latency significantly.”
Insight #2: Production AI requires workload-specific systems and operational controls.
Production infrastructure must support the business decisions organizations need to make. In financial services, the speed of data processing can affect risk assessment and capital availability, noted Moiz Kohari, vice president of enterprise AI and data intelligence at DataDirect Networks Inc., who spoke alongside Vince Chen, senior director of solutions architecture at Supermicro.
“If you’re a company like BlackRock or State Street where you’re looking at a trillion dollars on your books and you have 6% to 12% capital lockup, that’s a big deal,” Kohari said. “You’re carrying that risk on your books. We can do those calculations because we can move that data back and forth quickly. When you do that, you’re unlocking 6% of that capital, so that capital can be leveraged to do anything else.”
Meeting those requirements also means assembling components that work together at the required scale. Supermicro’s partner approach addresses that deployment burden through integrated configurations, according to Chen.
“For the enterprise customers to build the AI factory as an AI purpose-built infrastructure, there has been complexity in that,” he said. “What we are doing here is working with our partners to build vertically integrated and then pre-validated T-shirt size options for our customers to choose from.”
Deployment is only the beginning of the operational challenge. As pilots become production services, organizations must accommodate broader usage within infrastructure limits, explained Ruhi Sehgal, agentic AI solutions marketing lead at Nutanix Inc.
“But with this shift comes a new dynamic we know all too well, which is we have highly constrained resources that need to be shared by a massive set of new users,” she said. “How do I ensure resilience? What infrastructure admins do every day — which is managing multi-tenancy, ensuring security [and] optimizing performance — that’s exactly what AI needs.”
Insight #3: Enterprise data becomes useful through access, orchestration and governance.
An AI storage strategy must make enterprise data usable across applications while keeping it available. Lakehouse architectures built around open formats provide a foundation for connecting traditional analytics and newer AI workflows. MinIO Inc.’s AIStor supports Apache Iceberg tables and the Iceberg REST catalog, while Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s processors and Supermicro systems supply the underlying compute, memory and connectivity. Bringing those capabilities together gives organizations more flexibility in putting their data to work, pointed out Greg DeMichillie, vice president of product and technical marketing at MinIO.
“On the data lake side, I think it’s hard to overstate just what a big deal Iceberg has been,” he told theCUBE. “If you think back, it’s not that long ago that every database had its own proprietary format. The idea of an open table format was just bonkers … but we are really seeing now the incredible widespread adoption. That’s enabled us to do really clever things like integrating support for Iceberg into the storage tier.”
That flexibility must extend to documents, images, logs and other unstructured information spread across the enterprise. Coordinating access and movement across the data estate requires several complementary layers: Supermicro’s validated systems, Hammerspace Inc.’s unified namespace and data orchestration, Cloudian Inc.’s object storage and Seagate Technology LLC’s capacity for longer-term retention. Together, those components support a data life cycle spanning active AI use and archival storage, emphasized Sherry Lin, senior product manager of SDS solution at Supermicro. Governance remains essential throughout that life cycle, noted Peter Sjoberg, vice president of worldwide solution architects at Cloudian.
“We see a key goal to put that unstructured data under management so that it is protected, it is safe and secure,” Sjoberg said. “That’s exactly what we’re doing now as this data has moved into the AI era. That data will need to move for different purposes, and you will need to make sure it’s always under your control, unstructured or otherwise, so that you can bring it to your AI needs.”
Get more perspectives on storage and enterprise AI:
- Guests from Supermicro, Vast Data, Kioxia Holdings Corp. and Crusoe Inc. discuss their collaboration, the constraints of current enterprise infrastructure and how agentic AI is reshaping the industry.
- Guests from Supermicro, IBM Corp. and Kioxia talk about how workload requirements, data architectures and coordinated infrastructure design shape inference performance at scale.
- Guests from Supermicro, Hammerspace and Sandisk Corp. discuss how organizations are modernizing storage environments, consolidating infrastructure and building foundations capable of supporting both current and future AI workloads.
- Guests from Supermicro, Solidigm and DDN discuss how integrated AI data platforms can simplify inference deployment, support data control and expand with demand.
- Guests from Supermicro, Scality, Intel Corp. and Iron Mountain Inc. discuss how hybrid storage architectures are evolving, what service providers are learning from customer deployments and how organizations can balance agility with operational control.
- Guests from Supermicro, AMD and Nutanix Inc. talk about their collaboration and the practicalities of AI adoption.

articles.title: Apple One : la hausse de prix frappe la Belgique et la Suisse, et les abonnés français regardent leur facture
articles.text:
Apple a augmenté les prix d’Apple One Famille et Premium dans plusieurs pays européens, dont la Belgique et la Suisse, et prévient ses abonnés par mail. La France ne figure pas dans la liste des pays concernés à ce jour. Jusqu’à quand ?
Apple One a ceci de pratique que les fans de la marque finissent par l’oublier : un seul prélèvement mensuel, plusieurs services et la possibilité de profiter de tout l’écosystème de services proposé par la marque. C’est aussi ce qui rend les hausses de prix discrètes, voire indolores. Apple vient d’en lancer une nouvelle vague en Europe, et la liste des pays touchés réserve quelques surprises pour de nombreux utilisateurs européens.
Apple One Famille et Premier en hausse dans douze pays, Belgique et Suisse comprises
Le montant dépend des pays. En Espagne et au Portugal, les formules Famille et Premium augmentent de 2 € par mois, soit 24 € par an. Les hausses dans les autres pays et devises sont similaires. La formule Individuelle, la moins chère, n’a pas bougé.
Les abonnés concernés reçoivent un mail d’Apple depuis le 5 octobre. Les nouveaux abonnés paient le nouveau tarif immédiatement, tandis que les abonnés existants le verront appliqué à leur prochain renouvellement. Ces pays rejoignent des marchés déjà touchés plus tôt dans l’année.
Une troisième hausse en un an, déjà passée aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni et au Canada
Les formules Famille et Premium avaient déjà augmenté plus tôt aux États-Unis, en Australie, au Canada, au Royaume-Uni et dans quelques autres pays. L’offre Individuelle avait pour sa part renchéri aux États-Unis, au Brésil, au Chili et au Mexique.
En France, Apple One se décline en trois formules. Individuel est facturé 19,95 € par mois, avec 50 Go d'iCloud+, Apple TV, Apple Music et Apple Arcade. Famille coûte 25,95 € et passe à 200 Go d’iCloud+ avec les mêmes services. Premium, à 34,95 €, monte à 2 To et ajoute Apple Fitness+. L’abonnement est sans engagement et se résilie au plus tard la veille du renouvellement mensuel.
Rien n’indique pour l’instant que la France soit concernée, mais les hausses se rapprochent : au moins trois vagues cette année, et des pays voisins comme la Belgique, l’Espagne et la Suisse désormais touchés. À tarifs séparés inchangés, une hausse de 2 €, celle observée en Espagne et au Portugal, ramènerait l’économie de 22 € par mois affichée aujourd’hui sur la formule Premium à 20 €. Mieux vaut donc vérifier dès maintenant ce que chaque service vous coûterait séparément, au cas où.

articles.title: Des ChatGPT « voyous » ont pris d'assaut Wikipedia avec des millions de requêtes, que s'est-il passé ?
articles.text:
Après une plateforme de données des Nations unies, plusieurs sites du gouvernement américain ou encore un portail du gouvernement australien, c’est au tour de la Wikimedia Foundation d’avoir affaire à des agents IA d’OpenAI. En effet, Selena Deckelmann, directrice des produits et de la technologie de la fondation, affirme que des activités d’agents « voyous » d’OpenAI ont été découvertes sur Wikipedia, Wikidata, Wikimedia Commons et le service Etherpad hébergé par la fondation. Il n’est pas à proprement parler question d’une cyberattaque, mais d’activités non autorisées menées par les agents IA sur ces différentes plateformes.
Des activités d’agents IA d’OpenAI découvertes sur des projets Wikimedia
Les agents d’OpenAI auraient notamment effectué des millions de requêtes automatisées, visité des millions de pages, réalisé des centaines de milliers de requêtes sur Wikidata et tenté des modifications potentiellement malveillantes sur certains outils. Selena Deckelmann affirme par ailleurs que « des agents issus de l’environnement d’OpenAI ont utilisé d’autres wikis publics (des sites web collaboratifs qui ne nous appartiennent pas) pour communiquer et se coordonner entre eux ».
Un lien est également fait avec la panne partielle du Wikidata Query Service survenue du 7 au 11 mai 2026. La directrice des produits et de la technologie de la fondation estime que l’important trafic généré par les agents IA d’OpenAI « pourrait avoir contribué à une panne partielle du WQDS en mai », sans toutefois l’affirmer.
OpenAI accusé de ne pas assez sécuriser ses systèmes
Selena Deckelmann explique : « En tant qu’organisme technologique à but non lucratif hébergeant certaines des plus grandes et des plus utilisées plateformes de connaissances ouvertes au monde, nous sommes profondément préoccupés par l’impact des agents d’IA malveillants sur des plateformes comme la nôtre, construites par des bénévoles du monde entier et reposant sur la promesse d’un internet ouvert ». Elle fait par ailleurs état de coûts pour les serveurs et le personnel de la fondation, mais aussi de risques de panne.
Pour Selena Deckelmann, le constat est sans appel : « OpenAI doit reconnaître sa responsabilité de surveiller et de prévenir ces risques », et estime que « les entreprises spécialisées en IA n’en font pas assez pour sécuriser leurs systèmes et protéger le public des préjudices qu’ils causent ». Sam Altman, PDG d’OpenAI, lui répondrait sans doute qu’il faut accepter les conséquences négatives de l’IA pour pouvoir bénéficier des avantages qu’elle offre.
OpenAI a d’ailleurs été alerté de la situation et a annoncé collaborer sur le dossier. Drew Pusateri, porte-parole d’OpenAI, a déclaré dans un communiqué : « Nous apprécions les conclusions détaillées que Wikimedia nous a communiquées. Nous collaborons avec eux pour examiner et analyser l’activité qu’ils ont identifiée, en parallèle de notre enquête globale, et nous continuerons à partager les informations pertinentes au fur et à mesure de l’avancement de ces travaux ».

articles.title: Wall-mountable record, CD, and cassette players combo is a full hi-fi system with no wires — Trettire's Retro Ambient Audio System serves as functional decor
articles.text:
Wall-mountable record, CD, and cassette players combo is a full hi-fi system with no wires — Trettire's Retro Ambient Audio System serves as functional decor
Ought to elicit more than a few "wow, no wires" comments.
The resurgence of physical media has been in full swing in the alternative music scene for a while. Nowadays, likely as an effect of streaming services' shenanigans, even mainstream audiences are catching on to the tactile experience and ownership offered by a CD or a vinyl record. We covered the Syitren RM1 CD player frame only a few weeks ago, and now the concept is back in full-system form thanks to Trettitre's Retro Ambient Sound System (RASS).
The spiffy-looking setup comprises a vinyl turntable with RGB backlighting, a compact disc player, and a cassette player — all atop a magnetic metal rack complete with a phone holder. The star of the show is the record player, a unit packing an actual Audio-Technica AT-3600L phono cartridge, a self-balancing tone arm, and even a manual speed knob for up to ±5% adjustment. There's Bluetooth support with high-end AptX, AptX HD, and AptX Adaptive codecs, as well as an auxiliary 3.5 mm output.
The physical controls appear to be both simple and reassuringly sized — no menus or touchscreens here. Hi-fi vinyl player units do spend a large portion of their mechanical design on ensuring full vertical stability, however. The vertical orientation of this TTT-LP3 unit is almost a worst-case scenario for this task, so the self-balancing tonearm has its work cut out for it. It's worth noting that since all the components are magnetic, you can just pick them up and put them on a table.
The units are all fully wireless and attach to their frames magnetically, though there's no combined charging mechanism or power supply — each unit has its own battery, USB-C charging port, and Bluetooth connection. The TTT-LP3 record player does have the ability to charge wirelessly with the included T-shaped adapter.
The TTT-DP3 CD player's interface looks to be straightforward. There are physical buttons with individual shapes, and a small OLED screen for displaying track information. The dust cover atop the disc is also magnetic, which is quite a nice touch. Oddly, though, the specs do not list high-end audio codecs for this unit, a strange choice given that CDs have by far the widest sonic range of the physical media types on offer.
As for the TTT-CP3 cassette player, there's not much to say, in a good way. The buttons are decidedly chunky and inviting — one can only hope they elicit the same satisfying clunk as in old-school hi-fi units. As with the CD player, there's no mention of high-end audio codec support, but cassette tapes aren't known for low noise floors or pristine treble, anyway.
You can preorder Trettitre's Retro Ambient Sound System at Kickstarter for $399 if you're quick, with $76 shipping, under the "late pledge" or "early bird" headers. After that, the unit will set you back $429. The individual components are also available if you don't want to grab the entire setup.

Samsung Galaxy : One UI 9 commence à arriver sur d'anciennes générations de smartphones, dont les S24
Bonne nouvelle pour les personnes en possessions de certains anciens smartphones Samsung Galaxy : le constructeur y commence le déploiement de la version 9 de sa surcouche One UI. Android 17 et de nombreuses améliorations sont très proches.
Samsung Galaxy S26 FE
En bêta depuis plusieurs semaines sur un grand nombre d'appareils, One UI 9 arrive en version finale sur toujours plus de tablettes et de smartphones de Samsung. Après les Galaxy S26 qui ont été servis en priorité début septembre, puis les S25 et les smartphones pliants de l'an dernier, ce sont cette fois les appareils de 2024 qui sont concernés.

articles.title: Prime Video transmitirá los premios Emmy gratis y sin necesidad de suscripción
articles.text:
Prime Video transmitirá en exclusiva los premios Emmy en todo el mundo durante seis años, a partir de la ceremonia de 2027. La gala se verá en vivo y gratis, sin necesidad de suscripción, en más de 240 países y territorios.
El acuerdo cambia el recorrido habitual de los Emmy en Estados Unidos. Hasta ahora, la emisión rotaba entre ABC, CBS, FOX y NBC; desde 2027, la plataforma de Amazon concentrará la transmisión global de uno de los eventos centrales de la industria televisiva.
La ceremonia seguirá realizándose en septiembre, aunque con una distribución pensada para una audiencia que consume televisión fuera de la grilla tradicional. El cambio no es solo de pantalla: los Emmy pasan de un esquema de cadenas locales a una plataforma disponible en todo el mundo.
Qué cambia con la llegada de Prime Video
La Television Academy deja atrás el llamado “Wheel Deal”, el acuerdo que repartía los derechos de emisión entre las grandes señales de televisión abierta de Estados Unidos. La nueva alianza le da a los premios una única ventana internacional durante seis años.
Para el público, el dato principal es que la transmisión no tendrá muro de pago. Prime Video emitirá la ceremonia en directo sin exigir una membresía, una decisión que apunta a que la gala pueda seguirse en mercados donde los Emmy tenían una presencia más limitada.
Cris Abrego, presidente de la Television Academy, afirmó que el acuerdo permitirá que espectadores de más de 200 países vean los premios en vivo. Señaló que una plataforma fija abre la puerta a trabajar con el evento durante todo el año y no solo en la noche de la ceremonia.
La apuesta por un evento que dure más que una gala
La alianza contempla acciones más allá de la entrega de estatuillas. Prime Video prevé desarrollar contenidos y experiencias vinculadas a las series, las producciones y los talentos reconocidos por los Emmy.
La intención es que los premios tengan una presencia más constante dentro de la plataforma. En vez de aparecer una vez al año en una cadena distinta, el evento podrá tener continuidad antes y después de la ceremonia.
Mike Hopkins, responsable de Prime Video y Amazon MGM Studios, sostuvo que la transmisión gratuita forma parte de la estrategia de la compañía para ampliar su oferta de entretenimiento. La ceremonia de 2027 será la primera bajo este nuevo modelo de distribución global.
Amazon planea sacar de su balance USD 8.000 millones en chips de Nvidia
Amazon estudia transferir unos USD 8.000 millones en chips de Nvidia a un vehículo financiero externo para reducir el peso de esa infraestructura en su balance.
Luego, la compañía volvería a alquilar los mismos procesadores para utilizarlos en sus operaciones de nube e inteligencia artificial.
La operación incluiría miles de chips Grace Blackwell, ya instalados en más de una docena de centros de datos de Amazon en Estados Unidos.
Según lo publicado por Financial Times, el vehículo de propósito específico se financiaría con deuda de inversores externos para adquirir el hardware, mientras Amazon conservaría su uso mediante contratos de arrendamiento.
La empresa podría ofrecer a los inversores hasta un 10% de participación en el vehículo, aunque no mantendría una tenencia propia.
Si la estructura obtiene una calificación de grado de inversión, podría atraer a aseguradoras y fondos de pensión, que suelen evitar operaciones con mayor riesgo.
El modelo se parece al que utilizan las aerolíneas para financiar flotas, pero tiene una diferencia central: los chips de inteligencia artificial pierden valor con mucha más rapidez que un avión. La renovación constante de la tecnología de Nvidia puede volver menos atractivo el hardware anterior en pocos años.

articles.title: Russia to double internet censorship budget in 2027, plotting new VPN traffic fee
articles.text:
Russia to double internet censorship budget in 2027, plotting new VPN traffic fee
The Russian government is increasing its internet filtering infrastructure
- Budget doubled: Russia will spend $235m on internet blocking in 2027.
- There are plans to charge users a fee for international 5G internet traffic.
- A new legislative package aims to penalize domestic VPN hosting providers.
Russia has unveiled aggressive plans to double its spending on internet blocking infrastructure in 2027, signalling a massive escalation in its ongoing war against VPNs.
According to recent budget drafts uncovered by Russian independent media, the government intends to allocate nearly 20 billion rubles (approx. $235m) to its automated internet filtering system in 2027. In total, censorship spending is expected to reach an unprecedented 60 billion rubles over the next three years.
For everyday Russian citizens relying on VPN services to bypass state propaganda and access international news, the digital walls are rapidly closing in. Not only is the state upgrading its capacity to block traffic, but it is also exploring new ways to financially penalize users who attempt to tunnel out of the domestic internet.
This development follows a recent wave of disruptions where Russia escalated VPN blocks following State Duma elections in a major censorship crackdown.
A multi-billion ruble censorship machine
The Russian government’s internet censorship relies on the "Automated System for Ensuring the Security of the Internet" (ASBI).
This system controls specialized hardware known as TSPU (technical means of countering threats), which Internet Service Providers are legally required to install.
These devices filter network traffic, allowing the state to throttle or block unauthorized websites and VPN protocols.
Originally, the state planned to spend 9.87 billion rubles (approx $115m) on ASBI in 2027. However, the new budget proposal revealed by Verstka and corroborated by The Moscow Times shows a massive increase to 19.87 billion rubles. Overall funding for the federal censor, Roskomnadzor, will grow by 60% in 2027.
This cash injection is designed to vastly expand the system's capacity. Roskomnadzor has been tasked with reaching a 92% efficiency rate in blocking VPNs by 2030, increasing ASBI's throughput by 2.5 times to handle 954 Tbit/s of data.

Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
Traffic fees and server crackdowns
Alongside hardware upgrades, the Ministry of Digital Development is exploring financial deterrents. Kommersant reports that the government is discussing a new fee for users who consume more than 50GB of international traffic on 5G networks.
While telecom operators currently lack the technical capability to separate 5G and LTE international traffic in real-time, the intent is clear: to penalize users who constantly route their traffic outside the country via VPNs.
Simultaneously, a new legislative package dubbed "Anti-Fraud 3.0" aims to severely punish domestic infrastructure providers.
Under these rules, Russian hosting providers will be banned for a year from offering services to individuals who host VPNs or proxies if those services land on a Roskomnadzor registry.
Hosters will be forced to strictly identify their clients and verify the intended use of their physical and virtual servers.
What this means for VPN users in Russia
The situation for Russian internet users is becoming increasingly hostile.
As the Kremlin's war on the global web turned VPNs into Russia's new national utility, authorities have pivoted from simple IP bans to sophisticated Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) techniques.
Over 250 VPN services have already been blocked, echoing earlier campaigns that saw the largest in history, with Russia blocking over 20 popular VPNs in a major internet crackdown.
According to experts, internet providers now have the statistical data needed to precisely throttle VPN performance.
"Operators have accumulated enough statistics to move from total blocks to targeted suffocation of quality," noted Sergei Shcherbakov, technical director at Stakhanovets, highlighting the shift toward making VPNs unbearably slow rather than just outright banned.
Sarkis Darbinyan, expert at RKS Global and VPN Guild, told TechRadar that VPN operators are not standing still either.
"They are upgrading their protocols, adopting new traffic obfuscation methods, building alternative apps, and using many other guerrilla tactics," he said.
"None of this, however, guarantees that any given public VPN will remain accessible from Russia. For the end user, the result is a deteriorating VPN experience and an ever-shrinking number of services that actually work."
For now, Russian citizens continue to play a high-stakes game of cat-and-mouse, relying on advanced obfuscation protocols to bypass an increasingly well-funded digital iron curtain.

articles.title: Celulares Samsung passam a custar o dobro no Brasil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Celulares Samsung passam a custar o dobro no Brasil
Galaxy A07 e Galaxy A17 ficaram até 109% mais caros no Brasil desde o lançamento.
Resumo
- Celulares Samsung das linhas Galaxy A07 e Galaxy A17 tiveram aumentos de até 109% no Brasil desde seu lançamento.
- O Galaxy A07 4G de 256 GB passou de R$ 1.099 para R$ 2.299, por exemplo.
- O aumento de preços é justificado pelo cenário global de alta nos preços de componentes eletrônicos, como chips de memória RAM e armazenamento.
Normalmente, os preços dos celulares caem meses ou até algumas semanas após o lançamento. Mas tem sido diferente na linha Galaxy A: a Samsung reajustou os preços de alguns desses aparelhos em até 109%, como é o caso do Galaxy A07 4G com 256 GB de armazenamento. É o que aponta um levantamento do TecMundo.
O Galaxy A07 4G (LTE) foi lançado no Brasil em setembro de 2025 com preço oficial de R$ 899 para a versão com 128 GB de armazenamento e de R$ 1.099 para a opção de 256 GB. Agora, mais de um ano depois, a loja online da Samsung tem comercializado os mesmos modelos com estes preços (sem considerar eventuais descontos ou promoções):
- Galaxy A07 4G de 128 GB: R$ 1.299 (reajuste de 44,5%)
- Galaxy A07 4G de 256 GB: R$ 2.299 (reajuste de 109%)
Não são só esses smartphones. Outro exemplo notável é o do Galaxy A17 4G (LTE) de 256 GB, que foi lançado na mesma época por R$ 1.599 e, agora, custa R$ 2.399 (reajuste de 50%) na loja online da Samsung. Já o Galaxy A17 5G de 256 GB pulou de R$ 1.849 para R$ 2.699 (aumento de 46%).
É verdade que esses aumentos não foram aplicados subitamente. Alguns modelos das linhas Galaxy A07 e Galaxy A17 tiveram seus preços aumentados em abril deste ano. O que surpreende é a Samsung ter promovido mais uma rodada de reajustes poucos meses depois.
Modelos das linhas Galaxy A27, Galaxy A37 e Galaxy A57 também foram afetados, embora com percentuais de aumento menores.
Por que os celulares estão ficando mais caros?
Trata-se de uma tendência global, que afeta vários segmentos da indústria de tecnologia, não só o mercado de smartphones. Em todos os casos, o fator preponderante é o cenário de aumento crescente de preços de componentes eletrônicos, especialmente de chips de memória RAM e armazenamento.
Voltando à Samsung, é importante esclarecer que os reajustes não afetam somente a família Galaxy A. Recentemente, a linha Galaxy S26 também ficou mais cara no Brasil, com preços de R$ 300 a R$ 1.300 maiores.

Warhammer Survivors Bullet Heaven Gets Early November Launch Date and Release Pricing
Warhammer Survivors is an upcoming bullet heaven game set in the grim-dark Warhammer universe. As the name suggests, the game takes inspiration from the recent flurry of games similar to Vampire Survivors, and it features similar pixel graphics, to boot. As per a recent announcement, Warhammer Survivors now has a November 10 release date on Steam, GOG, Xbox Series, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, and mobile. The developer, Auroch Digital, was previously responsible for Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun, Boltgun - Words of Vengeance, and Starship Troopers: Ultimate Bug War!, so it's safe to say the studio has a decent background in sci-fi properties. According to the game's Steam page, it will launch with 40 playable characters from the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universes, over 75 iconic weapons, and boss battles with notable Warhammer monsters.Each character comes with their own set of unique abilities, stats, and starting weapons, and players can upgrade and swap them out as they progress through each run in the grimdark setting. Despite the permadeath mechanics, the game will also feature permanent progression that will be carried over to future runs, meaning not all is lost if you die to the never-ending horde.

articles.title: El jefe de la NASA pide tener mente abierta ante el aumento de reportes de OVNIs: "Si hay algo, debemos estar"
articles.text:
Los OVNIs han cambiado de nombre, pero no de fama. Siguen teniendo muchas personas pendiente de ellos, tanto en el ámbito de lo esotérico como entre científicos y gobernantes. El Gobierno de Donald Trump se ha puesto como reto analizarlos a fondo. Por eso, a principios de este 2026 ordenó al Departamento de Guerra y a otras agencias identificar y publicar archivos del Gobierno sobre vida extraterrestre, fenómenos anómalos no identificados (UAP) y OVNIs. Ante esta situación, el actual administrador de la NASA, Jared Isaacman, ha insistido en que, si se descubre algo, su agencia debería participar en las pesquisas.
Una postura clara. Isaacman hizo dichas declaraciones durante una entrevista realizada por Blake Burman en NewsNation el pasado 25 de septiembre. Cuando este le preguntó por el actual aumento de hallazgos de UAPs, dijo que deberíamos tener la mente abierta al respecto y que, en caso de encontrarse algo relevante, la NASA tendría que participar en ello. Lo más curioso, es que no es la primera vez que usa exactamente esa frase: "Tengamos la mente abierta". Ya lo hizo en 2023 cuando se anunció el compromiso en firme de Estados Unidos de estudiar más profundamente estos fenómenos.
No obstante, el administrador no considera muy probable que este aumento de UAPs tenga que ver con extraterrestres ni nada por el estilo. Para él hay dos posibles explicaciones. Por un lado, fenómenos naturales poco comprendidos por el momento. Y, por otro, los resultados de las pruebas sigilosas de algún adversario geopolítico.
PURSUE. La iniciativa con la que Trump ha querido desclasificar los vídeos y datos relacionados con UAPs y OVNIs se llama PURSUE, por las siglas de Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters. Toda esta información se está haciendo pública poco a poco en la web War.gov/ufo, con nuevas entregas cada pocas semanas. Cabe destacar que hay millones de registros, muchos de ellos en papel, por lo que hacerlos accesibles para el público general llevará mucho más tiempo que con los más nuevos.
UAPs u OVNIs. En realidad, podría decirse que estos términos hacen referencia a lo mismo. Si en PURSUE se usan los dos es básicamente porque los OVNis, objetos voladores no identificados, serían más antiguos y los UAPs, fenómenos anómalos no identificados (siglas en inglés) más nuevos. Se decidió cambiar el nombre porque este último es un concepto más amplio que, además, carece de las connotaciones pseudocientíficas que sí suelen tener los OVNIs (UFOs en inglés).
¿En serio hay más? Aunque con PURSUE se ha hablado de un aumento de las detecciones de UAPs, muchos expertos recuerdan que, en realidad, se trata de que se notifican más. En un informe preliminar publicado en 2021, se hablaba de la detección de 144 OVNIs en los últimos 17 años. Después, en solo un año, entre mayo de 2023 y junio de 2024, la cifra fue mucho más alta, con 757 avistamientos. Esto puede deberse a que hay mejores métodos de detección y, además, menos estigma a la hora de notificarlos.
Otro dato de los expertos. Además de llamar a la calma con respecto al aumento de OVNis, algunos expertos se muestran reticentes con que sea buena idea hacer pública toda esta información, pues creen que no puede ser bien interpretada por quienes carecen de conocimientos tecnológicos. Se podrían ver extraterrestres donde no los hay.
Lo que dice Isaacman. Además de insistir en que la NASA debe participar en las decisiones relacionadas con OVNIs y de asegurar que lo más probable es que no tengan relación con la vida extraterrestre, Isaacman sí que señala que no debemos descartar que realmente exista dicha vida. Pone como ejemplo las lunas Europa y Encélado, que cuentan con océanos subterráneos y, a pesar de eso, no se han estudiado aún con la suficiente profundidad en busca de vida. Habrá misiones que se dediquen a ello, pero por ahora todos los ojos están puestos en otros mundos, como Marte.
En realidad, la vida extraterrestre puede ser muy amplia. Un solo microorganismo bajo el suelo de Marte sería el hallazgo más importante en materia espacial de todos los tiempos. De ahí a que realmente allí fuera haya una civilización inteligente, hay un camino enorme. Quizás la hubiera y ya se haya extinguido o que aún exista, pero que esté demasiado lejos o no tenga las tecnologías necesarias para que podamos encontrarla. Puede haber millones de opciones, pero posiblemente la inmensa mayoría de OVNIs que Estados Unidos está desclasificando no tengan ni remotamente nada que ver con ellas.

articles.title: Hackers suspected of using AI agents for cyberattacks on South Korean banks, exposing data from about 25,000 customers — officials believe AI models enable actors 'to hack with ease even without specialized skills'
articles.text:
Hackers suspected of using AI agents for cyberattacks on South Korean banks, exposing data from about 25,000 customers — officials believe AI models enable actors 'to hack with ease even without specialized skills'
Most hackers are likely using AI tools to break into networks faster.
Cyberattacks using AI agents against several of the largest South Korean banks, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, and Shinhan Bank, are currently being investigated by South Korean authorities. According to The New York Times, at least 25,000 Shinhan Bank customers had their personal credit information leaked last week, while 99 customers and 20 current or former employees of Kookmin Bank have been affected. 89 Hana Bank customers were also affected by the hacks, which led to their information being stolen.
South Korea’s National Office of Investigation is looking at all three cases, which has also caught the attention of President Lee Jae Myung. The South Korean president said that there were signs that the hackers behind these incidents used AI models, “causing considerable public concern and anxiety,” and that he has instructed his cabinet to confirm the situation and to ensure that the damage from these incidents is minimized. “It’s now become possible to use AI to hack with ease even without specialized skills,” Lee said during the livestreamed cabinet meeting.
AI models are becoming more powerful with every release, and bad actors are taking advantage of them to find weaknesses in secure systems and exploit them. Anthropic reported the first instance of an AI-orchestrated cyberattack in November 2025, which was allegedly orchestrated by a Chinese state-sponsored group. A few months after that, a cybersecurity firm said that Taiwan was targeted by the first-ever end-to-end autonomous cyberattacks by China-linked hackers. Even AI labs that built these AI models aren’t immune from the AI-powered hacks, as security researchers breached OpenAI using Claude and gained access to its internal codebase.
There has been no indication yet of who’s behind the attacks on South Korea’s banking industry — speculation may focus on Seoul’s regional adversaries, but it can be difficult to trace and attribute hacks, especially if the actors know how to cover their tracks. Aside from that, AI agents are known to conduct unintentional cyberattacks on their own, with the Australian government complaining that it took OpenAI 84 days to inform it of a hacking incident involving Australia’s national health portal.
While the leading AI labs are believed to be putting safeguards in place to help prevent their models from being used in illegal and unethical ways, some hackers exploit hallucinations and trick AI agents into running malware. Aside from that, many open-weight and open-source models lack similar guardrails, making it easier for hackers to use them in their activities. While AI models haven’t replaced skilled attackers yet, they have made planning, reconnaissance, and attack execution so much easier and could serve as a force multiplier, allowing hackers to act more quickly and efficiently.

articles.title: Interdiction des lunettes connectées : ce pays européen envisage de passer le cap
articles.text:
Alors que les ventes de lunettes connectées explosent dans le monde, ce type de dispositif équipé de caméras suscite de plus en plus d’inquiétudes liées au respect de la vie privée. Depuis le 20 juillet dernier, les lunettes connectées sont interdites dans les 1 240 tribunaux de l’État de New York.
En France, le parquet de Paris a ouvert une enquête pénale à la suite d’une série de plaintes pour harcèlement sexuel. Aux Pays-Bas, une association de protection des consommateurs néerlandais demande purement et simplement l’interdiction des lunettes connectées Meta Ray-Ban. Il ne s’agit là que de quelques exemples : les lunettes connectées suscitent de réelles craintes. À un tel point que la Norvège envisage leur interdiction dans certains lieux.
Les lunettes connectées bientôt interdites dans certains lieux en Norvège ?
Le gouvernement norvégien travaille actuellement sur un projet de loi visant à interdire les lunettes connectées équipées de caméras dans certains lieux publics : plages, parcs, centres commerciaux, écoles, garderies, établissements de santé, salles de sport ou encore musées. Bien entendu, l’utilisation d’un tel dispositif dans un cadre privé resterait autorisée.
Torgeir Micaelsen, ministre norvégien des Affaires numériques, a expliqué être « inquiet de voir apparaître de nouvelles technologies puissantes où les gens risquent d’être photographiés, filmés ou enregistrés à leur insu ». Il précise ensuite : « Nous ne voulons pas d’une société où les gens s’inquiètent d’être enregistrés à leur insu, photographiés ou filmés dans des lieux et des situations où ils ont l’habitude de ne pas être surveillés ».
Ce projet de loi doit encore être présenté au Parlement norvégien, il n’est donc pas sûr qu’il entre en vigueur prochainement. Le gouverneur de Californie, Gavin Newsom, a par exemple opposé son veto à un projet de loi qui aurait sanctionné les personnes utilisant des lunettes connectées pour filmer quelqu’un à son insu dans des vestiaires, des cabinets médicaux et d’autres lieux où une personne peut raisonnablement s’attendre à préserver sa vie privée. Il a notamment estimé que la Californie disposait déjà de lois encadrant les enregistrements illégaux.
Certains constructeurs de lunettes connectées tentent de rassurer
En septembre dernier, Meta a dévoilé les Ray-Ban Meta Audio, des lunettes connectées sans caméra. L’objectif de l’entreprise américaine est de proposer un dispositif qui respecterait la vie privée, tout en continuant à vendre des modèles avec caméras. Par ailleurs, Meta a annoncé avoir ajouté de nouvelles restrictions à ses lunettes en août dernier. De son côté, HTC a dévoilé les Vive Eagle, des lunettes connectées qui misent sur le respect de la vie privée.
Ces deux exemples montrent que les constructeurs de lunettes connectées sont bien conscients du fait que l’étau se resserre autour de leurs appareils. Cependant, le problème semble insoluble pour eux : les caméras discrètement intégrées représentent l’un des principaux atouts des lunettes connectées. Les supprimer ou les rendre bien visibles ferait perdre une bonne partie de leur attrait.

articles.title: On call AI teaching agents: how MasterClass tackles tutoring costs - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
MasterClass bets AI teaching agents can broaden access to tutoring
AI teaching agents could make personalized instruction available to more learners by reducing the cost and staffing demands of one-to-one tutoring. MasterClass is exploring that potential through a system designed to adapt to how each student learns.
The shift is also feeding CoreWeave Inc.’s full-stack AI cloud push as companies move AI agents out of the lab and into production. Personalization needs a pedagogical framework underneath the technology, according to Mandar Bapaye (pictured, right), chief product officer of Yanka Industries Inc., d/b/a MasterClass.
“It’s not just you throw an agent, throw a chatbot in with a student and let them figure it out,” Bapaye said. “Having a very … scientifically and pedagogically backed backbone of your agentic system is of prime importance.”
Bapaye and Lukas Biewald (left), senior vice president of AI initiatives at CoreWeave, spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and John Furrier at the Fully Connected event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how MasterClass is building AI teaching agents, why multi-agent systems need rigorous evaluation and how CoreWeave’s stack supports that work at scale. (* Disclosure below.)
Putting AI teaching agents to work for every learner
MasterClass Executive, the company’s new AI-native business program, uses a multi-agent system to plan each lesson around how a learner engages. It watches for signs such as cognitive overload and fading motivation, then changes its approach, Bapaye explained. Biewald has advised the MasterClass team on the product’s development.
“I really think it’s through that rigorous evaluation and those loops like we talked about last time.” Biewald said. “Let’s try a new model, let’s try a new rubric, let’s see how it does, and let’s just keep doing it again and again and again and make it iteratively better every day.”
Production brings a different challenge. MasterClass runs about 10 agents behind every learner interaction and tracks inputs, outputs, tool calls and communication between agents. CoreWeave recently announced that MasterClass has selected W&B Weave to trace, monitor and improve those teaching agents, Bapaye explained.
“Once things are in production, observability becomes a nightmare because there are thousands of people who are interacting,” he said. “Now, what you need to figure out is, ‘Hey, we did all this good stuff during the eval period, but during production, how are the agents behaving? Are the experiences we are giving really good?’”
MasterClass built its own agent on Weave’s Model Context Protocol interface Each night, that agent reviews the traces and flags issues and likely root causes, Bapaye noted. The first cohort drew 30,000 applications for about 500 spots, and the second is nearing 50,000 applications.
“It’s cost, it’s supply and it’s quality,” he said. “It’s extremely costly to hire personal teachers, they are in very short supply … and the quality of teachers varies. AI solves pretty much all of these three aspects.”
