articles.title: AI-ready data without a rebuild, NetApp says - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
NetApp aims to make legacy data AI-ready without a rebuild
Enterprises sitting on decades of legacy information face a pressing question as artificial intelligence moves from pilots to production: Can that archive become AI-ready data without a costly rebuild of the infrastructure underneath it?
NetApp Inc. is betting it can answer that question with a platform that reaches well beyond its storage roots. The company is framing its intelligent data infrastructure strategy around a simple promise: Make data usable for AI where it already lives, according to Jen Prenner (pictured), senior vice president of product marketing at NetApp.
“For data to be usable for AI, it needs to be accessible, governed, protected, available,” Prenner said. “You need to be able to do that with all that data for your projects without re-architecting the data or moving it.”
Prenner spoke with theCUBE Research’s Christophe Bertrand and co-host Rebecca Knight at NetApp INSIGHT, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed making legacy enterprise data usable for AI, unified storage and built-in data protection. (* Disclosure below.)
Building AI-ready data without new silos
Making legacy data usable for AI requires support for different types of storage. NetApp’s unified approach spans file, block and object storage, Prenner explained. The company also announced plans for a fully managed storage service on Oracle Corp.’s cloud infrastructure, available within the next 12 months.
“Whether you want to store your data on the cloud, at the edge, or on-prem, or some combination of all three, which is what most customers do, we feel like allowing a unified strategy to take hold is how you access all of that data without creating that complexity, without creating more silos,” she said.
Protection must be built into every layer rather than bolted on, according to Prenner. NetApp combines its own data protection tools with an expanded partnership with Commvault Systems Inc. Its Console control plane also supports local deployment for environments that must remain disconnected from the cloud.
“Your fleet manageability, your observability, reporting, analytics, remediation — all of that can be done with Console within one tool,” she said. “So you don’t have to have separate teams, separate tools, which end up costing a lot of money.”
Storage remains the foundation of NetApp’s platform. Protection, control planes and data services build on that foundation to help enterprises put AI-ready data to use, according to Prenner.
“What we want folks to understand is that NetApp is far more than your storage provider,” she said. “We have 30 years of trust with our customers, but we also have a lot more so that customers can take their AI ambitions and turn them into something that’s real.”

articles.title: Icy Dock Releases EXLink MB308A5 PCIe 5.0 x16 NVMe Host Adapter Card
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 6th 2026
Icy Dock Releases EXLink MB308A5 PCIe 5.0 x16 NVMe Host Adapter Card
The ICY DOCK EXLink MB308A5 is a PCIe 5.0 x16 NVMe host adapter card with dual MCIO 8i (SFF-TA-1016) connectivity, designed for next-generation high-speed NVMe cabling. With an integrated PCIe Gen 5 redriver and 100 MHz clock buffering, it helps maintain signal integrity for 32 GT/s links across longer trace and cable routing commonly found in servers, workstations, and validation platforms.
PCIe 5.0 x16 Lane Bifurcation for Multi-Drive NVMe Topologies
With a PCIe 5.0 x16 interface delivering up to 512 Gbps of total bandwidth, the MB308A5 is designed for platforms that support PCIe lane bifurcation (x4 / x4 / x4 / x4). When enabled, the PCIe x16 interface can be allocated into four independent NVMe x4 links, allowing up to four NVMe SSDs to be addressed through MCIO cabling.Redriver for Reliable PCIe Gen 5 Signal Integrity
PCIe Gen 5 (32 GT/s) links are far more sensitive to loss and reflection - especially when signals must travel through extended PCB traces, risers, or external MCIO cables. The MB308A5 integrates a PCIe Gen 5 redriver to equalize and restore high-speed signals, helping preserve stable throughput in demanding configurations such as AI/ML, validation labs, and high-I/O workstation builds.
PCIe Clock Buffer, Sideband Buffering & SMBus Management
To maintain timing accuracy over MCIO-based NVMe cabling, the MB308A5 includes a built-in 100 MHz PCIe clock buffer to support longer routing paths. It also integrates SMBus switching and out-of-band reset management, along with buffered PERST#, WAKE#, and CLKREQ# signaling for stable operation in enterprise system designs and validation environments.
Validated NVMe Compatibility with ICY DOCK Mobile Racks & Cables
In PCIe Gen 5 deployments, integration margin is smaller, and compatibility validation becomes more critical. The MB308A5 has been validated with ICY DOCK MCIO-based NVMe mobile racks, enclosures, and cables to reduce integration risk and shorten system bring-up time for OEMs and system integrators building high-speed removable NVMe storage solutions.
Key Features
- Dual MCIO 8i (SFF-TA-1016) ports, compliant with SFF-9402 Rev 1.1
- PCIe 5.0 x16 interface supporting up to 512 Gbps total bandwidth
- Integrated PCIe Gen 5 redriver for extended trace/cable reach (32 GT/s signaling)
- 100 MHz PCIe clock buffer for stable enterprise timing
- Supports PCIe lane bifurcation (x4/x4/x4/x4) for flexible multi-NVMe topologies (host support required)
- Validated compatibility with ICY DOCK NVMe mobile racks and cables
- Universal PCIe slot support: PCIe 2.0 / 3.0 / 4.0 / 5.0
- Full-height bracket, CE/UKCA/RoHS/REACH compliant
- 2-year limited warranty

articles.title: Garmin's ultra-powerful Enduro 4 adventure watch and Approach S72 golf watch just launched — but I'd get the Garmin Fenix 8 Amazon deals instead
articles.text:
Garmin just launched two new smartwatches, including the Enduro 4 — but you might be tempted by this Fenix 8 discount instead
Two new devices for your wrist
- Garmin has launched the Enduro 4 with 90 days of battery life
- The Approach 72 also lands with dedicated features for golfers
- If you’re after a bargain, the Fenix 8 might be a better option
Garmin has just released two new contenders for our best Garmin watches list: the Enduro 4, an update to its popular line of high-performance, battery-first smartwatches, and a new Approach S72 golf watch that is intended to help people “better understand their whole game,” according to Garmin.
The Enduro 4 uses a 1.4-inch MIP display to provide up to 90 days of battery life, which Garmin says makes it the company’s “longest-lasting GPS smartwatch.” There’s a new ComfortFit fabric band replacing the older nylon hook-and-loop style on the Enduro 3.
Dedicated power modes are on board to extend accuracy or battery life, with grade-adjusted pace-based workout targets and the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro's new Epic and Stamina features to help you better understand your endurance. Otherwise, it's very similar to the old Enduro 3, right down to the weight (57g) and materials (Power Sapphire lens, titanium bezel, polymer shell).
As for the Garmin Approach S72, it looks like an upgrade over the older, excellent Garmin Approach S70. It comes with 'golf biometric data' that allow you to analyze your performance on the green through your heart rate, matching it to key moments during your game.
You can also make phone calls, use voice commands, and get up to 20 hours of battery life (or up to 16 days with GPS switched off).
Enduro 4 vs Fenix 9 Pro
Garmin has priced the Approach S72 at $ $799.99 / £699.99 / €799.99, while the Enduro 4 will set you back $899.99 / £799.99 / €899.99. The cost of the latter is interesting because it’s $200 shy of the Fenix 9 Pro, one of Garmin’s most capable (and most expensive) smartwatches.
If you opt for the Enduro 4, there are a few things you miss out on from the Fenix 9 Pro. That includes a 3,000-nit AMOLED display, the titanium case, a built-in speaker/microphone combination, and double the internal storage.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
However, the Enduro 4 has a few benefits of its own, notably relating to battery life: you’ll get up to 90 days of juice in smartwatch mode or up to 320 hours in activity mode, compared to up to 10 days with the Fenix 9 Pro. The Enduro 4 also boasts solar charging to keep itself topped up.
While the Enduro 4 is a little cheaper than the Fenix 9 Pro, whichever one you go for depends on your needs. The former focuses squarely on long-lived battery performance, while the latter is more of a high-end all-rounder for people who need the best of everything.

articles.title: How to find out if Amazon thinks you have 'flat buttocks' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
It shouldn’t come as a surprise that Amazon collects data about you based on what you buy. If you buy a lot of cat litter, Amazon will probably infer that you have cats, or if you buy a lot of anti-acne skin products, then Amazon might guess you’re prone to breakouts. Even if we know that Amazon customizes our shopping experiences based on our purchase history, it still comes as a surprise to see all of these personal details laid out in a convenient list. Especially when those details get uncomfortably intimate.
One Threads user came across this section of her Amazon settings, where you can see who the shopping giant thinks you are, and alongside more benign assumptions like “Shops from women’s departments” and “Probably owns a Shark robot vacuum,” she found that Amazon assumes she “has flat buttocks.”
“I stumbled upon a page of assumptions that Amazon has made about me based on my purchases and I’m literally speechless,” an Amazon customer, @fangirlinmegan, wrote on Threads. “I mean it ain’t wrong but damn did you have to call me out like that?”
In less than a day, the post garnered over a million views, including many from users who were curious what their own Amazon profiles might reveal. Here’s how you find out.
On desktop, you can find this page by hovering over where Amazon says “Hello, [your name]” in the upper right corner. Then click “Account” under the “Your Account” section. Under the “Ordering and shopping preferences” section, click “Your Shopping preferences.” From here, you can add in information of your own, like your shoe size, interests, and dietary preferences. But we’re not here to tell Amazon that it should stop selling you beef jerky since you’re a vegetarian. We’re here to see if Amazon thinks you have “flat buttocks.” When you scroll to the bottom of the page, you’ll see a blue hyperlinked option that says “Manage your information.” Once you click that, you’ll see what dirt Amazon has on you.
On the mobile app, you can get here by clicking the hamburger icon from the bottom menu bar, then navigating to “Account” > “Shopping preferences” > “About you.”
For me, Amazon has gleaned that I am someone who “practices photography,” “plays collectible card games,” and is “invested in the Apple ecosystem.” This is all true. Amazon has even flattered me by noting that I “read diverse non-fiction,” to which I say — why yes, I am indeed an open-minded intellectual with a thirst for knowledge. Thank you for noticing.
Other colleagues of mine found that Amazon correctly noted their interests in vinyl records and ceramics, as well as a penchant for “natural materials” in home decor and clothing that “prioritizes comfort.” None of us had anything as affronting as “has flat buttocks,” but the Threads user noted that this was likely because she had purchased “butt scrunch leggings.”
Tech companies know too much about us, and it’s jarring to realize just how closely they’re paying attention to how we use their platforms. We live in a world of alarming surveillance, but at least I know that Amazon doesn’t think my butt is flat.

articles.title: Navya Naveli Nanda’s venture to back deeptech, frontier tech ambitions
articles.text:
Navya Naveli Nanda’s venture to back deeptech, frontier tech ambitions
Navya Naveli Nanda’s Naveli Ventures plans to invest in deep-tech, space, AI, clean energy and other emerging sectors as India expands support for technology-led innovation.
Entrepreneur Navya Naveli Nanda formally introduced Naveli Ventures, a venture arm of the Nanda Family Office, with a focus on startups and research-led opportunities across deep-tech, space, clean energy, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing and health.
In a LinkedIn announcement, Nanda noted the platform would invest through direct startup investments, institutional funds, co-investments and academic and intellectual-property partnerships.
“We define ourselves not by sector but by the scale of the problem and the conviction of those solving it,” she wrote. She also said the family office’s relationships across industry, government, academia and the investor community could be used to support its partners.
Nanda is managing partner of Naveli Ventures, as per her LinkedIn profile.
Naveli Ventures LLP was incorporated in March 2023, with Nanda and Agastya Nanda as designated partners. Today’s announcement is principally the formal unveiling of an investment strategy. The family office is associated with the Nanda business group, including Escorts Kubota, the farm and construction-equipment company.
The development arrives as India is putting more public capital behind commercially difficult technologies. The government’s Research, Development and Innovation scheme has a planned corpus of Rs 1 lakh crore over six years, with deep-tech, AI, biotechnology, energy transition and space among its priority areas. Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0, notified in April 2026, adds a Rs 10,000 crore pool aimed partly at deeptech and technology-driven manufacturing.
Private capital is moving in the same direction, although unevenly. Capital-A closed the first close of a Rs 160 crore second fund in April, targeting manufacturing and deep-tech startups, while Bluehill.VC closed a Rs 400 crore frontier-tech fund in August.
Last month, IIT Madras, IIT Madras Research Park, and Unicorn India Ventures announced a Rs 450 crore first close for the IITM Unicorn Frontier Fund I, part of a planned Rs 1,000 crore deeptech fund.
Naveli’s promise of patient capital is timely but not unique.
“We are not chasing quick returns but looking to help build enduring companies alongside exceptional people for India’s future,” Nanda wrote. The harder question will be whether that long-term approach can help technologies move from research and prototypes to durable, scalable businesses.

articles.title: ChatGPT a trouvé un nouvel endroit où mettre des publicités
articles.text:
Depuis août dernier, il y a des publicités dans ChatGPT, notamment lorsqu’on prépare un voyage, qu’on compare des produits ou qu’on veut trouver un service. Mais dans un communiqué publié ce 5 octobre 2026, OpenAI a présenté un nouveau format : des publicités dans la génération d’images, pendant que l’utilisateur attend. Premiers tests aux États-Unis dans le courant du mois.
Des publicités dans la génération d’images de ChatGPT
La génération d’images avec ChatGPT est devenue chose commune : on écrit un prompt et on attend que le chatbot génère l’image souhaitée, avant de la télécharger ou de la partager. Mais durant la génération, il ne se passe rien, si ce n’est une animation pour faire patienter l’utilisateur. C’est précisément ce moment qu’OpenAI veut utiliser pour afficher des annonces sponsorisées. Un endroit parfait, puisque pendant ce temps, l’utilisateur ne fait rien, contrairement à lorsqu’il veut lire une réponse de ChatGPT.
L’entreprise se veut rassurante : « Les publicités seront clairement identifiées et resteront distinctes de l’image en cours de création. » Dans la capture d’écran montrée par OpenAI, on peut voir une annonce qui se place entre l’animation de la génération d’image et le champ textuel pour entrer la requête. Elle précise aussi que ces publicités n’influenceront pas les images générées par ChatGPT. Et avec 1,2 milliard d’utilisateurs par semaine, OpenAI est sûre d’avoir une audience à qui montrer ces annonces. Comme pour les publicités qui existent déjà, on imagine que les abonnés aux formules Pro et Entreprise ne les verront pas. Les premiers tests publics vont débuter aux États-Unis ce mois-ci ; pour le moment, OpenAI n’a pas indiqué quelle sera la suite de son calendrier.
Dans les pays de l’Union européenne, OpenAI va devoir montrer patte blanche
En août dernier, ChatGPT a été désigné comme un « très grand moteur de recherche en ligne » par la Commission européenne, au titre du Digital Services Act, ou DSA. Ce qui signifie que le chatbot a atteint au moins 45 millions d’utilisateurs mensuels dans l’Union européenne. Ainsi, OpenAI dispose de quatre mois pour se conformer aux obligations supplémentaires prévues par le DSA : la date limite est donc fixée à fin décembre 2026.
Un nouveau qui va essentiellement ajouter des obligations de transparence, de contrôle et d’évaluation des risques pour ChatGPT. OpenAI va devoir publier un registre public détaillé de toutes les publicités diffusées dans les pays de l’Union. Ces registres de publicités sont utiles pour les ONG, lanceurs d’alerte et associations de consommateurs afin d’observer des campagnes d’arnaques, des opérations de propagande de pays étrangers ou encore de publicités politiques non déclarées. De quoi constater les mécanismes à l’œuvre, mesurer l’exposition des utilisateurs et prévenir les autorités.

articles.title: Anthropic veut entraîner Claude avec votre voix : voici le nouveau réglage à connaître
articles.text:
Anthropic commence à demander l’autorisation d’utiliser les conversations vocales de Claude pour entraîner ses modèles. Le partage reste facultatif et bénéficie de son propre réglage. Une distinction importante, que l’on retrouve aussi chez ChatGPT et Gemini : refuser de donner sa voix ne signifie pas forcément que sa transcription sera elle aussi écartée.
Parler à Claude pourrait désormais contribuer à entraîner les futures versions de l’IA, mais seulement si vous l’acceptez. Anthropic commence à afficher une nouvelle demande d’autorisation concernant les enregistrements et les données issus des conversations vocales. Selon BleepingComputer, l’entreprise veut s’en servir pour améliorer la compréhension de la parole et les réponses de ses modèles.
Claude sépare les conversations vocales des échanges écrits
Lors de l’apparition du nouvel écran, l’utilisateur peut accepter le partage ou choisir Pas maintenant. Dans l’interface observée ce week-end par BleepingComputer, l’option est désactivée par défaut.
Anthropic aurait surtout prévu un réglage distinct de celui qui concerne les conversations écrites et les sessions Claude Code. Il deviendrait donc possible d’autoriser l’utilisation de ses échanges textuels pour améliorer les modèles tout en refusant celle de ses enregistrements vocaux, ou inversement.
Le bouton se trouve dans les paramètres de confidentialité. Anthropic indique également qu’un utilisateur peut revenir sur sa décision et supprimer les données vocales concernées.
Les captures publiées par nos confrères montrent ce réglage dans une interface en anglais, sans préciser le périmètre géographique du déploiement. Au moment d'écrire ces lignes, cette option n'était pas disponible sur les comptes que nous avons testés depuis la France, sur mobile et sur le Web.
ChatGPT et Gemini font eux aussi la différence entre voix et transcription
Cette séparation mérite d’être regardée de près. Lorsqu’on parle à un assistant, deux types de données peuvent en effet coexister : l’enregistrement de notre voix et le texte qui en est extrait. Refuser l’un n’entraîne pas nécessairement le refus de l’autre.
Même logique du côté de Gemini. Google propose une option distincte pour partager les enregistrements audio, les vidéos et les partages d’écran issus de Gemini Live. Elle est désactivée par défaut et, lorsqu’elle est activée, certains extraits peuvent notamment être examinés par des personnes chargées d’améliorer les services. Le texte issu de ces conversations dépend, lui, du réglage Conserver l’activité, activé par défaut pour les utilisateurs adultes. Vous savez maintenant quelles options désactiver… ou pas.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace

articles.title: Die Milchstraße im Vorruhestand: Warum wir laut einer Supercomputer-Simulation kosmisch extrem sicher leben
articles.text:
Milchstraße im Ruhestand: Warum unser Sonnensystem statistisch gesehen sicher ist
Unser Sonnensystem befindet sich in einer Region des Universums, in der biologisches Leben selten von zerstörerischer Strahlung bedroht wird. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt ein Team von Astrophysiker:innen, wie in einer im britischen Wissenschaftsmagazin Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist.
Die untersuchten Daten zeigen, dass die Milchstraße ihre unruhigste Phase der Sternentstehung hinter sich gelassen hat. Galaxien dieser Größenordnung und in diesem Entwicklungsstadium bieten die stabilsten Voraussetzungen, um Planeten vor energiereicher Strahlung zu bewahren.
EAGLE-Projekt: Supercomputer simuliert galaktische Evolution
Für die Analyse griffen die Wissenschaftler:innen auf das Eagle-Projekt zurück, das an der University of Durham im nordenglischen Durham beheimatet ist. Die Simulation kalkuliert die Ausdehnung des Raums, die Wirkung der Gravitation sowie das Verhalten von Gas, Sternen und Schwarzen Löchern.
Auf diese Weise entsteht ein mathematisches Modell, das die galaktische Evolution über Hunderte Millionen Lichtjahre nachzeichnet. Die Untersuchung beschränkt sich dabei nicht auf den bekannten Sicherheitsabstand eines Planeten zu seinem Heimatstern, der flüssiges Wasser ermöglicht. Die Analyse zielt auf das übergeordnete System: die galaktische habitable Zone.
Milchstraße: Die Parameter der sicheren Zone
Ein Sternensystem in dieser Zone darf dem dichten galaktischen Zentrum nicht zu nahe kommen, aber auch nicht zu weit außen am Rand kreisen. Am Rand fehlen die schweren Elemente, die in der Astronomie als Metalle bezeichnet werden und erst im Inneren früherer Sterne entstehen. Ohne diese Grundstoffe können sich keine festen Gesteinskrusten oder Ozeane bilden.
Ein Übermaß an diesen Elementen birgt jedoch andere Gefahren für entstehendes Leben. Astronomische Beobachtungen zeigen, dass in chemisch zu stark angereicherten Umgebungen bevorzugt riesige Gasplaneten entstehen. Diese Himmelskörper wandern im Laufe der Zeit nach innen, wirken wie ein Schneepflug auf benachbarte Gesteinswelten und stürzen sie ins Zentralgestirn.
Kosmische Katastrophen: Von Supernovae bis zu Gammablitzen
Die Modellierung sucht folglich nach Regionen, die eine ausgeglichene chemische Balance aufweisen. Zusätzlich berechnete das System fünf astrophysikalische Gefahrenquellen.
Dabei unterscheidet das Modell zwischen Ereignissen, die vorhandenes Leben auslöschen, aber eine spätere Erholung zulassen, und dauerhafter Zerstörung. Bei letzterer reißt die Strahlung dem Planeten die Atmosphäre weg oder verdampft die Meere vollständig.
Im frühen Universum bildeten Kernkollaps-Supernovae die größte Gefahr, also das explosive Ende sehr massereicher Sterne. Hinzu kommen Typ-Ia-Supernovae detonierender Weißer Zwerge sowie gebündelte Gammablitze, die noch über Hunderte Lichtjahre hinweg die Ozonschichten von Planeten zersetzen können.
Schwarze Löcher und Quasare zerstören Atmosphären
Eine weitere Bedrohung geht von aktiven Galaxienkernen aus, in denen supermassive Schwarze Löcher große Mengen an Materie anziehen. Diese Quasare strahlen intensive Röntgen- und UV-Wellen ab. Über Jahrmillionen hinweg heizt diese Energie planetare Atmosphären so stark auf, dass die Gase ins All entweichen und unbewohnbare Gesteinsbrocken zurückbleiben.
In den vergangenen fünf Milliarden Jahren hat sich laut der Simulation jedoch ein mechanischer Prozess an die Spitze geschoben. Wenn sich Sterne in dichteren Gebieten zu nahe kommen, wirkt ihre Anziehungskraft wie ein Hebel auf umliegende Planetensysteme. Solche gravitativen Störungen verzerren stabile Umlaufbahnen oder katapultieren erdähnliche Welten als heimatlose Körper in den interstellaren Raum.
Limitierungen: Modelle liefern keinen Beweis für Aliens
Trotz der hohen Rechenleistung verweisen die Forscher:innen auf die Grenzen ihrer Simulation. Die räumliche Auflösung reicht nicht aus, um kleinere galaktische Strukturen wie lokale Sternhaufen detailliert zu erfassen.
Zudem basieren alle Annahmen über lebensfreundliche Bedingungen auf den Parametern der Erde. Einen Beweis dafür, dass sich unter diesen Voraussetzungen tatsächlich biologische Organismen bilden, liefert das System naturgemäß nicht. Außerdem werden natürlich bislang unbekannte Mechanismen der Lebensentstehung nicht berücksichtigt.
Die Ergebnisse verdeutlichen dennoch die statistische Begünstigung unseres Standorts. Während junge Galaxien mit hoher Sternentstehungsrate lebensfeindliche Umgebungen darstellen, bietet der Rand der Milchstraße verlässliche Verhältnisse.
Heute erfährt im Schnitt nur noch einer von tausend Sternen in der Milchstraße ein folgenschweres Zerstörungsereignis. Unser Sonnensystem profitiert von einer Galaxie, die sich in einer stabilen Ruhephase befindet.

articles.title: Sons effrayants, phares qui clignotent, photobooth : Tesla lance son Halloween Mode — Frandroid
articles.text:
Tesla a annoncé son « Halloween Mode » ce mardi 6 octobre, dans un message publié sur X. Pour la marque, la voiture devient une « haunted house on wheels », une maison hantée sur roues, et le déploiement a déjà commencé. Tout arrive par une mise à jour logicielle. Tesla avait préparé le terrain le 1er octobre avec une courte vidéo où une voiture se cachait sous un drap de fantôme.
Un fantôme, des sons qui font peur et un photobooth
- L’avatar de la voiture, dans l’application Tesla, enfile un costume de fantôme.
- Le mode « Trick or Treat » joue des sons effrayants et fait clignoter les phares quand des visiteurs approchent (les enfants venus réclamer des bonbons, en théorie).
- Un nouveau spectacle lumineux à thème Halloween fait son apparition.
- De nouveaux habillages visuels (les wraps) aux couleurs d’Halloween s’ajoutent au catalogue.
- Un son de verrouillage spécial Halloween remplace le bip habituel.
- Un photobooth effrayant permet de prendre des photos depuis la voiture.
- Le propriétaire peut parler à distance depuis l’application. La voiture répète alors son message avec sa propre voix.
Tesla avait déjà fait le coup à Noël. Sa mise à jour des fêtes, fin 2025, avait ajouté le premier Photobooth et enrichi le Santa Mode, qui déguise la voiture en traîneau. Cet été, sa grosse mise à jour estivale avait apporté Grok, un karaoké et un contrôle parental.
Modèles, pays, version : Tesla ne dit rien
Le post X de Tesla ne précise ni les modèles compatibles, ni les pays concernés, ni la version logicielle nécessaire. Il s’agit de la version 2026.38.3, datée du 6 octobre.
Elle devrait être disponible sur les Model 3 et Model Y. Pour les Model S, Model X et le Cybertruck, Tesla n’a rien confirmé.
Cette version apporte aussi un réglage automatique des feux de croisement sur certains véhicules. Tesla envoie ses mises à jour par vagues. Vérifiez donc dans le menu Logiciel de la voiture si la 2026.38.3 vous est proposée. Sachez qu’Halloween tombe le samedi 31 octobre…

articles.title: Alerta de inicio de sesión sospechosa: cómo saber si es real o una estafa
articles.text:
Las alertas de inicio de sesión sospechoso en Facebook, Google o WhatsApp deben verificarse desde los canales oficiales antes de tomar cualquier decisión.
Plataformas, servicios streaming, aplicaciones de mensajería y entidades bancarias comparan cada acceso con la actividad frecuente de cada usuario. Si detectan una diferencia, pueden solicitar una comprobación adicional o enviar un aviso. La clave está en distinguir una notificación legítima de una campaña de phishing diseñada para robar contraseñas.
Por qué hay una alerta de inicio de sesión sospechoso
Cada vez que una persona ingresa en una cuenta, el servicio analiza señales como el dispositivo utilizado, la ubicación aproximada, la dirección de red, el navegador y el horario.
Si alguno de esos datos no coincide con los accesos habituales, el sistema puede marcar el intento como inusual. La alerta no confirma por sí sola que la cuenta haya sido vulnerada.
Hay explicaciones cotidianas para esos avisos. Puede ocurrir al estrenar un teléfono, iniciar sesión desde una computadora ajena, viajar a otra ciudad o conectarse mediante una red distinta.
Además, el uso de una red privada virtual, conocida como VPN, puede modificar la ubicación detectada. Incluso una aplicación de extraños autorizada puede provocar una advertencia al solicitar acceso a una cuenta.
Qué información permiten saber si el aviso requiere atención
El primer punto es revisar si se reconoce el dispositivo, la ciudad, el país y el horario que figuran en la notificación. Si el usuario no viajó, no usó un dispositivo nuevo ni cambió de red, el aviso merece una revisión inmediata.
La situación adquiere otra dimensión cuando aparecen otros indicios. Un cambio de contraseña sin autorización, correos enviados que el usuario no redactó, mensajes desconocidos o compras no reconocidas pueden revelar que una tercera persona obtuvo acceso.
Asimismo, los intentos fallidos repetidos requieren atención, porque pueden estar vinculados con pruebas masivas de contraseñas filtradas o ataques de fuerza bruta.
Cómo verificar si el mensaje es auténtico
Los atacantes aprovechan la urgencia que provocan este tipo de alertas. Pueden enviar correos, mensajes de texto o comunicaciones por WhatsApp con frases como “Proteger mi cuenta”, “Verificar identidad” o “Revisar la actividad reciente”. El objetivo es que la persona pulse un enlace sin comprobar quién lo envió.
Una alerta verdadera debe verificarse desde la aplicación o el sitio oficial, no desde el enlace recibido. Para hacerlo, conviene abrir Facebook, Google, WhatsApp u otro servicio de manera directa y consultar el apartado de seguridad, dispositivos conectados o actividad reciente.
Qué hacer si un extraño intentó entrar en la cuenta
Si la actividad es desconocida, el primer paso es cambiar la contraseña de inmediato. La nueva clave debe ser larga, exclusiva para esa cuenta y distinta de la anterior. Agregar un número o un símbolo al final de la contraseña anterior no ofrece una protección suficiente, porque esos cambios previsibles pueden ser probados por atacantes.
Otro punto necesario es activar la autenticación de dos factores, que exige una segunda comprobación además de la contraseña. Puede consistir en un código generado por una aplicación, una llave física de seguridad o una notificación en un dispositivo de confianza.
Con qué complementar el cambio de contraseña
El cambio de clave debe acompañarse de una revisión de las sesiones activas. La mayoría de los servicios permite consultar los dispositivos, navegadores y ubicaciones desde los que permanece abierta la cuenta.
Si aparece un dispositivo desconocido, corresponde cerrar esa sesión a distancia y, cuando exista la opción, finalizar los accesos en todos los dispositivos.
Es clave revisar las aplicaciones y servicios vinculados. Algunas herramientas de terceros conservan permisos para acceder a determinada información sin pedir la contraseña cada vez.
Eliminar las aplicaciones que no se reconocen o que no se utilizan reduce posibles vías de acceso. Si hubo movimientos financieros, compras o cambios en datos personales, el usuario debe informar el hecho al proveedor correspondiente desde sus canales oficiales.

articles.title: Ya en Action (y sólo hoy a 17,95 euros) el accesorio de cocina que espuma leche caliente o fría y hasta prepara chocolates a la taza
articles.text:
Como cada semana, el pasado miércoles Action renovó su catálogo de ofertas con decenas de productos a precios rebajados. Y aunque mañana vendrá con más novedades, aún estamos a tiempo de conseguir por 17,95 euros este espumador de leche que, además, sirve para preparar más bebidas calientes.
morpilot Espumador
Si no llegamos a tiempo (la promoción acaba hoy mismo, al final del día) o no tenemos ninguna tienda de Action a mano a la que acercarnos, siempre podemos aprovechar la Fiesta de Ofertas Prime de Amazon para comprar esta alternativa, también rebajada respecto a su PVP aunque algo más cara: 24,64 euros hasta mañana si somos miembros Prime o aprovechamos la suscripción gratuita de 30 días que ofrece Amazon.
Espumador de leche George Wilkinson Chocoluxe
Con cuatro modos de uso para cafés y más
Si echamos un vistazo rápido a tiendas como la propia Amazon en busca de espumadores de leche con funciones extra, como este de Action, vemos que la mayoría (por no decir todos) parten de los 20 euros incluso estando rebajados. Razón de más para valorar la compra de este Chocoluxe, que tiene una genial relación calidad precio.
Con una capacidad de 300 mililitros y una potencia máxima de 500 W, este espumador cuenta con cuatro modos de uso: espuma densa, espuma ligera, espuma fría y, ojo, leche o chocolate caliente. Siendo esa última perfecta para preparar chocolates a la taza ensuciando menos que con un cazo.
En esencia, se trata de un recipiente con diferentes marcas máximas para líquidos, una varilla en el fondo (que gira a diferentes velocidades) y una resistencia (para calentar a diferentes temperaturas). Así, dependiendo del modo elegido, la resistencia calienta más o menos (o nada, en el caso de espuma fría) y la varilla gira más rápida o más despacio.
De esta combinación de temperaturas y velocidades de giro, dependiendo de si echamos leche sola o leche con cacao en polvo, podemos preparar: espuma densa o ligera para el café, espuma fría para iced coffees, leche caliente (sin espumar, similar a calentarla en el microondas) y chocolate caliente sin grumos y buena textura (gracias al giro de la varilla).

articles.title: Norway wants to temporarily ban smart glasses in parks, beaches, and schools
articles.text:
The Worst Spectacle: Smart glasses are becoming an increasingly popular wearable for use in public, and privacy is paying the price. Authorities are looking for new regulatory frameworks to curb abuse, and Norway may already be ahead of the pack.
Norwegian authorities are preparing a temporary ban on AI-enhanced smart glasses, giving experts time to draft a new law that restricts potential abuse of the latest wearables. The government announced the plan on Monday, saying smart glasses will become an unwelcome guest in certain public places, at least for the time being.
According to Torgeir Eikstad Micaelsen, Norway's Minister of Digitalisation and Public Governance, people are increasingly concerned that smart glasses can be abused to invade privacy. Norwegians, and everyone else for that matter, can now easily become unwilling "guests" in photos and video clips recorded through a new-generation pair.
A temporary ban will give the government "time to conduct a thorough assessment and hold an informed debate that can lay the foundation for permanent regulation," Micaelsen said earlier this week.
Oslo, the capital and Norway's largest city by population, is now enforcing a total ban on smart glasses in schools. Meanwhile, oil and gas giant Equinor has banned the devices from both its offices and offshore facilities.
The ban could be enforced in parks, beaches, schools, and other public places where people don't necessarily expect to be recorded by a high-tech wearable. Places where there is no risk of a privacy violation would not be covered.
Micaelsen said the temporary measure is now a high-priority proposal for the government. He added that Norway must not become a society where people avoid public places for fear of being recorded or monitored without their consent, one that "can be experienced as unsafe and cause us to withdraw."
In fact, parts of Norwegian society have already reacted to the growing popularity of recording-ready smart glasses. Oslo, the capital and Norway's largest city by population, is now enforcing a total ban on smart glasses in schools. Meanwhile, oil and gas giant Equinor has banned the devices from both its offices and offshore facilities.
Some big tech players and AI companies are betting on smart glasses, hoping to position them as a bridge between customers and voice-powered chatbots. Needless to say, these companies also believe smart glasses could replace smartphones as the standard way to interact with AI on the go.
While companies like Meta are bullish on the technology's prospects, many are doing everything they can to avoid it. Norway is working on a broader regulatory effort, but smart glasses have already been shut out of public spaces such as New York's courts, and elsewhere in the world.

articles.title: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT outputs by default—but only in the EU
articles.text:
OpenAI will begin automatically watermarking text generated with ChatGPT in the European Union, the company has announced. It will also offer the watermarking feature in other regions, but it will be off by default outside of the EU.
The move in Europe is driven by a need to comply with the EU AI Act, which took effect in August. It requires marking content produced by AI models in a way that another tool can detect. Unfortunately, there is still no completely effective and reliable way to do that. A few standards already exist, like SynthID and the C2PA project, but they are relatively easy to circumvent for anyone with basic know-how.
The same is likely true for OpenAI’s watermark. Its method is proprietary; the company calls it textGrain, and has published a technical paper explaining how it works. But in general, it works like other LLM watermarking tools we’ve seen in the past: It puts patterns in the word choices that are not clear to a human reader, and that don’t meaningfully change the general quality of the output, but that someone with a key can use a specialized detector to find. OpenAI says it will be giving access to the detector to a limited number of researchers and organizations, and providing a request-for-approval process for others to be added over time.

articles.title: Madlad applies DLSS 5 to the original Duke Nukem and Pong — tens of games tested with outcomes ranging from trippy to genuinely interesting
articles.text:
Madlad applies DLSS 5 to the original Duke Nukem and Pong — tens of games tested with outcomes ranging from trippy to genuinely interesting
"It wasn't supposed to do that" was never a great deterrent for geeks.
Nvidia's highly advanced DLSS 5 photographic realism injector has been discussed to death and back. The internet has largely made peace with what the technology is and what it isn't, but that's not stopping anyone from adding DLSS 5 in places where it definitely wasn't meant to go: old DOS games like the original 1991 Duke Nukem, and even the 1972 Pong.
Valery Kryzhanovsky is the man who embarked on a mission to use the tech with old games, and the results are visible on his YouTube channel. His testing comprises most every type of game ranging from 2D platformers and RPGs, up to contemporary titles like The Witcher 3 and Marvel's Spider-.Man. If you want to try your hand at the same activity, he provides a blog post with instructions and some downloadables.
As you can see in the video below, Duke Nukem's gameplay actually looks interesting in parts, despite the amusing intro sections with race-changed characters. In the actual platforming, rectangular visual elements get embossed, adding a sense of depth, and the filter does a decent job of detecting objects like the player, enemies, and bullets, and not messing too much with inner portions of said sprites. Predictably, if the filter is applied too strongly, the results quickly start looking like an acid trip.
To inject the filter into 2D titles, Kryzhanovsky ran them in DOSBox, then used the popular ReShade filter to add DLSS 5 on top. The UI for configuring the parameters comes by way of RenoDX.
In a second blog post detailing what's happening and how, Kryzhanovsky explains that since DLSS 5 was never meant to be used on 2D static images or dumped into unsuspecting 3D titles — thus without motion vectors, object selection, and associated sundries that would inform it — it's important to choose at which rendering level it's injected: the render stage, after upscaling, or final output.
The injection point is as important as choosing the strength of the filter, which of the three color presets to use, or the number of passes. The techie notes that, for example, injecting DLSS 5 at the render stage in a 3D game changes actual face geometry, as he came to find when trying out RBDOOM-3-BFG.
Kryzhanovsky concludes that force-injected DLSS 5 works best with still images, a fact illustrated by the surprisingly consistent results he got with Heroes of Might and Magic. He believes the technology is promising but quite undercooked, and the lack of a temporal element (it only analyzes the one current frame) is currently one of its key drawbacks.

articles.title: SFR, RED et Prixtel augmentent leurs forfaits : tous les abonnés ne pourront pas refuser
articles.text:
Après Orange, SFR relance à son tour les hausses de tarifs pour ses abonnés actuels. Des clients de SFR, de sa marque low cost RED by SFR et de Prixtel, filiale de l’opérateur, reçoivent par mail ou par SMS l’annonce d’une hausse de leur forfait mobile ou de leur box, de 0,99 euro à près de 5 euros par mois selon les offres. Tous n’ont pas la possibilité de la refuser.
Des hausses de moins de 1 euro à près de 5 euros
Chez SFR, l’augmentation touche aussi bien les forfaits mobiles que les box, relève Que Choisir, qui cite des hausses de 1,49 euro, 2,49 euros, et jusqu’à 4,99 euros pour un abonnement Internet. Selon nos confrères d’Univers Freebox, une offre fibre 1 Gb/s facturée 17,47 euros passe ainsi à 22,46 euros par mois.
Chez RED by SFR, certains clients se voient proposer 20 Go de plus pour 1,99 euro de plus par mois. D’autres rapportent une hausse de 3,29 euros sur leur forfait mobile, sans aucune contrepartie. Le courrier de RED justifie la mesure par la volonté de continuer à offrir « une expérience de qualité au quotidien, toujours plus fluide et toujours plus rapide ». Prixtel semble lui aussi concerné et certains clients se verront facturer 0,99 euro de plus par mois pour 20 Go supplémentaires.
Pourquoi maintenant ?
SFR n’a pas expliqué ces hausses. Selon Que Choisir, deux pistes se dessinent : l’effet de la hausse des prix de l’énergie sur les coûts d’exploitation, et le rachat à venir de SFR par Bouygues Telecom, Free et Orange. Des tarifs plus élevés permettraient à SFR de se présenter sous un meilleur jour avant la vente. Orange a de son côté déjà relancé cette pratique, avec une hausse de 2 euros par mois de certains forfaits mobiles.
Peut-on refuser la hausse ?
Cela dépend des cas. Quand la hausse s’accompagne de gigas supplémentaires, l’opérateur propose parfois de la refuser depuis l’espace client, mais ce n’est pas systématique. Dans les cas rapportés par Que Choisir, les abonnés de SFR n’avaient que deux options : accepter le nouveau prix ou résilier.
La résiliation est protégée par l’article L. 224-33 du Code de la consommation. Un opérateur peut modifier un contrat unilatéralement à condition de prévenir l’abonné au moins un mois avant, et de lui laisser la possibilité de résilier sans frais ni pénalité dans les quatre mois suivant la notification. Chez RED by SFR, le mail détaille les démarches de résiliation : depuis l’espace client, par courrier, ou lors d’une portabilité vers un autre opérateur. Relisez donc attentivement le message reçu pour connaître vos options.
Comme toujours, comparez les offres du moment chez SFR et chez d’autres opérateurs, ou contactez le service client pour tenter de renégocier votre forfait mobile ou votre box.

articles.title: IBM and Red Hat patch 400-plus unknown Java flaws, open Clearinghouse for fix requests - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
IBM and Red Hat patch 400-plus unknown Java flaws, open Clearinghouse for fix requests
IBM Corp. and its Red Hat unit said today that their Lightwell open-source security program has found and fixed more than 400 previously unknown vulnerabilities in widely used Java libraries.
The companies also made Lightwell Clearinghouse generally available. Enterprise customers can use it to submit specific open-source dependencies to IBM and Red Hat for priority review and remediation.
The milestone is pitched at a risk the two companies say is growing as autonomous artificial intelligence agents get better at chaining several lower-risk software weaknesses into one serious attack. Because many businesses still run library versions that are years old, any patch has to be built for the exact release sitting in production.
For the more than 400 flaws, Lightwell engineers backported patches into the widely deployed versions of each library. Any fix that also applies upstream goes back to the open-source project under responsible disclosure protocols while Clearinghouse participants keep their embargo protections. Neither company has named the affected libraries.
Behind the fixes, engineers from both companies work alongside AI-assisted development workflows, and the builds run on Red Hat’s secure software supply chain infrastructure. Customers pull the patched packages from secured repositories that connect to their existing information technology processes, so nobody has to swap out security scanners or development pipelines to use them.
Those patched packages come through Lightwell Network, the general catalog IT teams draw on to fold verified patches into the workflows they already have. Fixes that come back from a Clearinghouse request are built to apply to older software versions a customer still runs.
Gunnar Hellekson, vice president and general manager of Lightwell at Red Hat, said AI agents “shifted the threat landscape overnight” by going after old dependencies at machine speed. Age and stability do not protect a codebase, he argued. Finding the bugs is “only half the battle,” Hellekson said, and the real work is backporting fixes into applications already in production so customers “do not have to pick between security and uptime.”
Lightwell dates backk to May, when IBM and Red Hat committed $5 billion and more than 20,000 engineers to securing open-source software. Lightwell Network went generally available in July with a launch catalog of more than 6,500 remediated dependencies, and a tier called Clearinghouse Premier opened to financial services companies on a limited basis at the same time. IBM and Red Hat extended Lightwell to universities, nongovernmental organizations and think tanks at no cost in August.

articles.title: “Vous n’êtes jamais véritablement anonymes” : elle planifiait une fusillade dans son “journal intime”, l'IA Claude la dénonce à la police
articles.text:
“Vous n’êtes jamais véritablement anonymes” : elle planifiait une fusillade dans son “journal intime”, l'IA Claude la dénonce à la police
Convaincue de confier ses pulsions à un simple journal intime en parlant avec l’IA Claude, une Étasunienne a été arrêtée après le signalement de ses menaces armées à l’encontre des forces de l’ordre locales.
À force d’interagir tous les jours et pour tout avec les IA, beaucoup finissent par leur confier leurs pires pensées, comme à un confident. Mais derrière l’écran, les garde-fous des modèles veillent au grain. Une internaute d'outre-Atlantique vient de l’apprendre à ses dépens lors de son arrestation alors qu’elle envisageait d’attaquer le bureau du shérif, rappelant que la confidentialité des agents conversationnels s’arrête là où commence le risque d’un passage à l’acte.
Les modérateurs d’Anthropic agissent au quart de tour pour sauver des vies
Selon le rapport d’arrestation révélé par la chaîne locale WINK News, Carli Michelle Heller, 30 ans, a écrit à l'IA Claude le 26 septembre qu’elle comptait ouvrir le feu sur les locaux des forces de l’ordre, avant d’affirmer le lendemain qu’elle s’était procuré une nouvelle arme à feu. Face à cette situation, les systèmes d’Anthropic ont transmis les messages à des modérateurs humains.
Conformément à la politique d’urgence du groupe, autorisant la levée de confidentialité en cas de risque létal, l’entreprise a immédiatement alerté la police. La suspecte a ensuite été interpellée sans incident chez elle à Bonita Springs (Floride) dans la foulée du signalement, sous le coup d’une inculpation criminelle pour menace terroriste électronique.
Interrogée après son arrestation, la suspecte a affirmé qu’elle utilisait l'intelligence artificielle d'Antrhopic comme un simple “journal intime”. De son côté, le shérif Carmine Marceno a rappelé les règles du jeu auprès de WINK News : “L’intelligence artificielle est un outil puissant, et comme toute technologie, elle peut être détournée. Quand quelqu’un utilise l’IA pour proférer ou faciliter une menace, nous devons la prendre au sérieux. Vous n’êtes jamais véritablement anonymes”.
Pour la chercheuse Chrissann Ruehle de la Florida Gulf Coast University, l’interface trompe la vigilance : “Les gens ont l’impression que la machine ne va pas les juger, mais l’IA n’est pas votre meilleure amie”. Ian Marlow, dirigeant de FITECH, rappelle aussi que le ton conversationnel fait vite oublier l’archivage des données, occultant le fait que chaque mot reste stocké sur les serveurs et peut être examiné à tout moment par l’éditeur.
Il s’agit déjà du troisième signalement de ce type transmis à la police par Anthropic depuis août. Des faits divers qui illustrent la responsabilité accrue pesant sur les développeurs d’IA, engagés dans un intense lobbying pour prôner la prudence, tout en déployant leurs modèles à vitesse grand V pour ne pas se laisser distancer par la concurrence.

articles.text:
McDonald’s é alvo de processo por usar IA para definir preços
Ação coletiva acusa a rede de violar leis de concorrência ao coordenar preços entre lojas próprias e franqueadas.
O McDonald’s virou alvo de uma ação coletiva nos Estados Unidos após a revelação de que a empresa coordena preços do cardápio por um sistema de IA. Protocolado na sexta-feira (02/10) por um consumidor na cidade de Chicago, o processo acusa a companhia de violar as leis antitruste do país.
A ação sustenta que a rede conspirou com franqueados independentes para alinhar e fixar preços usando os modelos de IA alimentados por dados comerciais sigilosos, segundo a Reuters. Afirma, ainda, que os valores deveriam ser definidos independentemente por cada empresa, mas que o sistema adotado pelo McDonald’s teria reduzido essa concorrência entre lojas.
A ação surge poucos dias após a agência revelar que uma ferramenta de precificação por IA usada pelo McDonald’s nos EUA usa histórico de compras locais para calcular a chamada “sensibilidade ao preço”. Ou seja, a empresa estima, pela tecnologia, quanto os consumidores de cada região estariam dispostos a pagar pelos lanches.
A investigação encontrou diferenças até mesmo entre lojas muito próximas, chegando a 21% em duas unidades a cerca de 3,2 km de distância em uma mesma cidade.
Ainda que a empresa afirme que os franqueados tenham autonomia para definir os preços, operadores relataram pressão para seguir as recomendações do sistema. A matriz envia relatórios de orientação e acompanha desvios em relação aos valores sugeridos, comportamento que pode impactar na renovação de licenças de franquia, segundo a Reuters.
Na avaliação dos autores da ação, o problema está nesse alinhamento dos valores cobrados. Os consumidores argumentam que o sistema centralizados de precificação elimina parte da concorrência, mesmo entre franquias, que deveriam tomar suas decisões comerciais de forma independente.
Em declaração, Lark Turner, advogado do autor da ação, acusou o McDonald’s de usar sua escala e os dados obtidos por meio da rede de franquias para aumentar os preços. Segundo ele, o restaurante “está alavancando seus tesouros de dados e seu sistema de franquias para extorquir os consumidores”.
O processo se soma a outras disputas nos Estados Unidos envolvendo o uso de algoritmos de precificação em mercados nos quais empresas independentes podem acabar adotando valores semelhantes. Casos relacionados a ferramentas digitais usadas nos setores hoteleiro e imobiliário também passaram a levantar questionamentos antitruste.
Em pronunciamento publicado ontem (05/10), o McDonald’s rejeitou as acusações e classificou o processo como infundado. “A inteligência artificial não define o preço de um Big Mac ou de qualquer outro item do cardápio”, declarou em nota.
A empresa afirmou que as alegações são “especulativas e desinformadas” e reiterou que a definição final dos preços cabe aos operadores das franquias. O McDonald’s também defendeu o uso de softwares de análise e recomendação de preços, dizendo que ferramentas desse tipo são utilizadas de forma legítima em diferentes setores da economia.

articles.title: Plan Tasks, Resources, and Deadlines in One Place With Microsoft Project 2024 for $49.97
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 6th 2026
Plan Tasks, Resources, and Deadlines in One Place With Microsoft Project 2024 for $49.97
Microsoft Project Professional 2024 is built for managing projects from the initial plan through completion, with tools for organizing tasks, coordinating resources, monitoring progress, and creating reports. For a limited time, you can get the desktop application for $49.97 on one Windows PC, with the license lasting a lifetime.
Rather than building every project schedule from scratch, you can start with pre-built templates and customize them to fit your needs. Define tasks and dependencies, and Project can calculate start and finish dates based on how those tasks relate to one another. Multiple timeline views also make it easier to get a visual overview of complex project schedules.Gantt chart task-path highlighting shows how individual tasks relate to one another. What-if scenarios allow project managers to test different assignments before committing resources. Baselines preserve the original plan so actual progress can be measured against initial schedules.
Microsoft Project also includes built-in reports such as Burndown and Resource Overview. These reports help communicate schedule, workload, and progress information to executives, clients, and other stakeholders.
Timesheets record hours spent on project and non-project work. That information can support payroll, invoicing, and internal resource management. The application can also synchronize with Project Online and Project Server.
Microsoft Teams for Business integration allows users to check a team member's online presence and begin chats or calls from a project plan. Teams for Business must be licensed separately.
The licensing terms are specific: The lifetime license covers one PC and connects to that device rather than a Microsoft account. Buyers should select the installation computer carefully.
Lifetime access to Microsoft Project Professional 2024 is available for $49.97 through October 4.

articles.title: OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design — specialized AI model will operate EDA tools, allowing engineers to deliver more sophisticated chips faster
articles.text:
OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design — specialized AI model will operate EDA tools, allowing engineers to deliver more sophisticated chips faster
Agentic AI comes to chip design
OpenAI and Synopsys have signed a multi-year agreement to jointly develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model optimized for semiconductor design using Synopsys's electronic design automation (EDA) tools. According to the September 30 announcement, the partnership “brings together OpenAI's advanced AI capabilities with Synopsys's industry-leading EDA tools and agentic AI capabilities to revolutionize the design of semiconductors.”
Engineers would delegate to agents that run the tools and execute the required processes until the work is ready for review. The companies say this would allow design teams to evaluate more options and deliver more sophisticated chips. Under the preferred partner agreement, OpenAI is licensing Synopsys's tools to develop the model — which will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure — after which the companies will jointly release the product and share revenue. The announcement did not disclose a release date or a pricing structure.
AI in chip design so far
Engineers use EDA tools to design and verify chips before manufacturing. This multi-step process begins with writing the hardware description in register-transfer level (RTL) code and using synthesis software to convert it into logic gates. Next, physical design tools lay out the circuit elements and route the connections between them. Lastly, designers close timing, verify functionality, and ensure manufacturing compliance before tapeout for fabrication.
Each of these stages requires several iterations — repeatedly running various tools and troubleshooting issues — to balance critical trade-offs: power, performance, and silicon area (PPA). Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens EDA have dominated this market for these tools long before the current AI boom. Given the technology's capabilities, it is only natural that AI has found its way into the chip design process, creating a sort of “silicon designing silicon” loop.
In March 2020, Synopsys launched DSO.ai (Design Space Optimization AI), a reinforcement learning tool that explores and learns from previous design optimizations to improve PPA. The company then launched Synopsys.ai Copilot in November 2023 — its first integration of generative AI — through a collaboration with Microsoft, integrating the Azure OpenAI service to provide natural language assistance within its engineering tools.
The company’s current direction is Agentic AI, first revealed at the Design Automation Conference in July, where it showed an autonomous verification workflow built on Nvidia's Agent Toolkit and Nemotron 3 Ultra model. On September 28, two days before the OpenAI deal, Synopsys announced its Autopilot platform and AgentEngineer, a portfolio of seven long-horizon agents covering verification, implementation, analog, manufacturing, meshing, combustion, and EMC analysis. The company reported more than 50 engagements, with availability planned for late 2026.
As detailed in our State of agentic AI in chip design tools roadmap, the move to agentic AI is not exclusive to Synopsys; Cadence and Siemens are also pitching autonomous design agents. Meanwhile, OpenAI, in collaboration with Broadcom, unveiled Jalapeño in June, the company’s first custom inference accelerator. OpenAI said the accelerator's design and optimization process leaned heavily on its AI models, allowing it to go from initial design to tape-out in just nine months. Now, GPT-Synopsys turns that internal experiment into a product.
GPT-Synopsys
According to the announcement, GPT-Synopsys will combine OpenAI's frontier models with Synopsys’s EDA software and domain expertise, allowing the model to reason about chip design and verification and operate Synopsys tools directly. Engineers would hand the model objectives such as PPA optimization, timing, and verification closure, while the agents run the tools, interpret the results, implement changes, and iterate toward verified outcomes for an engineer to review.
In other words, the model would be capable of making engineering judgments involved in using Synopsys software. The companies describe it as learning to operate the tools like an expert engineer, interpreting their outputs and using the results to guide further changes. This is the proposed specialization that takes the model beyond connecting a general-purpose model to a set of tools.
Synopsys’s EDA engines would perform the calculations and checks, with the model interpreting results and the agent software managing execution. GPT-Synopsys will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and is intended to integrate with Synopsys.ai and Autopilot, as well as work with customers’ own agent harnesses. Autopilot already provides services such as memory and governance.
Synopsys says early technology engagements are underway with leading semiconductor customers, but didn't name any. The immediate audience is professional semiconductor-design teams, with companies developing their own custom silicon also likely to use it. Although the announcement covers semiconductor design generally, OpenAI has a particular interest in improving the hardware that runs its models. “By helping them build better chips, we can build better AI and bring it to more people,” said Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder. Whether the service also makes advanced design more accessible to smaller teams will depend on pricing and the expertise still required to supervise it.
Questions and concerns
The recent announcement leaves a couple of questions and concerns unaddressed. First, hosting the model on OpenAI infrastructure raises concerns about how confidential designs are handled. The companies say customer data will be excluded from model training, encrypted at rest and in transit, and governed by configurable retention, audit, and permission controls. However, the release does not identify hosting regions or default retention periods. It also provides no contractual terms for ownership of generated outputs, use of third-party licensed design IP, or indemnities. The service's terms will likely address these questions.
Another question is the practical economics for users. The industry has realized that handing over everything to AI doesn't always result in cost savings, at least for now. Sometimes the reverse is the case. Earlier this year, Uber’s CTO and an Nvidia executive said AI was more expensive than human workers, although many companies are reportedly fine with the extra cost. For GPT-Synopsys, advanced engineering reasoning and faster design-to-tapeout could justify the service, but model calls, EDA runs, integration, and human review all consume resources. The announcement did not include a pricing structure. It also didn't specify a launch date.
Meanwhile, Synopsys’s main rival Cadence launched its ChipStack AI Super Agent in February for front-end design and verification, built on frontier LLMs. In April, the company announced a collaboration with Google to optimize ChipStack with Gemini on Google Cloud. At Computex, it extended ChipStack to what it calls Level-5 autonomy, powered by Nvidia's Nemotron models, with early access expected in the second half of 2026. The main difference is that while ChipStack is Cadence’s own agent software running on other companies’ general-purpose models, GPT-Synopsys will be an OpenAI model specifically trained to operate Synopsys’s tools.
Etiido Uko is a news contributor for Tom's Hardware covering the latest updates in big tech and the PC industry. He is a mechanical engineer and senior technical writer with over nine years of experience in documentation and reporting. He is deeply passionate about all things engineering and technology, and is an expert in gadgets, manufacturing, robotics, automotive, and aerospace.

articles.title: Solving the Five Hard Problems of NFC Antenna Integration at 13.56 MHz - EE Times
articles.text:
NFC at 13.56 MHz is one of the most widely deployed short-range wireless technologies in commercial electronics. It underpins contactless payment at point-of-sale, smart access credentials in building security, patient identification in healthcare devices, asset tracking in industrial logistics, device pairing in consumer electronics, and wearable authentication across an expanding range of IoT form factors.
Despite this breadth of deployment, NFC antenna integration remains one of the most consistently underestimated engineering tasks in 13.56 MHz system design. The NFC chipset receives the majority of design attention—selection, firmware integration, protocol stack validation—while the antenna is often treated as an afterthought: selected by size from a catalog and placed wherever convenient inside the product.
This approach reliably produces problems. In post-prototype bench testing, detection range is below specification. In enclosure testing, performance drops further. When the device is mounted in its real operating environment—near metal, inside a compact housing, worn on a wrist—NFC functionality degrades or fails entirely. The rework cost at this stage is substantial: PCB respin, antenna re-selection, ferrite material qualification, mechanical design changes, and compliance re-testing.
The root cause is not chipset inadequacy. In the vast majority of cases, the failure mode is antenna-related: wrong form factor, unshielded coil on a metal surface, rigid PCB placement where a flexible or cable-terminated antenna was needed, or a coil specification that was never validated against the actual chipset in use.
This paper examines five specific engineering challenges that arise from inadequate antenna selection. For each, it presents the physical mechanism behind the problem, its practical consequences in product development, and the engineering solution.
Challenge 1: performance degradation on metal substrates
The industry problem
Metal surfaces—battery packs, metal chassis panels, PCB ground plane, shielding enclosures, and metallic structural elements—are present in the majority of embedded device designs. Industrial handhelds use metal enclosures for durability. Access control readers mount on metal door frames. Payment terminals have internal shielding layers. Medical device panels are often metal for hygiene and regulatory compliance.
The consequence of placing a standard NFC coil directly on metal is severe and predictable: Detection range collapses. In many cases, read range is reduced by 90% relative to bench performance. In other words, the antenna ceases to function entirely within the tuned frequency band.
Root cause: eddy currents and inductance degradation
The physical mechanism is electromagnetic induction. An NFC coil operating at 13.56 MHz produces a time-varying magnetic field in the near-field region. When a conductive surface is present, the time-varying flux induces eddy currents within the conductor. By Lenz’s law, these eddy currents generate their own opposing magnetic field.
The practical consequence is a reduction in effective inductance. The coil’s resonant frequency—determined by the LC tank formed with the matching network—shifts away from 13.56 MHz, reducing coupling coefficient. The severity depends on the metal’s conductivity and permeability, its thickness relative to skin depth, and the distance between coil and surface. At distances below approximately 5 mm, performance degradation with unshielded antennas becomes practically significant for most metallic materials.
Engineering solution: high-permeability ferrite shielding
The effective solution is a ferrite sheet inserted between the NFC coil and the metal surface. Ferrite is a magnetically soft material with high relative permeability (µr typically 100–300 for NFC-grade materials) and low electrical conductivity. Its high permeability provides a low-reluctance magnetic path that preferentially channels the coil’s flux through itself rather than into the conductive metal below—preventing eddy current induction and preserving coil inductance.
The ferrite layer acts as a magnetic barrier rather than an electrical one: It does not block the field flow from the device face toward the reader or tag, but it redirects flux away from the metal material below the antenna. Figure 1 illustrates the ferrite shielding principle.
For any design in which metallic elements—battery, chassis section, shielding layer, or copper pour—are present within approximately 5 mm of the antenna plane, specify a ferrite-integrated antenna variant as the default. The performance margin provided by ferrite in borderline geometries consistently outweighs the minor additional cost.
Challenge 2: rigid placement constraints and PCB co-location
The industry problem
Product enclosures are designed around mechanical, thermal, and aesthetic requirements largely independent of NFC antenna positioning. The main PCB is frequently positioned at the rear or center of the device—not at the face where NFC reads must occur. Structural elements, battery compartments, display assemblies, and other subsystems occupy the space between the board and the housing face. In compact handheld devices, the physical distance between the required antenna position and the PCB can be 20–50 mm or more. A rigid PCB-mounted antenna cannot bridge this distance.
Engineering solution: cable-terminated antennas with Litz wire
Cable-terminated antenna variants, where the NFC coil is physically separate from the PCB and connected via cable, are the common solution. The antenna element is positioned at the housing face or RF window; the cable routes through the mechanical assembly to the NFC chipset on the main PCB.
Specify Litz wire for the cable. At 13.56 MHz, the skin depth in copper is approximately 18 µm. In a conventional stranded wire, this confines current to the conductor surface, raising series resistance and degrading antenna Q-factor. Litz wire—constructed from individually insulated fine strands each near or below the skin depth—distributes current across all strands, maintaining the Q-factor even over wire runs of 100 mm or longer.
Specify the antenna mechanical footprint and PCB connector header at the mechanical design phase—before finalizing whether a PCB-mounted or cable-terminated configuration is required. This preserves configuration flexibility through late-stage prototype testing without a board respin.
Challenge 3: connector reliability and board-level integration
The industry problem
NFC antennas physically separated from the main PCB require a connector that maintains reliability, survives the assembly process, and is manufacturable at production volumes without manual soldering of fine wires to the board. Direct solder connections of Litz wire to pads—common in prototype builds—are sensitive to wire dressing, are not robust at production volumes, and introduce uncharacterized series impedance. Generic 2-pin connectors are frequent sources of intermittent failures in vibration or thermal cycling.
Two-connector strategy: Pogo-pin and ACH
Two connector types address the full range of NFC antenna integration scenarios:
- Pogo-pin spring-loaded contacts: The spring mechanism maintains consistent contact force across dimensional tolerances, ensuring reliable electrical contact independent of small assembly variations. Best suited to separable or field-replaceable antenna modules.
- ACH locking board-to-wire connector: A compact, locking, polarized two-circuit connector that prevents accidental disconnection and eliminates polarity errors in production. Pre-crimped factory assemblies eliminate on-line crimping or soldering, a significant manufacturing quality advantage at high volume.
Table 1: connector selection guide
| Challenge | Engineering Solution | 
| Separable / removable antenna (service, modular design) | Pogo-pin | 
| Permanent installation, high production volume | ACH locking connector | 
| Vibration environment (industrial, vehicular) | ACH locking connector (preferred) | 
| Prototype / engineering evaluation | Either—pogo-pin simplifies changes | 
Challenge 4: chipset compatibility and pre-compliance validation
The industry problem
Published antenna specifications—inductance, Q-factor, resonant frequency—do not directly translate to system-level detection distance without additional analysis. Engineers routinely select an antenna based on RF parameters, integrate it with an NFC chipset, tune the matching network, and then find that detection distance is below specification. The discrepancy may result from an impedance mismatch between antenna and chipset output, or an incompatibility between the antenna’s inductance and the chipset’s recommended range. Resolving this without chipset-specific data requires iterative re-tuning that can delay product development by weeks.
The correct performance metric: detection distance
Detection distance—the maximum distance at which the NFC system reliably reads a tag—is the correct system-level performance metric. It captures the integrated effect of chipset performance, antenna coupling, tuning accuracy, and tag characteristics in a single measurable value.
Standardized detection distance testing presents a reference NFC tag at incrementally increasing distances and records the maximum reliable communication range. The test covers NFC Forum Tag Types 1 through 5, since each type has different resonant characteristics that interact differently with the reader antenna. Figure 2 illustrates typical detection distance versus tag type for a 40 × 30 mm NFC antenna validated against NXP PN7160 and ST ST25R3911B chipsets—two of the most widely used NFC front-end controllers in current commercial and industrial IoT designs.
Required RF parameters for tuning network design
In addition to detection distance data, four antenna RF parameters are required for tuning network design:
- Self-resonance frequency (Fres): The frequency at which distributed capacitance resonates with self-inductance. Operate the antenna below Fres; operation at or above Fres causes impedance inversion and severe performance degradation.
- Parallel resistance (RP) represents radiation and loss resistance in the parallel equivalent circuit model. Higher RP indicates lower loss and higher Q.
- DC resistance (RDC) is the ohmic resistance of the coil winding. Limits achievable Q-factor.
- Inductance at 1 MHz (L₁MHz): Measured well below self-resonance, this provides a stable reference value for initial matching network calculation.
Absence of these parameters from a supplier’s datasheet is a qualification risk indicator. Request and review the full parametric datasheet before finalizing antenna selection.
Challenge 5: late-stage design changes and specification volatility
The industry problem
NFC is frequently added to a product specification late in the development cycle—sometimes after mechanical design is already tooled—in response to market feedback, competitive positioning, or customer requirements. This pattern is particularly common in ODM and OEM environments where product specifications evolve rapidly. The consequence: Available PCB area is constrained, the enclosure is fixed, and metallic elements may sit near any feasible antenna location. Custom antenna development adds four to eight weeks of lead time and NRE cost to the critical path.
Engineering solution: identical-footprint configuration switching
When all configuration variants—bare coil, ferrite-integrated, cable-terminated, and cable-terminated with ferrite—share identical antenna element dimensions, engineers can address late-stage constraint discoveries without a PCB respin or mechanical tooling change. An engineer who discovers a metal-proximity problem after prototype testing can switch from the bare-coil to the ferrite variant without changing the layout. A placement constraint identified after tooling can be addressed by switching to the cable-terminated variant—repositioning the antenna element without modifying the PCB footprint.
This configuration flexibility effectively decouples the antenna selection decision from the mechanical design timeline. The recommended late-stage change mitigation strategy is:
- Step 1: Specify the antenna mechanical footprint using the largest anticipated form factor at mechanical design phase.
- Step 2: Place the antenna PCB pad and connector header for both direct-mount and cable-terminated configurations.
- Step 3: Use bare-coil variant for initial prototyping to establish baseline performance.
- Step 4: If metal proximity is identified during prototype testing, switch to ferrite variant (same footprint, no layout change).
- Step 5: If placement is suboptimal after enclosure testing, populate the cable header and use cable-terminated variant.
- Step 6: If both metal proximity and placement issues exist, switch to cable-terminated ferrite variant.
All four configuration transitions are achievable without PCB respin or mechanical tooling change.
Conclusion
NFC antenna integration failures share a common characteristic: They are predictable. The five challenges documented in this paper—metal-surface degradation, rigid placement constraints, connector reliability, chipset validation gaps, and late-stage specification changes—each arise from known physical mechanisms and addressable engineering choices. They are not inherent limitations of 13.56 MHz NFC technology; they are consequences of antenna selection that does not match the constraints of the specific application.
The engineering argument for a structured, well-characterized NFC antenna portfolio is therefore not primarily a product recommendation—it is a risk management argument. The cost of addressing these challenges through a well-specified standard catalog is, in every case, lower than the cost of discovering them through prototype failure and subsequent rework. Treat antenna selection as a system-level engineering decision that interacts with enclosure geometry, substrate materials, chipset tuning, mechanical tolerances, and compliance requirements simultaneously, and the majority of NFC integration failures can be avoided before they occur.
