articles.title: MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ Review: Ridiculous, in performance and price
articles.text:
I owned a PSP as a teenager, and some of my fondest memories of the time include playing Dragon Ball Z Shin Budokai 2 with my friends over LAN. But the golden PSP era eventually came to an end, and its successors, like the PS Vita, never really managed to capture quite the same magic. For a while, it seemed like handhelds had been pushed to the side by smartphones, PCs, and powerful consoles. As we know now, that’s obviously not the case.
In 2022, the Steam Deck revitalized handheld gaming, and it didn’t take long for other major PC players to jump in. Today, you have handheld PC gaming options from the likes of Lenovo, Asus, MSI, Ayaneo, and more, giving users several reliable options to pick and choose from.
My own experience with handhelds, since the PSP, hasn’t been the most extensive. I own a PS Portal, though I don’t truly consider it a standalone handheld, despite its recent cloud gaming capabilities. I’ve also spent considerable time with a friend’s ROG Ally X, though considering that it isn’t mine, I haven’t had the chance to really dig into it beyond casual gaming and general use.
That said, I’m far from new to gaming. Most of my gaming today happens on PC and PS5, and when I was presented with the opportunity to try out one of MSI’s latest and most powerful Claw handhelds, I was all game.
The handheld in question is the $2,200 MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ with Intel’s new Arc G3 Extreme processor, and well, it has a lot going for it. For reference, gaming handhelds often rely on chips originally designed for laptops and mobile PCs. Intel’s new chip takes a slightly different approach.
It is purpose-built and optimized for handheld gaming, and after spending some time with the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, I feel like the chip (and the overall package) succeeds in striking a balance between performance, power efficiency, portability, and thermals.
This might be a pro for some and a con for others. The new handheld has an 8-inch display and weighs 785g. The Steam Deck OLED, in comparison, weighs 640g. The extra weight does add up, and I’ve found my hands fatiguing with extended use. I wouldn’t necessarily call the new Claw light, but it is portable enough to carry around with ease, and I rarely ever found myself struggling to grip the handheld during shorter gaming sessions. That can be attributed to the Claw’s new controller-like design.
For reference, up until now, all Claws have had that flatter, slab-like rectangular look. The Claw 8 EX AI+ changes that by adopting more rounded grips that sit in the palms of your hands much better. It sure doesn’t make the 785g weight disappear, but it does make it a bit more manageable.
Circling back to the display, it has a peak brightness of 500 nits, which, for the most part, offers a perfectly usable experience outdoors. However, dark scenes do suffer, and direct sunlight quickly exposes the limits of the new Claw’s IPS panel. Yep, you’re getting an LCD IPS panel for $2,200.
The new Steam Deck and the Lenovo Legion Go 2 both feature OLED panels with 1,000 nits of peak HDR brightness and an overall better contrast ratio and colour gamut. Even Asus’ upcoming ROG Ally X20 is confirmed to rock an OLED panel with 1,400 nits of HDR brightness, making the new Claw’s IPS display feel hard to justify, especially at its price point.
It’s not a bad screen by any means, with a 1,920 x 1,200 resolution and a 48-120Hz variable refresh rate, but at this price point, and especially with competitors going for OLED panels, a glare-y IPS panel doesn’t cut it. That, however, is my only major gripe with the new Claw. In a briefing, MSI told me it is looking into OLED for future handhelds.
The rest of the handheld feels a lot more in line with the Claw’s premium positioning. Although this might not be a primary reason to buy the Claw, I like the fact that it can stand on the bottom of its display panel. It’s not a design feature that I expect many would care about, but it’s a nifty trick to prop the handheld up when I’m using it to consume content.
Elsewhere, MSI says that, compared to previous generations, the new handheld’s ABXY buttons are more rounded. I didn’t notice much of a change here, and compared to other controllers, the Claw 8 EX AI+ didn’t really stand out much. However, taken together with the D-Pad, the conveniently placed joysticks, which now use Hall Effect sensors, by the way (you don’t need to worry about drift!), and easy-to-reach M1 and M2 back buttons, the Xbox-like layout feels well thought out and comfortable to use.
I personally wouldn’t put the overall control experience in the same league as the PS5 controller and its layout, but that’s an argument for a different day.
The new Claw is generous when it comes to connectivity too. The device has two Thunderbolt 4 ports along the top, alongside a microSD Express card reader, a 3.5mm audio jack, volume controls, and a power button that doubles as a fingerprint reader.
All ports and buttons, barring the main controller ones, are limited to the top of the device. This does make charging while gaming a little awkward, considering that the charging cable has to dangle from the top. The same applies when you connect the handheld to a monitor. A bottom placement for one of the ports would have made sense, but its absence doesn’t necessarily break the experience.
On the other hand, MSI seems to have nailed the internals. I pried the Claw’s back open to reveal what’s inside, and unsurprisingly, the handheld’s 80Wh battery occupies a large part of the inside. I could squeeze roughly 3 hours of gaming on MSI’s Endurance Mode, while maxing out power gave me around an hour of gaming. More on that later.
Two fans cool the handheld, and from my brief time with the new Claw, I can confirm that the fans do a great job. The handheld never really got hot, even during extended gaming sessions, with the only noticeable heat coming from the exhaust vents.
For what it’s worth, the fans do become audible under sustained load, but nothing crazy. Of course, I’ve only had the Claw 8 EX AI+ for a short duration. It will take longer-term use to see how well the cooling system holds up, especially after factors like dust buildup come into play.
Elsewhere, prying the back open also gave me a clear look at the 1TB SSD. MSI is using a PCIe Gen 4 x4 M.2 2280 SSD, making future at-home storage upgrades relatively straightforward.
Arc G3 Extreme is the real star here
The 14-core CPU (2 Cougar Cove performance cores, 8 Darkmont efficiency cores, and 4 Darkmont low-power efficiency cores) is paired with Intel’s integrated Arc B390 graphics. You might have come to associate “integrated” graphics with weak performance, but that’s really not the case here.
For starters, MSI gives you a lot of control over performance. I could manually set the Claw’s PL1 as high as 35W and PL2 to 45W. For reference, PL1 figures represent the amount of power, in watts, that a processor can draw and sustain over long and continuous workloads. PL2 figures represent higher short-term power limits that a processor can draw for brief moments when performance is needed. MSI’s last Claw, the Claw 8 AI+, maxed out at 30W PL1 and 37W PL2.
For the Arc G3 Extreme, being able to draw more power equals more room to offer better performance, but that does come at a cost.
Using the new Claw on its max power draw settings does force its fans to work harder, but as I mentioned earlier, they do a surprisingly good job of keeping the handheld cool without getting too loud. The bigger trade-off, however, is battery life.
Yep, the Claw is a portable device, but running it at full power while you’re out and about simply isn’t practical. As I mentioned earlier, maxing out the Claw gave me roughly an hour of gaming, with slight discrepancies depending on brightness.
That quick battery discharge is precisely why the Claw offers power modes. When you’re at home, you can plug the Claw in and let the Arc G3 Extreme go crazy. And when you’re actually using the device as a portable machine, you can tweak PL1 and PL2 to something more conservative. MSI says 17W offers a good sweet spot between performance and efficiency, and the same goes for the pre-built Endurance Mode.
When running Forza Horizon 5 at 1,920 x 1,200 resolution, high settings, and XeSS disabled, I recorded 78fps in Endurance Mode, albeit when connected to power. When unplugged, Endurance Mode caps framerates at 30 by default, though you do have the option to raise the limit to 40 or 60fps. Manually pushing PL1 to 35W and PL2 to 45W under the same settings pushed the game all the way up to 110fps.
Then there’s the MSI AI Engine. It automatically adjusts your system’s power consumption based on what you’re doing, and it seems to work pretty well. When simply using the handheld for browsing, looking for games, downloading them, or using the handheld as a mini PC, the mode keeps power draw relatively low. It automatically ramps up when it detects you’re gaming. Under the same Forza Horizon 5 settings as mentioned above, AI Engine mode returned 103fps and 102fps across two identical runs. That’s remarkably close to the 110fps max I recorded while manually pushing the Claw to its limits.
It’s worth noting that I was stuck at 47fps during one AI Engine Horizon 5 benchmark run, though that seems to have been an anomaly, as I haven’t been able to reproduce it.
All of the figures above were without any type of upscaling involved. However, I also wanted to see how well the Arc G3 Extreme would manage more demanding titles, where upscaling would need to do some of the heavy lifting. I turned to Black Myth: Wukong for that.
I tested Intel’s XeSS and frame generation across a repeated area in the game with the same enemies and surroundings, and that’s when the benefits of Intel’s chip became even more apparent.
With the Claw ramped up to the max and Black Myth: Wukong’s in-game settings on high, the handheld offered 50-60fps with XeSS enabled and frame generation off. With frame generation enabled, that figure climbed all the way up to 85-110fps. Although the increase is immediately noticeable visually, it’s important to remember that generated frames aren’t equivalent to natively rendered ones.
Considering that input and game responsiveness are still tied to the original underlying framerate, Wukong looked great at 85-110fps with frame gen on, but it didn’t necessarily feel as responsive as a game actually running natively at 85-110fps. That said, the underlying 50-60fps was already plenty responsive, so frame generation made sense here.
Similarly, with AI Engine mode and frame generation disabled, the Claw offered 42-47fps. With frame generation enabled, the same run offered 70-83fps. That’s already much better than what most mid-range pre-built PCs, or higher-end PCs from a few years ago, offer.
I tried the same Wukong run on Endurance Mode (while plugged in), and that, naturally, pulled things back considerably. With frame generation disabled, I recorded 29-37fps. With frame gen enabled, the same run got bumped up to 46-58fps, which was still perfectly playable.
For what it’s worth, Forza Horizon 5 already runs so well on the Arc B390 GPU that I didn’t need to rely on frame gen. More demanding titles are where the technology makes a stronger case for itself.
More than a gaming machine
Gaming is, of course, the most important aspect of the new Claw. However, considering that it can double as a capable mini PC, I had to run some other general tests. Directly connecting the Claw to an external monitor through one of its Thunderbolt 4 ports is simple, though with additional peripherals in the picture, a dock serves as a good addition to the setup.
I wrote much of this review using the Claw as a mini PC, and everything went smoothly. At the risk of sounding redundant, using the Claw as a mini PC for everyday tasks is going to be a breeze.
I ran Geekbench 7 with Windows set to the Balanced power option, and the Arc G3 Extreme came back with a single-core score of 2,256 and a multi-core score of 14,661.
I also ran Cinebench with the Claw pushed to its maximum settings, and it returned a single-thread score of 410 and a multi-thread score of 3,511.
Based on the CPU benchmarks, the Arc G3 Extreme leaves the AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme, the processor that Asus is using in its latest ROG Ally, in the dust. At least on paper. This makes the Claw 8 EX AI+ among the most, if not outright the most, powerful PC gaming handhelds on the market right now.
For what it’s worth, I’m going hands-on with the new Ally too, so it’ll be interesting to try out AMD’s offering after spending considerable time with the Arc G3 Extreme.
Who is the Claw 8 EX AI+ actually for?
The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ is an enthusiast-grade device that’s built for those with deep pockets. Don’t get me wrong, the handheld is seriously impressive. The Arc G3 does a lot of the heavy lifting, while MSI’s controls give you enough room to balance power and performance. However, $2,200 is a lot to ask.
At that price, you’re already encroaching on the upper mid-range and the lower-high-end range of gaming laptops that offer better performance, and that makes some compromises of the Claw, and PC gaming handhelds in general, harder to ignore. To get the most out of demanding AAA games, you’d need to run the handheld at its maximum settings, with additional tools like frame generation enabled. This absolutely decimates the Claw’s battery life.
So, essentially, your options are either to run the Claw in a lower power mode and sacrifice performance, get roughly an hour of high-performance portable gaming, or simply keep the device plugged in for extended gaming sessions. That’s exactly where the value proposition starts to get murky for me. If I’m going to have to keep the device plugged in for demanding gaming sessions, I’d rather put my money toward a gaming laptop or a PC.
That, however, is a gaming handheld issue that’s not necessarily limited to MSI. And the company does get a lot right. The handheld’s cooling system is excellent, the device is comfortable to grab and grip, connectivity is generous, and upgrading storage is as seamless as on modern PCs. The star of the show, of course, is the Arc G3 Extreme, which manages to fit impressive gaming performance in an integrated GPU. MSI’s AI Engine is also great at anticipating power needs, while general reliability means the device can easily double as a mini PC.
If you’re someone who wants one of the most powerful PC gaming handhelds available on the market, the steep asking price doesn’t faze you, and you’re fine with the general limitations that involve plugging in handhelds for extended high-power gaming sessions, then there’s no better option than the Claw 8 EX AI+. The LCD is a sore spot in the otherwise premium package, but it’s still sharp, smooth, and something you’ll get used to fairly quickly.

iPhone 16 Plus com tela grande chega à melhor oferta em meses
iPhone 16 Plus (128 GB) com OLED de 6,7" e câmera de 48 MP recebe desconto exclusivo de 38% apenas para assinantes Amazon Prime
O iPhone 16 Plus de 128 GB está saindo por R$ 5.849 à vista apenas para assinantes do Amazon Prime. O celular da Apple, equipado com tela OLED grande de 6,7″ e câmera wide de 48 MP atinge um dos menores preços recentes, com desconto de 38% sobre o original de R$ 9.499.
Embora menos avançado que a linha iPhone 17, o iPhone 16 Plus é hoje a opção mais acessível de celular da Apple com tela grande, sem recorrer a um Pro Max mais caro. Sua LPTO Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,7″ com brilho de até 2.000 nits reproduz imagens com cores vivas e tem visibilidade garantida em qualquer ambiente.
Seu kit de câmeras inclui uma wide de 48 MP com OIS igual à do iPhone 17e e uma ultrawide de 12 MP, que captam belas imagens em ambientes amplos. A frontal de 12 MP tira ótimas selfies. Todas filmam em 4K a 60 fps.
O chip Apple A18 e os 8 GB de RAM permitem rodar apps pesados em multitarefa e soluções do Apple Intelligence localmente. Os 128 GB de armazenamento podem ser expandidos com planos do iCloud.
O corpo de alumínio do iPhone 16 Plus é reforçado pelo vidro Ceramic Shield sobre a tela, resistente a quedas e pancadas, enquanto a certificação IP68 confere resistência em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.674 mAh resiste a até 27 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a fabricante. O suporte ao MagSafe e o carregamento rápido de 25 W via USB-C garantem que o celular não fique sem energia durante o dia, ideal para usuários sem tempo a perder com tomadas.
O iPhone 16 Plus de 128 GB (R$ 5.849 à vista só para assinantes do Amazon Prime) foi atualizado para o iOS 27 e deve receber pelo menos mais quatro atualizações do sistema operacional. O celular da Apple possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.3 e NFC.

articles.title: Paramount completes $111B Warner merger, creating “Skydance” behemoth
articles.text:
Paramount Skydance completed its $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery today, after a last-ditch effort to block the deal was rejected by Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan.
The post-merger company is called Skydance, taking the name of a firm that Paramount bought in a separate deal last year. The new Skydance combines two of the largest movie studios, streaming services Paramount+ and HBO Max, CBS, CNN, “and a portfolio of live sports including CBS Sports and TNT Sports, as well as a deep programming library and expansive collection of brands and franchises,” Skydance said today in a press release announcing completion of the deal.
The merger was delayed a bit by a lawsuit filed by California and 11 other states. In July, US District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín in the Northern District of California ruled that the combination would likely reduce competition substantially and violate antitrust laws.
California settled the lawsuit last month, and the other states involved went along with the compromise. A coalition of free speech and media advocacy groups urged the judge to reject the settlement, saying it will give residents of the states that sued Paramount “virtually nothing.”
Martínez-Olguín approved the settlement on September 30, saying the deal “represents a reasonable factual and legal resolution of the dispute.” She wrote that a typical settlement “does not fully remediate an alleged violation or even necessarily resolve the ultimate factual and legal issues of a case.” It “reflects a compromise of the claims short of full adjudication—compromise that may leave some dissatisfaction for both sides and the public but a compromise that saves the risk, time, and expense of litigating through trial.”
The settlement addresses the lawsuit’s complaints about film distribution “by requiring certain minimum thresholds of investment and release of domestic films,” and addresses complaints about licensing of basic cable channels with “requirements for continued, separate negotiations of distribution for the two entities’ basic cable holdings,” the judge wrote. Objections based on “hopes and desires for the proposed consent decree to reach farther—to achieve more—do not rise to the level of legal violations upon which the Court can reject the parties’ negotiated resolution,” she wrote.

articles.title: Anthropic earmarks $100 million to train over 10,000 AI engineers in push to develop enterprise AI
articles.text:
Anthropic earmarks $100 million to train over 10,000 AI engineers in push to develop enterprise AI
Anthropic wants 10,000 FDEs by 2027, with a twist
- Anthropic wants to train 10k FDEs from large institutions and consultancies
- Using their customers could extend Claude's reach significantly
- Training will include a simulated deployment and an actual deployment
Anthropic has announced plans to spend a mammoth $100 million to launch its Claude Frontier Academy, a training scheme designed to support enterprise AI adoption.
The company is targeting 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers (FDEs) by the end of 2027, who will be able to identify use cases, handle security considerations and drive deployment for Claude customers.
"Claude Frontier Academy trains people the way our own engineers learn, and we want those who graduate to set the standard for how AI gets built inside a business," Steve Corfield, Global Head of Business Development and Partnerships at Anthropic explained.
Anthropic to train 10,000 FDEs
The training scheme starts with a simulated enterprise deployment before trainees enter a 12-week residency "where they lead a real Claude use case at their own organization."
The initial cohorts are set to include engineers from major consulting and financial organizations, including Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley and Novo Nordisk.
Anthropic has already given out more than 175,000 Claude certifications to workers across 46,000 companies part of its broader Claude Partner Network, but the drive behind its latest FDE scheme is clear.
The easier it becomes for enterprise customers and consultancies to deploy Claude, the more customers Anthropic is likely to have. Additionally, working with consultancies gives Anthropic access to their customers, extending its reach.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Rival company OpenAI already has its own extensive FDE scheme, too, but there's a key difference. OpenAI's focus is on training its own workers to go off and transform customers' companies, but Anthropic's latest announcement is primarily about training other companies' engineers to become FDEs.
Reuters recently reported that OpenAI has experienced a twofold increase in enterprise sales since July 2026, and while specific figures are kept closely under wraps, we do know that enterprise deals are far more lucrative for companies like Anthropic than consumer subscriptions.
So while a $100 million commitment to train engineers may sound like a large sum, Anthropic clearly hopes it will pay off in the long run.

articles.title: AI computing startup Lambda to raise $4B ahead of planned IPO | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Cloud provider Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation, marking what could be its last private round before a planned 2027 IPO, according to The Wall Street Journal. Coatue Management and Blackstone are leading the round.
A letter to investors reviewed by the Journal shows Lambda’s backlog grew from $15 billion in June to $50 billion in September. While that might look like a hearty increase in demand, much of that increase appears to be driven by a $35 billion commitment from one company: Anthropic, which signed a deal with Lambda in late August.
That means Lambda’s valuation, which has climbed significantly since its 2025 funding round, could be leaning heavily on Anthropic’s ability to keep paying. Still, with reliable GPU capacity so scarce, investors are clearly still willing to bet on companies that provide it, especially ones with large contracts with a major AI lab.
For neoclouds like Lambda, demand isn’t so much the problem as is the cost of meeting it. Data center buildouts are largely funded by debt — of which Lambda just raised an additional $1 billion last week — and lenders are getting choosier about who they offer cash to and under what circumstances. Lambda’s decision to raise more now not only sets the tone for its IPO pricing, but also gives it access to more capital before the scrutiny of public markets arrives.
If and when Lambda does IPO — the company was reportedly meant to debut this year, but has pushed that back amid market uncertainty — it will join other Nvidia-backed neoclouds, like CoreWeave and Nebius, that now depend on the health of their stock to fund their data center buildouts. British neocloud Nscale filed for an IPO last month and is expected to begin trading soon.
Lambda, Coatue, and Blackstone did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: Antseed launches a decentralized marketplace for AI inference that dramatically lowers developers' costs - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Antseed launches a decentralized marketplace for AI inference that dramatically lowers developers’ costs
Developers now have a much cheaper way to access cutting-edge artificial intelligence inference capabilities with the launch of Antseed today.
It’s a new peer-to-peer marketplace that makes it possible to access almost any frontier model at a small fraction of its normal cost by bypassing centralized gateways in favor of independent and mainstream providers.
The launch of Antseed came as its controlling entity, the Antseed Foundation, closed on a $2.4 million token funding round led by Spark Capital, an early investor in Anthropic PBC, with participation from Collider, DCG, North Island Ventures, Reciprocal Ventures, Venice.ai and Relay Capital.
Antseed’s marketplace was created to help developers combat what the startup says is the “skyrocketing cost” of AI inference, or the computing power required to run AI models and generate responses. It cites data from Gartner Inc., which projects that global spending on AI cloud infrastructure is likely to grow to $42 billion by the end of this year.
The problem with inference is that developers have had few options until now but to access models through centralized middleman gateways and application programming interfaces that are controlled by just a handful of model providers. These companies have the ability to dictate the costs and usage limits, and they can adapt their pricing on the fly, leading to unpredictable price spikes for inference workloads.
Antseed’s open inference marketplace is meant to get around this challenge by giving anyone the ability to route AI requests across hundreds of independent and mainstream model providers, bypassing those centralized gateways. In effect, this forces model providers to compete for every request by lowering their prices. Antseed claims this is what allows users to access leading frontier models by up to 97% less than their official API prices.
The marketplace relies on a self-hosted local router, through which providers can list their available inference capacity, utilizing hardware they own, and set their own prices. Antseed verifies that each provider does indeed provide access to the models it claims to serve. The marketplace is built on the idea of reputation: If a provider fails a verification check, its reputation will decrease, and its routing priority will decline.
Antseed co-founder Amos Meiri compares its marketplace to the file-sharing service BitTorrent. He says it enables developers to maintain their existing AI workloads and configure routing for each request based on their cost, latency, capability and privacy requirements.
“What BitTorrent did for files, Antseed is doing for AI inference, with no central server and no company deciding who gets access or what it costs,” he said. “As agents make more model calls and inference becomes a material operating cost, developers need a simple way to route each request based on price, performance, capability and privacy. Antseed gives them one compatible local endpoint and access to a competitive market of independent providers, without locking their applications into a single centralized gateway.”
Antseed’s decentralized approach to model access enables model pricing to be dictated by open market dynamics, and it’s entirely anonymous too, so developers aren’t required to sign up to the service or provide any details at all. Because the router runs locally on the provider’s own systems, developers can also choose to go with hardware-verified providers that ensure strict prompt confidentiality. Developers can also access models through a pay-per-request pricing model, so there’s no need to commit to rigid, subscription-based pricing tiers.
Meiri said this strategy is already getting traction as a growing community of developers begin to realize the cost benefits Antseed providers. He points to on-chain data that shows how Antseed has processed almost 150 billion tokens across 202 active providers so far.
Spark Capital co-founder and General Partner Santo Politi said inference is to AI what fuel is to airlines. “It’s a core operating cost that companies need to manage as they scale, but right now only a handful of companies control the wells,” he explained. “Antseed is the counterweight to that centralized control, serving as a decentralized open market that gives developers the freedom to choose how they source compute while creating a direct market for providers to compete.”

articles.title: CXL-Connected MRAM Address AI Storage Latency - EE Times
articles.text:
The memory bottleneck in AI systems gets a lot of attention, but storage latency is a growing pain point too. Everspin Technologies thinks it can address it with what it says is the industry’s first CXL-attached DDR4 MRAM.
At the SNIA Developer Conference in Santa Clara, Calif., Everspin demonstrated its combined MRAM modules with a CXL controller, creating pool of persistent memory accessible through CXL.mem semantics, which allows MRAM to act as a new tier of storage between DRAM and NAND flash.
Everspin’s demo used a Supermicro server equipped with an AMD EPYC 9355 processor and an AMD Alveo U250 FPGA card incorporating a Wolley CXL 3.2 controller. Four 1-GB Everspin DDR4 MRAM modules created a contiguous 4-GB memory space. The platform passed both MemTester and Google Stress App validation tests, which Everspin said demonstrates its readiness for customer workload evaluations.
In a briefing with EE Times, Steffen Hellmold, Everspin’s VP of corporate strategy, said the goal is not to position MRAM as a NAND replacement. Instead, the company said it sees the technology as a high-performance persistent cache layer. “Augment your solid-state storage with some MRAM, and you get a very high-performing combination,” he said.
Storage bottlenecks can drive system utilization to less than 50%, Hellmold added, which can leave expensive GPUs sitting idle waiting for I/O operations to complete. “CXL-MRAM can provide 100× lower latency than NVMe NAND SSD,” Hellmold said.
Hellmold said that persistent memory accessible with memory semantics rather than storage protocols can significantly accelerate checkpointing, key-value caches, and scratchpad workloads in AI systems. “If a GPU has to wait 100 microseconds or 100 nanoseconds for a checkpointing operation to complete, that determines how fast the GPU can move on to the next task,” he said.
Unlike battery-backed DRAM approaches, MRAM also retains data without power, Hellmold said, which eliminates concerns associated with batteries or supercapacitors used for power-failure protection.
Once touted by some vendors as a potential DRAM successor, MRAM has found more traction in niche but valuable applications where persistence, endurance, and low latency are critical. MRAM has already been used in data center storage applications for more than 15 years, serving functions ranging from journal memory to write-data buffers and caches.
Memory hungry data centers, meanwhile, are not only gobbling up high volumes of HBM and DRAM but are also being architected to make use of a variety of memories for different tasks, including LPDDR4, SRAM, and MRAM.
Whether CXL becomes the catalyst that expands MRAM adoption remains an open question. The emerging interconnect standard has gained momentum as hyperscalers seek memory pooling and expansion technologies, but commercial deployments remain in their early stages.
“The memory shortage has greatly helped us to basically push the use case of CXL attached memory,” Hellmold said. “MRAM certainly will be very attractive as a complement.”
Jim Handy, principal analyst at Objective Analysis, told EE Times in an interview that Everspin’s CXL demonstration validates the long-discussed concept of using CXL as a standard way to connect new memory technologies to modern servers. While CXL deployments to date have focused primarily on DRAM expansion and pooling, Everspin’s demonstration shows how alternative memory technologies can also benefit from the emerging ecosystem, he said.
Using MRAM connected via CXL is also better than approaches that attempt to replicate NVDIMMs in CXL because it doesn’t require any big backup capacitors, Handy added. It also doesn’t require users to install specialized DIMMs directly into server memory slots, “getting a little bit too much into the bowels of the server.”
MRAM’s native persistence makes it particularly attractive for handling “data in flight” that must survive power failures before being committed to SSDs or hard drives. Common applications include financial systems, gaming machines, and storage networks where preserving system state is critical, Handy said. “If they lose their status during a power outage, that’s a real problem.”
The use of CXL also helps overcome one of the practical barriers that has limited broader experimentation with emerging memories.
“It is cool that they put it into a CXL module,” Handy said. “It does allow pretty much anybody who wants to experiment with it to just plug it into a system and go.”

articles.title: Tool löscht Apple Intelligence von deinem Mac
articles.text:
Über 10 Gigabyte Speicherplatz sparen: Open-Source-Tool entfernt Apple Intelligence
Mit dem Einzug von macOS 27 hat Apple seine KI-Funktionen stärker in das System integriert. Apple Intelligence lässt sich damit nicht mehr einfach per Schalter vollständig deaktivieren und der Speicher anschließend wieder freigeben.
Apple Intelligence braucht viel Platz
Vielmehr werden die erforderlichen Modelle nach der macOS-27-Installation automatisch geladen, wenn eine Internetverbindung aktiv ist. Dabei benötigt Apple Intelligence eine Menge Speicherplatz, gerade wenn es um Geräte mit kleiner SSD geht. Offiziell belegt die KI auf Macs zwischen acht und 14 Gigabyte.
Einige Nutzer:innen berichten aber, dass auf ihrem Mac teils über 30 Gigabyte durch KI-Funktionen belegter Speicherplatz angezeigt wurde, wie Mac Life schreibt. Wer Apple Intelligence komplett von seinem Mac entfernen und dadurch Speicherplatz freiräumen wollte, war bisher auf komplizierte Umwege angewiesen. Das soll jetzt anders sein.
Remove-Mac-AI: Tool entfernt KI-Funktionen
Denn mit Remove-Mac-AI steht ein Open-Source-Tool bereit, dass Apples KI-Modelle und -Funktionen restlos von der SSD schmeißen soll, wie Caschys Blog berichtet. Darüber hinaus verhindert das Tool auch den erneuten automatischen Download.
Wer sich für die Löschung der lokalen Modelle entscheidet, muss allerdings damit leben können, dass Apple-Intelligence-Funktionen wie die Schreibtools oder die erweiterten Siri-Funktionen damit auch nicht mehr zur Verfügung stehen. Dem Entwickler des Tools zufolge sollen aber grundlegende Systemfunktionen wie die klassische Diktierfunktion weiterhin voll einsatzfähig bleiben.
Änderungen reversibel, Ausnahmen möglich
Die von Remove-Mac-AI vorgenommenen Änderungen sollen zudem auch nach kleineren Updates wirksam bleiben und sich wieder rückgängig machen lassen. Auch ist es möglich, dass man einzelne Bereiche vom Abschalten ausnehmen kann. Das Tool ermöglicht auch eine Art Trockenlauf, über den man sich anzeigen lassen kann, wie sich die Änderungen auswirken.
Das Open-Source-Tool, das über die Kommandozeile bedient wird, steht bei GitHub zum Download bereit. Die ersten Stimmen von Nutzer:innen sind positiv. Dennoch gilt: Nutzung auf eigene Gefahr.

articles.title: Telus, AST SpaceMobile complete first satellite-to-smartphone network test
articles.text:
Canadian telecom giant Telus and satellite manufacturer AST SpaceMobile have completed the first integration between Telus’ wireless network and AST SpaceMobile’s satellite constellation.
The press release says the test marked “significant milestones” in accessing broadband data, making voice calls, and sending texts directly between smartphones and satellites.
According to Telus, the goal is to allow customers to use eligible smartphones beyond the reach of cell towers and help close existing coverage gaps.
Telus notes this coverage will expand access to emergency services and support workers in remote or northern communities.
Interestingly, wireless research platform PlanHub says that when the two companies announced the commercial partnership in March, the pair targeted late 2026 for service; today’s announcement uses a broader timeline, noting that the service is expected to be available to Telus customers within the next year. However, AST SpaceMobile failed a development test in April, so I imagine that pushed the timeline back a bit.
I should also point out that Telus isn’t the only Canadian telecom company that is offering (or planning to offer) satellite-to-mobile service. Rogers launched its satellite-to-mobile service, Rogers Satellite, with Starlink in July, 2025, while Bell will also use AST SpaceMobile for its upcoming satellite-to-mobile service.
Source: Telus, AST SpaceMobile via PlanHub

articles.title: The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Personal AI agents, like Meta’s Muse, Instinct, ChatGPT’s Dots, and others, are kicking off a new wave of consumer AI that involves more than just responding to queries. These AI agents can actually get things done on users’ behalf, like booking flights, making dinner reservations, ordering groceries, and more, all without having to be technical enough to set up OpenClaw or some other agent on your own computer.
But consumers adopting these agents are often running into issues when the website on the other end of their request blocks the AI from completing the job.
Most recently, Amazon began blocking Meta’s Muse AI agent from its retail site, meaning that the agent could no longer browse or make purchases from its product catalog.
However, the problem is not limited to Amazon or Muse. User complaints across social media indicate their agents are often running into similar blocks. Some of these are intentional, like Amazon’s, while others are the result of websites’ traditional anti-bot measures designed to protect against spam and malicious activity.
What’s not clear to the end user is whether or not the block is accidental on the website owner’s part, which leaves them frustrated with both the service provider or retailer and the agent trying to facilitate the transaction.
For instance, TechCrunch has seen a handful of complaints on social media claiming that Muse couldn’t complete a purchase on Walmart’s retail website. (NBC also reported that this was a problem Walmart had faced in its tests of the AI agent.)
But a spokesperson for Walmart told us these weren’t intentional. In fact, Walmart is partnered with Muse, as was announced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September. The company said it wants to be where its customers are, and that now includes being available through AI agent experiences.
The issue that Walmart customers often appear to be running into (see below) is that the website presents a button that has to be clicked to verify the visitor is human. If that experience is interrupted, the check could fail, and the agent gets booted out.
It’s an indication that the current technology we use to verify humans and keep websites safe from spam and bots may not be the best fit for the agent-first era of the web we’re now moving into.
To address this problem, industry partners including Meta, Walmart, Stripe, Sierra, Genesys, Rocket, NiCE, and Decagon have begun working on an open standard that would dictate how AI agents can communicate with businesses, helping to separate the good bots acting on behalf of the user and the bad. This protocol will be specifically focused on agent-to-agent communication for the purposes of online commerce, Meta said in a blog post.
In the meantime, consumer confusion abounds.
Although Walmart is at least trying to be accessible via AI agents, other companies aren’t so keen on the idea or haven’t fully embraced the technology.
For example, flight booking is currently one of the main use cases being positioned for agents, but many people have reported issues with airlines rejecting their agents’ requests.
Delta, for instance, told us that the company is taking steps to protect customers from unauthorized automated activity, and that if it were to open up to AI agents, it would have to be done with “security and the customer experience in mind.”
“While Delta does not currently have a partnership or integration that enables a third-party AI agent to shop for or book Delta flights on a customer’s behalf on our digital platforms, we’re continuing to evaluate how new technology, including external AI agents, could enhance the way customers engage with Delta,” said Delta’s general manager of Global Communications, Heena Chavda, in response to our questions about whether or not it was blocking agents, as some users complained.
United was not quite as direct as Delta, but a spokesperson pointed us to the part of its Terms of Use policy, which says that the user agrees “not to use any robot, spider, other automatic device, or manual process to monitor or copy this website or the content contained therein or for any other unauthorized purpose without United’s prior written permission.” (United didn’t respond to a follow-up question about whether it was blocking specific personal AI agents, like Muse.)
Early adopters’ complaints across social media have referenced a number of brands that are reportedly blocking AI agents, including Yelp, eBay, Zillow, Pizza Hut, Adidas, and various airlines. Some believe that the blocking activity seems to have recently increased.
A couple of people even said eBay suspended their accounts because of their use of agentic AI. Another complained that Google kicked out Instinct while it was cleaning up their Gmail inbox for them.
Despite the push to have agents book tables at restaurants and other tedious tasks, Yelp told us that it doesn’t permit non-human traffic on its platform unless the agent has paid to access Yelp’s content and data through its data licensing program. That means agents trying to use its site to get a quote, add a user to a waitlist, or book them a table will likely fail if they don’t have a formal partnership with Yelp.
eBay told TechCrunch that its approach is not to prohibit all third-party shopping agents from completing purchases. Instead, its policies restrict unauthorized agents and actions, like automated scraping and model training.
Adidas, Zillow, and Pizza Hut either didn’t respond or declined to provide a comment by the time of publication.
One major company involved in this space is Cloudflare, which offers sites protection from AI agents that could be training on its data and managing other automated activity. Some suspect that Cloudflare and other content delivery networks (CDNs) like it are currently disrupting Muse traffic. This is attributed to a change to crawler defaults on September 15, which allows site owners to block AI training while allowing other types of bots. Existing sites that were previously set to block AI bots for security reasons were then shifted to block AI agents on any pages that had ads.
However, when we asked if Cloudflare had any insight into what was happening with the blocking of these personal AI agents, like Muse and others, the company said it didn’t have any specific data to share at this time. It pointed us instead to its free public data hub, Cloudflare Radar. The site shows the increase in bot activity (which Cloudflare has also commented on previously), but it doesn’t help differentiate between the good bots and the bad ones.
Cloudflare also has a vested interest in mitigating AI traffic to websites, as it now runs a marketplace where AI bots have to pay for the data they access. It recently began testing a new web browser built specifically for AI agents.
Given the rapidly evolving space, Meta’s decision to form specific brand partnerships for Muse access seems to be the right way to go, as is its decision to focus on new standards. In doing so, it assures its customers that its agent, at least, is welcome at these partners’ sites — so any issues with access would be reportable bugs.
Meta also maintains a list of “connectors” (a.k.a. partners) inside the Muse app, which continues to grow. Many of Meta’s newly announced partners haven’t yet shown up in this list. But given Muse’s rapid expansion, which now includes partnered tools for small businesses, a bigger reorganization of Muse’s connector list is likely soon to be underway.
“Turning away a personal agent means turning away the customer behind it. We’d rather work with businesses to address the underlying concerns than see them lose that customer,” Meta said in its announcement about the newly announced plans to develop a standard. “There is a path that is good for users and good for businesses. It starts with clear norms, gives businesses more predictable control, and evolves toward a more efficient way for agents to work together.”

articles.title: C'est fait, la fusion Paramount et Warner vient d'avoir lieu, Hollywood sous choc
articles.text:
C’est le coup de la décennie dans l’industrie du divertissement. Au terme de douze mois d’un bras de fer impitoyable qui aura vu la diplomatie américaine, l’administration Trump, la justice fédérale et une armée de stars s’écharper, l’empire Skydance a scellé l’absorption de Warner Bros. Discovery pour 81 milliards de dollars en fonds propres (environ 72 milliards d’euros ; 111 milliards de dollars au total avec la dette).
Dès mardi, l’action historique de Warner a disparu des écrans du Nasdaq pour céder sa place à un symbole unique à la Bourse de New York : SKYD (Skydance).
Le nouvel ensemble pèse près de 70 milliards de dollars de chiffre d’affaires annuel, aligne plus de 200 millions d’abonnés en streaming et annonce déjà la fusion prochaine de HBO Max et Paramount+ dans une plateforme unique.
Le hold-up de David Ellison contre Netflix
Pour mesurer l’ampleur du coup, il faut se souvenir qu’au début de l’année 2026, Warner Bros. était à deux doigts de céder ses studios et son activité de streaming à Netflix. C’était sans compter sur David Ellison, le patron de Skydance. Après avoir racheté Paramount l’an passé pour 8 milliards de dollars, le fils du fondateur d’Oracle a rejeté le compromis, lançant une OPA hostile pour rafler la totalité du groupe Warner, y compris son réseau de chaînes d’information comme CNN.
Rachetant les actions Warner à 31 dollars l’unité, Ellison a fini par essouffler la concurrence et forcer Netflix à jeter l’éponge fin février.
La fronde d’Hollywood et les chèques du Golfe
L’opération a pourtant failli capoter sous le poids des polémiques. En avril, une pétition réunissant des milliers de figures de l’industrie, de Denis Villeneuve à Jane Fonda en passant par Mark Ruffalo, dénonçait un projet destructeur d’emplois et toxique pour la diversité culturelle. L’actrice Sally Field avait même profité de la tribune des Emmy Awards pour tancer cette concentration de pouvoir. À l’opposé, des piliers comme Tom Cruise et James Cameron ont publiquement salué la promesse d’Ellison de garantir au moins 30 sorties de films en salles par an avec une fenêtre exclusive de 45 jours.
Le montage financier a encore davantage fait grincer des dents à Washington. Pour boucler l’accord, Skydance a levé 47 milliards de dollars en fonds propres, épaulée par les fonds souverains d’Arabie saoudite, du Qatar et des Émirats arabes unis. Malgré les alertes sur les risques d’ingérence étrangère, dénoncés par l’opposition démocrate, la FCC (le régulateur américain de l’audiovisuel et des télécoms) a tamponné le dossier, estimant que ces capitaux servaient « l’intérêt public ».
CNN sous contrôle et compromis judiciaire
Le volet politique n’était pas moins explosif. Régulièrement ciblée par Donald Trump, la chaîne d’information CNN passe désormais sous la coupe d’une famille notoirement proche de l’exécutif américain. Pour éteindre les poursuites intentées par 12 procureurs généraux d’États démocrates, Skydance a dû accepter la création d’un comité de journalistes censé garantir l’indépendance éditoriale de CNN et CBS News.
Le groupe s’est aussi engagé à injecter 300 millions de dollars (environ 268 millions d’euros) supplémentaires par an dans la production américaine. Un juge fédéral a validé cet accord le 30 septembre. Le groupe a également versé plus de 23 millions de dollars à la Writers Guild of America pour solder leur litige.
À la tête du nouvel empire, David Ellison reste président du conseil d’administration et CEO. Il partage désormais la direction avec l’ancien patron de Mattel, Ynon Kreiz, nommé co-CEO pour piloter les opérations au quotidien et l’intégration des deux groupes.
L’objectif affiché est d’extirper au moins 6 milliards de dollars (environ 5,4 milliards d’euros) de « synergies » d’ici trois ans, un terme pudique pour des réductions de coûts qui laissent présager des suppressions de postes.

articles.title: TikTok veut transformer le fil « Pour toi » en boutique : un clic suffira pour acheter
articles.text:
TikTok veut que vous achetiez sans jamais quitter l’application. Et pour y parvenir, la plateforme chinoise a trouvé la solution idéale : elle lance un assistant alimenté par l’intelligence artificielle (IA), et le paiement en un clic.
L’entreprise a attendu le moment opportun. Son annonce, ce lundi 5 octobre, intervient en amont de l’Advertising Week de New York, un événement marketing incontournable. Si jusqu’alors, les utilisateurs devaient passer par TikTok Shop pour faire du shopping, l’achat va désormais s’intégrer au cœur même de l’application.
Un assistant pour conseiller, un bouton pour acheter
Ainsi, un agent conversationnel, qui agira comme un assistant shopping, sera bientôt disponible sur TikTok. Il sera en mesure de comprendre le contexte de l’échange et retiendra ce que l’utilisateur cherche afin de ne pas avoir à répéter ses critères. Il servira de guide en temps réel, donnant des informations clés sur les caractéristiques du produit, les délais de livraison, le choix de la taille ou encore, la disponibilité en stock.
Cet assistant aidera aussi à finaliser l’achat, le tout dans une seule discussion. Pour l’heure néanmoins, on sait qu’il sera intégré à plusieurs endroits de l’application, mais pas où exactement. La deuxième fonctionnalité, « Buy Direct » (Achetez maintenant), est un outil de paiement intégré qui se déclenche directement depuis le fil Pour toi. Concrètement, il suffira d’un seul clic pour acheter auprès d’une marque sans être renvoyé vers un autre site.
TikTok présente ces deux outils comme les premières briques de son « commerce agentique » : l’IA prend désormais en charge une partie des démarches d’achat à la place des usagers. Dans cette optique, il faut s’attendre à voir davantage de fonctionnalités de ce type à l’avenir.
Une révolution dans l'e-commerce
Cette nouvelle annonce témoigne de la direction prise par toute l’industrie. En mars, Meta a présenté pour Instagram et Facebook un assistant d’achat IA, avec un bouton de paiement en un clic fonctionnant avec Stripe et PayPal. De son côté, Snapchat a intégré des agents IA sponsorisés, tandis qu'Apple teste un assistant dans son application App Store. Plus globalement, la plateforme Shopify a ouvert son checkout aux agents IA dans le navigateur, de quoi mettre en lumière l’essor de cette pratique révolutionnaire pour l’e-commerce malgré des risques inédits.
L’opportunité est très alléchante pour TikTok, puisque l’idée est bien entendu de garder l’utilisateur au sein de son application. Il pourra poser des questions à son assistant plutôt que de se rendre sur un chatbot, par exemple. À noter que pour l’instant, la plateforme n’a précisé ni le calendrier du déploiement ni les pays concernés pour ces nouveautés. Mais il y a fort à parier sur une démocratisation globale une fois que le système sera bien rodé.

articles.title: Es útil proteger con aluminio el pasaporte frente a ciberataques: verdad o mito
articles.text:
En redes sociales circulan videos en los que algunos turistas envuelven el pasaporte con papel de aluminio para evitar ciberataques. La práctica parte de una preocupación concreta: que un delincuente pueda acercar un lector al documento y extraer la información almacenada en su chip sin que el titular lo advierta.
Los pasaportes electrónicos, incluidos los de Alemania, incorporan chips de identificación por radiofrecuencia, conocidos como RFID. Sin embargo, los especialistas consideran que la lectura no autorizada exige una proximidad que vuelve improbable el ataque en las condiciones habituales de un aeropuerto.
Qué datos guarda el chip de un pasaporte electrónico
En los pasaportes alemanes, el chip RFID facilita controles fronterizos rápidos y dificulta la falsificación, de acuerdo con la Oficina Federal de Seguridad de la Información. El sistema permite verificar que la información del documento coincide con la identidad de quien lo presenta ante las autoridades migratorias.
El chip puede almacenar la foto digital, nombre, lugar de nacimiento, sexo, color de ojos, estatura y domicilio. Incluye dos huellas dactilares, que se recogen al tramitar el documento.
El acceso a esos datos no depende solo de captar una señal de radiofrecuencia: los sistemas de control utilizan mecanismos de seguridad para leer la información.
Cuál es la probabilidad de que alguien lea el pasaporte al pasar cerca de su dueño
La hipótesis que difunden los videos consiste en que un delincuente podría captar los datos del pasaporte mientras camina junto a su titular, sin contacto físico.
En la práctica, el alcance de un lector RFID es muy corto. El dispositivo debería estar a una distancia mínima del documento para intentar establecer comunicación con el chip.
La situación se asemeja al uso de tarjetas de pago sin contacto, aunque el pasaporte cuenta con protecciones específicas. Los expertos señalan que el lector tendría que estar prácticamente apoyado sobre el documento.
Por eso, la posibilidad de que una persona extraiga datos al cruzarse con un viajero en una fila o en una sala de embarque se considera extremadamente improbable.
Qué riesgos digitales sí existen en un aeropuerto para los viajeros
Las redes WiFi públicas figuran entre las amenazas más comunes para los viajeros. En aeropuertos, cafeterías y terminales pueden aparecer conexiones con nombres similares a los de establecimientos o aerolíneas. Algunas carecen de cifrado o fueron creadas por atacantes para interceptar información de quienes se conectan.
Según PowerDMARC, esos espacios pueden facilitar el robo de cookies de sesión o el secuestro de accesos a sitios web. Con esos datos, un delincuente podría ingresar en una cuenta ya abierta sin conocer la contraseña.
Por este motivo, conviene evitar operaciones bancarias, compras o gestiones sensibles desde redes públicas y utilizar datos o una red privada virtual cuando sea necesario.
Cómo operan el phishing en aeropuertos
El phishing puede aprovechar momentos de viaje. Los atacantes envían correos o mensajes que imitan a aerolíneas, hoteles, agencias o servicios de rastreo de equipaje.
Buscan que el pasajero entregue contraseñas, códigos de acceso o datos de tarjetas bajo la excusa de una reserva cancelada, un cambio de puerta o una incidencia con el vuelo.
PowerDMARC sostiene que estas maniobras representan el 33% de los ciberataques contra viajeros. Antes de abrir un enlace, es clave revisar el remitente, ingresar a los servicios desde sus aplicaciones oficiales y no compartir códigos de verificación. Las empresas legítimas no suelen pedir por mensaje una contraseña completa ni datos bancarios.
A qué otros riesgos se exponen los viajeros
El robo o la pérdida del teléfono puede exponer aplicaciones bancarias, correos electrónicos y documentos almacenados en el dispositivo. Un código de bloqueo robusto, la autenticación biométrica y las opciones de localización o borrado remoto reducen el impacto si el dispositivo queda en manos ajenas.
Otro riesgo es el cambio fraudulento de SIM. Mediante engaños a una compañía telefónica, un atacante puede transferir el número de la víctima a otra tarjeta y recibir sus mensajes de autenticación.
Proteger la cuenta del operador con una clave adicional y evitar publicar datos personales que faciliten suplantaciones resulta más útil que envolver un pasaporte en aluminio.

articles.title: Incendie sur le porte-avions Charles-de-Gaulle : ce que l'on sait du feu qui s'est déclaré à Toulon
articles.text:
Alors que le porte-avions de la marine française profite d’un arrêt technique dans son port d’attache de Toulon depuis la fin du mois d’août, un incident est venu perturber le chantier. L’alarme s’est déclenchée en fin de matinée sur le Charles-de-Gaulle, mobilisant rapidement les équipes de marins sur place pour circonscrire le feu avant qu’il ne s’étende.
L’intervention rapide des marins et des secours
Peu avant 11h30, l’alerte retentit dans un local technique de moins de 10 mètres carrés, situé à proximité immédiate du hangar aviation. Ce dernier se trouve totalement vide d’appareils puisque le navire est à quai pour cette période de maintenance programmée jusqu’à la fin de l’année. Face aux flammes, les marins à bord réagissent immédiatement avant de recevoir le renfort des marins-pompiers de la base navale de Toulon.
L’incendie est rapidement maîtrisé à 12h35, puis déclaré entièrement éteint à 13h50. Les équipes d’intervention poursuivent alors leurs investigations sur place, épaulées par le renfort du bataillon des marins-pompiers de Marseille. Aucun blessé n’est à déplorer et la préfecture maritime confirme qu’aucun impact n’est constaté sur les installations nucléaires du bâtiment.
Une enquête en cours pour connaître les origines de l’incendie
D’après les premiers éléments communiqués par la préfecture maritime, le feu serait directement lié à des travaux de découpe au chalumeau menés dans le local technique. Cette hypothèse va cependant demander des vérifications approfondies, les équipes mobilisées continuant d’inspecter la zone pour écarter tout risque de reprise.
À lire : Un traceur Bluetooth à 5 euros a trahi l’escorte secrète du Charles de Gaulle pendant 24 heures
Pour rappel, le Charles-de-Gaulle venait de passer son été en Méditerranée orientale, déployé pour faire face aux menaces d’extension du conflit au Moyen-Orient, avant de regagner son port d’attache fin août. Cet arrêt technique doit durer jusqu’au début du mois de décembre, le bâtiment devant être remplacé à l’horizon 2038 par un nouveau porte-avions baptisé La France Libre.

articles.title: Dell's AI Data Platform gets a knowledge graph for agents and faster Nvidia processing - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dell’s AI Data Platform gets a knowledge graph for agents and faster Nvidia processing
Dell Technologies Inc. today expanded the Dell AI Data Platform with a semantic layer and a knowledge graph intended to give artificial intelligence agents trusted context from a company’s own data.
Dell is also speeding up data processing on Nvidia Corp. graphics chips.
The new features are aimed at enterprise data that was never organized with an AI reader in mind. Much of it predates agents entirely. Dell said agents end up burning tokens on every query to piece together answers that should already exist.
Dell’s first fix is the Unified Semantic Layer, which gives every application the same business definitions and rules to work from, including any ontologies a company already maintains. An agent working across several systems no longer has to guess whether a “client” and an “account” are the same customer.
Alongside it sits the Enterprise Knowledge Graph, which tracks how a company’s data connects. When an agent asks a question, the platform draws on the graph to pull in every related table and vector index the agent is allowed to see, wherever the data lives. In Dell’s example, a manufacturer chasing a fault on a production line can trace one odd sensor reading all the way to the orders now at risk.
Knowledge Agents are built on top of the graph. Each one covers a single topic and works only from its assigned slice of company data. Customers decide what data an agent can see and how much it is allowed to spend. Nvidia’s Nemotron Retriever models handle reasoning and visual understanding for the agents. Because all three components hold some of a company’s most sensitive information, they run inside the customer’s own data center.
Arthur Lewis, president of Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group, said many enterprises have spent years making their data accessible without making it usable. An agent that can find a customer record but has no idea what it means or whether it can be trusted “isn’t intelligent,” he said. “It’s just fast.”
On the processing side, the Dell Data Processing Engine will run on graphics processing units using Nvidia’s cuDF library. Dell’s own September tests on a PowerEdge R770 server with Nvidia RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs found Apache Spark jobs ran 3.9 times faster on average than on central processing units alone. The best result was a 20.4-times speedup on a batch data mining job, and the company noted that the tests used default settings with no tuning. Apache Arrow moves data between Dell storage and the engine so jobs can query it in place.
Dell PowerScale storage will support up to 500 tenants in a single cluster. Each tenant will get more granular role-based access control, and PowerScale will be able to encrypt and authenticate file traffic over the Network File System protocol with mutual Transport Layer Security. Dell is pitching the changes at AI service providers and enterprises running shared platforms.
A new Dell Storage Performance Tool benchmarks S3-compatible object storage across training, inference and checkpointing workloads to help customers size AI infrastructure. Dell is also expanding its implementation services for the platform to move customers from deployment into production.
The Unified Semantic Layer, Enterprise Knowledge Graph and Knowledge Agents are due in the first half of 2027. PowerScale’s multitenancy and security updates arrive in November. The accelerated Data Processing Engine follows in December, and more Apache Arrow acceleration is expected in the first half of next year. Customers can get the Storage Performance Tool and the new services today.
