articles.title: Neutrino physicist wins 2026 Nobel Physics Prize
articles.text:
Francis Halzen, a physicist at the University of Wisconsin, Madison, has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics “for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.” Halzen spearheaded the development and construction of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory in Antarctica, enabling physicists to capture high-energy neutrinos created in the distant universe.
“It was a great surprise, and I obviously didn’t expect it,” Halzen said during a news conference in Stockholm, Sweden, speaking by phone from Italy. While the Nobel was awarded to Halzen, he emphasized that his work was the result of a “large collaboration” with other researchers.
“This reflects on the really courageous people who joined me in this project when really no respectable conservative physicist would have joined me. But many talented people did, and that’s why I’m here,” he said.
“I am shocked and absolutely delighted that Francis was awarded the Nobel this year,” said particle physicist Danielle Norcini of Johns Hopkins University in a statement. “He is the scientific visionary and driving force behind [IceCube]. It has transformed our understanding of the universe by detecting the first high-energy neutrinos from beyond our galaxy, opening an entirely new field of neutrino astronomy. The experiment is the extraordinary achievement of hundreds of scientists, engineers, and collaborators, but Francis was the person who dreamed big enough to imagine an experiment of this scale and then relentlessly pushed to make it a reality.”
Ghost particles
As previously reported, neutrinos travel near the speed of light. John Updike’s 1960 poem, “Cosmic Gall,” pays tribute to the two most defining features of neutrinos: They have no charge, and for decades, physicists believed they had no mass (they actually have a teeny bit of mass). Neutrinos are the most abundant subatomic particle in the universe, but they very rarely interact with any type of matter. We are constantly being bombarded every second by millions of these tiny particles, yet they pass right through us without our even noticing. That’s why Isaac Asimov dubbed them “ghost particles.”
That low rate of interaction makes neutrinos extremely difficult to detect, but because they are so light, they can escape unimpeded (and thus largely unchanged) by collisions with other particles of matter. This means they can provide valuable clues to astronomers about distant systems, further augmented by what can be learned with telescopes across the electromagnetic spectrum, as well as gravitational waves. Together, these different sources of information have been dubbed “multimessenger” astronomy.
Neutrinos were first proposed by Wolfgang Pauli in a 1930 letter to colleagues. He was trying to explain some baffling experimental results on radioactive beta decay in atomic nuclei, where energy appeared to be missing—something he deemed (correctly) to be impossible. He thought a new kind of subatomic particle with no charge and no mass may have carried away the missing energy; it was Enrico Fermi who later dubbed it a neutrino.
Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines first observed these ghostly particles in 1956, thanks to fusion reactions in nuclear power plants that proliferated after World War II. Ten years later, physicists detected the first solar neutrinos. This snagged Ray Davis Jr. and Masatoshi Koshiba a Nobel Prize in 2002, shared with Riccardo Giacconi (who was honored “for pioneering contributions to astrophysics, which have led to the discovery of cosmic X-ray sources”).

articles.title: India's JioHotstar takes partnership route for Middle East expansion | TechCrunch
articles.text:
JioHotstar, the streaming platform with more than 500 million monthly active users backed by Indian conglomerate Reliance Industries, is expanding into the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) through Starzplay, one of the region’s largest streaming services. The new overseas push comes after its debut in the U.K., Canada, and Singapore.
Under the partnership announced Tuesday, JioHotstar will have a dedicated section in Starzplay’s app and on its website, offering Indian films, TV shows, originals, and reality franchises across multiple languages. This is different from JioHotstar’s September launch in the U.K., Canada, and Singapore, where it replaced Hotstar and debuted as a stand-alone streaming service.
The expansion is part of Reliance’s push to build JioHotstar into a global streaming platform after establishing a massive audience in India. MENA has one of the world’s largest South Asian diaspora communities, giving JioHotstar a sizable potential audience for its Indian films, television shows, and original programming.
As with its earlier debut in the U.K., Canada, and Singapore, JioHotstar’s own sports offering in India will not be available in MENA. However, a plan bundling JioHotstar with Starzplay’s sports offering, including cricket, is priced at AED 49.99 (about $13.60) a month. JioHotstar is also available through Starzplay’s Plus monthly plan at AED 34.99 (around $9.50).
With MENA’s large Indian diaspora in focus, new JioHotstar originals will premiere in the region simultaneously with their release in India, with audio available in up to 10 languages. The catalog spans Hindi, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, and Bangla, among other languages, and includes shows such as “Bigg Boss” and “Koffee with Karan.” Additionally, JioHotstar is putting particular emphasis on Malayalam programming, given the large Malayali population in the region.
JioHotstar was created after Reliance and Disney merged their Indian media businesses into an $8.5 billion joint venture in 2024. The service, which combined JioCinema and Disney+ Hotstar, launched in India in February last year.
Before JioHotstar’s launch, Hotstar was available in MENA. Disney Star expanded its distribution deal with evision, e&’s media and entertainment arm, in 2024, making it the regional home of Hotstar Specials. Evision is also a major shareholder in Starzplay, where JioHotstar will now have its first dedicated streaming presence in the region.
Starzplay counts more than 2.3 million subscribers and has built a sizable South Asian audience in part through its cricket offering.
Financial terms of the partnership were not disclosed. Starzplay CEO Maaz Sheikh described bringing JioHotstar to the platform as a “strategic investment.”

articles.title: Xbox prepara algo más grande que una consola y ofrece más detalles de Project Helix
articles.text:
Xbox ha revelado más detalles sobre su consola de próxima generación. Aunque la compañía ya había definido que Project Helix sería el siguiente paso, la información se ha liberado a cuentagotas y solo sabemos que se tratará de un equipo con capacidades de PC. Hoy se sabe que la compañía no solo piensa en una consola, sino en una familia de dispositivos que intentará cubrir todos los frentes.
En una reunión con empleados, la jefa de Xbox, Asha Sharma, dijo que Project Helix llegará como una familia de dispositivos. De acuerdo con Windows Central, la directora ejecutiva señaló que primero se lanzará una gran consola, seguida de opciones para aquellos que prefieren jugar en las portátiles:
“Nos estamos moviendo a una familia de dispositivos para la Gen 10”, dijo Sharma. “Hay cosas que somos los mejores del mundo para fabricar, y hay otras en las que colaboraremos. Así que iremos compartiendo más detalles sobre ello a medida que avancemos nuestros planes”. La responsable de Xbox añadió que el sistema operativo comienza a verse bien y que el equipo está muy ilusionado con eso.
Hasta ahora se sabe que Project Helix será capaz de ejecutar juegos de PC y usará un chip AMD con soporte para tecnologías como ray tracing y path tracing. La nueva consola también implementará la versión más reciente de FSR, el escalado inteligente de AMD que podría debutar con generación de fotogramas. En este campo, Sony está tomando la delantera con PSSR y QSSR, los sistemas de escalado que se implementaron en la PS5 Pro y la PS5 base, respectivamente.
Al contar con soporte para juegos de PC, es un hecho que Asha Sharma y su equipo implementarán una versión de Windows enfocada completamente al gaming. Xbox ha intentado emular a SteamOS en los últimos meses, pero todavía no lo consigue.
Xbox Game Pass fue una estrategia fallida, pero no desaparecerá
Asha Sharma mencionó que la estrategia anterior de Game Pass llevó a Xbox a una crisis de la que ya se están recuperando. “"Estamos tomando las decisiones correctas para reinvertir en el negocio, tras un mínimo histórico, hemos empezado a volver a crecer, más de 2 o 3 veces lo que éramos, y esperamos que eso continúe“, señaló.
Tras los cambios de este año, la compañía planea hacer que el servicio de suscripción se vuelva más flexible para los jugadores. Hace unos meses se rumoreó que Xbox ofrecería suscripciones de Game Pass "a la carta", en las que cada usuario podría elegir el tipo de contenido al que quiere acceder. Esto beneficiaría a un número importante de suscriptores de Ultimate, quienes han expresado que no les interesa Fortnite o los juegos viejos de Ubisoft y EA.
Pese a que ya se habla de la próxima generación, Xbox no quiere olvidarse de la Series X y S. Asha Sharma dijo que fortalecer la generación actual es clave y añadió que Xbox no tiene el derecho de crecer más allá de la consola si no puede servir a sus jugadores más valiosos de forma adecuada. Para ganárselos, la compañía ha implementado iniciativas como el programa de digitalización, que otorga una licencia digital a quienes tienen un disco en formato físico.
“Existimos para estar donde juega el mundo, sabremos cuando tengamos mil millones de personas activas a diario, y tenemos derecho a ganar porque ahora estamos centrados en nuestros aficionados y franquicias”, mencionó Sharma.
La fecha de llegada de Project Helix todavía está en el aire. La crisis de memoria obligó a la compañía a replantear la estrategia para que la consola sea asequible y flexible.

articles.title: NVM Ventures launches with €23.6 million fund targeting dual-use companies | EU-Startups
articles.text:
NVM Ventures has officially launched with the announcement of a €23.6 million first close for the NVM Venture Lazio compartment. The compartment aims to build a portfolio of 10–15 dual-use companies at pre-Seed and Seed stage working in STEP Technologies.
The fund was established on the initiative of Andrea Bonabello and Niccolò Bienati, founding partners and Board Members of Ulixes Capital Lux, who lead its strategic direction. They are joined by the Fund Managers Giorgio Gulienetti and Alessandro Casiraghi, who serve as key persons for the NVM Venture Lazio compartment.
“Institutional investors are rediscovering emerging managers. According to the IPEM Allocation and Fundraising Trend Report 2027, 88% of Limited Partners are now interested in managers raising their first, second or third fund, up from 65% the year before, and 64% are willing to commit to a Fund I.
“This interest is also driven by strong results: research conducted in the United States by the National Association of Investment Companies found that emerging manager programmes outperformed by 700 basis points. NVM Ventures was created to meet this demand in Italy, with the goal of fostering a new generation of capable, ambitious managers who currently struggle to raise their first fund.” says Andrea Bonabello, founding partner and Board Member of Ulixes Capital Lux, General Partner of NVM Ventures.
Key investors include Lazio Innova, which committed €18.83 million through Lazio Venture 2, the Lazio Region’s fund of funds co-financed by the ERDF Regional Programme 2021–2027, under which the new compartment was selected.
This launch comes amid increased investment into European defence, dual-use and strategic DeepTech.
EU-Startups has tracked approximately €1.73 billion across ten relevant defence and dual-use company financings in 2026, spanning autonomous systems, space, cybersecurity, drone defence and advanced materials.
Italy has been part of this activity: Puglia-based Mirai Robotics raised €3.6 million for dual-use maritime autonomy, Turin-based ORiS secured €5 million for space and dual-use wireless power technology, while Rome-based Physical AI cybersecurity company Exein raised €234 million while reaching unicorn status.
Lazio Innova has also already backed another specialist vehicle this year, committing €16 million to the €20 million Eureka! Fund II – Deep Tech Lazio, which similarly targets early-stage STEP and DeepTech companies.
“With NVM Venture Lazio, we are further expanding the specialist expertise in dual-use frontier technologies within the regional venture capital platform. Investing in a first-time fund also reflects our commitment to backing emerging managers with distinctive skills, helping build new professional and investment capabilities for the benefit of the entire ecosystem.” adds Andrea Ciampalini, Director General of Lazio Innova.
NVM Venture Lazio invests in DeepTech startups with dual-use applications. Its core sectors include aerospace, maritime, robotics and autonomous systems, cybersecurity, AI for defence, energy infrastructure, new materials, advanced manufacturing and biotechnology.
The multi-compartment structure allows NVM Ventures to pair each investment thesis with a specialist investment team, while giving emerging fund managers a shared institutional framework for governance, risk management and compliance
The fund says Lazio is the only Italian region that hosts the entire aerospace value chain, from research to manufacturing to services. According to Lazio Region data, more than 300 companies with around 23,000 employees operate in advanced technologies across the region, generating annual revenues of over €5 billion, including €1.6 billion in exports.
This concentration of research, talent, industry and institutions creates a real opportunity to turn technologies born in labs and research programmes into companies capable of scaling very quickly.
NVM Venture Lazio steps in at the most delicate stage for a DeepTech startup: the move from technology validation to product development, and from first customer to industrialisation.

articles.title: No tener el celular actualizado hará que WhatsApp bloquee el acceso a la cuenta
articles.text:
Lo particular de la medida es que no requiere instalar una nueva versión de la aplicación. Se trata de un cambio aplicado desde los servidores de la compañía, por lo que puede activarse sin previo aviso en las cuentas afectadas.
Cómo funciona el nuevo bloqueo en WhatsApp
Cuando el sistema detecta que el teléfono necesita una actualización, aparece un aviso que explica al usuario que debe actualizar el software antes de continuar. La pantalla indica que hay que ingresar a los ajustes del dispositivo y verificar si existe una actualización disponible.
Una vez instalado el nuevo software, el usuario puede volver a abrir WhatsApp y completar el inicio de sesión con normalidad. El aviso también muestra instrucciones para comprobar qué versión del sistema operativo tiene instalada, pensadas para quienes no saben si su equipo está actualizado.
No existe forma de omitir este paso. Si el dispositivo queda dentro de los afectados, actualizar el sistema operativo se vuelve obligatorio para acceder a la cuenta.
WhatsApp no detalló públicamente qué versiones concretas de Android o iOS provocan el bloqueo. El despliegue llega de forma progresiva a determinadas cuentas, lo que significa que no todos los usuarios con un sistema antiguo ven el aviso por ahora.
Por qué WhatsApp exige actualizar el sistema operativo
Un teléfono sin actualizaciones durante años puede conservar vulnerabilidades conocidas que facilitan la instalación de malware. Los atacantes buscan activamente esas fallas en sistemas operativos desactualizados para infiltrarse en los dispositivos.
Un sistema operativo desactualizado facilita que un atacante explote vulnerabilidades conocidas e instale malware capaz de interceptar la información antes de que la aplicación la cifre, lo que deja expuestas las conversaciones pese a cualquier protección adicional que ofrezca WhatsApp.
Una vez que el malware infecta el equipo, puede interceptar los datos antes de que la aplicación los cifre. El cifrado de extremo a extremo protege los mensajes, pero no puede blindar un contenido que el atacante ya capturó directamente en el dispositivo.
Esto implica que un sistema operativo obsoleto no solo expone a WhatsApp: vuelve vulnerable a cualquier aplicación instalada en el teléfono. Por eso, la compañía decidió hacer explícita esa dependencia y condicionar el acceso a que el equipo cumpla con un estándar mínimo de seguridad.
Este bloqueo no implica que WhatsApp haya identificado una vulnerabilidad crítica en su propia aplicación. El origen del problema está en la seguridad del sistema operativo, de la cual depende cualquier software que funcione sobre él.
El antecedente de los clientes falsos en Italia
La medida llega después de un incidente registrado en Italia, donde WhatsApp notificó a cerca de 200 usuarios cuyos dispositivos fueron comprometidos a través de una versión falsa de la aplicación. Ese episodio impulsó a la compañía a reforzar de manera activa el acceso a las cuentas.
En paralelo, WhatsApp está probando una alerta dirigida a usuarios que conectan su cuenta mediante clientes no oficiales de WhatsApp Web. Ese aviso aparece en la pantalla de dispositivos vinculados y pide a los usuarios que regresen al cliente oficial de la aplicación.
Cómo afecta esto a los usuarios
Para los usuarios, la consecuencia directa es que mantener el sistema operativo actualizado dejó de ser una recomendación y se convirtió en un requisito para poder usar WhatsApp. Quienes todavía no vieron la pantalla de bloqueo podrían encontrarse con ella en el futuro, si el software de su dispositivo queda por debajo del mínimo que exige la compañía.
El despliegue continúa de forma gradual en cuentas de Android y iOS, sin que WhatsApp haya precisado un cronograma determinado ni los sistemas operativos específicos que activan la restricción.

articles.title: Samsung 9100 Pro SSDs slashed up to 41% while supplies last — huge price cuts hit all capacities from 1TB to 8TB
articles.text:
Samsung 9100 Pro SSDs slashed up to 41% while supplies last — huge price cuts hit all capacities from 1TB to 8TB
Amazon Big Deals is in full swing with big discounts on a wide range of products. Given the current SSD market, any storage deal is worth considering. If constant price hikes have kept you from upgrading your storage, now may be a good time to check out Samsung's 9100 Pro lineup. For a limited time, and while supplies last, Amazon has slashed the price of the Samsung 9100 Pro 1TB, 2TB, 4TB, or massive 8TB drives.
Crucially, some of these Gen 5 drives are now actually cheaper than the Gen 4 990 Pro from Samsung, or priced so similarly that they're a no-brainer.
- Check out the Samsung 9100 Pro 1TB deal on Amazon
- Check out the Samsung 9100 Pro 2TB deal on Amazon
- Check out the Samsung 9100 Pro 4TB deal on Amazon
- Check out the Samsung 9100 Pro 8TB deal on Amazon
The Samsung 9100 Pro, one of the best SSDs, features Samsung's homegrown Presto controller and 236-layer V8 NAND, delivering maximum sequential read and write speeds of up to 14,800 MB/s and 13,400 MB/s, respectively. Speeds vary slightly by capacity. Still, at that level of performance, the Samsung 9100 Pro can handle everything from daily tasks to more specialized, intensive workloads without hiccups.
In today’s landscape with rapidly rising SSD prices, choosing a drive based solely on performance is no longer sufficient. The warranty matters just as much, and the Samsung 9100 Pro offers coverage that protects your investment. The PCIe 5.0 drive comes with a five-year limited warranty and very generous endurance ratings across the board. For example, the 2TB is rated for 1,200 TBW — for perspective, you could write one-third of the drive’s total capacity every day for the next five years and still be covered by the warranty.
The Samsung 9100 Pro is a high-end PCIe 5.0 SSD featuring Samsung's own Presto controller and 236-layer NAND. The 1 TB model delivers sequential read and write speeds up to 14,700 MB/s and 13,300 MB/s, respectively.
The Samsung 9100 Pro is a high-end PCIe 5.0 SSD featuring Samsung's own Presto controller and 236-layer NAND. The 2 TB model delivers sequential read and write speeds up to 14,700 MB/s and 13,400 MB/s, respectively.
The Samsung 9100 Pro is a high-end PCIe 5.0 SSD featuring Samsung's own Presto controller and 236-layer NAND. The 4TB model delivers sequential read and write speeds up to 14,800 MB/s and 13,400 MB/s, respectively.
The Samsung 9100 Pro is a high-end PCIe 5.0 SSD featuring Samsung's own Presto controller and 236-layer NAND. The 8TB model delivers sequential read and write speeds up to 14,800 MB/s and 13,400 MB/s, respectively.
The Samsung 9100 Pro is one of the top-performing drives in the PCIe 5.0 category. If you are coming from a PCIe 4.0 SSD or from the Samsung 990 Pro, its predecessor, the improvement is night and day. The Samsung 9100 Pro may not look as fast on paper because rivals have higher rated speeds. However, the Samsung 9100 Pro delivers strong real-world performance matched with good efficiency.

At $0.199 per GB, the 2TB model provides the best value. Doubling the capacity from 1TB to 2TB raises the overall cost by roughly 60%, which still makes it an attractive option for many users. Upgrading to 4TB and 8TB raises the cost per GB to $0.28 and $0.287, respectively. The jump from 2TB to 4TB results in a 2.81 times price increase for double the capacity. In contrast, the price difference between 4TB and 8TB is nearly proportional, at a 2.05 times increase for double the capacity.
If you require 4TB of storage, purchasing two 2TB drives saves you $323 compared to a single 4TB drive. Similarly, buying four 2TB drives saves you $707 versus an 8TB drive. So, if you have the luxury of extra unused M.2 slots, smaller 2TB drives can save you a lot.

articles.title: Voitures électriques à moins de 25 000 € : les ventes vont être multipliées par sept en 2026
articles.text:
Le bonheur des uns fait le malheur des autres. L’ONG basée à Bruxelles Transport & Environment (T&E) a publié ce lundi 5 octobre 2026 son dernier bilan sur la voiture électrique en Europe. L’organisme y estime que les ventes de modèles électriques affichés à moins de 25 000 euros seront sept fois plus élevées en 2026 qu’en 2024. Alors que les prix des carburants s’envolent bien au-delà des 2€/litre, la voiture électrique arrive enfin au niveau du prix d’une citadine thermique.
Cela se ressent sur les immatriculations. D’après l’Association des constructeurs européens d’automobiles (ACEA), 1,64 million de voitures 100 % électriques ont été immatriculées dans l’UE entre janvier et août 2026, soit 45 % de plus que sur la même période de 2025. Elles pèsent désormais 21,7 % du marché, contre 15,8 % un an plus tôt, et devancent d’environ 6 600 unités les voitures à essence pure.
Et la courbe ne fléchit pas. Après le cap d’une voiture neuve sur quatre franchi en juillet, la part de l’électrique a encore grimpé en août. La France a atteint 38 % ce mois-là, selon T&E, et les chiffres de septembre ont confirmé la bascule du marché français.
Le choc pétrolier, accélérateur inattendu
En France, le litre de gazole a pris 50 centimes entre le 27 février et le 31 mars 2026, a calculé franceinfo. C’est presque deux fois plus que la hausse du SP95-E10 sur la même période.
Avec les sanctions contre la Russie qui ont suivi l’invasion de l’Ukraine, le Moyen-Orient est devenu le premier fournisseur de gazole raffiné de l’Europe. La guerre dans la région touche donc directement ce carburant, le plus consommé en France.
À l’échelle de l’Union européenne, T&E chiffre la hausse du diesel à 38 % depuis le début du conflit. Ainsi, un plein de 50 litres coûte 30 euros de plus qu’avant la guerre. Au total, le choc pétrolier a déjà coûté 53 milliards d’euros aux automobilistes européens, dont 40 milliards pour le seul gazole.
En face, une voiture électrique rechargée à domicile coûte deux fois moins cher à l’usage qu’une thermique, d’après les calculs de l’ONG. Un conducteur étant passé à l’électrique au début de la crise aurait déjà économisé environ 350 euros à la mi-septembre.
Des électriques à moins de 25 000 euros qui font mouche
La crise n’aurait pas eu le même effet sans voitures abordables à vendre. Pendant des années, la voiture électrique à 20 000 euros est restée une promesse. Au premier semestre 2026, près de 40 nouveaux modèles électriques sont arrivés sur le marché européen, et T&E en imagine une soixantaine sur l’année. Entre 2021 et 2025, la moyenne tournait plutôt autour de 15 par an.
Les modèles d’entrée de gamme se sont multipliés plus vite que les autres. D’ici fin 2026, 16 modèles électriques seront proposés sous les 25 000 €, le double par rapport à 2025, dont quatre sous les 20 000 €. Toutefois, le thermique garde encore une large avance sur le segment d’entrée de gamme. Entre 20 000 et 25 000 €, les modèles essence ou diesel sont aujourd’hui 4,4 fois plus nombreux que les électriques.
Mais au fur à mesure que les mois passent, les prix d’accès des électriques diminuent également. Dacia Hipster ou encore Citroën 2CV électrique, les voitures électriques à moins de 15 000 € ne seront bientôt plus des mirages non plus. Sous les 20 000 €, l’ONG estime qu’il y aura une dizaine de modèles électriques en 2028, contre 20 thermiques déjà disponibles.
Au-delà de la réalité économique pour le portefeuille des automobilistes à la pompe, pourquoi cet essor maintenant ? Transport et Environnement y voit l’effet des objectifs européens de CO2. La réglementation impose que chaque constructeur doive respecter une moyenne d’émissions sur l’ensemble des voitures neuves qu’il vend sous peine d’amende, la fameuse norme CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy). Entre 2021 et 2024, ce plafond n’a pas bougé, et les marques avaient peu de raisons de lancer des modèles bon marché.
Le nouvel objectif, calculé en moyenne sur 2025-2027, les oblige cette fois à vendre davantage d’électriques, donc à en proposer de moins chères. Selon l’ONG, à mi-parcours, les constructeurs ont déjà comblé 75 % de l’écart qui les séparait de la cible, tandis que les ventes de modèles dont le prix de départ est inférieur à 25 000 € devraient être sept fois plus élevées en 2026 qu’en 2024.
Volkswagen est l’exemple type avec sa nouvelle ID. Polo vendue à partir de 24 995 €. Le constructeur allemand fait un véritable carton avec sa citadine à tel point que les délais de livraison s’allongent jusqu’à 10 mois. Pour Lucien Mathieu, directeur de la thématique automobile chez T&E, les constructeurs qui se plaignaient du manque d’appétit des clients avaient tout faux : « Le problème n’était pas la demande, mais ce qu’ils avaient à offrir. »
Bruxelles peut-elle casser l’élan ?
Le rapport de T&E est aussi un plaidoyer contre les assouplissements des objectifs CO2 pour 2030 et 2035, dont le vote est prévu cet automne. Selon les projections de T&E, ce revirement stratégique ferait plafonner la part de l’électrique à 22 % des ventes en 2030, contre 47 % avec la proposition de la Commission. Les ventes de modèles sous 25 000 euros chuteraient de près des trois quarts.

articles.title: Prime Day : Amazon brade 15 de ses appareils jusqu’à -69%, du Kindle Colorsoft aux caméras Blink et Ring
articles.text:
Liseuses Kindle, lecteurs Fire TV, caméras Blink et sonnettes Ring : Amazon profite de ses Jours Flash Prime pour baisser le prix de ses propres appareils. Sur la sécurité de la maison, le prix d’achat ne dit pas tout, et nous détaillons aussi ce que coûte l’abonnement.
Les Jours Flash Prime se tiennent le mardi 6 et le mercredi 7 octobre, mais Amazon a commencé à baisser ses propres gammes avant l’événement. Particularité de cette sélection : sur les 16 offres retenues, une seule est réservée aux membres Prime, le support Blink à projecteurs. Treize d’entre elles restent valables jusqu’au lundi 12 octobre à 23 h 59, selon les dates affichées au moment de notre sélection.
La sélection réunit douze produits Ring et Blink, deux liseuses Kindle et deux lecteurs Fire TV. Plusieurs offres sont des packs : vérifiez le nombre de caméras indiqué sur chaque ligne. Les remises sont calculées à partir du prix le plus bas que nous avons relevé sur les 30 jours précédents.
Tous les appareils Amazon en promotion
Pour profiter du Prime Day, n’oubliez pas de devenir membre Amazon Prime. Vous bénéficiez d’un essai gratuit de 30 jours, c’est donc le bon moment pour tester.
- Liseuse Amazon Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition 32 Go à 199,99 € au lieu de 299,99 €
- Liseuse Amazon Kindle Scribe 64 Go avec stylet premium à 259,99 € au lieu de 479,99 €
- Pack 4 caméras Blink Outdoor 4 et sonnette vidéo 2K+ à 84,99 € au lieu de 274,99 €
- Pack 4 caméras extérieures Blink 2K+ et sonnette vidéo 2K+ à 107,99 € au lieu de 309,99 €
- Support Blink avec projecteurs Arc et 2 caméras Mini 2K+ (réservé aux membres Prime) à 59,99 € au lieu de 149,99 €
- Caméra Ring Spotlight Cam Plus sans fil à 69,99 € au lieu de 149,99 €
- Sonnette vidéo Ring Battery Video Doorbell Pro 4K à 149,99 € au lieu de 249,99 €
- Caméra extérieure avec projecteur Blink (nouvelle génération) à 37,99 € au lieu de 94,99 €
- Interphone connecté Ring Intercom Video (nouvelle génération) à 48,99 € au lieu de 99,99 €
- Sonnette vidéo sans fil Ring et caméra intérieure Ring à 49,99 € au lieu de 99,99 €
- Caméra extérieure Ring Stick Up Cam sans fil et caméra intérieure Ring à 34,99 € au lieu de 79,99 €
- Lot de 2 caméras Blink Mini 2K+ à 34,99 € au lieu de 79,99 €
- Sonnette vidéo filaire Ring Video Doorbell Wired (nouvelle génération) à 39,99 € au lieu de 79,99 €
- Amazon Fire TV Cube à 109,99 € au lieu de 159,98 €
- Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus à 37,99 € au lieu de 69,99 €
- Caméra intérieure Ring Indoor Cam (2e génération) à 24,99 € au lieu de 49,99 €
Six offres passées au crible
Sur ces appareils, le prix affiché n’est qu’une partie du coût. Les caméras et sonnettes Ring et Blink ont besoin d’un abonnement pour conserver les vidéos, quand les Kindle et les Fire TV s’appuient sur les services d’Amazon. Voici ce qu’il faut savoir sur six offres de la liste.
- Pack Blink Outdoor 4 à 84,99 € : quatre caméras extérieures, une sonnette vidéo et le module de synchronisation, pour 69 % de moins que le prix de référence. La Blink Outdoor 4 filme en 1080p avec un angle de 143 degrés et tient jusqu’à deux ans sur deux piles AA, selon Blink. Sans abonnement, vous recevez les alertes de mouvement et la vue en direct, mais rien n’est enregistré : comptez 3 € par mois et par appareil avec Blink Basic, ou 10 € par mois pour tous vos appareils avec Blink Plus.
- Lot de 2 Blink Mini 2K+ à 34,99 € : soit 17,50 € la caméra, moins que les 19,99 € de l’offre à l’unité que nous avons relayée le 5 octobre. Cette petite caméra d’intérieur filme en 2 560 x 1 440 pixels. Sans abonnement, les vidéos ne sont pas sauvegardées dans le cloud, mais un Sync Module 2 associé à une clé USB permet de les stocker localement.
- Ring Battery Video Doorbell Pro à 149,99 € : c’est la seule sonnette 4K de la sélection, avec un zoom jusqu’à 10x selon Ring. Alimentée par batterie, elle se passe de câblage. Comme les autres produits Ring, elle dépend de l’abonnement Ring pour conserver l’historique des vidéos ; la fiche mentionne un essai gratuit de 30 jours.
- Ring Intercom Video à 48,99 € : il s’adresse aux habitants d’immeuble. Branché sur l’interphone existant, il permet de voir qui sonne, de parler au visiteur et d’ouvrir la porte du hall depuis le smartphone, y compris avec des clés virtuelles pour les proches. Vérifiez la compatibilité de votre interphone avant d’acheter.
- Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition à 199,99 € : c’est la liseuse couleur d’Amazon, avec recharge sans fil, certification IPX8 et éclairage à réglage automatique. Notre test lui a attribué 6/10 : rendu des couleurs réussi et rémanence quasi absente, mais un écran de 7 pouces trop petit pour la BD et un prix élevé face à la concurrence. Elle revient ici au prix que nous avions déjà relevé à la rentrée.
- Fire TV Cube à 109,99 € : dans notre test du Fire TV Cube, nous lui avions attribué 8/10 pour sa connectique complète, avec port Ethernet et entrée HDMI, son Wi-Fi 6E et sa commande vocale Alexa. Nous le réservions toutefois aux installations home cinéma. Pour un usage courant, notre test orientait vers un Fire TV Stick 4K, bien moins cher : le modèle 4K Plus de la sélection est à 37,99 €.
Ring ou Blink : lequel choisir ?
Les deux marques appartiennent à Amazon et fonctionnent avec Alexa, mais elles ne visent pas tout à fait le même usage. Blink mise sur des caméras sur piles et un module de synchronisation qui relaie le Wi-Fi : ses packs offrent ici le plus de caméras pour le prix, jusqu’à quatre caméras et une sonnette pour 84,99 €. Ring propose des sonnettes plus complètes, jusqu’à la 4K, et un interphone connecté pensé pour les immeubles.
Dans les deux cas, l’abonnement fait partie du budget, puisque sans lui les vidéos ne sont pas conservées dans le cloud. Si vous voulez éviter tout frais mensuel, des caméras à carte microSD existent chez d’autres marques, et notre comparatif des meilleures caméras de surveillance distingue les modèles qui fonctionnent sans abonnement.
Appareils Amazon et Jours Flash Prime : vos questions
Faut-il être membre Prime pour profiter de ces offres ?
Non, sauf pour le support Blink avec projecteurs Arc, réservé aux membres Prime. Les 15 autres offres de la sélection s’affichent au même prix pour tous les clients.
Les caméras Blink et Ring fonctionnent-elles sans abonnement ?
Oui, mais de façon limitée, car les vidéos ne sont alors pas enregistrées dans le cloud. Chez Blink, vous gardez les alertes de mouvement et la vue en direct, et un Sync Module 2 avec une clé USB permet un stockage local ; chez Ring, l’abonnement est quasi indispensable pour conserver l’historique.
Jusqu’à quand durent ces promotions ?
Les deux Kindle et le support Blink sont remisés jusqu’au mercredi 7 octobre à 23 h 59. Les treize autres offres courent jusqu’au lundi 12 octobre à 23 h 59, selon les dates affichées sur les fiches au moment de notre sélection.
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Comment profiter des Jours Flash Prime Amazon ?
Afin de profiter du Prime Day d’automne d’Amazon, vous devez avant tout souscrire à un abonnement Amazon Prime. Pour ça, rien de plus simple, il vous suffit de créer un compte Amazon puis de souscrire à l’une des offres Amazon Prime :
- Amazon Prime à 69 € par an
- Amazon Prime à 6,99 €/mois
- Amazon Prime Student 3,49 €/mois (pour les étudiants et les 18-22 ans)
Si vous n’avez jamais été abonné, Amazon vous permet de bénéficier d’un essai gratuit de 30 jours au service Amazon Prime.

articles.title: Prime Deal Days: Amazon lockt mit Surface-Geräten von Microsoft – aber lohnen sich die Angebote wirklich?
articles.text:
Microsoft Surface bei Amazon: Welche Rabatte zu den Prime Deal Days halten, was sie versprechen
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Zu den Prime Deal Days bietet Amazon zahlreiche Angebote aus Bereichen wie Elektronik, Haushalt und Mode. Laut dem Einzelhandelsriesen sind auch einige Surface-Geräte von Microsoft während der zweitägigen Rabattaktion um mehr als 40 Prozent reduziert. Doch wie gut sind die Angebote wirklich? Der Preisvergleich zeigt, wie viel Prime-Mitglieder tatsächlich sparen.
Bei diesem Surface-Tablet sparst du 600 Euro
Beim Microsoft Surface Pro handelt es sich um ein Zwei-in-eins-Tablet mit abnehmbarer Tastatur. Je nach Bedarf gibt es Modelle in verschiedenen Größen sowie mit unterschiedlicher Leistung. Das 12-Zoll-Modell ist die kompaktere und günstigere Variante für Streaming, Recherche und mobiles Arbeiten. Der Akku soll bis zu 16 Stunden durchhalten. Bei Amazon ist es mit dem Prozessor Snapdragon X Plus, 8 Gigabyte RAM und 256 Gigabyte Speicher ab 629 Euro erhältlich. Die unverbindliche Preisempfehlung liegt bei 949 Euro, Amazon gibt daher 34 Prozent Rabatt an. Beim Hersteller kostet das Modell aber nur 699 Euro, der tatsächliche Rabatt fällt also deutlich kleiner aus. Trotzdem lohnt sich der Kauf, denn laut Vergleichsportalen ist das der günstigste Preis seit Einführung.
Das größere Surface Pro mit 13-Zoll-Bildschirm und Snapdragon-X2-Elite-Prozessor lohnt sich für alle, die sich für anspruchsvolle Aufgaben mehr Leistung wünschen. Es ist auch für rechenintensive Bildbearbeitung und Videoschnitt geeignet. Das Tablet verfügt über 16 Gigabyte RAM und 512 Gigabyte internen Speicher. Der Akku hält laut Hersteller bis zu 15,5 Stunden durch. Bei Amazon kostet das neue Modell jetzt 1.299 Euro. Beim Hersteller selbst ist es in dieser Ausstattung ab 1.899 Euro erhältlich. Das entspricht einem Rabatt von 32 Prozent – du sparst also 600 Euro. Laut Vergleichsportalen ist das der günstigste Preis, seit das Modell im Juli dieses Jahres auf den Markt kam.
- 12″ Microsoft Surface Pro mit Snapdragon X Plus, 8 GB RAM und 256 GB Speicher Amazon*
- 13″ Microsoft Surface Pro mit Snapdragon X2 Elite, 16 GB RAM und 512 GB Speicher Amazon*
So viel kannst du bei Surface-Laptops sparen
Auch bei den Surface-Laptops gibt es anlässlich der Prime Deal Days Angebote. So ist das Modell mit 13-Zoll-Touchscreen laut Amazon von 1.349 Euro auf 799 Euro reduziert, was einem Rabatt von 41 Prozent entspricht. Es verfügt über den 8-Core-Prozessor Snapdragon X Plus, 16 Gigabyte RAM und 512 Gigabyte SSD-Speicher. Der Akku hält laut Microsoft bis zu zwölf Stunden durch, bei lokaler Videowiedergabe sogar bis zu 23 Stunden. Damit eignet sich der Laptop für Nutzer:innen, die ein leichtes, leises und ausdauerndes Windows-Gerät für typische Produktivitätsaufgaben suchen. Im Microsoft-Store kostet das Gerät ab 849 Euro und ist somit ebenfalls deutlich günstiger als die Preisempfehlung. Bei Amazon sparst du trotzdem mehr. Vergleichsportalen zufolge ist das aktuelle Angebot der günstigste Preis seit April 2026.
Den Microsoft Surface Laptop gibt es auch mit einem 13,8 Zoll großen Bildschirm. Dank des 12-Core-Prozessors Snapdragon X2 Elite lohnt sich das Modell insbesondere für Nutzer:innen, die sich einen schlanken, mobilen Laptop wünschen und damit auch unterwegs Multitasking- und Kreativ-Programme nutzen möchten. Laut Hersteller hält der Akku bis zu 20 Stunden am Stück durch. Mit 16 Gigabyte RAM und 512 Gigabyte internem Festplattenspeicher kostet der Laptop bei Amazon aktuell 1.199 Euro. Gegenüber der Preisempfehlung entspricht das einem Rabatt von 33 Prozent. Aber wie gut ist der Deal wirklich? Der Vergleich zeigt, dass Käufer:innen auch bei Microsoft direkt sparen können: Dort kostet das Gerät aktuell 1.442 Euro. Trotzdem ist das Gerät bei Amazon um einiges günstiger. Vergleichsportalen zufolge ist das sogar der beste Preis seit Einführung des neuen Surface-Modells im Juni 2026.
- 13″ Microsoft Surface Laptop mit Snapdragon X Plus, 16 GB RAM und 512 GB Speicher bei Amazon*
- 13,8″ Microsoft Surface Laptop Snapdragon X2 Elite, 16 GB RAM und 512 GB Speicher bei Amazon*
So gut sind die Amazon-Angebote wirklich
Der Preisvergleich zeigt: Die von Amazon angegebenen Rabatte fallen nicht immer so hoch aus wie beworben. Teilweise bietet auch Microsoft seine Surface-Geräte selbst deutlich unter der unverbindlichen Preisempfehlung an. Wer den größtmöglichen Rabatt herausholen will, sollte vermeintliche Angebote deshalb immer prüfen. Ein Blick in etablierte Preisvergleichsportale zeigt allerdings, dass sich die Prime Deal Days bei einigen Surface-Tablets und -Laptops wirklich lohnen. Zum Teil bietet Amazon sogar die besten Preise seit Markteinführung.

articles.title: SAP expands Joule into an agentic work layer as Autonomous Enterprise goes live - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
SAP expands Joule into an agentic work layer as Autonomous Enterprise goes live
SAP SE today announced a shift from promising agentic artificial intelligence autonomy to defining a path for users to interact with agents for work outside apps, not just within them.
During SAP Connect 2026, the company said it is making Autonomous Enterprise architecture, introduced at Sapphire in May, generally available this month alongside Joule Work and Desktop, with an expanded suite of autonomous assistants and agents.
“When we talk about autonomous enterprise, we realize that it’s going to be a journey for the customer, and it’s not something you draw a line to say starting tomorrow will be autonomous just because you now have these agents and assistants,” Manoj Swaminathan, SAP’s president and chief product officer of Autonomous Suite, told SiliconANGLE in an interview.
Joule, SAP’s generative AI assistant, debuted in 2023 and has become the company’s autonomous workhorse. Today, the company announced numerous upgrades, making it a powerful automation, productivity and development tool that acts as a conversational interface layer for customers that works alongside apps rather than within them.
According to Swaminathan, “autonomous” doesn’t mean simply handing everything to agents and then letting them go; it means providing humans the tools to observe, describe, and trust agents before delegating processes to them. This starts with the opportunity to control, govern, and understand how agents will work with their data, apps, and enterprise context before setting agents loose, and with the transparency to see and audit their activity.
“First principle is it’s AI on apps as opposed to AI in apps,” Swaminathan explained.
Front and center, Joule Work provides the framework to bring AI assistants to customer workflows, allowing autonomy to work with both SAP and non-SAP applications. A user looking at a screen has already experienced AI agents working within apps, where they can open up a word processor and have an agent write them a memo, or an email program, and have an agent look up past conversations. But having an agent understand enterprise resource planning and connect finance documents and email conversations without needing to jump between the two becomes SAP’s domain.
For example, Swaminathan gave an example of total corporate spend. Rather than treating the question as belonging to one application, Joule could determine that answering it requires information from ERP, travel and expense systems and the procurement platforms. It could then combine those records, present the result as one business answer.
This interface system is called Joule Desktop and it lives where the customer does with their apps and grabs the same enterprise information. It provides an intelligent layer that can perform duties that deal with the work itself rather than bind them to in-application resources.
“Joule is no longer a natural language chat client for us; it is a full-screen experience,” Swaminathan said.
With the framework’s general availability, Jule will receive updated agents for finance, supply chain, spend, workforce/customer experience, and other industry specializations across the autonomous suite. This will give customers access to deep capabilities and agents with domain expertise, knowledge and business acumen that can touch enterprise data.
Moving from AI models to autonomous enterprise
According to Swaminathan, enterprise customers bring their data and cloud lakehouses; SAP organizes that data and provides it with a structured knowledge graph. General-purpose models and agents from OpenAI Group PBC and Anthropic PBC cannot provide this when simply pasted on top of enterprise data. ERP data, processes, semantics, policies and relationships all matter – this is the “secret sauce” that SAP brings to the table.
SAP isn’t alone in this trend. Salesforce Inc. and ServiceNow Inc. are also driving an industry trend toward headless applications, context layers and agentic control planes. Enterprise AI is becoming less about adding copilots to applications themselves and more about building an intelligent layer on top of the customer experience.
Swaminathan stressed that the opportunity for SAP customers is the ability to declare intent; the agent decides which systems to involve and then gets the work done. The human always stays in the loop, retains governance, auditability, and transparency and agents are treated like employees in the system, including security, systems of record, and execution. Agents are another layer on top of the old application interface that act as intelligent conversational tools on behalf of humans.
“Autonomous enterprise is not a vision anymore,” Swaminathan said. “It is real, with general availability in October.”
SAP will continue using AI units as the primary commercial monetization for these capabilities. The model will be primarily consumption-based rather than purely subscription-based, with agent inference consuming units and SAP providing customer visibility into that usage.
The Joule updates and other autonomous enterprise capabilities will become available throughout October and customers can already see agents in SAP’s Discovery Center.

DoorDash customers can now order from Costco in Canada. This joins existing options from the likes of Uber Eats and Instacart.

articles.title: SELUTION SLR™ wins historic US FDA nod for in‑stent restenosis
articles.text:
SELUTION SLR™ wins historic US FDA nod for in‑stent restenosis
The technology Amit Bohora co-founded at MedAlliance, and later sold to Cordis in a landmark $1.135 billion deal, has just become the first and only sirolimus drug-eluting balloon approved in the US.
The US Food and Drug Administration has approved the SELUTION SLR™ (Sustained Limus Release) Drug-Eluting Balloon for coronary in-stent restenosis (ISR), Cordis announced this month. This is the first and only sirolimus drug-eluting balloon approved for use anywhere in the United States.
For Amit Bohora, who co-founded MedAlliance and helped take SELUTION SLR from an early research concept to a globally commercialized therapy before the company was acquired by Cordis in October 2023 for $1.135 billion, the approval is a personal milestone in a technology he spent over a decade building.
It took more than a decade, thousands of patients, and one of medtech’s biggest recent exits to get here. A milestone years in the making
The approval rests on the SELUTION4ISR trial, a multicenter, randomized study of more than 400 patients across 48 sites in the United States, Canada, Brazil and Europe, which met its primary endpoint of non-inferiority against standard-of-care treatment at 12 months. It adds to a clinical evidence base that now spans more than 5,000 patients worldwide — and lands just as Cordis confirms it has completed enrollment in a 960-patient US trial evaluating the balloon for de novo lesions in small coronary vessels, setting up a second FDA filing to come.
The US performs close to one million percutaneous coronary interventions a year, and roughly one in 10 of those cases involves treating in-stent restenosis, an artery re-narrowing inside a previous stent.
Until now, US physicians reaching for a drug-coated balloon in these cases had only a paclitaxel-based option. SELUTION SLR changes that calculus, becoming the first sirolimus-based alternative available in the country.
Reflecting on the technology, Bohora said when they set out to build SELUTION at MedAlliance, the goal was never simply to create another device - it was to give physicians a genuine, stentless alternative for patients living with coronary artery disease.
“Seeing the therapy now approved by the USFDA for in-stent restenosis, one of the toughest problems in interventional cardiology, is an incredibly proud moment. It validates years of research, clinical trial work, and the conviction that sustained sirolimus release, without a permanent implant, could change how physicians think about re-treating a narrowed artery,” he said.
Bohora led MedAlliance's clinical programs, regulatory approvals, and global expansion during his time with the company, including building out R&D facilities in Switzerland and Singapore and manufacturing capability in the US. “What began as a contrarian conviction that cardiology must break free from permanent metal -has earned the world's most rigorous regulatory validation. US FDA approval is not just a commercial win; it is a clinical victory for millions living with coronary artery disease,” he said. .
Bohora said MedAlliance aimed to prove that visionary entrepreneurship, rooted in deep science, can redefine global healthcare. “Our $1.135 billion acquisition by Cordis amplified that mission. Seeing SELUTION SLR™ unlock the US market proves that transformative Indian leadership and global innovation can forever change the paradigm of cardiovascular care.”
Dr. Praveen Chandra, Principal Investigator, SELUTION First-in-Man Trial, offered a clinical perspective. “Leading the First-in-Human clinical trial for SELUTION, I witnessed early on how sustained sirolimus delivery could fundamentally alter vascular healing without adding more metal. This FDA approval is a historic vindication of that science. It reflects Amit’s uncompromising dedication to translational clinical rigor, turning a bold idea into a therapy now transforming lives across the globe.”
Why this matters
SELUTION SLR is now the only sirolimus drug-eluting balloon on the US market, a category the MedAlliance team, under Bohora's leadership, effectively created years before the science was proven at this scale.
Commercially available in more than 65 countries and used to treat over 250,000 patients worldwide, the device's US clearance under its current owner, Cordis, marks a milestone few medtech founders ever get to see: an invention they helped originate becoming standard of care in the world's most demanding regulatory market.
About Amit Bohora
Amit Bohora is the co-founder of MedAlliance, the Swiss medical technology company that originally developed the SELUTION SLR Drug-Eluting Balloon. He led the company's journey from early-stage research through worldwide commercialization - spearheading its clinical, regulatory and manufacturing expansion - until MedAlliance's acquisition by Cordis (USA) in October 2023, in a transaction valued at USD 1.135 Billion. Mr. Bohora is not affiliated with Cordis and does not speak on the company's behalf; this piece reflects his personal perspective as a cofounder on a technology he helped create.
About SELUTION SLR™ DEB
SELUTION SLR™ uses proprietary Sustained Limus Release (SLR) technology, originally developed by MedAlliance, to deliver a controlled release of sirolimus to the vessel wall over roughly 90 days, without leaving a permanent implant behind. With this approval, it becomes the first and only sirolimus drug-eluting balloon available in the U.S. market. SELUTION SLR is now owned and commercialized by Cordis.

articles.title: El adelanto electoral deja en el aire varias decisiones clave para la electricidad del futuro en España
articles.text:
El pasado 5 de octubre, el presidente del Gobierno Pedro Sánchez anunció lo que muchos ya esperaban: una nueva llamada a las urnas el próximo 29 de noviembre que decidirá el color de la próxima legislatura.
Con esta nueva convocatoria electoral, algunos de los planes del actual Ejecutivo que estaban en tramitación quedan en el aire. Muchos de ellos están relacionados con el sector energético, que atraviesa además un momento especialmente delicado por la situación internacional. Algunos tendrán que esperar; otros, podrán ir tirando. Lo que sí tendrán en común es que estarán rodeados de incertidumbre hasta que se forme un nuevo Gobierno. Y es que muchas entidades clave temen no tanto que estos marcos regulatorios no acaben saliendo adelante como que su aprobación pueda alargarse mucho en el tiempo.
La planificación eléctrica, en manos del próximo Ejecutivo. El Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica presentó una propuesta para la electrificación de la red de transporte que debía servir como hoja de ruta para adaptar las infraestructuras energéticas a la descarbonización de la economía y al aumento de la demanda eléctrica industrial.
Con el posible cambio de Gobierno, este plan queda en el aire y, como indica El Periódico de la Energía, su tramitación difícilmente podrá completarse en el Congreso antes del 29N. A la espera de informes de la Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia, y al depender tan directamente del MITECO y afectar a varios gobiernos autonómicos, su aprobación final seguramente quedará en manos de la decisión que se tome en las urnas.
El mercado de capacidad también queda en el aire. Cuenta 20 Minutos que la vicepresidenta tercera Sara Aagesen propuso en un primer borrador en septiembre de 2025 aumentar la red de electricidad en 27.700 megavatios para aliviar su saturación. A pesar de la aprobación de un mercado de capacidad el pasado mes de septiembre de 2026 y de la regulación de sus condiciones, es muy posible que se retrase notablemente el lanzamiento de la primera subasta y que sigamos recurriendo al SRAD para equilibrar el sistema.
Producción eléctrica fuera de la península. Según El Correo, otro de los expedientes cuya aprobación podría quedar pendiente es el que afecta a los territorios no peninsulares de Ceuta y Melilla y que regula la actividad de producción eléctrica en estos enclaves. De acuerdo con este medio, la interconexión submarina por cable con Ceuta reducirá la dependencia de la generación local y quedará pendiente definir el papel de la central de ciclo combinado que operaba hasta ahora en la ciudad autónoma.
Los centros de datos. Entre los planes de Sánchez también se encontraba la aprobación de un Real Decreto para regular este tipo de instalaciones que generó cierta polémica y que, según apunta El Periódico de la Energía, cuenta con más de 10.500 alegaciones interpuestas, lo cual complica que pueda resolverse todo en tan solo dos meses. La propuesta contemplaba que el 80% del consumo de los centros de datos se hiciese con generación renovable ajustable hora a hora, cuyas fuentes no superasen los 18 meses de antigüedad: cuestiones que, según las voces más críticas, eran muy difíciles de cumplir.
Sin embargo, las últimas informaciones apuntan a que el Gobierno pretende aprobar la regulación de los centros de datos antes de las elecciones.
Un problema de incertidumbre. A diferencia de otras políticas públicas, las decisiones energéticas tienen una particularidad importante: muchos de los proyectos que dependen de ellas tardan años en desarrollarse. De ahí que el problema no sea únicamente quién resulte vencedor el próximo 29N, sino qué prioridad se le dará a los expedientes abiertos, cuáles se mantendrán en la agenda de la próxima legislatura y a cuáles se les dará carpetazo en un cajón.

articles.title: Alliance backs Kenyan fintech Cloud9 with $500k investment
articles.text:
Alliance, a New York-headquartered crypto accelerator and founder community that invests in early-stage crypto and fintech startups, has invested $500,000 in equity in Cloud9, a Kenyan fintech that provides digital banking services for businesses.
The investment is part of Cloud9’s ongoing pre-seed round, which also attracted investment from Techstars NYC and strategic angel investors, bringing the company’s total funding to $1 million.
The investment comes as Cloud9 pushes beyond digital banking to build payment infrastructure for African businesses trading across borders after making two acquisitions in three months.
The company plans to use the new funding to expand its cross-border payment corridors, improve its product experience, launch virtual and physical cards, and grow its base of African consumers and businesses using the platform to participate in global trade.
Cloud9 launched its product in early 2026 and says it has since created more than 25,000 accounts, with transaction volume growing by more than 15% week over week. It is positioning the platform as financial infrastructure for African businesses trading across borders.
“Kenya already skipped the bank branch once. Mobile money became how the country pays for almost everything, but only within its borders,” said Tesh Mbaabu, Cloud9’s founder and chief executive officer. “With Cloud9, a merchant in Nairobi should be able to pay a supplier in Guangzhou as easily as they pay a vendor down the street. Where an entrepreneur is based should not limit who they can buy from or sell to.”
Cloud9 says users can hold multiple currencies, including Kenyan shillings, US dollars, euros, pounds and Chinese yuan. They can send payments to suppliers in more than 100 countries, receive international payments through virtual accounts, and withdraw funds to mobile money when they need local currency.
The company also offers tools for payroll, bulk payments and team approvals for businesses, while its Cloud9 Wealth product gives Kenyan users access to savings vaults and global stock markets. Its treasury operations cover more than 120 countries, and its payment network currently supports direct payments to Mainland China, Hong Kong, India and Southeast Asia, as well as intra-African collections and local-currency disbursements. The company said it is targeting businesses involved in global trade. Kenya imports from China were worth $4.31 billion in 2024.
Stablecoins are a key part of how Cloud9 moves money between countries. A customer may hold dollars, euros, or Kenyan shillings and initiate a payment in one of those currencies. Cloud9 then uses USDC or USDT to move value between countries and currencies on the backend.
“Stablecoins are becoming the settlement layer for global trade, and Africa is where that shift matters most,” said Imran Khan, general partner at Alliance. “Tesh has built for African merchants at scale before, and Cloud9 is turning stablecoin rails into an everyday bank account for the entrepreneurs who need it most.”
The company’s push into cross-border payments comes as it expands beyond banking through acquisitions. In August, Cloud9 acquired social commerce platform Chpter in an undisclosed all-stock deal, its second acquisition in three months. In May, the company acquired Kenyan ticketing platform M-Tickets for about KES 100 million ($773,000) in an all-stock transaction.
The acquisitions give Cloud9 access to businesses at different points in their commercial activity. M-Tickets brings it closer to event organisers and consumer spending, while Chpter adds businesses that sell and communicate with customers through platforms such as WhatsApp and Instagram. Cloud9’s stated strategy is to layer financial services onto those existing transactions and customer relationships.
Mbaabu and Mesongo Sibuti launched Cloud9 in October 2025, weeks after leaving Chpter, where they served as co-founders. They joined Chpter in early 2024 to help accelerate the social-commerce company’s growth and stepped down from day-to-day operations in September 2025.
Cloud9 operates in a competitive Kenyan payments market, with Safaricom’s M-Pesa remaining embedded in everyday payments. Companies such as Pesapal, Flutterwave, Wise, and other payment providers serve businesses with payment collection and cross-border capabilities.
Cloud9 generates revenue from foreign-exchange spreads and transaction fees when customers make payments. It also charges monthly fees on some multi-currency accounts and wallets. The company noted that it is building additional products around the business account, including cards and credit options.
“Cloud9’s mission is to simplify, democratise, and accelerate access to financial tools, helping individuals grow wealth, businesses scale faster, and communities participate in global markets, all through one platform,” the company said.

The company says stablecoins serve as the settlement layer for many of its transactions. A customer may hold dollars, euros or Kenyan shillings and initiate a payment in one of those currencies. Cloud9 then uses USDC or USDT to move value between countries and currencies on the backend.
“That makes transfers faster and cheaper than correspondent banking and lets Cloud9 open new corridors without a bank in each one,” Mbaabu said.

articles.title: Apple préparerait deux vagues de nouveaux produits en octobre (on fait le point)
articles.text:
La firme de Cupertino ne compte pas lever le pied en cette fin d’année. En effet, Apple ferait deux lancements de produits au mois d’octobre, avec chacun plusieurs nouveaux produits, qui viendraient s’ajouter au lancement de l’iPhone Duo, attendu pour le 23 octobre.
Un premier rendez-vous autour de la maison connectée
Mark Gurman de Bloomberg a récemment affirmé qu’un événement se tiendrait le mardi 13 octobre pour dévoiler un tout nouveau hub domotique, le HomePod avec écran, une nouvelle version du HomePod mini ainsi qu’un nouvel Apple TV. Ces trois produits devraient donc ouvrir le bal des festivités automnales pour la marque américaine.
Mais d’autres rumeurs entourent cette période, comme celle du lancement d’un nouvel iPad mini équipé d’un écran OLED, d’une puce A20 Pro, d’une caméra frontale en orientation paysage et d’un nouveau système audio. Reste à savoir si cette tablette rejoindra les accessoires connectés dès le 13 octobre ou si elle patientera jusqu’à la seconde vague de produits pressentie pour ce mois d’octobre.
Des nouveaux Mac dès la fin du mois ?
Plusieurs sources confirment qu’une seconde salve d’annonces interviendra durant la dernière semaine d’octobre. Si la nature exacte de ce catalogue reste à confirmer, certaines sources s’attendent à une annonce autour de nouveaux Mac et MacBook.
Parmi les pistes évoquées figurent plusieurs modèles de MacBook Pro dotés d’un écran OLED avec un nouveau design plus fin et léger, un MacBook Pro de 14 pouces d’entrée de gamme équipé d’une puce M6, ainsi qu’un nouvel iMac, également attendu avec cette puce. Une configuration haut de gamme de Mac Studio avec une puce M5 Ultra et 512 Go de mémoire vive est également attendue d’ici la fin du mois, qui s’annonce chargée du côté d’Apple.

articles.title: Flagged by the Machine: How Google Ads Suspended an Open-Source macOS Term as Malicious
articles.text:
Automated verification pipelines inside major distribution platforms continue to create operational bottlenecks for systems utility developers. Przemyslaw Alexander Kaminski, the creator of RACE, an open-source native macOS terminal multiplexer written in Rust, recently detailed the automated suspension of his ad distribution account following an ad campaign launch. Despite distributed release binaries passing native operating system notarization and independent antimalware inspections, security policy crawlers flagged the developer account under compromised site and malicious binary designations. The incident highlights the disconnect between developer tools utilising advanced POSIX process orchestration and automated safety heuristics.
RACE differs from conventional grid-based terminal multiplexers such as tmux by implementing an infinite canvas architecture where shell surfaces can be arbitrarily positioned, resized, and grouped. Architecturally, the multiplexer detaches command execution from window layout lifecycles, guaranteeing that child interactive shells persist across desktop application restarts or UI crashes. Under macOS, this requires managing pseudoterminal pairs and background worker processes through either an internal PTY host daemon or an external dtach backend.
Automated security scanners evaluate binary safety and web endpoints by analysing file signatures, static strings, and dynamic process execution patterns. In typical desktop application spaces, an executable that persistently forks orphaned background workers capable of receiving arbitrary command-line input shares behavioural signatures with persistent backdoors and remote access trojans.
When Kaminski provisioned campaigns pointing to the product documentation domain and binary downloads, the campaign platform flagged the destination infrastructure for malicious software violations. A manual verification sweep by the author revealed clean reports across third-party malware analyzers as well as the Google's own diagnostics tools. Google Search Console and the Google Safe Browsing verification service reported zero compromised assets across the domain root and download infrastructure.
// Diagnostic payload submitted during automated appeal review
{
  "target_binary": "RACE.dmg",
  "notarization_status": "Apple Notarized Developer ID",
  "google_safe_browsing": "CLEAN",
  "search_console_security": "NO_ISSUES_DETECTED",
  "virustotal_positives": 0,
  "process_lifecycle": "documented_pty_multiplexing"
}
Attempts to remediate the suspension uncovered circular dependencies inside the platform's automated enforcement loop. Submitting diagnostic reports via standard appeal interfaces resulted in deterministic rejections without disclosing the specific binary hash, rule match, or network artefact triggering the policy flag. Seeking account support was blocked by prerequisites that the underlying security suspension must be resolved first.
Image Source: https://xlii.space
To isolate whether runtime daemon persistence caused the flag, the developer modified the lifecycle teardown routines in version 1.0.39, introducing explicit user prompts and process cleanup hooks to terminate orphaned multiplexing threads upon parent deletion. A later edit to the post underlines that the policy suspension was ultimately rescinded only after community escalation surfaced the operational deadlock to engineering teams:
Through the apparent magic of Hacker News, my Google Ads account has been reinstated. Still no explanation of what triggered the suspension, but thank you to everyone who helped make it visible (and/or fixed).
The case illustrates the systemic tension between security automation and non-standard systems programming. As platform operators rely increasingly on black-box behavioural models to inspect software ecosystems, developers building legitimate native utilities that manage processes, manipulate memory maps, or hook low-level kernel abstractions face growing friction across distribution and commercial infrastructure. Engineering teams distributing developer-focused binaries must anticipate false positives by documenting process topologies and isolating persistent worker agents from primary UI binaries. Kaminski stated in his article that he will continue his fight on all possible paths, even in the EU Court.

articles.title: Paris- and London-based Spiko raises nearly €80 million to help businesses and individuals put idle cash to work | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Spiko, a tokenised cash fund platform with headquarters in Paris and London, has raised €80.03 million ($90 million) in a Series B funding round. The round follows an €18.9 million Series A in July 2025, bringing its total funding raised to date to roughly €106.7 million ($120 million).
The round was led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA), a global venture capital firm with more than €33.78 billion ($38 billion) in assets under management. The round also saw the return of existing investors Index Ventures, Speedinvest, and White Star Capital, alongside a broader group that includes Bpifrance, Flourish Ventures, Shapers, Blockwall, Frst, EQNX, Mirana Ventures, and Wintermute Ventures. Notable angels, including Axel Weber, former president of the Bundesbank, and the founders of Qonto, also participated.
“Paul-Adrien and Antoine are building the default home for cash. Money market funds are where trust is earned, and the same model extends naturally to new markets and new products,” said Philip Chopin, Managing Director and Head of Europe at NEA.
Founded in 2023 by Paul-Adrien Hyppolite and Antoine Michon, Spiko designs and distributes its own regulated cash funds. Hyppolite is a former Deputy Head of the Financial Markets division at the French Treasury, while Michon is a former technology advisor to the French government who previously led deployments at Palatir.
Spiko’s regulated cash funds are available in four currencies — euro, dollar, pound sterling, and Swiss franc — and can be accessed via web and mobile app, or through an API that lets financial platforms embed the funds directly into their own products.
The company argues that Europe and the US collectively hold around €44.4 trillion ($50 trillion) in cash and deposits, most of which earns little or nothing. With central bank rates currently at 2.5% in the euro zone and close to 4% in the US, Spiko says each percentage point of yield on that sum represents around €444.6 billion ($500 billion) annually, which flows predominantly to banks and large financial institutions, leaving individuals, small businesses, and others out.
Spiko issues its funds on blockchain infrastructure, which has allowed it to become the world’s largest issuer of tokenised cash funds, ahead of BlackRock and Franklin Templeton. Since it operates on the same rails as stablecoins and smart contracts, the approach makes cash programmable: a company can automate its treasury rules once and have Spiko execute them continuously, including turning idle cash into yield-bearing funds.
“Every person and every organisation holds cash, yet whether it earns anything still depends on who you are and how much you have. Yield should be universal. Our ambition is to make all cash earn by default, around the clock,” said Hyppolite, co-founder and CEO of Spiko.
In just two years, Spiko has grown to more than €2.4 billion ($2.7 billion) in assets under management, a more than fivefold increase over the past 12 months. The platform now serves more than 10,000 businesses and individuals across more than 25 jurisdictions, including startups, VC funds, research institutions, public institutions, and medical practices.
While traditional money market funds were built around the business-hours market, Spiko is positioning its cash funds as the ideal one for a world in which money moves continuously through software and AI agents.
Spiko will use the fresh capital to launch new funds, open new markets, and expand the team. The company already operates from hubs in Paris and London, and is actively building out local presence across Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, and the Nordics.

articles.title: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D drops to $429 with a free $70 MSI AIO cooler and Onimusha game
articles.text:
In brief: The AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, a chip we called the new gaming CPU king when it launched in November 2024, is currently available for $429 from Newegg. Better still, it's part of a deal that includes a $70 MSI MAG AIO cooler and the new Onimusha game, also $70, absolutely free.
In a time when most PC hardware has become so expensive that many people are avoiding upgrading, it's refreshing to see a deal like this.
CPUs haven't been affected by the memory crisis like other components, but it's still great to find a processor available for around $70 less than its launch MSRP. It's listed for $469, but there's another $40 off by using the special promo code: FTTF7668.
Technically, the entire package represents $210 more value than buying the CPU at launch. Included in the purchase is a very nice MSI MAG CoreLiquid A13 240 Black - AIO ARGB Liquid Cooling kit. The two-fan cooler is usually $70 when bought alone, and should pair well with the Ryzen 7 9800X3D.
If you're still not convinced, the CPU also includes the new Onimusha: Way of the Sword game. It's got a Metascore of 83 on Metacritic and a Very Positive rating on Steam (91% positive), where you can also try the demo. It's normally $70, too, further illustrating what a good deal this is.
The Ryzen 7 9800X3D's gaming performance, from our review
We wrote in our original review of the 9800X3D, which we gave a score of 90, that it represented excellent value even at its $480 MSRP. Like all X3D CPUs, the 8-core/16-thread CPU leverages AMD's 3D V-Cache.
This second-generation design moves the extra cache beneath the CPU cores, improving cooling and allowing higher clock speeds. The results speak for themselves: across our 14-game test suite, the 9800X3D was 11% faster than the 7800X3D, while beating Intel's Core i9-14900K by 27% and the Core Ultra 9 285K by 33%.
Some individual gains were even bigger, with Hogwarts Legacy running 21% faster than on the 7800X3D. It also proved efficient, using 36% less power than the 285K in Cyberpunk 2077 while delivering 45% more performance. That's plenty of gaming muscle to go with the bundled cooler and free game.

articles.title: R$ 58 milhões: governo vai levar fibra a 2 mil CRAS • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
R$ 58 milhões: governo vai levar fibra a 2 mil CRAS
Centros de Referência de Assistência Social receberão Wi-Fi com conexão via fibra óptica e 300 Mb/s de velocidade.
O governo federal anunciou que vai levar internet de alta velocidade a 2 mil CRAS, os Centros de Referência de Assistência Social. Os pontos de Wi-Fi serão instalados em unidades de todo o país e prometem velocidade de 300 Mb/s, além de conexão via fibra óptica.
O Ministério das Comunicações explicou que os R$ 58 milhões são provenientes do Fust, o Fundo de Universalização dos Serviços de Telecomunicações, que recebe contribuições obrigatórias das empresas do setor. Segundo o ministro Frederico de Siqueira Filho, a medida vai facilitar o acesso aos serviços oferecidos tanto pelos profissionais quanto pelas pessoas atendidas nas unidades.
Além disso, a novidade promete maior integração entre os CRAS, o que deve fortalecer o Sistema Único de Assistência Social (SUAS). De acordo com o ministro do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome, Wellington Dias, a conectividade “contribui para enfrentar a exclusão digital das pessoas que mais precisam dos serviços públicos”.
A conectividade e a integração entre unidades prometem facilitar o acesso a informações tratadas em diferentes partes do país. Além disso, o governo federal fala em maior agilidade para atualizar informações do Cadastro Único. Esse tipo de movimento pode ser interessante para melhorar a base de dados da população e auxiliar no trabalho de assistência social por todo o Brasil.
Já do lado da população, a ideia passa por aumentar o acesso aos serviços públicos e benefícios, além de oportunidades de emprego, por exemplo. Vale lembrar que ainda são cerca de 10% dos brasileiros sem acesso à internet, segundo levantamento do IBGE. A oferta de Wi-Fi em unidades públicas como os CRAS é uma maneira de diminuir esse índice.
O governo federal informou que esse é o primeiro uso do Fust com objetivo de aumentar a conectividade nos CRAS, dando sequência a outras iniciativas do Fust Direto, que levou Wi-Fi a escolas e instituições de saúde. O caso mais recente aconteceu em setembro, com edital de R$ 50 milhões para investimentos em mais de 1,8 mil Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBS).
As propostas podem ser apresentadas pelas empresas de telecomunicações até 13 de outubro. Serão investidos cerca de R$ 58 milhões para levar Wi-Fi a pelo menos 2.029 CRAS.

articles.title: Brook StarRay Wireless Controller Now Available
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 6th 2026
Brook StarRay Wireless Controller Now Available
Brook Gaming introduces the Brook StarRay Wireless Controller, combining native PS5 support with an Xbox-style asymmetrical stick layout. Available now through the Brook Amazon Store and Brook official online shop, StarRay supports PS5, PC (Steam), iOS, and Android via Bluetooth or USB-C wired connection. On PS5, players can also power on the console directly using the HOME button.
Precision and Speed for Every Game
StarRay features Hall Effect analog sticks for precise, durable control with reduced risk of stick drift, along with mechanical buttons that deliver up to 30% faster input response.For PC players, StarRay supports up to a 1000 Hz polling rate via wired connection. Its dual-mode triggers can switch between a 15 mm long-stroke trigger for precise control in racing games and a 0.3 mm quick trigger for faster inputs in FPS and action games.
Customize Your Play with the StarRay App
The StarRay App supports Turbo, Macro, button remapping, joystick sensitivity and dead-zone adjustment, and firmware updates, giving players the flexibility to fine-tune their controls for different games and play styles.
StarRay also features two top auxiliary buttons, two rear buttons, dual vibration motors, RGB lighting, and anti-slip grips for greater flexibility and comfort.
Key Features
- Native PS5 support with Xbox-style asymmetrical stick layout
- Hall Effect sticks and mechanical buttons for precise, responsive control
- Dual-mode triggers: 15 mm long-stroke / 0.3 mm quick trigger
- Up to 1000 Hz polling rate on PC via wired connection
- StarRay App customization: Turbo, Macro, button remapping, joystick adjustment, and firmware updates

Availability
The Brook StarRay Wireless Controller is available now through the Brook Amazon Store and Brook official online shop.
