articles.title: Google Docs et Drive adoptent enfin Markdown : la nouveauté qui va tout changer
articles.text:
Il était temps ! Après de longues années de développement, Google Drive et Google Docs gèrent enfin le format Markdown.
Cela fait bien longtemps que Google s’intéresse au Markdown : Google Docs permettait jusqu’ici d’exploiter le format pour créer des listes et faire un peu de mise en page, mais c’était, somme toute, assez limité. Chez la concurrence, même le vénérable Bloc-notes de Microsoft est devenu compatible avec la fameuse syntaxe en 2025. pCloud a, quant à lui, glissé le format dans sa future suite bureautique. Il était donc grand temps que Google passe la seconde et c’est désormais chose faite.
Google Docs et Drive sont enfin compatibles avec le format Markdown
Jusqu’à aujourd’hui, pour travailler sur un fichier Markdown, il fallait importer le document dans Google Drive puis le convertir au format Docs, au risque de faire sauter toute la mise en page et tous les commentaires. Mais ces temps troublés sont enfin derrière nous : Docs et Drive sont désormais entièrement compatibles avec les fichiers Markdown.
Google a annoncé la bonne nouvelle hier sur son blog : « nous introduisons la possibilité de visualiser, de modifier et de collaborer sur des fichiers Markdown (.md ou .markdown) directement dans Google Docs, ainsi que de visualiser des aperçus rendus dans Google Drive ».
Dans les faits, les utilisateurs vont pouvoir modifier des fichiers Markdown sans avoir à les convertir. Il sera possible d’utiliser de nombreuses fonctionnalités de Docs : édition en temps réel, travail à plusieurs, ajout de commentaires et bien plus encore. Google précise qu'il ne sera pas nécessaire de « saisir du code source brut ».
Côté Google Drive, il sera notamment possible de « visualiser des documents entièrement formatés et esthétiques, avec des liens cliquables et des tableaux structurés. »
Un déploiement progressif durant le mois d’octobre
Alors, pourquoi cet intérêt soudain de Google pour ce format ? S’il s’agit d’un langage prisé par les développeurs et autres rédacteurs techniques, le Markdown est, par les temps qui courent, devenu tout bonnement incontournable. Comme le rappelle si bien Chandhu Totha, Vice-président de Google et ingénieur en chef de Google Workspace, dans un récent post paru sur X.com : « Markdown est devenu le langage commun entre les humains et les agents d'IA : spécifications, plans, fichiers README, tableaux, listes de tâches, documents générés… La plupart de ces fichiers commencent par l'extension .md. »
- Fonctionnalités de collaboration
- Synchronisation dans le Cloud
- Compatibilité avec les formats Microsoft Word et PDF
- mood15 Go d'espace gratuit
- upload5 To en limite d'envoi
- home_pinServeurs en Europe
Markdown est, en effet, une manière simple d’écrire du texte tout en indiquant sa structure. Il est indispensable pour les LLM qui l’utilisent pour mieux comprendre et préserver la structure des documents. La prise en charge de ce format dans Drive et Docs est donc davantage due à l’engouement pour l’IA qu’à un véritable amour du Markdown. Pour preuve, Chandhu Totha a aussi précisé qu’il sera possible d’ « importer des fichiers .md dans Notebook et (de) les synchroniser au fil du temps ! »
Quoi qu’il en soit, le résultat est tout de même là et la fonction sera bientôt accessible à tous les clients Workspace ainsi qu’aux titulaires d’un compte personnel. Le déploiement a démarré hier et se poursuivra durant une quinzaine de jours.

articles.title: Nobelpreis für Physik geht an Neutrinoforscher: Hier erfährst du mehr zu den Teilchen
articles.text:
Nobelpreis für Physik geht an Neutrinoforscher: Unser Explainer zu den Teilchen
Für die kleinsten Teilchen, die Neutrinos, erhält der amerikanische Forscher Francis Halzen jetzt die größte Auszeichnung: den Nobelpreis für Physik. Seinen Erkenntnissen ist es zu verdanken, dass das Neutrino-Observatorium Icecube in der Antarktis eingerichtet werden konnten. Das Observatorium ist ein kilometerlanges Array aus Photonendetektoren, das unter dem Eis am Südpol vergraben ist. Wenn Neutrinos das Eis durchdringen, stoßen sie gelegentlich mit Atomen zusammen und erzeugen dabei Teilchen, die als Myonen bezeichnet werden. Diese Myonen erzeugen beim Durchqueren des Eises Licht, das vom Detektor erfasst wird, wodurch Wissenschaftler:innen die Richtung des eintreffenden Neutrinos bestimmen können.
Doch die Erkenntnisse reichen weiter als bis in den Südpol: Mithilfe von Icecube können Forscher:innen Neutrinos aus extrem energiereichen Prozessen im fernen Universum nachweisen. So sorgte auch diese Meldung Anfang 2025 für großes Aufsehen in der Wissenschaft: Forschende meldeten erstmals den Nachweis eines extrem hochenergetischen Neutrinos. Aber was sind diese Neutrinos überhaupt? Und warum ist das spannend?
Der nachfolgende Text wurde ursprünglich am 19.02.2025 veröffentlicht. Anlässlich der Auszeichnung von Francis Halzen mit dem Nobelpreis für Physik, stellen wir unseren „Explainer für Neutrinos“ hier nochmals zur Verfügung. Ein Text über die Preisträger des Medizin-Nobelpreises findet ihr hier.
Ein kurzer Ausflug in die wunderbare Welt der Teilchenphysik schafft zumindest ein wenig mehr Klarheit.
Was sind Neutrinos?
Neutrinos sind Elementarteilchen, die mit nahezu Lichtgeschwindigkeit durch das Universum flitzen. Sie sind elektrisch neutral, besitzen nur eine sehr kleine Masse und unterliegen nicht der starken Wechselwirkung (dazu weiter unten). Was bedeutet, dass sie fast gar nicht mit Materie „wechselwirken“, also extrem schwer nachzuweisen sind.
Neutrino-Detektoren sind dementsprechend extrem große, komplexe Maschinen. Das hochenergetische Neutrino, das Anfang 2025 für so viel Aufregung sorgte, ist vom KM3NeT nachgewiesen worden. Der europäische Detektor ist eigentlich noch im Aufbau. Wenn er fertig ist, wird er aus einer riesigen gitterförmigen Matrix von Lichtsensoren bestehen, die im Mittelmeer vor der Küste von Sizilien am Meeresboden verankert ist. Doch als die Anlage Anfang 2023 zu zehn Prozent fertiggestellt war, maß sie bereits einen ungewöhnlich hellen Lichtblitz von einem sich horizontal bewegenden Neutrino mit extrem hoher Energie.
Warum sind Neutrinos so schwer nachzuweisen?
Um das zu erklären, müssen wir zumindest kurz in die Teilchenphysik einsteigen: Nach dem Bau der ersten Teilchendetektoren wurden zahlreiche neue Elementarteilchen gefunden – in den frühen 1960er Jahren war ihre Zahl auf über 400 angewachsen. Erst das seitdem entstandene und immer weiter ausgebaute Standardmodell der Teilchenphysik brachte wieder Ordnung in den Teilchenzoo, indem es erklärte, wie sich die neuen Teilchen durch elementare Bausteine zusammensetzen lassen.
Wie funktioniert dieses Standardmodell?
Das Standardmodell geht davon aus, dass es einige, wenige Elementarteilchen gibt. Genauer gesagt gibt es zwei Familien von Elementarteilchen: Quarks und Leptonen. Aus Quarks und Leptonen sind Materie und Antimaterie zusammengesetzt.
Auf Quarks und Leptonen wirken jeweils spezifische Kräfte. Salopp gesagt ist das wie bei Superhelden, die ihre jeweiligen Superheldenkräfte haben. Auf Elektronen wirken zum Beispiel elektromagnetische Felder, auf Quarks die starke Wechselwirkung und die elektromagnetische Wechselwirkung und so weiter. Auf das Neutrino hat nur die sogenannte schwache Wechselwirkung Einfluss.
Die Kräfte zwischen den Elementarteilchen werden laut Standardmodell durch den Austausch virtueller Teilchen, sogenannte Bosonen, vermittelt. Zu jeder spezifischen Kraft gehören jeweils spezifische Bosonen. Jedes Elementarteilchen tauscht ständig solche virtuellen Bosonen mit dem ihm umgebenden entsprechenden Feld aus.
Berücksichtigt man nun noch, dass auch in der Kernphysik Erhaltungssätze gelten, kann man schon fast nachvollziehen, wie Kernreaktionen ablaufen.
Wenn zum Beispiel freie Neutronen radioaktiv zu Protonen zerfallen, muss zum einen die gesamte elektrische Ladung erhalten bleiben. Daher wird bei diesem Zerfall ein Elektron frei. Gleichzeitig muss aber auch die Zahl der Leptonen erhalten bleiben. Weil bei dem Zerfall ein Lepton – das Elektron – entsteht, muss auch ein Antilepton bei dem Prozess frei werden: Das ist ein Antineutrino.
Kann man das irgendwie nutzen?
Die meisten auf der Erden existierenden Neutrinos entstehen, wenn kosmische Strahlung auf die Erdatmosphäre trifft. Weil diese Neutrinos beinahe ungebremst durch die Erde fliegen, kamen Physiker auf die Idee, modulierte Neutrinostrahlen zur interkontinentalen Kommunikation zu nutzen – klingt verrückt, aber der Pirelli-Konzern hat das Konzept noch Anfang der 2000er aktiv erforscht. Im Prinzip funktioniert die Idee tatsächlich, allerdings bisher nur auf kurze Distanzen und mit einem enormen Aufwand.
Antineutrinos entstehen aber auch bei radioaktiven Zerfällen – also beispielsweise in Atomkraftwerken. Das Energie-Spektrum dieser Antineutrinos kann im Prinzip verraten, ob in einem Atomreaktor waffenfähiges spaltbares Material hergestellt wird. In Großbritannien entsteht solch ein Detektor. Neutrinos entstehen aber beispielsweise auch durch Supernova-Explosionen. Sie sind daher Spuren, die auf kosmische Großereignisse hinweisen.
Was war jetzt an dem gemessenen Neutrino so wichtig?
Seine Energie und seine Flugrichtung: Die Neutrinos aus der Höhenstrahlung fliegen vertikal. Das jetzt registrierte Neutrino hatte aber eine horizontale Flugbahn. Weil der Detektor erst zum Teil aufgebaut ist, konnten sie allerdings seinen Ursprungsort nicht feststellen.
Neben der ungewöhnlichen Flugrichtung hatte das Teilchen aber auch sehr viel mehr Energie als alles, was bisher auf der Erde gemessen wurde. Das KM3NeT-Team schätzte die Energie des ursprünglichen Neutrinos auf 220 Petaelektronenvolt.
Als Ursprungsort für das Teilchen käme möglicherweise ein supermassereiches Schwarzes Loch in Frage, das stark magnetisiert ist. Sein Wirbelfeld kann Teilchen wie Protonen oder kleine Kerne auf enorme Geschwindigkeiten beschleunigen. In Zukunft wird KM3NeT ein System einsetzen, das andere Beobachter innerhalb von nur 20 Sekunden nach der Entdeckung eines hochenergetischen Neutrinos über den möglichen Ursprungsort informiert, damit sie dort nach kosmischen Ereignissen suchen können, die die Quelle dafür sein könnten.

articles.title: Anant Ambani launches national initiative for animal welfare
articles.text:
Anant Ambani launches national initiative for animal welfare
Champions of Care by Vantara brings together over 50 organisations to support around two million community animals across India every year.
On World Animal Day, Anant M Ambani, Executive Director of Reliance Industries Limited and founder of Vantara, launched Champions of Care, an initiative aimed at supporting community animal welfare efforts across India through long-term assistance to local organisations.
The initiative brings together more than 50 animal welfare organisations from across India. It aims to support organisations working with street animals such as dogs, cats, working donkeys and horses, and abandoned cattle. It will also provide assistance for veterinary hospitals, mobile rescue units, feeding programmes and rehabilitation efforts. The initiative is expected to reach about two million animals every year.
The announcement followed a two-day meeting at Vantara in Jamnagar, attended by representatives of participating non-profits and eight members of the Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI).
The initiative will provide support to local animal rescue organisations, including medical equipment, ambulances, diagnostic tools and staff training. It will also fund infrastructure upgrades such as solar power systems, rainwater harvesting facilities and designated quarantine areas to support the day-to-day operations of participating organisations.
“Every day, there are countless people who quietly care for animals in need, often with limited resources and little recognition,” said Anant Ambani. “Through Champions of Care, we hope to stand alongside this work, strengthen the care available to community animals, and help build a more compassionate India.”
SP Gupta, a member and former chairman of the AWBI, highlighted Ambani’s focus on listening directly to rescuers to deliver solutions.
The network is designed to keep growing, with plans to bring more animal welfare partners on board in the coming years.

articles.title: The biggest AI risk may already be inside your company
articles.text:
Half of South Africans surveyed have bypassed their employers’ restrictions on artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the past year, exposing companies to a new security risk that traditional cyber controls may struggle to contain.
Prejlin Naidoo, partner at Oliver Wyman, a global strategy and risk consultancy, shared the findings at a cybersecurity roundtable hosted by Marsh, an international risk and insurance adviser, in Johannesburg on Tuesday.
They point to a growing problem for companies racing to adopt generative AI. The corporate security perimeter now extends beyond networks and devices to employees and the AI tools they use.
Naidoo said the Oliver Wyman Forum Global Consumer Survey 2026 South Africa report is based on responses from 903 South Africans. The report, due to be released in November, found that 50% of those surveyed had bypassed enterprise AI restrictions over the past year. Naidoo said the figure was likely to be underreported.
Naidoo said the figure was likely to be underreported. “This creates an entirely new kind of threat perimeter,” Naidoo said.
Companies have traditionally approached cybersecurity by securing their networks, devices and approved applications. But employees can now bypass those controls by copying company information into public AI tools such as large language models (LLMs).
Sensitive information can therefore leave a company’s controlled environment without a conventional cyberattack. The risk may also not be concentrated among junior employees. “When we dig into the data, managers are actually much more likely to be guilty of this than their teams,” Naidoo said.
Managers often have access to more sensitive commercial, financial and customer information, potentially making unauthorised AI use a bigger data-security problem than companies assume, said Naidoo.
The problem also persists even where employees have access to enterprise AI tools. Other research points to a similar gap between AI adoption and workplace preparedness. A 2025 Kaspersky study found that 72.5% of professionals surveyed in South Africa use AI tools for work, but only 30% had received training on the cybersecurity risks associated with AI.
Naidoo said communications, media and technology companies have some of the best access to enterprise AI tools in South Africa. Yet 31% of employees in the sector still use unapproved AI tools, compared with 34% across other industries.
He warned that simply giving employees approved AI products or blocking unauthorised ones may not be enough to control how businesses use AI.
The issue is also moving beyond data security to the reliability of AI-produced work. Naidoo said 35% of people surveyed had seen AI-generated work passed off as human work, raising questions about the provenance and reliability of information entering corporate systems.
“Those are two really important areas that I think we need to watch,” Naidoo said, referring to employees sharing sensitive company data with AI tools and the integrity of AI-generated work.
Consumer adoption creates another layer of risk as people become more comfortable letting AI make decisions for them. Naidoo stated that consumer trust in AI has increased fourfold in Oliver Wyman’s research, from 11% in 2023 to 44% now.
At the same time, 41% of people surveyed said they would be comfortable allowing an AI agent to place an order on their behalf. That growing trust creates new opportunities for businesses. It also expands ways AI can interact with company systems, customer information and transactions.
The discussion at the Marsh cybersecurity roundtable also highlighted why AI-related risks cannot be separated from broader cyber resilience. Marsh Africa and South Africa chief executive officer (CEO) Spiros Fatouros said recent cyber incidents involving South African insurance companies showed how attackers can gain access through suppliers and partners rather than directly attacking a targeted company’s systems.
“The key message is that cyber resilience can no longer be viewed solely as an internal IT issue,” Fatouros said.
He argued that companies need to consider the security of suppliers, partners, cloud providers and other organisations connected to their operations. The same principle applies to employees and the AI tools they use.
Keletjo Chiloane, a career and workforce consulting executive at Marsh, said companies also need to redesign the division of work between humans and machines rather than simply inserting AI into existing processes.
“AI is not just a technology implementation. It changes how work gets done, which means organisations need to rethink roles, responsibilities and the skills people need to work alongside these systems,” she said.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Retailers are pulling back from self-checkout after years of theft, errors, and questionable time savings
articles.text:
Connecting the dots: The retail and tech industries have long promoted self-checkout as a way to speed up transactions and lower labor costs, but its popularity might be waning. Years of data suggest that the technology increases losses and doesn't actually save much time.
Only about one-third of surveyed retailers plan to invest in self-checkout technology this year, significantly fewer than in 2025, according to an annual retail industry report. While self-checkout lanes have always frustrated some customers, major retailers have only recently either stepped away from the technology or at least slowed down its deployment.
Of 340 retail operators surveyed in 2026's Voice of the Retail Industry Survey, only 36% say they plan to invest in self-checkout, down seven percentage points from last year. Self-checkout was the least popular technology and the only one to see lower interest YoY. Other investments, such as automated invoices, electronic shelf labels, and accounting software, attracted at least 40% of surveyed retailers.
Prior data on self-checkout suggests why: It largely hasn't delivered on its promises and may have revealed why retail still needs trained cashiers.
Many likely believe self-checkout saves time compared to a cashier lane, but the opposite may be true. Shortly after the practice began in the late 1980s, Kroger group vice president Donald F. Dufek told The Oklahoman that self-checkout actually takes shoppers longer, but shoppers believe the process is faster because they are the ones scanning items.
Compared with experienced staff, customers typically scan items more slowly and are more likely to make mistakes, thus holding up lines. Many shoppers also likely have stories of machines not scanning items properly. A 2021 survey showed that more than two-thirds of shoppers have experienced issues at self-checkout lanes. The technology also increases retailers' losses from theft, both accidental and deliberate.
Because of these and other issues, retailers still must hire staff to watch and assist customers in self-checkout lanes. In recent years, Walmart, Costco, and Kroger have increased staff involvement in self-checkout lanes. Meanwhile, Dollar General removed self-checkout from 12,000 stores in 2024. Around the same time, Target limited self-checkout lanes to 10 items or fewer because they are most useful for customers buying small numbers of items.
Amazon also famously tried to offload retail labor before changing course. In 2022, the company debuted grocery stores without cashiers or checkout lines but abandoned the idea two years later after admitting it had simply passed the work on to remote cashiers in India.

articles.title: ASUS Republic of Gamers Ships ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Router
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 6th 2026
ASUS Republic of Gamers Ships ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Router
ASUS Republic of Gamers (ROG) today announced that the ROG Rapture GT-BN98 quad-band WiFi 8 gaming router is now shipping, delivering ultra-high reliability and next-generation performance for demanding network environments. In today's multi-device environments driven by gaming, streaming, and smart home usage, users need more than peak speed. They need stable, predictable, and efficient connectivity. The GT-BN98 delivers this through WiFi 8 technology, intelligent bandwidth optimization, and enhanced network visibility, ensuring consistent performance even under heavy loads.
WiFi 8 Ultra-High Reliability
The ROG Rapture GT-BN98 delivers up to 25,000 Mbps of bandwidth and features advanced technologies such as new MCS rates, UEQM, and NPCA for improved throughput and coverage. Unlike previous WiFi generations focused on peak speed, WiFi 8 prioritizes ultra-high reliability by improving performance consistency across varying signal conditions. It reduces sudden speed drops and enhances stability in real-world environments, especially in multi-device and long-range scenarios. Users experience smoother and more stable connections across the entire home, with less performance fluctuation over distance. Whether gaming, streaming, or using IoT devices, connections remain consistent and reliable.Adaptive Quality of Experience
Adaptive QoE dynamically allocates bandwidth based on real-time network conditions and application demands, optimizing traffic across gaming, streaming, and background tasks. Traditional Quality of Service relies on static rules, while adaptive QoE continuously adjusts in real time. This ensures that network resources are always allocated efficiently, even in highly congested or multi-tasking environments. Users enjoy smooth and uninterrupted performance, even when multiple high-bandwidth activities occur simultaneously. Gaming remains responsive while streaming and downloads can continue without disruption.
WiFi Insight
WiFi Insight is an interactive feature available through the ROG Rapture GT-BN98's web interface that continuously scans both WiFi and non-WiFi interference across all bands and provides clear, visualized reports on network health. It goes beyond basic channel scanning by enabling full-spectrum analysis, real-time channel switching, and 24-hour event tracking. This ASUS-exclusive feature provides deep visibility into hidden interference sources that are typically difficult to detect. By automating both detection and optimization, WiFi Insight ensures stable and efficient connections, even in congested environments where traditional routers may struggle. Users gain a clear, visualized understanding of their network conditions, making it easier to identify and resolve interference issues. With greater transparency and automated optimization, users can enjoy more stable connections and smoother performance across gaming, streaming, and everyday use.
GTNet
GTNet is a third-party service integrated into the ROG Rapture GT-BN98's web interface that analyzes real-time network conditions and dynamically routes traffic through the most reliable path to game servers, prioritizing lower latency over the shortest distance. Traditional routing selects the shortest path, which may not always deliver the best performance. GTNet intelligently evaluates latency and congestion to find the fastest route, improving overall connection quality. Gamers benefit from reduced latency, fewer lag spikes, and more stable connections, resulting in smoother and more competitive gaming experiences.
Extreme wired connectivity
Two 10G ports and four 2.5G ports provide the ROG Rapture GT-BN98 with high-speed wired connectivity, supporting advanced network configurations and bandwidth-intensive applications. As internet speeds and device demands increase, high-speed wired connectivity becomes essential. This configuration offers both flexibility and future-ready performance for modern networking setups.
ASUS AiProtection
Lastly, ASUS routers offer AiProtection with enhanced always-on security, featuring built-in ad and tracker blocking, malicious site filtering, and infected device blocking for safer browsing. These features provide continuous, real-time defenses across all connected devices. By automatically blocking threats and unwanted content at the network level, they help ensure a safer, more private, and worry-free online experience for everyday use.

articles.title: Elon Musk é tema de documentário que promete mostrar o que existe por trás do bilionário
articles.text:
Um novo documentário de quatro horas sobre Elon Musk promete ir além da imagem pública do bilionário para investigar o homem por trás de algumas das empresas mais importantes do setor de tecnologia e da crescente influência política que ele conquistou nos últimos anos.
Dirigido pelo premiado documentarista Alex Gibney, Musk estreou no Festival de Cinema de Veneza e será posteriormente dividido em dois episódios de duas horas para exibição pela HBO.
O filme levou cerca de três anos para ser produzido e começou como uma investigação sobre o homem mais rico do mundo. Ao longo das gravações, porém, a trajetória de Musk ganhou uma dimensão política cada vez maior, especialmente após sua aproximação com Donald Trump.
O próprio Gibney conta que inicialmente não queria fazer um filme sobre Musk. A ideia lhe parecia apenas mais um documentário sobre um homem poderoso e moralmente ambíguo. A percepção mudou quando surgiu a possibilidade de tratar a história como um retrato do poder no século XXI.
Segundo o diretor, a combinação de poder financeiro, inovação e dados permitiu que um novo tipo de indivíduo acumulasse uma influência que antes estava reservada principalmente aos Estados nacionais.
Musk rejeitou o filme desde o início
- A relação entre Musk e Gibney começou mal;
- Quando o documentário foi anunciado, em outubro de 2023, Musk o classificou como um “filme de ataque”, embora praticamente nada da produção tivesse sido filmado naquele momento. Depois, chamou Gibney de “idiota”;
- O diretor respondeu com um trocadilho e, segundo contou posteriormente, esperava que a brincadeira pudesse abrir espaço para uma conversa com Musk e talvez convencê-lo a participar do filme;
- Isso não aconteceu.
Depois da estreia em Veneza, Musk passou a publicar ataques contra a produção. Gibney afirmou que o bilionário estava reagindo de maneira mais organizada do que outros personagens retratados em seus documentários, utilizando advogados e uma rede de contas automatizadas.
Para o diretor, enfrentar Musk também significa lidar com alguém que possui enorme poder financeiro, proximidade com a Casa Branca e uma influência extraordinária sobre o setor espacial.
O documentário questiona a própria história de Musk
Parte do filme revisita acontecimentos conhecidos da trajetória do bilionário, mas apresenta uma interpretação diferente para alguns deles.
Um dos episódios examinados é a história do quarto lançamento da SpaceX, depois de três fracassos consecutivos. A narrativa tradicional apresenta aquele voo como um momento decisivo em que Musk estaria próximo da falência caso o foguete não funcionasse.
Segundo o documentário, porém, essa versão seria um mito: a NASA já estava aprovando bilhões de dólares em financiamento, independentemente do resultado daquele lançamento.
O filme também aborda a relação de Musk com a Tesla e questiona alguns dos elementos que ajudaram a construir sua imagem de engenheiro visionário.
Outro episódio envolve o sistema de assistência ao motorista da Tesla. O documentário apresenta imagens de um acidente no qual um veículo atravessa uma interseção e atinge um carro estacionado, matando uma mulher que estava deitada próxima ao veículo. A produção também questiona a maneira como dados relacionados ao acidente teriam sido tratados pela empresa.
O lado pessoal de Musk
A produção também mergulha em aspectos menos conhecidos da vida pessoal do bilionário.
Justine Musk, primeira esposa de Elon, fala sobre a maneira como pessoas do círculo do empresário se referiam às mães de seus filhos e descreve uma espécie de “linha de montagem” para a geração de crianças.
O documentário também apresenta o relato de Ashley St Clair, que teve um filho com Musk. Segundo ela, um representante do bilionário a teria incentivado a assinar um acordo de confidencialidade em troca de US$ 40 milhões (aproximadamente R$ 214 milhões) em pagamentos relacionados ao sustento da criança.
Em uma mensagem de voz apresentada no filme, ela teria sido alertada de que as coisas não terminavam bem para mulheres que escolhiam recorrer à Justiça contra Musk.
A transformação política
Um dos argumentos centrais de Musk é que a guinada política do bilionário teria sido motivada também por interesses pessoais e empresariais. Segundo o filme, Musk e suas empresas eram alvo de pelo menos 32 investigações conduzidas por 11 órgãos governamentais.
Nesse contexto, a aproximação com Trump é apresentada como parte de uma estratégia para proteger seus negócios.
Musk destinou US$ 300 milhões (aproximadamente R$ 1,6 bilhão) à campanha presidencial de Trump em 2024 e posteriormente entrou no governo, liderando o Departamento de Eficiência Governamental, o DOGE.
A passagem pelo governo durou poucos meses, mas, nesse período, Musk participou de cortes profundos na USAID e na ajuda externa dos Estados Unidos.
Para Gibney, a relação entre os dois acabou formando uma espécie de simbiose: Musk tinha dinheiro para ajudar a manter Trump no poder, enquanto Trump tinha poder para proteger os interesses financeiros de Musk.
Leia mais:
- Trump reúne líderes de tecnologia e anuncia acordo sobre segurança de IA
- SpaceXAI vai virar SpaceXSI após nova proposta de Donald Trump
- Elon Musk ajudará Pentágono a definir armas das próximas guerras
O homem que diz querer salvar a humanidade
O documentário também investiga a justificativa que Musk costuma apresentar para seus projetos.
O bilionário afirma repetidamente que suas ações têm como objetivo ampliar a presença da humanidade além da Terra e preservar a chamada “luz da consciência” mesmo diante de uma eventual destruição do planeta.
Gibney questiona até que ponto essa visão é genuína ou conveniente.
O diretor compara Musk ao magnata do aço Andrew Carnegie, que morreu em 1919. Segundo Gibney, ambos compartilham a crença de que estão excepcionalmente posicionados para salvar a civilização.
A ideia, argumenta o cineasta, também funciona como uma justificativa para a acumulação de riqueza e poder: se alguém acredita estar trabalhando por uma causa superior, seus próprios interesses podem ser apresentados como parte de uma missão maior.
Entre conquistas reais e promessas
O documentário não ignora as conquistas de Musk.
Gibney reconhece que empresas associadas ao bilionário produziram tecnologias importantes, citando os satélites da Starlink, os foguetes da SpaceX e os próprios carros da Tesla.
O problema, segundo ele, está na distância entre essas realizações e algumas das promessas feitas por Musk.
Como exemplos, temos a promessa de carros totalmente autônomos, a ideia de estabelecer uma população humana em Marte dentro de uma década, robôs para todas as casas e até centros de processamento de dados instalados no espaço.
Para Gibney, é justamente essa combinação de conquistas concretas e promessas que ajuda a explicar o poder financeiro de Musk.
“É a mentira que faz ele ganhar dinheiro”, afirma o diretor, resumindo sua interpretação de que Musk teria desenvolvido uma habilidade extraordinária para convencer o mercado a financiar projetos baseados em promessas que nem sempre se concretizam.
Um homem cada vez mais irritado
A imagem apresentada pelo documentário também é a de um Musk progressivamente mais agressivo. O bilionário passou de discursos sobre a preservação da humanidade para manifestações cada vez mais focadas na defesa da civilização europeia e estadunidense contra uma suposta “invasão”.
O filme também aborda o apoio de Musk ao partido alemão de extrema direita AfD e sua participação em eventos ligados ao ativista britânico Tommy Robinson.
Enquanto isso, Musk passa horas atacando adversários reais e imaginários — e, mais recentemente, o próprio Gibney, diz o The New World Substack.
Depois de três anos tentando entender o bilionário, o diretor chegou a uma conclusão particularmente dura.
Um investidor do Vale do Silício, entrevistado em caráter reservado, teria descrito Musk como “o homem mais miserável que já conheci”.
Para Gibney, a combinação de riqueza e poder não parece ter produzido felicidade. Ao contrário, o documentário termina sugerindo que, por trás da imagem do bilionário capaz de transformar setores inteiros da economia, existe um homem profundamente infeliz.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Google prepara una alternativa real al Face ID para los Pixel
articles.text:
Desde que Apple lanzó Face ID hace casi una década, ningún móvil Android ha podido acercársele. El desbloqueo facial eficiente parece ser una de las funciones negadas para quienes no poseen un iPhone. La buena noticia es que Google ya trabaja en una solución definitiva que llegará en la próxima actualización de Android 17.
Hace unos meses surgieron rumores de que Google está desarrollando una alternativa real al Face ID para sus dispositivos Pixel. Los móviles de la tecnológica cuentan con desbloqueo facial y certificación biométrica de Clase 3, que protege pagos y aplicaciones bancarias. El problema es que su rendimiento depende mucho de que te encuentres en un área iluminada.
Google está desarrollando una alternativa que mejora la autenticación facial con poca luz. De acuerdo con Android Authority, la beta 1 de Android 17 QPR3 incluye referencias a Face Active Illumination, una función dentro de Face Unlock. El código incluye referencias a un interruptor general y una escala de brillo con tres niveles que se pueden ajustar a través de un control deslizante. También se incluyen permisos para activarlo en la oscuridad, durante tu horario de descanso y cuando activas la función No molestar o al conducir.
Aunque la filtración no menciona la pieza de hardware responsable de esta iluminación, lo más lógico sería pensar que el Pixel usaría la luz de la pantalla. El reporte menciona que la función se encuentra en una fase muy temprana, ya que los desarrolladores apenas consiguieron activarla y su interfaz está casi vacía. La mayoría de los textos de la app están ofuscados, excepto el de No molestar.
Project Toscana, la alternativa de Android al Face ID
Face Active Illumination podría estar relacionado con Project Toscana, una iniciativa de Google que busca resolver el desbloqueo facial de una vez por todas. El gigante tecnológico ya ha probado varias fórmulas, pero hasta ahora ninguna le ha dado resultado. Si hacemos memoria, el Pixel 4 usaba radar e infrarrojos para un reconocimiento 3D, mientras que el Pixel 7 volvió a lo básico usando la cámara frontal para abrir la pantalla de bloqueo.
Project Toscana es el siguiente intento para renovar la autenticación facial en los Pixel y Chromebooks. Hace unos meses, una filtración reveló que esta alternativa ya conseguía desbloquear los dispositivos con una velocidad equiparable a la de Face ID en distintas condiciones de iluminación. Según el reporte, Google usó un Pixel con una cámara perforada y dos Chromebooks con cámaras externas, cuyas placas estaban a la vista.
La filtración no mencionaba nada sobre la tecnología, aunque Google seguiría el camino del iPhone. Con Face ID, Apple implementó un sistema infrarrojo que resulta invisible y el usuario no tiene que decidir cuándo se activa. Google quiere que sus Pixel se desbloqueen al momento sin añadir luz o recortar la pantalla para añadir un sensor.
Por el momento no existe información oficial sobre Project Toscana o Face Active Illumination. Es probable que este último sea un paso intermedio antes de implementar una tecnología que ofrezca las bondades de Face ID a los usuarios de Android.

articles.title: Learn all about scaling, fundraising, founder how-tos, and more at TechCrunch Founder Summit, November 4 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
There isn’t a single manual to read or prompt to give an LLM that can equip you with the skills and knowledge to build a company. But on November 4, TechCrunch Founder Summit gives founders the next-best thing: A packed day at Boston’s SoWa Power Station, where investors and operators share how they’ve navigated crucial decisions.
The Founder Summit’s agenda is built around core questions every founder eventually has to answer about capital, leadership, and what they’re actually building toward. And each session is designed to build upon each other. Like your startup’s founding team, these sessions work together to drive outcomes.  
This is a breakdown on how the full event agenda fits together, and what you can expect to learn by attending. Keep in mind that tickets are at their lowest price point before they increase on October 16, so this is the ideal moment to grab your seat. You can save $200 on both Investor and Founder passes up until that deadline.
For a limited time, you can also get a second ticket for 50% off, and for even larger groups, there are bundle discounts available to groups of four or more.
Capital: How you raise, and who you raise from
Fundraising advice often stops at “How do I get the term sheet?” This track goes further, because getting a yes is only half of the equation. The other half is making sure it’s the right yes.
Underscore partner Brian Devaney opens with a candid read on today’s fundraising climate, including what investors are actually screening for right now, how founders can differentiate in a crowded market, and the specific moments where founders give up leverage without realizing it.
That’s the part most founders obsess over — as well as who ends up on the cap table once the round closes. This is where Vineet Edupuganti, co-founder and CEO of Cogent Security, picks up the thread. After raising an $11 million round, he learned firsthand that not every check is equal. He’ll walk through how to actually evaluate investors and navigate those trade-offs before you sign, not after.
This all frames fundraising as a two-part decision. First, win the leverage in the room, then spend it wisely on the right partners. Founders who only solve the first part often find themselves fighting their own cap table later.
Grab your pass and get all these fundraising insights. Bring your co-founder at 50% off.
Leadership: When the job changes, so does the team you need
No founder stays the same kind of leader forever. After all, the skills that get a company to its initial customers rarely match what’s needed when its customer list expands and the employee count grows. This track tackles that shift from two angles: the founder’s evolution, and the decisions on employees that either support or sabotage it.
HubSpot co-founder and Sequoia partner Brian Halligan has experienced this arc many times, first by building through HubSpot’s own stages of growth and now by advising founders doing the same from the investor’s seat. He’ll unpack how the CEO job transforms at each stage, the leadership habits that stop working once a company outgrows them, and how to keep reinventing yourself without losing what made you effective in the first place.
But a founder’s evolution doesn’t happen in isolation — it’s constrained by who’s actually in the building. NEA partner Melissa Taunton brings the hiring half of that equation, breaking down how early team decisions quietly set the ceiling on a company’s culture, speed, and ability to execute long before anyone notices the cracks. The founders who scale smoothly, in her experience, are the ones who treat early hires as architecture decisions, not just headcount.
Get your ticket, learn the skills every founder needs, and bring a teammate along.
Building for the future: AI, market fit, and knowing a winner when you see one
This is the track where the agenda gets most forward-looking, and it’s really three questions in sequence: What are you building, do people actually want it, and will it be big enough to matter?
7AI co-founder and CEO Lior Div starts with the “what.” Adding AI features to an existing product is a tactical decision, and building a company where AI is the foundation from day one is a structural one, touching everything from team composition to how go-to-market actually works. He’ll explore what founders need to rethink when AI isn’t a feature, but the premise.
Next, Kent Bennett from Bessemer Venture Partners tackles the question, “Do people want it?” This is a necessary gut check right after a session on ambitious AI-native building: It’s easy to mistake early traction or investor enthusiasm for real product-market fit. He’ll unpack the signals that genuinely indicate fit and the metrics that mislead founders into scaling too early.
Finally, TDK Ventures investment director Tina Tosukhowong zooms out to the category level with an explanation of the firm’s “King of the Hill” framework, which is the discipline top investors use to judge whether a company isn’t just viable, but also positioned to define its entire category on economics, scalability, and timing. It’s the lens that explains why some well-built, well-funded products never break out, while others soar to success.
Get ahead of the race to make the most of AI tools to build and register today.
The priceless lessons from a founder who’s seen it all
It’s one thing to hear these ideas in the abstract. HqO co-founder and CEO Chase Garbarino closes the agenda as a working example of all three tracks at once. After all, he’s raised $200 million from the right investors, scaled a team across more than 30 countries, and built a category-defining company, all without ever relocating from Boston.
He’ll break down the real advantages and disadvantages of building outside a major hub, and what every founder outside Silicon Valley should know before assuming they need to be somewhere else.
The Summit doesn’t stop when the sessions end
The agenda is the backbone of Founder Summit, but the day is also built around forming connections that can kickstart a nascent venture or lead to a new investor. Roundtable discussions dig deeper into the Summit’s themes in smaller, more candid settings, where you can actively workshop with experienced startup community members. And the Braindate networking app pairs founders with investors and peers facing the same problems outlined in the agenda.
“Founder Summit Week” runs November 1-7, with Side Events happening across Boston for anyone who wants more than one day with the startup community.
By joining Founder Summit on November 4, you’ll leave with a lot more than helpful notes — you’ll leave with a working framework for the capital, leadership, and product decisions that would’ve otherwise taken months of trial and error to figure out on your own. Register now before prices increase on October 16. Bring your co-founder or partner with you at 50% off. Or, save even more by bringing your cohort of four more.

articles.title: Xbox has secured exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights
articles.text:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told employees that Microsoft is getting ready to do something around Grand Theft Auto VI that “no other platform holder is doing” during an employee all-hands this morning. According to sources familiar with Microsoft’s plans, Xbox has managed to land a deal for the exclusive game streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI.
Xbox has secured exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights
The streaming rights come in November, when Microsoft is opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming.
The deal will mean only Xbox Cloud Gaming can stream Grand Theft Auto VI to players at launch, but it’s not clear how long the agreement will be in place. Rockstar Games still hasn’t announced a PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI, so this deal will allow Xbox to market its Xbox Cloud Gaming service to PC players who would otherwise need an Xbox Series X / S or PS5 console.
News of the streaming rights comes around a month after Microsoft announced some major changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming. From November, the same month Grand Theft Auto VI releases, Microsoft is limiting streaming hours to just 15 hours for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for Premium subscribers, and just five hours for Game Pass Essential.
Microsoft is also opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming with a pay-as-you-go option next month, rather than being limited to Game Pass subscriptions. The pay-as-you-go option is perfectly timed for Grand Theft Auto VI, allowing those who don’t own an Xbox, or who primarily play from a phone, to stream the game by paying for a bundle of hours.
During the Xbox all-hands, Sharma also told employees that Project Helix, the next generation of Xbox hardware, will be a “family of devices” and that Microsoft will partner with others on some of those devices. Sharma first called Helix a family of devices last month in an interview, after Microsoft and AMD announced a “strategic multi-year partnership” last year to work together on “a portfolio of devices,” including Microsoft’s next-generation Xbox console.

articles.title: MeOut Summit 2026: Meet the Pitch Marathon contestants | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Startups from across Europe are set to take part in an exclusive Pitch Marathon at the MeOut Summit 2026, held at Budapest’s Akvárium on 25–26 November 2026.
The event will feature a Pitch Marathon wherein selected startups will present on the Summit’s second stage, showcasing their ventures and receiving direct feedback from a panel of venture capital and ecosystem representatives.
Unlike a traditional pitch competition, the Pitch Marathon has no rankings, prizes or winner. Instead, it offers founders a platform to introduce their companies to an international audience while gaining candid, investor-led feedback on their business, positioning and pitch.
Participating startups
Ambr Institute is a Norway-based startup founded in 2022 which converts fragmented patient and laboratory data into disease-risk scores and simulated treatment outcomes within seconds, building on research and clinical data from more than 600,000 patients.
Founded in Finland in 2026, Arki Life is a digital housing-management platform connecting property managers, housing boards, residents and service providers.
AssureDrop, a UK-based startup founded in 2024, is making patient-derived organoid testing scalable. Its proprietary platform enables researchers and drug developers to generate up to 10× more drug-response data from scarce patient samples, helping them test more treatment options and identify the most promising candidates faster. By miniaturising each experiment, it can also reduce the cost per data point by up to 3×, while helping reduce experimental waste and reliance on animal models.
Germany-based Aurolicht systems, founded in 2026, combines facility-scale AI data-centre infrastructure with a recurring grid-to-chip software and control layer. Its business model mixes licensed and reference hardware designs, engineering integration and subsystem partnerships with longer-term software subscriptions, licensing royalties and services tied to ongoing infrastructure operations.
Founded in Hungary in 2026, azta.ai is an AI-powered legal and tax research platform for tax advisers, accountants and lawyers. It indexes more than 22 million primary-source documents across 24 European jurisdictions, answers professional questions in natural language and provides article-level citations linking directly to underlying legislation.
bm25 labs is a Czech startup founded in 2026 developing Industrial Troubleshooter, an on-premise AI agent for diagnosing production-line equipment faults in real time. It reasons over manufacturers’ PLC code, schematics and live process data, with planned edge deployment so proprietary control logic can remain securely on-site.
Slovakia-based Coverally, founded in 2023, replaces traditional rental security deposits with a digital, card-based alternative. Its platform provides deposit pre-authorisation using Coverally-backed funds and manages verification, payments, rental requests and incidents, allowing customers to rent high-value assets without tying up their own cash in deposits.
Founded in Poland in 2025, Droppey Mind is building an enterprise control plane for governed autonomous physical work. Its platform sits above validated autonomous systems, translating operational intent into permitted, capability-matched execution and verified outcomes, with an initial focus on warehouse and retail environments requiring controlled automation.
FraudSpect is a Hungary-based startup founded in 2026 building a fraud-intelligence platform for screening companies, websites and crypto wallets. Its database combines regulatory registers, sanctions lists and investigated scam cases to identify licensing, sanctions or fraud risks, with subscriptions, data feeds and APIs available for institutional users.
Founded in Hungary in 2024, GenuForm AI is a MedTech startup developing an AI-based solution to optimise knee-cartilage transplantation. The company aims to support more effective treatment planning and clinical decision-making around cartilage repair and also plans to provide cartilage tissue for use in transplantation procedures.
Austria-based infrared.city, founded in 2023, provides an AI climate-intelligence layer for cities and buildings. Its models simulate wind, heat, solar exposure and light within seconds, helping architects, engineers and infrastructure operators assess environmental performance. The technology is sold through professional subscriptions and enterprise licences.
IrisInfosec is a Czechia-based startup founded in 2026 developing an automated privacy and consent-management platform. Its technology is designed to help organisations manage compliance requirements across major European regulatory frameworks.
Founded in Austria in 2024, Main Sequence is building a control layer between AI code generation and enterprise execution. Its platform creates governed, standardised development environments for AI coding assistants and can deploy APIs, pipelines and applications automatically, with role-based access, audit trails and metered compute built in.
Belgium-based MEP Analytics, founded in 2025, describes its product as “the digital twin of EU politics.” The company is developing a technology platform focused on modelling, structuring and analysing European political activity, with the aim of making complex EU institutional dynamics easier for users to monitor and understand.
moonlight is a Slovakian startup founded in 2026 developing an AI health layer that turns a 30–60 second smartphone face scan into measures such as heart rate, heart-rate variability, breathing and personalised recovery insights. Its model combines a freemium consumer subscription with SDK licensing for digital-health and enterprise partners.
Founded in the United States in 2021, NaviSavi is a travel-content platform with 250,000+ rights-cleared videos from over 6,000 creators across 190+ countries. Its technology organises and tags this library so travel brands, platforms and AI systems can discover relevant content for marketing, commerce, media and bookings.
France-based Proskope, founded in 2022, is developing TumorScreen, an immune-cell biosensor for cancer detection. The point-of-care blood test is designed to detect functional changes in circulating immune cells and return results in under an hour, using a pay-per-use model for laboratories, hospitals and clinics.
R-Space is an Austrian space-technology company founded in 2021 developing Argus, a satellite platform for real-time Earth observation and surveillance. The system combines data acquisition, analysis and rapid decision-making technologies to provide timely situational awareness for users that need faster access to actionable information from orbit.
Founded in Austria in 2021, sendance is building a scalable sensor and data platform that helps manufacturers turn assistive devices into connected, data-generating products. Its technology supports the development and operation of smart devices while enabling manufacturers to create new services and business models based on data and AI.
Hungary-based Sorank, founded in 2025, is a subscription SaaS AI SEO platform that helps businesses rank higher on Google and get cited in AI search engines such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity.
Umax Health is a UK startup founded in 2023 combining a wearable device with an AI platform to enrich mental healthcare with physiological and contextual data. It synchronises cardiovascular, electrodermal, temperature and motion signals with patient-reported and therapy information, giving clinicians a longitudinal view to support more personalised care.
Founded in 2024 and based across Finland and Spain, WorkGuardAi is an AI-powered SaaS platform for construction-site monitoring. It uses LiDAR data and machine learning to measure progress from site imagery and compare it automatically with DWG engineering plans, relying on third-party cameras, drones and sensors rather than proprietary hardware.
Explore the programme in full
With two stages, 50+ speakers, the Global Startup Awards Grand Finale, startup pitches and a growing calendar of side events, the MeOut Summit 2026 is bringing together multiple parts of the European startup ecosystem under one roof.
The full programme is live and will continue to evolve as more speakers, sessions and activities are announced.
Explore the MeOut Summit agenda in full and book your tickets here to enjoy two days in Budapest.

articles.title: All-electric camping gets a solar upgrade: The 2027 Pebble Flow
articles.text:
There is, I think, a pent-up demand for bringing electrification to camping. Anyone who’s had their sleep disturbed by the sound of someone else’s generator running at night would probably agree.
Certainly, any time we cover an electric van, comments are filled with people wondering if and when a camper conversion might appear. Kia showed off such a concept a couple of years ago, as did Winnebago, and Volkswagen is adding a camper trim to its electric ID. Buzz. And then there’s the world of trailers. Colorado Teardrop sadly didn’t make it, and some other electrified trailers remain in development. But for a couple of years, you’ve been able to buy the Pebble Flow. And for 2027, it’s getting an update.
Introduced in 2025, the streamlined Flow is built atop a 45 kWh LFP battery pack that, for 2027, can be recharged by up to 4 kW of solar panels, which Flow says should be sufficient to generate more electricity than you’ll use in an average day of camping. Earlier Flows could be specced with an optional 1.1 kWh panel on the roof; the new kit adds another 2 kWh via four portable panels.
The Flow has a gross vehicle weight of 6,800 lbs.
