Usefully, the LFP battery is bidirectional, with an output of up to 12 kW, which means you can even use it to charge your EV in a pinch.
If you don’t want to wait several days, the pack will AC charge at up to 6.6 kW and will even DC fast charge (0–80 percent in less than a hour, Pebble says). And it can also regeneratively brake, recapturing up to 42 kW thanks to the in-wheel electric motors that help push the trailer along as you tow. And for 2027, Pebble has added a boost setting to this assist, which provides 54 hp (40 kW) of assistance rather than just easing the slack.
This being the mid-2020s, of course there’s some degree of automation, controlled by an updated version of Pebble’s operating system. The onboard Nvidia Orin processor and four surround cameras, plus those powered wheels, mean that the Flow can see your hitch ball and couple itself, plus you can use an iPad app to maneuver it remotely to park it at your chosen site. You can even remotely activate the dumping process for the black water tank.
Of course, all that technology means this is not a budget-level travel trailer; it starts at $159,000 for the Magic Pack or $189,000 for the Founders Edition.
Jonathan is the Automotive Editor at Ars Technica. He has a BSc and PhD in Pharmacology. In 2014 he decided to indulge his lifelong passion for the car by leaving the National Human Genome Research Institute and launching Ars Technica's automotive coverage. He lives in Washington, DC.
Also, for what is certainly a low-volume vehicle, they've got to amortize all the production equipment.
Having done a very small manufacturing business, oh man the prices we could've lowered if we had higher volumes. If you know you're making 50k widgets, you can buy a machine that'll make each of them for like 10x less. If your entire production run is likely to be 500 units, you're not going to be able to purchase machinery that only has an ROI after 10k units.
This comes up in another rich-man's hobby: general aviation. So many plane startups with good ideas, but if they can't hit their production numbers then they get into a high-price -> low sales -> horrendous amortization -> higher prices death spiral. So everyone just buys and meticulously maintains ancient cessnas.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 6, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 6, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, October 6, 2026.
YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Why keeping children off social media may not be enough to keep them safe
Designing a safer and more responsible digital ecosystem for children in India requires a balanced approach combining strict legal accountability, better content moderation by platforms, parental controls, and active digital literacy.
Harmanpreet Kaur steps down from India women's team captaincy
Indian women's cricket team captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from her position in all three formats. Harmanpreet says she has done her duty as a leader and is now ready to play for the love of the game again.
Funding news
Beyond Appliances raises Rs 110 Cr in Series B round led by Fireside Ventures
Kitchen appliances brand Beyond Appliances has raised Rs 110 crore in a Series B round of funding led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital and other investors. The Bengaluru-based company will use the funding towards research and development and its new manufacturing plant. The startup will also use the capital to enter new product categories in the kitchen appliances space and strengthen its presence across its existing portfolio.
Read more
Wellness brand SuperMush raises $3M in Series A round led by NDude Labs
Indian healthcare and wellness investment firm NDude Labs has led a $3 million Series A investment in SuperMush, a functional wellness brand focused on research-backed ingredients including nootropics, adaptogens and functional mushrooms. The funding will support product expansion, high-efficacy formulations, team building, and infrastructure.
SuperMush has expanded to more than 1,000 Target stores over the past year and now has a retail footprint exceeding 2,000 stores across the US, including Target and Sprouts. Founded in 2022 by Alli Schaper and Brian Friedman, the company has also launched Shilajit, Creatine and Lion’s Mane gummies. SuperMush plans to strengthen its presence across retail, direct-to-consumer and marketplaces as it seeks to establish itself as a leading functional wellness brand.
Lorazzo raises Rs 15 Cr to expand kitchen and bathroom brand
Design-led kitchen and bathroom brand Lorazzo has raised Rs 15 crore in a funding round led by Sauce, with participation from Sprout Venture Partners, Panthera Peak and Alteria Capital. The company plans to use the capital to expand its product portfolio, invest in product development, strengthen its team and grow its online and offline presence across India.
Founded in 2024 by Jatin Luthra and Saurabh Gupta, Lorazzo offers faucets, sinks, sanitaryware, shower systems, bidets and smart toilets. The company said revenues have grown six times over the past 12 months and it is targeting Rs 100 crore in revenue over the next two years.
CureMeAbroad raises $1.1M pre-seed funding
Cross-border healthcare platform CureMeAbroad has raised $1.1 million in a pre-seed round led by healthcare-focused venture capital fund SteerX Ventures, with existing investor AIRA also participating. The funding will support expansion into international patient markets, growth of its hospital network, and development of its technology platform.
Founded in 2025 by Aditya Oza and Mikhail Bohra, CureMeAbroad enables patients to discover and compare hospitals, verify providers, obtain treatment estimates and book healthcare abroad. The platform currently attracts more than 22,500 visitors a month and has a hospital network across six countries.
The company plans to expand its accredited hospital network, strengthen AI capabilities and enter specialties including orthopaedics and oncology. CureMeAbroad is targeting $100 million in annual patient treatment bookings by FY2028.
ReFit Global raises $1M from UAE family office
Refurbished electronics company ReFit Global has raised $1 million from a UAE-based family office, with Bestvantage Investments acting as exclusive adviser. Besides providing capital, the investor will support the company’s international expansion by facilitating access to partners, customers and opportunities across Gulf and African markets.
ReFit plans to deploy the funding towards expanding its retail footprint, strengthening refurbishment capabilities, investing in technology infrastructure, and developing an integrated omnichannel platform. The company operates a network of more than 75 distributors, 2,000 wholesalers, and 50,000 retail outlets across India, alongside 12 ReFit Xpress stores. It reports a 92% refurbishment yield and capabilities extending to L4-level chip repairs. The company plans to deepen its pan-India presence while exploring international expansion.
CurvetAI raises Rs 6 Cr in pre-seed round
AI workspace platform CurvetAI has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed round led by Merak Ventures, with participation from angel investors. Founded in December 2025 by Vivek Dubey and Utkarsh Gupta, CurvetAI enables users to access and combine multiple AI models within a single visual workspace. The platform supports text, image, audio and video models and helps users compare outputs and route tasks to appropriate models.
CurvetAI has more than 100,000 monthly users globally, with India and the US its largest markets, and has started generating revenue. The company will use the capital to strengthen technology infrastructure, expand its team and develop agent-based capabilities. CurvetAI began as an AI tools and prompt discovery platform before evolving into an integrated workspace for using multiple models.
IndigoTex raises Rs 5 Cr in funding round led by IAN Angel Fund
IAN Angel Fund has led a Rs 5 crore funding round in IndigoTex, a deeptech textile startup developing waterless wool finishing technology and wool-blended fabrics. SIDBI, FITT and IIT Delhi Angels also participated.
The funding will support manufacturing and factory setup, sales and operations expansion, commercialisation of IndiWool Denim and washable wool and poly-wool fabrics, R&D and international certifications. IndigoTex’s IndiWool Denim combines the durability of denim with wool’s thermal and comfort properties.
The company is also developing ECOTEX Wool, a technology designed to enable washable wool fabrics and reduce dependence on dry cleaning. Founded in 2024 by Satendra Singh, B S Butola and Dilip Singh, the IIT Delhi-originated startup is exploring markets across Europe, North America, Australia and other cold-climate regions.
Sober & Co raises Rs 75 lakh to expand zero-sugar mixers
Better-for-you mixer brand Sober & Co has raised Rs 75 lakh in a funding round led by Sunaina Bhattacharya and Anuj Dhariwal of New Ground Collective, representing a syndicate of seven angel investors. The capital will support inventory, manufacturing capacity, quick-commerce advertising and team expansion as the brand targets a wider national retail presence. Sober & Co uses monk fruit to sweeten its zero-sugar, zero-calorie mixers, and currently operates across retail, HoReCa, Blinkit and D2C channels.
Other news
Amazon India to set up 50 new Ashray centres
Amazon India plans to set up 50 new Ashray centres across the country. The expansion will take the total number of Ashray centres to 200 and is on track to reach 250 centres by the end of 2026. The company also announced the expansion of its mobile Ashray vans to Bengaluru — the fourth city after Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
Launched in 2024 in Delhi NCR, Ashray is a delivery driver welfare initiative equipped with air-conditioned seating, drinking water, charging points for mobile phones, clean washrooms, first-aid kits, and comfortable resting space. Each centre accommodates 10–15 people at a time, allows free access for up to 30 minutes per visit with convenient parking, and operates year-round from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. at high-footfall locations such as petrol pumps and commercial spaces.
Pine Labs launches unified merchant platform in Singapore
Payments technology company Pine Labs has launched a unified platform for merchants in Singapore combining payment acceptance, acquiring, installment payments and customer engagement. The platform integrates cards and alternative payment methods with bank and brand-backed installment payment plans, allowing merchants to offer flexible checkout options through a single technology layer. Pine Labs is also integrating its Fave consumer payments and engagement app, which offers rewards, cashback and merchant-funded offers.
The company said the unified platform can reduce multi-vendor complexity, improve conversion and support higher-value purchases through instalments while strengthening customer loyalty. Pine Labs already operates across more than 20 markets and serves Singapore brands including Courts, iStudio, CapitaLand and FairPrice. The Singapore launch follows its recent payments expansion in the Philippines through a partnership with GCash.
Spyne’s Vini AI handles 4.5 lakh dealership leads
AI automotive retail technology company Spyne said its Vini AI conversational platform has been deployed across 115 US dealerships, handling more than 4,50,000 leads, 900,000 conversations and 312,000 minutes of customer calls. Spyne estimates that opportunities handled through Vini have been associated with more than $85 million in dealership revenue. The platform helps dealerships manage customer interactions across calls, SMS, website chat and email, including lead follow-up, reactivation and appointment scheduling.
At Paragon Honda, published 30-day results showed $314,000 in recovered revenue and a 48% appointment-to-sale rate. At Bob King Mazda, Vini helped drive 30% higher demand capture and a 12% increase in service appointments. Spyne has integrated Vini with major dealership systems including VinSolutions, Tekion and CDK.
VORAN partners with Italian gyro manufacturer for light aviation
Indian aviation startup VORAN Private Limited, founded by Rajiv Rawat, has entered a strategic collaboration with an Italian gyro manufacturer to develop capabilities across light-aviation design, manufacturing, maintenance, repair and overhaul, skills and innovation. VORAN said its objective is to build an Indian light-aviation ecosystem rather than simply sell or manufacture aircraft.
The company is exploring both gyroplane and helicopter opportunities, subject to technical feasibility and regulatory requirements. Its model seeks to connect Indian engineers, technicians, pilots, MSMEs, manufacturers, training organisations and MRO companies with international aviation expertise. VORAN is also exploring future unmanned or remotely operated gyroplane concepts for specialised applications. The company emphasised that safety, engineering discipline, training, quality and regulatory compliance will form the foundation of the capability-building process.
ServiceNow launches AI Workflow Factory in India
ServiceNow has announced AI Workflow Factory and Autonomous Engineer solutions to help enterprises identify, build and scale AI-powered workflows across fragmented legacy infrastructure. Announced in India at World Forum Mumbai, the solutions are designed to help businesses move from AI experimentation to governed execution. AI Workflow Factory combines process mining, autonomous engineering and application development into a continuous workflow improvement loop, while AI Control Tower provides governance over AI assets, workflows and agent actions.
ServiceNow said the approach can help enterprises scale operations in days rather than months. India is a key market for the company, with enterprise AI investment growing 119% in a year according to its 2026 Enterprise AI Maturity Index. AI Workflow Factory is globally available, while Autonomous Engineer is available through early access.
Pluckk expands clean-label food brand into UK
Digital-first clean FMCG brand Pluckk has expanded into the UK, marking its first major international market entry. The brand is currently available in 17 stores and has secured a 15% share of the protein bar category within its first month. Pluckk plans to reach 100 stores within three months and around 500 stores within a year, while expanding its UK portfolio from a few products to more than 50 SKUs across juices, functional drinks, snacks, salads and other clean-label categories.
The company has built a presence across England and Wales and is evaluating expansion into the UAE, Saudi Arabia and the US. Pluckk expects international markets to contribute 25-30% of overall revenue. In India, the company operates across 50-plus cities and has an annualised revenue run rate exceeding ₹140 crore.
Azim Premji University to host 10th Social Enterprise Idea Challenge
Azim Premji University will host the 10th edition of its National Social Enterprise Idea Challenge on October 9, 2026. The initiative, launched in 2016, gives college and university students an opportunity to develop and present solutions to social and environmental challenges.
Ten teams have been shortlisted for this year’s final, representing institutions including IIT Kharagpur, IIT Madras, IIT Guwahati, IIM Kashipur and Azim Premji University. Their ideas address child safety, rural innovation, waste management, water conservation, healthcare, women’s livelihoods, accessibility and sustainable fashion. Projects include AI-powered child safety platform CipherGuard, leak-detection solution JalRakshak and AI-enabled digital stethoscope JivaScope. The event will feature presentations, a panel discussion, cultural performances and around 45 enterprise stalls. Winning teams will receive grants worth Rs 2 lakh.
Good Monk targets Rs 150 Cr ARR this fiscal year
Preventive nutrition brand Good Monk is on track to close the current financial year with ₹150 crore in annual recurring revenue, representing a 10-fold increase in 15 months, the company said. Repeat-purchase revenue has grown faster than overall revenue, indicating increased customer adoption. Good Monk has also improved its profitability, moving from a negative 50% EBITDA position and targeting EBITDA positivity within the current fiscal year.
More than 65% of its revenue now comes from non-metro cities. Its flagship products have become among the top-ranked multivitamins on Amazon India. The company is expanding into more specific, clinically validated nutrition products across age groups, supported by end-product clinical trials. Good Monk said it will continue focusing on addressing everyday nutrition deficiencies at price points suitable for Indian households.
MathWorks, MapmyIndia collaborate on ADAS development
MathWorks and MapmyIndia Mappls have announced a collaboration to help automotive engineers develop and validate Advanced Driver Assistance Systems for Indian road conditions. The integration combines MapmyIndia’s high-definition maps with MATLAB, Simulink and RoadRunner, allowing engineers to create digital twins of Indian roads and simulate complex traffic scenarios. The companies said Indian roads present unique challenges, including heterogeneous traffic, variable lane behaviour, changing infrastructure, potholes, speed breakers and faded markings. MapmyIndia’s HD maps provide lane-level geometry, traffic controls and detailed local road attributes. The
companies believe the integration will enable earlier virtual validation of ADAS systems, reducing reliance on costly physical testing and accelerating development of solutions designed specifically for India. The collaboration connects location intelligence with Model-Based Design workflows for simulation, algorithm development and system validation.
Cyient launches Intelligent Engineering Solutions business unit
Lifecycle engineering services company Cyient has launched Intelligent Engineering Solutions, a new business unit designed to accelerate technology-led growth and translate AI capabilities into measurable customer outcomes. IES combines data, engineering expertise and business context through CYiNGINE, Cyient’s lifecycle engineering intelligence platform.
The unit will provide solutions across engineering, service, and quality and regulatory lifecycles, covering areas from design and planning to operations. CYiNGINE uses governed industrial data, engineering knowledge and AI to support faster design cycles, predictive maintenance, improved asset availability and faster certification. IES will be led by Harjott Atrii, Chief Business Officer at Cyient. The company said the new unit reflects its strategy of moving beyond project-based services towards long-term, outcome-based partnerships across industrial engineering.
ideaForge launches two variants of ZOLT tactical UAV
Indian drone manufacturer ideaForge Technology has launched two new variants of its multi-role tactical UAV platform, ZOLT Hybrid and ZOLT Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicle (UCAV). The launch expands the company’s portfolio into long-range intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance and UCAV applications. The battery-powered ZOLT UCAV offers 2-3 hours of endurance and 30-50 km line-of-sight transmission, while the hybrid variant combines an IC engine with battery power to provide more than six hours of endurance and up to 100 km transmission. The platform incorporates anti-jam communications, GNSS-denied navigation and onboard intelligence for electronic-warfare environments. ideaForge said ZOLT can support border surveillance, reconnaissance, target acquisition and day-and-night long-range operations. A high-altitude variant is also planned.
Daimler appoints Alejandro Rodriguez Cuadra as DICV R&D head
Daimler India Commercial Vehicles (DICV) has appointed Alejandro Rodriguez Cuadra as Head of Research & Development at DICV. He will additionally serve as Global Head of Engineering Backbone at Mercedes-Benz Trucks. His dual role will focus on strengthening engineering collaboration between Mercedes-Benz Trucks, DICV and Daimler Truck Innovation Centre India, while harmonising global engineering processes. Alejandro has held senior leadership roles in manufacturing engineering, product preparation, ramp-up management and R&D across Germany and Türkiye.
Prabhakar Atla appointed CEO of ALTEN India
Engineering and technology consulting company ALTEN India has appointed Prabhakar Atla as its new CEO, effective October 5, 2026. Atla, who was previously President and Chief Operating Officer of Cyient, succeeds Balaji Viswanathan. He brings more than three decades of experience leading global organisations and managing large P&Ls across sectors including aerospace, communications, rail, energy and semiconductors. Atla has worked across Europe, India, the US, Japan and Australia and previously served as President and CFO at Cyient before becoming President and COO. ALTEN India has more than 8,500 employees across 13 Centres of Excellence in eight Indian cities, supporting sectors including automotive, aerospace, defence, telecom and semiconductors.
BITS Pilani appoints Prof. Mohan Krishnamoorthy as Amaravati director
BITS Pilani has appointed Prof. Mohan Krishnamoorthy as Director of its Amaravati campus, effective January 2027. He will lead the development of the new campus and its academic, research and industry ecosystem, with a focus on emerging technologies including computer science and artificial intelligence. Krishnamoorthy is currently Associate Deputy Vice-Chancellor for India Engagement at RMIT University and Director of Industry Research and Interactive Learning Solutions at BITS Pilani. He previously served as founding CEO of the IIT Bombay-Monash Research Academy and helped establish the UQ-IIT Delhi Research Academy.
At BITS Amaravati, he will focus on AI and data, robotics and advanced manufacturing, digital transformation, life sciences and healthcare, as well as technologies addressing societal and environmental challenges.
Eggoz appoints Boman Irani as brand ambassador
Clean and high-protein egg brand Eggoz has appointed actor Boman Irani as its brand ambassador and launched a new campaign built around the 'Eggoz effect'. Conceptualised by ANC, the campaign uses humour to highlight the role of food in energising everyday moments. The film is set in a sleepy office where Irani's character triggers a burst of activity after lunch, linking the transformation to Eggoz eggs.
The company said the campaign reflects its positioning around nutrition, taste and everyday enjoyment. Eggoz Co-founder and CEO Abhishek Negi said Irani’s warmth and humour made him a natural fit for the brand. The campaign also highlights Eggoz’s quality proposition, including eggs from hens on a special herbal diet, rigorous quality standards and its distinctive orange yolk.
BULLET Microdrama to roll out 100+ AI-powered microdramas
BULLET Microdrama, backed by ZEE Entertainment Enterprises, is expanding its content slate with more than 100 AI-powered microdramas. “Do Deewane aur Ashiqui” is the first title to launch under the initiative. BULLET is working with production partners and Trinetra AI, an AI-native filmmaking and content intelligence platform, to develop short-form vertical stories for mobile-first audiences.
Trinetra AI tools support multiple stages of production, including script evaluation, storyboarding, character creation, shot breakdown, video generation and audio orchestration. The company said AI can help accelerate production of microdramas, which typically comprise 60-100 high-hook episodes, while allowing creators to experiment with complex story worlds and genres.
Cognizant launches Activate unit for emerging enterprises
Cognizant has launched Cognizant Activate, a new business unit aimed at helping emerging enterprises adopt AI and accelerate digital transformation. The unit combines Cognizant’s AI Builder capabilities with an operating model designed for high-growth companies seeking faster deployment and lower complexity. It will offer pre-configured solutions covering data and AI, cybersecurity, enterprise applications, cloud modernisation and managed services.
The initial focus will be on financial services, healthcare, manufacturing and retail/CPG. Cognizant said emerging enterprises face challenges similar to larger businesses, including legacy technology and cybersecurity risks, but require solutions tailored to their scale. Activate will use pre-built AI accelerators, compressed implementation timelines and Cognizant’s ecosystem partnerships. CEO Ravi Kumar S said the initiative brings enterprise-grade AI capabilities to emerging businesses while adapting delivery to their speed and ambitions.
90+ My Tuition App launches FUTURE+ initiative
Bengaluru-based K-12 edtech company 90+ My Tuition App has launched FUTURE+, an initiative aimed at extending learning beyond conventional school tuition and introducing students to skills relevant to the future of work. The launch represents the company’s evolution towards a broader K-12 learning ecosystem focused on both academic requirements and longer-term professional capabilities. Founder Vingish Vijay said tuition addresses students’ present learning needs while FUTURE+ focuses on their future. The company plans to introduce additional future-focused courses.
Procol recognised among global AI-powered spend intelligence providers
Agentic AI procurement platform Procol has been recognised as the only Indian vendor among 16 global providers in Everest Group’s Innovation Watch: AI-Powered Spend Intelligence 2026. The assessment has positioned Procol as an “Influencer” and highlights the shift from historical spend reporting towards continuous, AI-enabled procurement intelligence.
Procol’s platform combines spend, supplier, contract, category, pricing and risk data to support decision-making. Its Spend Analytics Agent provides real-time insights and benchmarks, while its AI Control Tower gives procurement and finance teams conversational access to spend, supplier and invoice data. The platform manages more than $30 billion in spend across over 200 enterprises in 10-plus countries and operates on existing ERP systems including SAP and Oracle.
Genefied promotes Krishna Khandelwal to chief sales officer
Enterprise SaaS company Genefied has promoted Krishna Khandelwal to chief sales officer from his previous role as vice president of sales. Khandelwal, who has been with the company since its early days, will now lead revenue strategy and enterprise expansion across its product portfolio. His mandate covers SupplyBeam, GenuineMark, Rewardify and DWAM, with a focus on multi-product adoption among existing customers and expansion into new categories.
DraperU India Demo Day sees two startups secure investments
DraperU India has concluded its latest DraperU Founders Program with a Demo Day in Hyderabad, where 13 startups pitched their businesses to more than 150 investors, venture capitalists and industry leaders. Startups Ordo and WearSynapse secured investment commitments of Rs 25 lakh each from DraperU India, along with a commitment from Hyderabad Angels’ Rathnakar Samavedam. Both startups will also represent DraperU India at Draper University’s Hero Training Program in Silicon Valley. Ordo, WearSynapse and Creator Studio additionally won a share of a Rs 90,000 IDFC FIRST Bank prize pool. The 12-day residential programme focused on strengthening products, business models, go-to-market strategies, storytelling and fundraising. The next DraperU Founders Program is scheduled to begin in early 2027 in Hyderabad.
Mastercard security chief Michael H Lashlee joins Bloo Advisory Board
Bloo, a US and India based technology company has appointed Michael H. Lashlee, Chief Security Officer at Mastercard, to its Advisory Board, as the company expands its enterprise telemetry infrastructure for security, operations and AI. Lashlee will advise Bloo on enterprise security strategy, the requirements of large and regulated organisations, and global expansion. He brings extensive experience from Mastercard and a 25-year career with the US Secret Service. Bloo’s Datafabric provides long-term access to high-fidelity telemetry, while its SynthAI platform uses this data to support investigation, decision-making and AI-driven security and operations.

articles.title: La SNCF brade 450 000 billets de TGV à −45 % pendant quelques jours
articles.text:
Si vous avez prévu de prendre le train cet automne, c’est le moment de regarder les prix. La SNCF lance une vente flash sur une sélection de TGV INOUI, en première comme en seconde classe.
Du mardi 6 au jeudi 8 octobre 2026 inclus, la SNCF propose 450 000 billets à 45 % de réduction directement sur son site SNCF Connect, en première comme en seconde classe. L’opération concerne une sélection de TGV INOUI en France, mais aussi plusieurs liaisons européennes.
Quelles destinations et quelles dates sont concernées ?
L’offre permet de voyager du 2 au 30 novembre, sur une sélection de trajets en France et en Europe. Une ligne bénéficie d’une période plus large : Paris–Lyon, dans les deux sens, avec des voyages du 16 octobre au 30 novembre. C’est la seule liaison de cette vente flash qui permet de partir pendant les vacances de la Toussaint.
En plus des trajets en France métropolitaine, l’offre concerne les TGV INOUI vers l’Italie, l’Espagne, le Luxembourg et Bruxelles, ainsi que les TGV Lyria vers Genève uniquement.
Vous pouvez aussi rejoindre Francfort, Stuttgart, Mannheim ou Karlsruhe, en Allemagne. Ces liaisons sont assurées conjointement par la SNCF et Deutsche Bahn, la compagnie ferroviaire allemande, avec des TGV français et des ICE, leurs équivalents allemands. La réduction peut y atteindre 45 %, mais elle peut aussi être moins élevée selon le billet : pour ces destinations, la SNCF annonce plutôt une remise « jusqu’à 45 % ».
Est-ce que ces billets valent le coup ?
Si vos dates sont déjà fixées, cette vente mérite un coup d’œil, notamment pour un déplacement autour du 11 novembre. Pensez à comparer plusieurs horaires : un départ un peu plus tôt ou plus tard peut permettre de trouver une place au tarif promotionnel. La remise est calculée sur le tarif du jour, et le prix final varie donc selon le train choisi. Si vous avez une carte Avantage, comparez aussi les tarifs proposés avec celle-ci : la promotion ne se cumule pas avec les autres réductions SNCF, promotions ou codes avantage.
Pour un départ en décembre ou plus tard, les ventes d’hiver SNCF et OUIGO sont déjà ouvertes, avec des billets annoncés dès 19 € chez OUIGO.

articles.text:
Si vous souhaitez vous offrir un téléviseur 4K sans vous ruiner, ou simplement vous équiper d’un second écran pas trop cher pour votre chambre, par exemple, alors le Xiaomi TV F 55 2026 pourrait bien vous convenir. Même si sa fiche technique n’est pas aussi développée que celle d’autres modèles plus premium de la marque, cette référence sous Fire TV reste tout à fait digne d’intérêt, surtout quand elle est proposée à moins de 330 euros pendant les Jours Flash Prime d’Amazon.
Ce qu’il faut savoir sur le Xiaomi TV F 55 2026
- Une dalle LCD 4K de 55 pouces + 60 Hz
- Un port HDMI 2.1 compatible eARC et ALLM
- Fire TV
Auparavant affiché à 479 euros, le Xiaomi TV F 55 2026 est aujourd’hui disponible en promotion à 329 euros sur Amazon, pour les abonnés Prime, jusqu’à ce mardi soir.
Un TV élégant avec des images bien nettes
Le Xiaomi TV F 55 2026 est un modèle plutôt élégant, avec son design métallique, ses pieds latéraux discrets et son cadre très fin, qui rend l’expérience un peu plus immersive. En d’autres termes, ce téléviseur ne fait pas tache dans un salon. Ce dernier embarque une dalle LCD 4K UHD de 55 pouces, dotée d’un système de rétroéclairage DLED ; ici, pas de QLED, et encore moins d’OLED, mais l’écran devrait tout de même afficher des images bien nettes.
Il prend par ailleurs en charge les formats HLG et HDR10, qui permettent notamment de mieux restituer les détails dans les zones très sombres comme dans les hautes lumières, pour une image plus contrastée. Un mode Filmmaker, qui affiche l’image telle qu’elle a été pensée par le réalisateur d’un film, sans traitement artificiel, est aussi disponible. Et côté audio, les formats Dolby Audio, DTS:X et DTS Virtual:X sont tous supportés.
Un modèle sous Fire TV
Le Xiaomi TV F 55 2026 dispose de trois ports HDMI, dont un HDMI 2.1 compatible eARC. Il est donc possible d’y brancher une barre de son afin de profiter d’un rendu sonore plus immersif. Vous pouvez aussi connecter une console next-gen, mais attention : la dalle se limite à un taux de rafraîchissement de 60 Hz en 4K, ce qui empêche de profiter de la 4K à 120 Hz sur les consoles récentes. Il faut donc se contenter ici de la 4K à 60 Hz ou du Full HD à 120 Hz. La fluidité reste toutefois au rendez-vous avec ce dernier mode, mais les joueurs les plus exigeants sur la qualité d’image pourraient être frustrés.
Enfin, ce téléviseur fonctionne sous Fire OS, basé sur Android, qui propose une interface intuitive et complète, avec les plateformes de streaming phares bien mises en avant. Et Alexa est évidemment de la partie. Le TV est également compatible avec Apple AirPlay : vous pouvez donc diffuser des films, de la musique ou des photos directement depuis un iPhone, un iPad ou un Mac.

articles.title: Follow the money: how blockchain boosts aid accountability - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
African technologists and entrepreneurs are applying blockchain in innovative ways, creating a new financial infrastructure for the continent with wide-ranging benefits, including for the humanitarian sector.
Through its Blockchain Ventures investment programme – supported by Ethereum Foundation and GSR Foundation – UNICEF Office of Innovation provides funding and technical assistance to emerging market startups building innovative blockchain-based solutions.
The transparency and efficiency that make blockchain a powerful fintech tool also offer a solution to one of humanitarian response’s most persistent challenges, says Sandy Om’Iniabohs, Impact and Research Lead at Convexity in Nigeria: opacity, fraud and unverifiable impact.
What problem was Convexity Humanitarian Aid Transfer Solution (CHATS) originally built to solve?
The idea for CHATS came directly from our work on the ground. Our team used to conduct fraud investigations and projects for local and international NGOs, and we saw how funds were diverted when it came to distributing aid to recipients.
One example is from a programme focused on providing families living in displaced populations with access to healthcare. Before we began, we went around camps for displaced people conducting needs assessments. You’d ask community members why the camp clinic was closed, even though there was a clinic there. They would explain that a foundation, an organisation or the government had donated pharmaceutical products, but the people in charge were basically free to disburse them – and sometimes those products were just sold off for personal interest instead of being provided to the community.
We realised this was something we could help solve. CHATS is a digital cash and voucher distribution platform that makes it possible for all recipients to have a wallet account attached to an identifiable and verified individual. Beneficiaries without access to smartphones or the internet have multiple channels of claiming their aid using text short codes and QR codes, SMS vouchers, and tap-and-go cards. With CHATS and with blockchain, you can see clearly who is collecting what, where and when. It provides real oversight across the whole process.
How does CHATS help tackle aid diversion?
In plain language, diversion is stolen or misused aid. What CHATS does is make it much harder for people acting in their own self-interest to divert aid that is meant for displaced and impoverished people.
Every person has an assigned card or voucher connected to them. If someone who is supposed to receive one strip of malaria pills is suddenly collecting 10, you immediately see that something is wrong. The records are there. It raises flags and makes it far more difficult to hide what is going on.
CHATS also works for cash transfers. What advantages does it have over traditional systems?
We’ve done multiple cash transfers on CHATS. There are several advantages. CHATS is capable of coordinating the whole disbursement flow end-to-end.
In displacement settings, many people no longer have access to formal documentation like national ID cards. CHATS addresses that inside the system, so identity verification and documentation become part of the same workflow. The disbursements themselves and the monitoring are handled on CHATS too. Then you have reporting: you can do your impact reporting and have programme oversight from one place. So instead of stitching together lots of separate tools, programme stakeholders and managers can coordinate everything on a single platform.
Many humanitarian managers associate blockchain with cryptocurrencies, financial speculation and misuse. How do you explain it to them?
I like to explain blockchain as a notebook. Imagine a notebook with an infinite number of pages where everything that’s written stays there. It cannot be erased, it cannot be hidden, it cannot be changed. If I carry out a transaction, it is written there. If someone else carries out a transaction, it is written there. You can see the full history, and it is permanent.
On top of that, you can verify whatever is being conducted across the board. That verification and that transaction history save time. By saving time, they make things faster and cheaper. These are benefits we can apply directly to the problems we see in the field. By being cheaper and faster, we get to children and families more quickly while building in accountability.
Often when people hear “blockchain” they say it sounds very technical. You have to explain the benefits in non-technical terms. Don’t focus on how complicated it may be; focus on how beneficial it is to organisations and recipients. Convexity builds and maintains the technical side. For a user, they just need to know that it is fast, cheap, transparent, verifiable, and that the records cannot be changed.
CHATS has multiple access channels – quick codes, vouchers, QR codes. Why is that so important at the last mile?
Something we’ve learned is that adaptation looks very different across contexts. On the malaria programme, for example, we tried to stick to what already exists on the ground. We don’t want to introduce too much friction.
If you give people something they’re not used to, or say they have to rely on smartphones, you introduce friction and the programme can fail. So we meet recipients where they are. We make things as simple as possible and adapt the solution to their current context.
We’ve also learned it is important to configure where and how value is used. If you simply give a debit or credit card to a family and say, “You can use this in a primary healthcare centre,” there is a good chance they might use it outside that centre – go to an ATM and withdraw cash, for example. Then it’s not meeting the needs it was intended for.
With our NFC cards, if you give one to a family and it is configured for healthcare, the place they can spend it is that primary healthcare centre. So the original idea behind the aid – what it was intended for – is actually realised.
You also talk about “geofencing” aid disbursement. What does that mean in practice?
Geofencing creates a virtual boundary around a specific location, where certain things cannot occur outside that boundary. The idea came from observing a common challenge in humanitarian distribution. If the goal of a programme is to revive a region that has been affected by disaster, you often see funds being spent outside that region. The intention is to revive the local economy, but the money leaks out.
With geofencing, funds are used only within a specific location. If this room is geofenced, recipients can only use those funds within this room. It keeps money circulating inside the affected community, supports local businesses, and still meets the objectives for which the funds were provided.
UNICEF was one of your early institutional backers. Beyond funding, what difference has that made?
Beyond capital, the mentorship has been very important. We had business mentors and tech mentors who were amazing – going through our business models, how we reach out to partners and how we explain CHATS. The support and guidance we’ve had, and the relationships we’ve built with UNICEF, have really helped us grow.
Entrepreneurship can be very lonely. Founders are still figuring things out. So having access to mentors who help you build your skills, and to a community of like-minded founders, goes a long way. You also learn from others’ pain points so that when you encounter them, you have existing information on how to respond.
There is also credibility. When you go to a humanitarian agency, they often ask, “Who has used this?” Being able to say that UNICEF was an early funder of CHATS, and has been instrumental in building it, helps open conversations in a conservative sector.
Who are you looking to partner with now?
CHATS is a plug-and-play infrastructure layer, so we are looking to partner with organisations doing large volumes of disbursements, implementing large scale aid programmes.
Our current partners include Mercy Corps Ventures, Collaborative Futures and a consortium of partners, the Nigerian Red Cross, as well as private donors. We’re looking to build on these relationships as we expand.
What is the future for CHATS?
We’re expanding into other African countries – Sudan, Kenya and others – and we believe that CHATS will mean faster distributions that are more transparent and less fragmented. We are bridging the gaps that have prevented funds from reaching recipients over the last mile while making it harder for funds to be diverted.

articles.title: Hack The Box's AI Range Enterprise Edition tests whether AI agents can do their jobs - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Hack The Box’s AI Range Enterprise Edition tests whether AI agents can do their jobs
Cybersecurity training company Hack The Box Ltd. today introduced AI Range Enterprise Edition to let security teams test whether their own artificial intelligence agents can do the jobs they have been assigned.
The release is seeking to take on a problem in how security teams vet their agents. Hack The Box says an agent may be put into production after a strong benchmark result or vendor test without ever being checked against the work it will handle day to day. Human staff in the same role usually are. An agent’s performance can also drift after deployment as the model underneath it gets updated.
Hack The Box launched the original AI Range last December. Since then, AI labs, government customers and hyperscalers have been testing agents on it, according to the company. Corporate security teams get the same testing with the enterprise edition, and each agent is appraised against the role it has been given.
The appraisal method goes by the name Agentic Worker Competence. Each agent gets a score for its assigned role and a pass-or-fail mark in each environment it works through, with results tracked over time. New environments are added on a regular basis as fresh vulnerabilities and attack patterns turn up in the wild. Customers can rerun the appraisal whenever an agent, its model or its data changes.
Chief Product Officer Gerasimos Marketos summed up the process as “connect the agent, assign it a role and let it work.” The platform then logs how the agent copes with each task on its own, he said, and security leaders can use those results to decide what work an agent is ready for.
The launch also covers the human staff who work alongside agents. Leaders need “confidence in both sides of the workforce” as AI takes on more cybersecurity tasks, according to founder and Chief Executive Haris Pylarinos.
Penetration tester and security operations center analyst are the only two roles with AI-augmented versions at launch. In the analyst version, practitioners lean on AI to review alerts in realistic scenarios. Whatever the AI recommends doing next is theirs to evaluate.
Grading in those roles runs through what Hack The Box calls Agentic Operator Competence Scoring. The scenarios test whether a practitioner catches errors in an agent’s reasoning and knows when to step in. Holding back is scored as well, based on whether someone lets AI-driven work run when it does not need correcting.
AI Range Enterprise Edition and the two AI-augmented roles are available now, with more cybersecurity roles planned for the coming months.
Hack The Box is a venture capital-backed startup that raised $55 million in a Series B round led by The Carlyle Group Inc. in 2023, with Paladin Capital Group and Marathon Venture Capital also participating. The company says it has more than 800 enterprise customers and a community of more than 4 million cybersecurity professionals.

articles.title: “L'électrification, la bascule est faite” : Renault promet une voiture électrique 15 % moins chère d'ici 2030
articles.text:
“L'électrification, la bascule est faite” : Renault promet une voiture électrique 15 % moins chère d'ici 2030
Une électrique au prix d'une hybride avant la fin de la décennie : François Provost, directeur général de Renault, a pris date sur France Inter. Il désigne aussi le coupable des tarifs actuels, réclame dix ans de trêve réglementaire et fixe ses conditions aux constructeurs chinois.
Samedi 3 octobre 2026, à neuf jours de l'ouverture du Mondial de l'Auto de Paris, François Provost était l'invité de l'émission On n'arrête pas l'éco sur France Inter. Le directeur général de Renault Group y a acté la victoire de la voiture à batterie, promis une baisse d'environ 15 % du prix de ses modèles électriques d'ici 2030 et annoncé plus de 10 milliards d'euros d'investissements en France sur cinq ans, "si le contexte social et politique en France le permet".
Prix de la voiture électrique : l'objectif de Renault pour 2030
"L'électrification, la bascule est faite", tranche le dirigeant, avant de nuancer : "Ça ne veut pas dire 100 % électrique." Les immatriculations lui donnent raison. En septembre, près de 42 % des voitures neuves vendues en France étaient 100 % électriques, soit plus de 65 000 unités et un volume doublé en un an, selon AAA Data. Lui y voit l'effet des aides publiques, de la baisse des coûts et d'un carburant au prix devenu "absolument incontrôlable".
Renault revendique un quart de ce marché. Au classement par modèle, le Tesla Model Y domine pourtant septembre avec 8 183 immatriculations, devant la Renault 5 (5 224) et la nouvelle Twingo (4 992). Depuis janvier, la R5 totalise 31 998 exemplaires.
Le groupe se fixe un cap : aligner d'ici 2030 le prix d'une électrique sur celui d'une hybride, soit "typiquement" 15 % de moins. L'hybride, allégée de plus de 1 000 euros de coûts, rejoindrait le tarif du thermique avant cette échéance.
D'ici là, François Provost invite à raisonner en coût d'usage. Chez Renault, neuf électriques sur dix partent en location. Une R5 se loue 150 à 170 euros par mois et coûterait 500 euros par an à l'utilisation, contre 2 000 euros pour une Clio essence de dix ans, d'après son calcul. La Twingo s'affiche à partir de 99 euros par mois. Il assure que "les clients qui passent à l'électrique ne reviennent pas en arrière".
Normes européennes : 3 000 euros de surcoût par voiture, selon Renault
Pourquoi le neuf reste-t-il si cher ? Le patron accuse la réglementation : au moins 3 000 euros ajoutés par véhicule en dix ans, et autant d'ici 2030 avec 108 nouveaux textes attendus.
	
Si un Français ne peut pas s'acheter de voiture neuve et qu'il est obligé de conserver sa voiture de douze ans d'âge, vous croyez qu'il y a plus de sécurité ? Vous croyez qu'il y a moins d'émissions ?
"Le logiciel européen, il est complètement faux", assène-t-il, avant de réclamer "un gel pendant dix ans". Un quart des ingénieurs du Technocentre, le centre de recherche du groupe à Guyancourt, se consacre selon lui à la mise en conformité permanente. Il préférerait les voir traquer les coûts. La Plateforme automobile, qui fédère la filière française, avance des ordres de grandeur voisins.
Bruxelles a déjà entrouvert la porte. Dans son plan automobile de décembre 2025, la Commission européenne prévoit de réduire au minimum les nouvelles obligations pendant dix ans pour une future catégorie de petites électriques. Le dirigeant veut étendre la trêve, et chaque norme gelée préserve aussi sa marge.
Dacia Spring : la nouvelle génération quitte la Chine pour la Slovénie
Les 10 milliards ont surgi au détour d'une question embarrassante : le retard pris pour rapatrier de Chine la production de la Dacia Spring. François Provost a esquivé et déroulé son bilan industriel. Treize milliards investis en cinq ans, 500 000 voitures sorties des usines françaises en 2025, au moins 25 % de plus attendues en 2026.
Le dossier Spring est pourtant soldé depuis un mois. Dacia a lancé le 8 septembre la deuxième génération de sa citadine, écoulée à plus de 210 000 exemplaires depuis 2021 selon la marque. Affichée à 17 900 euros hors aides et donnée pour 250 km d'autonomie, elle sort désormais de l'usine slovène de Novo Mesto, sur la plateforme de la Twingo. Cette origine européenne lui rouvre l'accès aux aides à l'achat françaises.
Le rapatriement profite donc à la Slovénie, où sont assemblées les deux électriques les plus abordables du groupe.
Quant à la future enveloppe française, sa destination reste inconnue. Le 10 juillet, dans un communiqué, le dirigeant évoquait 13 milliards supplémentaires "si les conditions sont réunies". Le montant cité à l'antenne est en retrait.
Face aux marques chinoises, il juge le flux d'importations "trop rapide" et réclame à Bruxelles un accord avec Pékin, sans guerre tarifaire. Sa doctrine : accueillir ces constructeurs s'ils produisent sur le continent avec des équipementiers européens, à l'image d'Envision, groupe chinois qui a investi selon lui 1,5 milliard d'euros à Douai pour les batteries de la R5.

articles.title: Apple está empezando a cortar el acceso a los agentes de IA por motivos de seguridad
articles.text:
Septiembre y octubre están siendo movidos en lo que respecta a las inteligencias artificiales metiendo las narices donde no deberían. Este verano, uno de los modelos de OpenAI se coló en instituciones oficiales, llegando al punto de entrar sin permiso a sistemas del gobierno australiano y desencadenando una pequeña crisis diplomática. Hace unos días, el agente Muse de Meta se refirió a cosas que no debería conocer.
Hay quien está tomando nota, y Apple acaba de dar un portazo a esas IA que quieran meterse donde no les llaman.
El caso Muse. Hace unas semanas, Meta presentó un nuevo agente personal: Muse. Según la compañía, no se trata de un simple chatbot que responde preguntas, sino que se puede encargar de muchas otras tareas como enviar correos, rellenar formularios, hacer tareas algo más complejas como reservar un viaje, etc. Uno de los ejemplos que proponía la compañía es un usuario enviando un vídeo de una receta y que Muse lo convierta en una lista de la compra.
Claro, Meta quiere que le demos permiso total a nuestra vida (y ya sabemos que Meta no es la compañía más fiable a mínimo que nos preocupe la privacidad). Pues bien, poco después de presentar Muse, un periodista llamado Jason Aten contó que Muse había hecho referencia a una conversación suya en la app 'Mensajes' sin que él creyera haberle dado permiso. Meta respondió que el acceso es opcional y que Muse sólo puede leer en 'Mensajes' si el usuario concede el acceso a todo el disco y activa la opción correspondiente.
Desde Ars Technica cuestionan la explicación porque cualquier app puede leer casi todo el disco, y pasó lo que tenía que pasar.
En corto. El pasado 2 de octubre. Apple publicó un corto aviso en su web de desarrolladores que apuntaba a un endurecimiento de los accesos a ciertas partes del disco duro en macOS. Este permiso se ha diseñado para que las apps de copia de seguridad funcionaran, dejando a una app saltarse buena parte de los controles de privacidad del sistema para leer prácticamente todo (correos, mensajes, historial, archivos, etc).
A partir de ahora, el agente que quiera entrar a esos recovecos del sistema, tendrá que justificarlo haciendo saltar un aviso muy específico que avise al usuario. Básicamente, cuanto más capaces y autónomos sean, más crecen los riesgos en este nivel de acceso, y lo que Apple quiere es que el usuario conozca los riesgos asociados con ciertos niveles de acceso para "tomar decisiones informadas sobre sus propios datos y privacidad".
No es el primer portazo. Unos días antes, Amazon ya había bloqueado Muse en su tienda. El argumento de Amazon es que Muse pasa sin avisar a la tienda, no se identifica como un agente y se hace con credenciales de clientes. Meta niega la mayor, pero para Amazon, estos agentes deberían operar abiertamente y respetar la decisión de cada proveedor de servicios (tiendas en este caso) de participar o no.
Tampoco es la primera vez, ya que Amazon ya había llevado a Perplexity a los tribunales por su navegador Comet. Al final, aunque la base es distinta (Apple protege los datos de sus usuarios y Amazon su negocio y su ecosistema publicitario), el resultado es el mismo: el agente no puede entrar a todas partes como Pedro por su casa.
No hace falta ser Amazon, ya que una plataforma de reserva de restaurantes bloqueó Instinct hace unos días. Según ellos, "la actividad automatizada no aprobada puede suponer un riesgo en la plataforma y compromete la experienica justa de reserva para los comensales". Sin embargo, en CNN probaron a reservar una mesa en ese servicio usando Muse y... pudieron.
El poder. ¿Cómo nos afecta esto? Pues si todas empiezan a bloquear agentes de terceros debido a intereses comerciales o porque cuentan con un agente propio (Amazon es una de las más involucradas en la IA y es evidente que prefiere que uses un agente desarrollado por ellos para comprar en Amazon antes que uno de Meta que les pueda robar información), los agentes no serán tan útiles como prometen.
No todas cierran la puerta y, mientras Amazon bloquea, Walmart y Shopify sí permiten el paso. Sin embargo, en un Internet más cerrado con los agentes, los que tienen la sartén por el mango es el servicio "de siempre". El usuario no va a salir de Amazon porque no pueda comprar con el agente que paga de otra compañía, se va a quedar en Amazon.
Ahora bien, también hay un riesgo porque si las plataformas cierran la puerta, éstas pueden quedarse fuera de las recomendaciones de compra para el usuario y ganarían menos dinero. Es un riesgo que Amazon, debido a su posición dominante, puede permitirse, pero Recambios Manolo SL quizá no.
Tiene sentido que sea Apple. Al final, en esta nueva era de los agentes, la cuestión va a ser menos qué puede hacer sino dónde puede entrar. En esa conversación, las grandes plataformas 'tradicionales' tienen el control, pero volviendo al cerrojazo por parte de Apple, tiene sentido que sean precisamente ellos los que se muestren más recelosos.
Los de Cupertino llegan con retraso a la conversación de la IA (agentes incluidos) y están en una posición en la que pueden decidir cómo se entra y quién lo hace. Lo que no pueden permitirse es presumir de privacidad en cada keynote y que gran parte de su campaña publicitaria se centre en esa privacidad y protección del usuario y que luego un agente externo sepa cosas del usuario que no debería saber.

articles.title: Ninja Forms plugin flaw exploited to hack WordPress sites
articles.text:
Hackers are exploiting stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in two unrelated WordPress plugins, Ninja Forms and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce, to install backdoors and create rogue admin accounts.
Both vulnerabilities received a high severity score and require an authenticated session to exploit. They are tracked as CVE-2026-93836, affecting WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce versions 8.6.6 and older, and CVE-2026-94504, affecting Ninja Forms versions 3.15.3 and older.
The Ninja Forms plugin for WordPress is installed on more than 500,000 sites and allows creating custom forms without writing code.
WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce allows storing group products into bundles and is active on more than 30,000 WordPress sites.
The campaign was identified on October 4 by researchers at WordPress security platform Patchstack, against users of WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce. The next day, the same activity was observed against Ninja Forms.
In both attacks, the same JavaScript payload was delivered from ‘imgcdn1[.]com,’ indicating the same threat actor behind the exploitation attempts against the two plugins.
According to the researchers, the attacker tries to plant malicious JavaScript (x.js) in WooCommerce order data or Ninja Forms submissions. When a logged-in administrator loads the content, the script executes using the authenticated WordPress session.
When launched, it retrieves the necessary administrative nonces and uses legitimate WordPress functions to install a malicious plugin masquerading as “WP Smart Thumbnails” version 1.2.4 from “MediaPress Labs” and create an administrator account.
At that stage, the JavaScript payload and the malicious plugin’s PHP scripts establish four access mechanisms to the compromised site:
- A visible administrator account
- An administrator account concealed from the WordPress user list in the dashboard
- A secret login URL that authenticates as the site’s oldest existing administrator
- An unauthenticated file manager accessible through a direct request to the malicious plugin’s main PHP file
The file manager can't execute commands, but it could still be used to introduce additional payloads on the site.
Even if the WP Smart Thumbnails plugin is removed from the infected website, the hidden account and secret login URL continue to function as persistence mechanisms through separate auxiliary attack plugins featuring backdated timestamps to evade detection.
“The [hidden] account does not appear in Users → All Users, does not appear in the Administrator filter, and is not counted in the totals above the list,” Patchstack explains, adding that “It is a fully privileged administrator the site owner cannot see.”
Patchstack says that exploitation is currently limited, but advises site admins to upgrade to the latest versions of the affected plugins, WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce version 8.6.7 or later and Ninja Forms 3.15.4 or later.
Updating the vulnerable plugin prevents further exploitation but does not clean an existing infection. Administrators are strongly recommended to check for signs of compromise.

articles.title: IA et jeux vidéo : les créateurs de Resident Evil ont trouvé la recette magique
articles.text:
Plus de 27 titres de Capcom tournent sur le RE Engine, et environ 2 000 développeurs y travaillent. Le 2 octobre, lors de sa conférence ouverte RE:2026, l’éditeur japonais a dévoilé REX, un chantier au long cours destiné à transformer ce moteur maison en « moteur de jeu de la génération IA ». Derrière l’étiquette se cache une série de sous-projets aux noms de code limpides, RE:Dox, RE:UI, RE:Log, RE:Flows ou encore RE:Runtime, de la documentation du code jusqu’aux outils d’exécution.
Du code compris, écrit et testé par la machine
Le programmeur Satoshi Ishida a résumé l’ambition devant l’audience : « à l’avenir, l’IA pourra comprendre les programmes et les créer automatiquement, ou réaliser des tests de jeu pour détecter les bugs ». L’entreprise vise, selon ses propres mots, « un avenir où nous créerons des jeux avec l’IA ». Le cœur de REX consiste à rendre les entrailles du moteur lisibles par les humains comme par les modèles, condition pour que ces derniers y contribuent sans rien casser. Deux premières briques, consacrées à la documentation et aux journaux, sont déjà publiées en open source.
Début 2025, les équipes de Capcom montraient déjà un outil interne s’appuyant sur les modèles de Google pour brasser des centaines de milliers d’idées d’objets de jeu. REX étend cette logique au moteur entier, jusqu’au code qui fait tourner les jeux.
Et la promesse faite aux joueurs, alors ?
Le 16 février 2026, devant ses actionnaires individuels, Capcom s’était engagé à n’implémenter aucun élément généré par IA dans les contenus de ses jeux. La promesse tenait en deux volets : des outils dopés à l’IA pour gagner en productivité, avec des expérimentations en graphisme, en son et en programmation, et une interdiction ferme côté contenus. REX exécute le premier volet sans toucher au second. Le compte rendu de la conférence du 2 octobre n’emploie d’ailleurs pas une seule fois le terme d’IA générative. L’IA s’arrête à la porte de l’atelier : les mondes que traversent les joueurs restent dessinés, composés et écrits par des humains.
Square Enix veut de son côté automatiser 70 % de son assurance qualité et de son débogage d’ici fin 2027, un objectif affiché en novembre 2025. L’éditeur de Final Fantasy a depuis annoncé, en mars, l’intégration de l’IA Gemini de Google dans Dragon Quest X. Le patron d’Ubisoft qualifiait au même moment l’IA de « révolution aussi grande pour notre industrie que le passage à la 3D ». Electronic Arts s’est, lui, allié à Stability AI pour générer des textures destinées à ses jeux. Capcom borne l’exercice par écrit depuis février.

articles.title: FBI Arrests ‘Most Wanted’ Developer of Ploutus ATM Malware
articles.text:
A Venezuelan national believed to be a leader of Tren de Aragua (TdA)’s ATM jackpotting activities and the developer of the infamous Ploutus ATM malware has been arrested.
According to the US, TdA is a violent transnational criminal organization that engages in different types of trafficking, robbery, fraud, extortion, and various types of financial crimes targeting US organizations, including ATM jackpotting.
The organization is blamed for ATM jackpotting attacks across 47 states, the District of Columbia, and foreign countries.
On October 2, Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre, 50, also known as ‘Prometheus’ and ‘The Engineer’, who was sanctioned last week by the US Treasury, appeared in court to face charges associated with his role in TdA.
He has been on the FBI’s top 10 most wanted fugitives list since March 2026, becoming the first individual added to that list for cybercrimes.
Canelon Aguirre was indicted in the US in December 2025 along with 21 other individuals for bank burglary, fraud, and money laundering conspiracy.
The US has not shared details on how he was apprehended, but noted that he will remain detained pending trial, after entering not guilty pleas.
According to the US, Canelon Aguirre is one of the masterminds behind the ATM jackpotting attacks carried out by TdA using Ploutus.
Members of the operation exploited vulnerabilities in ATMs to deploy the malware, which allowed them to force the systems to dispense cash without debiting accounts.
Ploutus contained anti-analysis capabilities to hinder forensic analysis and could also erase itself from the infected systems to hide its tracks.
To date, 120 defendants have been charged for their roles in the conspiracy, and three of them have been sentenced to prison: Oddry Arnoldo Cabrera Torrealba, Carlos Javier Padron, and Juan Manuel Gouveia Aguilera.

articles.title: Google cambia las reglas: dile adiós a usar Gemini Flash y Pro sin pagar
articles.text:
Si usas Gemini a diario con una cuenta personal y sin una suscripción de Google AI, te traemos malas noticias. A partir de esta misma semana, Google implementará nuevas restricciones que ya no te permitirán usar los modelos Flash y Pro desde la app de Gemini sin pagar.
Para ser más precisos, si usas Gemini sin pagar perderás el acceso a los modelos Flash y Pro desde el viernes 9 de octubre. Todavía podrás usar la aplicación e interactuar con el chatbot de inteligencia artificial de forma gratuita y sin tope de uso, pero estarás limitado a la variante Flash-Lite, que está optimizada para entregar respuestas más rápidas y que es menos potente que las otras todavía a disposición.
Sin dudas estamos hablando del cambio más grande que Google ha implementado en Gemini desde la introducción del selector de modelos en su aplicación. La compañía ya había modificado los límites de uso de su inteligencia artificial, adoptando una modalidad de doble barrera de tiempo, con topes de 5 horas y semanales, como la que usan Claude y otras plataformas similares. Asimismo, ha introducido una solución similar en Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM).
Pero las restricciones en la disponibilidad de Gemini Flash y Pro a través de la app no impacta solamente a quienes la acceden gratis. No todas las suscripciones de pago brindarán acceso a ambos modelos, lo cual también impacta en quienes ya están suscriptos a Google AI Plus, el plan más barato a disposición.
Gemini Flash y Pro ya no se podrán usar gratis
Así como quienes acceden a Gemini sin pagar una suscripción estarán limitados a Flash-Lite, quienes tengan el plan AI Plus en su cuenta personal de Google podrán utilizar los modelos Flash-Lite y Flash, pero no la variante Pro. Esta última versión será accesible para quienes compren la suscripción a Google AI Pro o AI Ultra.
Así las cosas, entonces, así quedan ordenados los modelos disponibles en cada plan:
- Acceso gratis a Gemini con cuenta personal: solo Flash-Lite;
- Google AI Plus (4,99 euros al mes): Gemini Flash-Lite y Flash;
- Google AI Pro (21,99 euros al mes): Gemini Flash-Lite, Flash y Pro;
- Google AI Ultra (99,99 euros al mes): Gemini Flash-Lite, Flash y Pro.
Tengamos en cuenta que los planes Pro y Ultra difieren entre sí en cuanto a límites de uso de los distintos modelos, como también en la cantidad de almacenamiento en la nube y el acceso a otros servicios de Google que incluyen.
Si no tienes interés en pagar 4,99 euros mensuales (o más) para acceder a las IA más potentes de Gemini, tendrás que conformarte con Flash-Lite o migrar a alternativas de la competencia.

articles.title: Le Français WhiteLab Genomics, dont l'IA a déjà trouvé le chemin du cerveau, se donne les moyens de ses ambitions
articles.text:
La start-up française WhiteLab Genomics vient de lever 22 millions d'euros. Une bonne nouvelle pour celle dont l'IA conçoit les vecteurs des médicaments génomiques de demain, dont certains ont déjà atteint le cerveau lors d'essais in vivo.
Concevoir des médicaments génomiques grâce à l'IA, c'est l'objectif de WhiteLab Genomics, qui a officialisé ce mardi 6 octobre une levée de 26 millions de dollars (22 millions d'euros) en Série B. La start-up, née à Paris en 2019, passée par Y Combinator et lauréate du programme French Tech 2030, s'intéresse surtout au trajet du traitement, à savoir comment le livrer aux bonnes cellules, et seulement à elles. Ses résultats obtenus in vivo, autrement dit sur du vivant, laissent entrevoir des pistes face à certaines des maladies neurologiques les plus redoutées.
Comment l'IA de WhiteLab a forcé la porte du cerveau
Pour faire un peu de pédagogie, certes bien nécessaire, il faut savoir que le principe des médicaments génomiques est de glisser des instructions génétiques au cœur des cellules, pour en modifier le fonctionnement. Leur intérêt clinique est aujourd'hui largement démontré, mais il y a encore un casse-tête logistique à régler. Il faut en effet que le « colis » arrive à bon port. C'est tout le rôle des vecteurs, des coursiers microscopiques. Les virus adéno-associés (AAV) figurent parmi les plus utilisés, et les chercheurs ont appris à les transformer en livreurs.
Pour dessiner de meilleurs coursiers, WhiteLab s'appuie sur ALFRED, sa plateforme d'IA maison. Au lieu de tout tester à la main, l'outil passe en revue les pistes possibles et désigne les plus prometteuses, que les chercheurs vérifient ensuite en laboratoire, puis sur le vivant. L'objectif est de gagner du temps, de réduire les coûts et de limiter les risques. Avec l'Institut du Cerveau, à Paris, ALFRED a ainsi imaginé de nouveaux AAV. Lors des tests in vivo, ces vecteurs ont franchi la barrière hémato-encéphalique, un filtre naturel entre le sang et le cerveau qui protège ce dernier mais bloque aussi de nombreux médicaments. Une fois passés, ils ont surtout ciblé le cerveau, sans signal détectable dans le foie, un organe où ce type de vecteur a tendance à s'accumuler.
Pour les patients, c'est évidemment très prometteur. Car mieux viser le système nerveux central, c'est-à-dire le cerveau et la moelle épinière, ouvrirait les médicaments génomiques à des maladies qui s'y logent, par exemple Alzheimer, Parkinson, la maladie de Charcot (SLA), mais aussi certaines maladies génétiques rares, comme les maladies de surcharge lysosomale. Dans ces dernières, les cellules n'arrivent plus à éliminer certains déchets et finissent par s'encombrer. Les cancers du cerveau sont aussi concernés, à commencer par le glioblastome, l'une des tumeurs cérébrales les plus agressives. Pour David Del Bourgo, le cofondateur et PDG de WhiteLab, « l'essentiel est de savoir si ces concepts fonctionnent dans les organismes vivants ». Et sur ce terrain, il assure que la société a « déjà présenté des résultats très probants ».
Après les virus, l'IA de WhiteLab s'attaque aux nanoparticules lipidiques
Concernant la levée de fonds (26 millions de dollars, on le rappelle), le tour de table est mené par le fonds AVP. Deux nouveaux venus s'y joignent avec Yaday Health, basé à Miami, et Blast Club, le club d'investisseurs du très médiatique Anthony Bourbon et Samuel Guez. Omnes Capital et Debiopharm Innovation Fund remettent au pot. David Del Bourgo dit vouloir « changer d'échelle » sur plusieurs technologies et bâtir un portefeuille d'actifs biologiques validés, à développer seule, ou avec des laboratoires. Les AAV conçus par son IA ont un autre atout. Leurs séquences, très éloignées de l'existant, offrent un potentiel de brevets différenciants et ont été pensées pour une future production à grande échelle. D'où l'intérêt des investisseurs…
La start-up ne compte en plus pas s'arrêter aux virus. Son IA planche désormais sur un autre type de transporteur, sans virus cette fois. Il s'agit des nanoparticules lipidiques, qui sont de minuscules capsules de lipides (des graisses) qui enveloppent le traitement pour le protéger. Ce sont elles qui ont été popularisées par les vaccins à ARN messager, ça rappelle des souvenirs. WhiteLab s'intéresse aussi au contenu du colis, avec des promoteurs synthétiques. Placés devant le gène thérapeutique, ces courts fragments d'ADN jouent le rôle d'interrupteurs : ils décident dans quelles cellules, et à quel moment, le gène s'allume. L'objectif est de concevoir en même temps le véhicule et sa cargaison, plutôt que d'améliorer chacun dans son coin. François Robinet, qui représente le fonds AVP, vante une IA qui fonctionne « réellement in vivo, et pas seulement sur le papier ».
Côté business, WhiteLab, déjà implantée à Paris, Boston et Montréal, va étoffer ses équipes bostoniennes, développer sa présence sur la côte Ouest américaine, poursuivre son expansion en Europe et explorer le Japon et la Corée du Sud. L'entreprise, qui est à un tournant, mais désormais le cap sur le congrès annuel de la Société européenne de thérapie génique et cellulaire (ESGCT), où elle présentera de nouvelles données issues de ses travaux avec Sanofi, Cytiva, l'Institut du Cerveau et l'Institut Imagine.

articles.title: Prime Deal Days: Amazon reduziert Samsung-Galaxy-Geräte – hat aber nicht immer den besten Preis
articles.text:
Prime Deal Days: Amazon reduziert Samsung-Galaxy-Geräte – hat aber nicht immer den besten Preis
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Auch Samsung bleibt vor den Auswirkungen der Speicherkrise nicht verschont. Erst Anfang Oktober hatte das Unternehmen die Preise für die aktuelle Galaxy-S26-Serie nachträglich angehoben. Die gute Nachricht: Bei Händlern ist die Preiserhöhung bislang noch nicht angekommen. Zu den Prime Deal Days hat Amazon die Smartphones sogar günstiger im Angebot. Aber nicht jeder Deal kann überzeugen.
Galaxy-S26-Serie bei Amazon reduziert, anderswo günstiger
Allen voran das Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra ist beim Versandhändler reduziert. Amazon wirbt hier und bei vielen anderen Gadgets des Herstellers stets mit dem Zusatz „Exklusiv auf Amazon“. In der Regel bezieht sich das auf die erweiterte Garantie, die der Versandhändler anbietet. Beim S26 Ultra sind es drei statt zwei Jahre. Es liegt entsprechend ein wenig in eurer Betrachtung, ob die beiden Extras euch einen Aufpreis wert sind. Denn günstig ist das Galaxy S26 Ultra nicht. 1.015 Euro ruft Amazon auf. Die Konkurrenz ist teilweise bei unter 1.000 Euro – ohne die beiden Extras.
Das Smartphone sorgt besonders durch seine Display-Technologie für Aufsehen. Das sogenannte Privacy Display lässt sich so einstellen, dass Sitznachbarn im Zug oder anderswo nichts mehr auf dem Bildschirm erkennen. Außerdem hat es von allen Smartphones der Galaxy-S26-Serie die beste Kamera.
Wenn euch die Farbe weniger wichtig ist, könnt ihr beim Galaxy S26 Plus ebenfalls anderswo einen besseren Deal machen. Amazon ruft 849 Euro auf. Das ist aber nur bei der schwarzen Variante der beste Preis. Auf den etablierten Vergleichsplattformen sind die anderen Varianten teilweise deutlich günstiger. Beim Galaxy S26 lässt sich anderswo ebenfalls mehr sparen – wenn man auf das zusätzliche Garantiejahr verzichten kann. 819 Euro ruft Amazon für die Ausgabe mit 512 Gigabyte auf.
Samsung Galaxy Tabs im Angebot
Neben den Top-Smartphones sind bei Amazon einige Tablets reduziert. Dazu zählt das Galaxy Tab A11 Plus, das sich vor allem fürs Surfen auf der Couch eignet. Amazon verkauft es mit drei Jahren Garantie für 195 Euro. Zum selben Preis bekommt ihr das Gerät zudem bei Mediamarkt und Saturn. Dort müsst ihr lediglich auf das zusätzliche Jahr Herstellergarantie verzichten.
Bessere Deals sind das Galaxy Tab S10 FE mit elf Zoll großem Display und das größere Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus mit 13,3-Zoll-Bildschirm. Bei beiden gehört der S-Pen zum Lieferumfang. Zu den weiteren Vorzügen gehören ein wasserdichtes Gehäuse und ein höher aufgelöstes Display als beim Tab A11 Plus. Bei Amazon kosten die Geräte 399 beziehungsweise 599 Euro. Bei beiden handelt es sich um den aktuellen Bestpreis.
Beim Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra muss man wiederum ganz schön weit scrollen, bis Vergleichsportale das Gerät mit dem riesigen 14,6-Zoll-Bildschirm anzeigen. Amazon bietet auch hier wieder eine Garantie über drei Jahre an. Das Tablet kostet dafür 1.189 Euro. Bei Konkurrenten wie etwa Notebooksbilliger ist es mit 1.049 Euro deutlich günstiger.
Samsung Galaxy Watch für 169 Euro bei Amazon
Wer auf der Suche nach einer günstigen Smartwatch ist, muss wie bei den Apple-Angeboten auf die Geräte aus dem Vorjahr schauen. Amazon bietet die Galaxy Watch 8 ab 169 Euro an. Mit der Smartwatch könnt ihr Workouts und eure Schlafdaten tracken, mit Gemini interagieren und ihr sollt sogar dazu in der Lage sein, über euren Sensonr eure Ernährung zu tracken. Derzeit bietet kein anderer Händler die Uhr zu dem Preis. Bei der stylischen Galaxy Watch 8 Classic stimmt das dagegen nicht. 279 Euro ruft Amazon auf. Die Konkurrenz liegt teilweise zehn Euro darunter.
Samsung-Kopfhörer zum Bestpreis
Es müssen ja nicht immer die Airpods sein. Bei Amazon gibt es derzeit die Galaxy Buds 3 FE als günstige Alternative. Sie sind spritzwassergeschützt, bieten aktive Geräuschunterdrückung und kosten derzeit nur 69 Euro. Andere Anbieter sind aktuell teurer.
