articles.title: “Hace cosas que no entendemos y no sabemos cómo detenerla”: Sam Altman advirtió sobre el riesgo de perder el control de la IA
articles.text:
El director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman, concedió una entrevista a Vanity Fair en la que abordó tres de los frentes más sensibles del debate sobre la inteligencia artificial: el uso de ChatGPT en la infancia, la apertura de modelos pese a sus riesgos de seguridad y la posibilidad de que la tecnología represente una amenaza existencial para la humanidad.
El CEO de 41 años también habló sobre las tensiones internas que atraviesa su compañía mientras negocia el equilibrio entre innovación acelerada y controles de seguridad, en momentos en que la opinión pública exige mayor transparencia sobre el impacto social de estas herramientas.
El límite que Altman impone al uso de IA por parte de menores
Altman se mostró categórico sobre el uso de la inteligencia artificial durante la infancia y amplió su postura a la relación de los niños con la tecnología en general.
“Soy muy partidario de limitar la tecnología en general para los niños”, sostuvo, y señaló que prefiere que los menores dediquen más tiempo a jugar al aire libre en lugar de pasar ese tiempo frente a las pantallas.
Consultado sobre cuándo permitiría que sus propios hijos interactúen con ChatGPT, el directivo fue igual de cauto: “No tengo una edad en mente para dejar que mis hijos hablen con ChatGPT, pero ciertamente no es ahora”.
Sin embargo, matizó que esa prudencia no implica desconocer el papel que la tecnología tendrá en el futuro de las nuevas generaciones. “Está claro que los niños que nacen hoy crecerán en un mundo con IA y tendrán que saber usarla. Dudo que la primera infancia sea el momento adecuado para eso”, explicó.
El ejecutivo vinculó esta postura con una preocupación más amplia sobre el efecto de las pantallas en el desarrollo infantil, al señalar que un cerebro en formación requiere protección especial frente a tecnologías cuyo impacto todavía no se comprende en su totalidad.
Al referirse a los usos que cualquier persona debería evitar, sin importar su edad, el directivo sostuvo que la inteligencia artificial “no debe reemplazar la conexión humana”.
Sam Altman advirtió sobre el riesgo de perder el control de la IA
Sobre el riesgo de extinción vinculado a la inteligencia artificial, reconoció que la posibilidad no debe ser subestimada. “El hecho de que exista algún peligro, de que no sea cero, creo que es algo que todos deberíamos tomarnos muy en serio”, afirmó, y recordó que evitar ese desenlace forma parte de la misión fundacional de OpenAI.
En ese sentido, advirtió que “la IA es mucho más capaz que nosotros y tan inteligente que hace cosas que no entendemos y no sabemos cómo detenerla”.
También planteó que un accidente grave de seguridad podría derivar en una pérdida real de control, con un escenario en el que la inteligencia artificial escapara, provocara daños en internet y la sociedad no pudiera volver a controlarla.
El respaldo a los modelos abiertos y la advertencia sobre ciberataques
Consultado sobre la seguridad de los sistemas de código abierto, reconoció que esta política conlleva riesgos que la sociedad deberá asumir como costo de la libertad tecnológica.
“Se avecina una oleada de problemas de ciberseguridad derivados de estos modelos”, afirmó el directivo, quien defendió que la alternativa de prohibir estos desarrollos resultaría más perjudicial a largo plazo. El CEO explicó que dentro de la industria existen voces que proponen vetar el código abierto para evitar que sistemas enteros terminen vulnerados.
Sin embargo, descartó esa postura: “No creo que ese sea el precio de la libertad. Como sociedad, creo que tendremos que aceptar algunos incidentes cibernéticos graves derivados de los modelos de código abierto a cambio de la libertad que estos ofrecen”.
Altman planteó que la seguridad en cualquier industria se negocia constantemente entre costos y beneficios, y citó el ejemplo de la aviación, un sector con regulación estricta que igual registra accidentes. Para el fundador de OpenAI, definir el umbral de riesgo aceptable corresponde al proceso político y no exclusivamente a las compañías tecnológicas.
Altman propone estándares previos al lanzamiento inspirados en la aviación
Al hablar sobre la regulación de la inteligencia artificial, señaló que la industria debería aprender de sectores como la aviación y el automotor, especialmente de sus mecanismos de seguridad.
“Aquí hay algunas cosas que creo que han funcionado bien en otras industrias de las que deberíamos aprender”, afirmó, y destacó el trabajo de la Junta Nacional de Seguridad del Transporte (NTSB) de Estados Unidos en la investigación y reporte de accidentes e incidentes.
También propuso establecer estándares previos al lanzamiento y un marco de responsabilidad para las empresas que desarrollan estos sistemas.
Además, sostuvo que las evaluaciones de seguridad deben comenzar durante el entrenamiento de los modelos y no únicamente antes de su publicación: “Ahora decimos que, incluso durante el entrenamiento, pueden surgir problemas”.

articles.title: AMR in Africa: The data gap behind the crisis
articles.text:
This contributor piece by Chinaza Esiaba was first published on TechCabal Insights.
For years, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Africa has been described through increasingly stark numbers. AMR happens when bacteria and other microbes evolve to resist the drugs used to treat them, making common infections harder to cure and, in some cases, untreatable. A Lancet analysis estimated that western sub-Saharan Africa had the world’s highest death rate attributable to bacterial AMR in 2019: 27.3 deaths per 100,000 people. The figures establish the scale of the threat. They also expose a paradox: where resistant infections are a serious concern, the laboratory evidence needed to track them is often scarce.
The World Health Organisation (WHO) estimates that one in five laboratory-confirmed bacterial infections in its African Region in 2023 was resistant to antibiotics. That estimate cannot capture infections that are never tested. The visibility gap extends beyond Africa. 48% of countries did not report resistance data to the WHO’s Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System (GLASS) in 2023, and about half of those that reported lacked systems to produce reliable data.
This is a public health challenge with a health tech dimension. AI diagnostics and prescribing tools depend on laboratories that can test infections, records that link results to patients, and surveillance systems that turn individual tests into evidence about local resistance. For governments and investors, building those connections may be the more immediate opportunity.
Clinicians need diagnostic evidence to prescribe well
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention says that one in two hospitalised patients receiving antibiotics is treated with more than one antibiotic. Watch antibiotics, which have a significant impact on antimicrobial resistance (AMR), such as ceftriaxone, cefuroxime and ciprofloxacin, also account for a large share of prescriptions. Nigerian studies have found high levels of empirical prescribing, that is, starting treatment before laboratory evidence identifies the organism or confirms which antibiotic will work. Dr Ifeyinwa George, a pharmacist and AMR programme manager at DRASA Health Trust, a Nigerian nonprofit focused on infection prevention and public health security, has pointed to limited laboratory capacity as a barrier to detecting and tracking resistant pathogens.
An Africa CDC-led study of 14 countries found that only 1.3% of roughly 50,000 laboratories in participating networks performed bacteriology testing. Of approximately 187,000 samples tested for resistance, 88% lacked clinical information such as the patient’s diagnosis or prior antibiotic use. In a survey of 219 Kenyan health facilities, 61.6% did not offer bacterial culture testing and only 16.9% performed antimicrobial susceptibility testing. As Ghanaian AMR researcher Prof Beverly Egyir put it, “When we do not test, we are essentially flying blind.”
This gap can persist even where testing is available. At Cape Coast Teaching Hospital in Ghana, laboratory reports took an average of 3.4 days from sample receipt to upload into the electronic health system. It is tempting to look at numbers like these and reduce AMR to an antibiotic-overuse problem. Africa’s experience is more complicated: without diagnostic evidence, clinicians may prescribe empirically due to a lack of information, not simply because they disregard stewardship. Giving them better information requires functioning laboratories, timely results, and systems that link those results to patient records.
Medicine quality is another part of the data gap
Resistance surveillance also needs to account for the medicines patients receive. In 2025, Ghana’s Food and Drugs Authority found counterfeit pharmaceutical products worth GH₵42 million ($3.6 million). Additionally, Nigeria’s National Primary Healthcare Development Agency stated that about 70% of medicines distributed in the country were substandard or counterfeit. Substandard medicines with too little active ingredient can also expose bacteria to inadequate concentrations and contribute to resistance.
That is a case for better medicine traceability and reporting. Nigeria’s National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) uses a Mobile Authentication Service that allows consumers to check medicine codes via text message. Batch tracking, rapid alerts and shared records can help regulators find suspect products and remove them from circulation. The WHO is moving in a similar direction. Its 2026 digital-transformation guidance specifically encourages countries to move from fragmented, paper-based reporting of substandard and falsified medicines to interoperable digital reporting systems. These tools are part of the AMR response because medicine quality changes what treatment a patient actually receives.
When the data infrastructure exists
Some countries are building systems that make more advanced analysis useful. South Africa’s National Institute for Communicable Diseases publishes an AMR surveillance dashboard that draws on laboratory data and helps show which pathogens are becoming resistant. In Ghana, researchers using whole-genome sequencing have studied cholera isolates alongside samples from other African countries to examine resistance genes and how strains are related. These methods can answer sharper public health questions when sample collection and routine data are sufficient to support them.
Kenya provides a practical example of how that foundation grows. According to the WHO’s account of the programme, two model surveillance sites established in 2017 grew into a network of 32 sites across 27 countries. The country now integrates resistance, antibiotic use, and consumption data into a central warehouse and began submitting individual-level data to GLASS in 2025. Susan Githii, Kenya’s GLASS focal person, says the richer data help the team understand resistance trends and guide decisions. The remaining work includes connecting hospital systems and filling missing patient fields.
The investment test
The lesson is not that Africa should abandon AI, rapid diagnostics or clinical decision-support software. These tools need somewhere solid to land. For healthtech investors, the AMR opportunity may lie in systems that make laboratory evidence usable: software that delivers susceptibility results to clinicians, connects data across hospitals and helps regulators trace suspect medicine batches. AI could use that foundation to flag unusual resistance patterns or support treatment decisions. It cannot fill in for infections that were never tested or medicines whose quality is unknown.
The harder question is who keeps that infrastructure running. The EU-backed ARILAC initiative is set to strengthen laboratory and data systems in eight countries over four years. At its launch in July 2026, Africa CDC called for those systems to be included in national budgets. Its 2026–2030 AMR framework also identifies sustainable financing as a priority. Laboratories need steady supplies, maintained equipment, and skilled staff long after a grant ends. Investors need a credible path for health systems to pay for and keep using the tools they fund.
Technology alone will not slow resistance; infection prevention, vaccination, clean water, and responsible antibiotic use remain essential. But the strongest investment case may be in the infrastructure that tells clinicians which treatments still work locally, shows public health teams where resistance is rising, and helps regulators keep poor-quality medicines from reaching patients.

articles.title: China quiere usar RISC-V para escapar de Arm/x86 y le está ayudando una empresa de EEUU a hacerlo
articles.text:
La arquitectura RISC-V interpreta un papel central en la estrategia de China. Esta tecnología es una alternativa abierta tanto a los diseños x86-64 de Intel y AMD como a las CPU con arquitectura Arm que tanto han proliferado durante los últimos años. Para el país liderado por Xi Jinping representa la oportunidad de sostener su desarrollo tecnológico a pesar de las sanciones de la alianza liderada por EEUU. De hecho, el Gobierno chino ha creado un consorcio de empresas e institutos de investigación que persigue desarrollar chips con esta arquitectura.
Tencent, Alibaba y la Academia de Ciencias de China son algunas de las organizaciones que están trabajando en el desarrollo de procesadores con arquitectura RISC-V, y la Administración de EEUU está muy preocupada. Lo está debido a que esta tecnología puede utilizarse para poner a punto superordenadores extraordinariamente capaces. De hecho, Europa ya tiene listo EPAC (European Processor ACcelerator), su primer chip RISC-V, y precisamente ha sido diseñado para residir en el interior de los próximos superordenadores europeos.
En este escenario resulta sorprendente que una de las empresas que está trabajando codo con codo con las compañías y los centros de investigación chinos sea estadounidense. MIPS, una organización propiedad de GlobalFoundries que se dedica al diseño de procesadores RISC-V, está trabajando estrechamente con empresas chinas en la evolución y la estandarización de esta arquitectura. Curiosamente, su nombre procede de la histórica arquitectura RISC Microprocessor without Interlocked Pipeline Stages, y su colaboración con China ha sido confirmada oficialmente por Yankin Tanurhan, su director de tecnología.
UN VISTAZO A...
China ya está llevando RISC-V a los centros de datos
La colaboración de MIPS y las empresas chinas está respaldada por RISC-V International, una organización internacional sin ánimo de lucro que mantiene y desarrolla el estándar abierto RISC-V. No obstante, en este proyecto también participan compañías europeas y universidades de varios continentes. No lo están llevando a cabo solo MIPS y las entidades chinas. En cualquier caso, para China RISC-V es fundamental en su esfuerzo para sostener su desarrollo tecnológico al margen de las arquitecturas x86-64 y Arm.
Alibaba y StarFive ya tienen procesadores RISC-V para servidores
Las empresas chinas llevan varios años incorporando procesadores RISC-V en microcontroladores, dispositivos IoT y sistemas industriales y de automoción, pero ya están llevando esta arquitectura también a los centros de datos para inteligencia artificial (IA). RISC-V ha adquirido una importancia estratégica creciente para China a medida que EEUU ha endurecido las sanciones en el ámbito de los semiconductores.
Alibaba ya tiene procesadores RISC-V para servidores. Y StarFive anunció en marzo el lanzamiento de un procesador RISC-V de 12 nm llamado Lion Rock. Este chip también está destinado a los servidores, y su producción a gran escala está prevista entre finales de 2026 y comienzos de 2027. Un apunte interesante: el chip que podéis ver justo encima de estas líneas es el TH1520 de T-Head, la filial de semiconductores de Alibaba. Este SoC incorpora una CPU de cuatro núcleos XuanTie C910 con arquitectura RISC-V de 64 bits.
En el contexto de esta arquitectura hay una perspectiva que merece la pena que no pasemos por alto: en una tecnología abierta como RISC-V controlar la evolución del estándar es tan importante como fabricar los circuitos integrados. Y China y EEUU lo saben. Las compañías que participan en RISC-V International pueden contribuir a decidir qué extensiones y funcionalidades terminan formando parte de las especificaciones finales que utilizará toda la industria. Esta capacidad de influencia es demasiado importante para que estas dos superpotencias la pasen por alto.

articles.title: Como o El Niño pode afetar a agricultura brasileira
articles.text:
A chegada do El Niño deve mudar a rotina do campo brasileiro. Enquanto produtores do Sul precisam se preparar para chuvas intensas e excesso de água, outras regiões terão pela frente seca, calor e irregularidade das precipitações.
Para reduzir os impactos, a Embrapa reuniu recomendações específicas para cada área. Entre as medidas está o uso do Zoneamento Agrícola de Risco Climático (Zarc), ferramenta que indica as melhores épocas para plantar de acordo com o risco climático de cada cultura e região.
Chuvas fortes no Sul, seca em outras áreas
Na Região Sul, as chuvas devem ser mais intensas e concentradas entre setembro e dezembro. O excesso de precipitação pode provocar encharcamento, erosão e perda de nutrientes, além de dificultar a semeadura, a aplicação de insumos e a colheita.
A umidade elevada também favorece doenças. Trigo e outros cereais de inverno, arroz irrigado, soja, milho, frutas de clima temperado e hortaliças estão entre as culturas mais expostas.
No Centro-Oeste, Mato Grosso, Goiás e Distrito Federal apresentam maior risco de seca, enquanto o sul de Mato Grosso do Sul tende a receber mais chuva. O período mais crítico está previsto entre novembro de 2026 e janeiro de 2027.
No Nordeste, a preocupação se concentra na menor oferta de água e nas temperaturas elevadas. A situação hídrica inicial, porém, é mais favorável do que durante o episódio de 2015/2016: em agosto de 2026, os reservatórios nordestinos estavam próximos de 51% da capacidade, contra cerca de 23% em agosto de 2015.
No Norte, a redução dos níveis dos rios pode afetar navegação, transporte, abastecimento, agricultura de várzea, pesca e aquicultura. Já no Sudeste, áreas mais secas e mais chuvosas podem ocorrer até dentro de um mesmo estado.
Recomendações mudam conforme a região
As orientações da Embrapa levam em conta as culturas e as condições locais. Entre as medidas estão:
- Centro-Oeste: se o atraso da soja for grande, reavaliar o milho segunda safra e considerar alternativas como sorgo ou milheto, de menor custo e risco.
- Nordeste: ampliar a captação e o armazenamento de água com estruturas como cisternas, barreiros-trincheira e barragens subterrâneas.
- Norte: no arroz de várzea e terras baixas, ajustar o plantio ao regime de vazante e evitar drenagem excessiva.
- Sudeste: no café, acompanhar principalmente a floração e o enchimento dos grãos, fases sensíveis ao déficit hídrico e ao calor.
- Sul: no arroz irrigado, ajustar a semeadura, garantir drenagem rápida e monitorar doenças como a brusone.
Conservação ajuda a reduzir os riscos
No Centro-Oeste, a Embrapa recomenda agir antes que as condições adversas apareçam. No Sul, essa preparação também passa pelo planejamento da microbacia hidrográfica, com medidas para controlar o escoamento da água e reduzir os efeitos de eventos extremos.
Leia mais:
- El Niño agrava seca e deixa milhões em risco no Corredor Seco da América Central
- Brasil terá meses de extremos com El Niño mais forte, aponta Inmet
- Super El Niño pode provocar 451 mil mortes por calor até 2027; Brasil está entre os mais afetados
Essa preocupação com a preparação aparece nas recomendações dos pesquisadores. Rodrigo Garcia, da Embrapa Agropecuária Oeste, destaca que o investimento em tecnologia e práticas conservacionistas pode aumentar a resiliência dos sistemas produtivos. “Esse investimento, somado à adoção de práticas agrícolas mais conservacionistas, aumenta a resiliência do sistema de produção, superando possíveis desafios climáticos que são cada vez mais recorrentes”, afirma.
No Sudeste, essa mesma lógica se volta para a qualidade do solo. Ederson Jesus, pesquisador da Embrapa Agrobiologia, chama atenção para a recuperação de áreas degradadas e o uso de bioinsumos. Segundo ele, “a recomendação central é reforçar a base biológica dos sistemas produtivos: solo coberto, áreas degradadas recuperadas e bioinsumos que ajudam a planta a enfrentar déficit hídrico e calor”.
Com cenários tão diferentes entre as regiões, a orientação da Embrapa é adaptar as decisões às condições de cada propriedade e se antecipar aos efeitos do fenômeno. O objetivo é reduzir a exposição das lavouras e dos rebanhos aos extremos de chuva, seca e calor durante o El Niño 2026/2027.

articles.title: Navigating Open Source Governance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: The 2026 State of OSPOs and Open Source Management
articles.text:
Navigating Open Source Governance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: The 2026 State of OSPOs and Open Source Management
Hilary Carter | 06 October 2026
As open source software continues to serve as the backbone for modern digital infrastructure, the operational mechanisms designed to manage, protect, and guide its adoption must continuously evolve. Over the past few years, Open Source Program Offices (OSPOs) have transitioned from novel operational units to critical corporate functions. Today, as artificial intelligence reshapes software development and organizational strategy, OSPOs are stepping into an even broader, highly strategic role across global enterprises.
Coinciding with Open Source Summit Europe, LF Research, in partnership with the TODO Group, is thrilled to share the key findings from our latest report, The 2026 State of OSPOs and Open Source Management, sponsored by CNCF and the FinOps Foundation. We are truly appreciative of their sponsorship, as well as to the organizations who participated as distribution partners for the survey on which this year’s findings are based, especially CURIOSS, GitHub, InnerSource, OpenChain, and OpenSSF. Several leaders from the TODO Group community also participated in interviews, sharing their practitioner perspectives.
Additionally, this year’s report features a foreword from Stephen Augustus from Bloomberg, one of the most well-known voices from open source and an active leader from the TODO Group and numerous other open source project communities.
Here are a few of the report’s principal findings:
Open source management reaches new heights
This year’s research reveals that open source program offices are reaching an unprecedented level of organizational stability. A substantial 57% of OSPOs have remained in the same organizational home over the last 2-3 years, signaling that executive leadership increasingly views open source management as a permanent, core business capability.
Furthermore, as organizations expand, their open source structures tend to formalize significantly. Over half of large enterprises (53%) maintain a formally structured OSPO, whereas mid-size and small organizations lean more heavily on informal setups or emerging operational frameworks.
At the same time, regional adoption patterns are shifting dramatically. The Asia-Pacific region is poised to lead the next wave of expansion, with 20% of organizations planning an OSPO—double the planning rate observed across the Americas and Europe.
Steering the artificial intelligence transformation
Perhaps the most defining trend highlighted in the study is the rapid integration of AI governance and agentic workflows into daily OSPO operations. Rather than treating open source software and artificial intelligence as separate disciplines, organizations are leveraging established open source governance frameworks to manage the complexities of modern AI systems.
Key findings regarding AI governance and implementation include:
- Pervasive governance involvement: A striking 79% of OSPOs involved in AI governance actively contribute to policy formulation, evaluation of open models and datasets, risk management, and legal reviews.
- Early lifecycle engagement: Among OSPOs participating in AI decision-making, 85% are brought in at or before the technology selection phase, ensuring compliance and security standards are met from inception.
- Addressing core vulnerabilities: The top AI-related risks managed by OSPOs focus heavily on licensing and intellectual property risks (65%) and security vulnerabilities (65%), followed closely by data privacy concerns (59%).
- Emergence of agentic AI: AI agents are actively entering open source operations, with 69% of organizations currently prototyping or actively running agentic tools for OSPO workflows, including 18% operating agentic AI in production settings.
Unlocking strategic value across the enterprise
Beyond risk mitigation and compliance, OSPOs are increasingly recognized as catalysts for operational speed and software reliability. Respondents in our research highlight software quality, security, and compliance as the single most impactful outcome delivered by an OSPO (58%), with open source ecosystem participation (49%) and accelerated development speed (47%) trailing right behind.
As new programs emerge to capture these benefits, the upcoming wave of adoption appears imminent. Among organizations currently planning an OSPO, 79% expect to officially launch their initiative within two years, and 66% intend to back these offices with dedicated, full-time staff.
Do you agree or disagree with any of these findings from your personal experience? Let us know whether the trends that this report reveals are in line with your realities. We’ll be sure to pass any feedback or points of interest along to our report authors Bianca Trinkenreich, Ana Jiménez Santamaría, and Adrienn Lawson. Their efforts have produced an important reference on the role of the OSPO and open source best practices and management today.
To explore the complete dataset, practical case studies, and detailed recommendations for building sustainable open source operations, we invite you to access the full library of insights on our research portal: https://www.linuxfoundation.org/research

articles.title: Two mystery PlayStation products have leaked — one might be a PlayStation Portal OLED
articles.text:
Is Sony about to announce a new PlayStation Portal game streaming handheld? The Wi-Fi Alliance recently certified two unannounced PlayStation products of some kind, and the certification documents indicate that they could be updates to the PlayStation Portal, which might mean we’re getting the OLED screen rumored earlier this year.
Two mystery PlayStation products have leaked — one might be a PlayStation Portal OLED
The Wi-Fi Alliance recently leaked two new PlayStation devices that seem like they could be updates to Sony’s handheld for streaming.
The two devices, which are classified as “Gaming Console/Peripherals,” have model numbers of CFI-Y2000 and CFI-Y2105, which sound like a clear step up from the CFI-Y1001 model number for the currently available Portal. The docs say that the new models run on Android 15, which further indicates that they might be Portals; the current model also runs Android. (The PS5 home console, on the other hand, runs a custom OS.)
While Sony is expected to eventually announce a PlayStation handheld that natively plays PS5 games on next-gen AMD graphics, its PlayStation Portal streams games instead, either from your home PlayStation or from Sony’s cloud. That can make for a far more affordable device, something Sony itself pointed out this June: “Cloud streaming also requires minimal memory, making it an increasingly attractive low-cost thin client device in the current market environment where memory prices are rising.”
The new gadgets don’t look like they’re getting dramatically improved Wi-Fi for streaming, though: they’re certified for 1x1 2.4GHz and 5GHz Wi-Fi, but not 6GHz and seemingly without more antennas.
There’s not much more to glean from the certification docs, unfortunately — I’ve embedded them at the end of this article, if you want to see them for yourself — and PlayStation didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. But as reported by VideoCardz, hardware leaker KeplerL2 said earlier this year that Sony was working on “another version” of the Portal for this year that would be an “OLED version.”
The original Portal, which has an 8-inch LCD screen, launched in late 2023.

articles.title: Pinterest's AI now turns beauty Pins into action plans | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Pinterest on Tuesday showed off a new feature that will leverage AI to take action on your saved inspiration from beauty-related Pins, like hair and nail ideas, and turn them into actionable plans you can take with you to the salon.
“Beauty Guides,” which are powered by the company’s visual intelligence and generative AI technology, Pinterest Intelligence, will translate Pins into terms and phrases used by stylists and nail artists that everyday users may not know, like “balayage,” “root melt,” or “almond nails.”
The feature is a small but practical way to introduce AI into users’ everyday lives, as it slots into something that people are already doing: bringing a photo of their inspiration to the salon. That’s useful to a large extent, but having the right terminology at hand while you discuss what parts of the look you want to edit or change can be useful as well.
Plus, the guides offer the sort of information that can help users plan for their visit, like the time each part of the process may take and the cost. (Balayage goes into the hundreds of dollars, so that’s information you might like to have up front!)
The action guides will show up when you tap on the “Get the Guide” button within the app, and will then offer details about what, specifically, you should ask for to achieve the same look, the time it takes, price range, and maintenance requirements, like how often you’ll need to trim, tone, or touch up, for instance.
At launch, the feature will work across Pins related to hairstyle, color, nail shape, and finish.

articles.title: Nikkei discloses breaches of employees’ Microsoft, Google email accounts
articles.text:
Over the weekend, Japanese publishing giant Nikkei disclosed that unknown attackers recently breached two employee email accounts and used one to send thousands of phishing emails.
In a Sunday statement, the company said an employee's Google Workspace account was accessed in late July, exposing the personal information of employees and business partners.
Nikkei changed the account's password after discovering the breach in early August, following a notification from Google.
While this incident may have exposed the names and email addresses of 1,646 individuals, Nikkei says the affected data doesn't include information about readers or interviewees.
More recently, threat actors accessed another employee's Microsoft 365 account in September and used it to send 9,000 phishing emails targeting Nikkei staff and interviewees.
"On September 30th , emails containing links to malicious websites were sent to internal staff and to interviewees with whom several employees had been in contact," the media giant said. "Our company has changed its passwords, and no unauthorized logins have been confirmed since then. We have contacted the recipients individually and requested that they delete the emails."
The company also warned affected individuals to watch for suspicious emails that may impersonate Nikkei or its subsidiaries in new phishing attacks.
Nikkei has yet to attribute the attacks to a specific threat actor or hacking group and hasn't shared whether the two incidents are connected.
These are the latest in a string of security incidents Nikkei has disclosed in recent years. Last year, the company also revealed that its Slack messaging platform had been breached, affecting more than 17,000 employees and business partners.
In May 2022, Nikkei's Singapore subsidiary was hit by a ransomware attack that affected a server "likely" containing customer data. Three years earlier, in late September 2019, Nikkei lost approximately $29 million in a business email compromise (BEC) attack that targeted a Nikkei America employee.
Nikkei owns the Financial Times and The Nikkei, the world's largest financial newspaper, and is one of the world's largest media corporations.
It controls more than 40 affiliated companies involved in publishing, broadcasting, events, database services, and the index business, has 37 foreign editorial bureaus and over 1,500 journalists worldwide, and has over 3.7 million digital paid subscriptions.

brusex-00 - 12 hours ago
Incidents like this show why password resets alone should not be the end of the response. Organizations should also review active sessions, OAuth permissions, forwarding rules, MFA settings, and sign-in logs after an email account compromise.
The fact that one compromised account was then used to send thousands of phishing emails also highlights how quickly a single account can become a trusted attack channel. Conditional access, phishing-resistant MFA, and regular employee awareness training can significantly reduce that risk.

articles.title: Engineer sentenced for locking over 3,000 devices on employer network
articles.text:
A former core infrastructure engineer at an industrial company headquartered in New Jersey was sentenced to 32 months in prison for locking thousands of devices on his employer's network in a ransomware-style attack.
57-year-old Daniel Rhyne from Kansas City, Missouri, pleaded guilty to his role in a failed extortion plot targeting the New Jersey company that employed him after being arrested in August 2024 and released after his initial appearance in federal court.
According to court documents, he remotely accessed the company's network without authorization using an administrator account between November 8 and November 25 and scheduled tasks on the domain controller that changed the password of the administrator account to "TheFr0zenCrew!", deleted 13 domain admin accounts, and changed the passwords for 301 domain user accounts to "TheFr0zenCrew!".
Rhyne also added scheduled tasks that changed the password for two local admin accounts to "PsPasswd" (blocking access to 254 servers), changed the password for two more admin accounts (blocking access to an additional 3,284 workstations), and shut down random servers and workstations on the company's network over several days in December 2023.
On November 25, Rhyne sent coworkers a ransom email titled "Your Network Has Been Penetrated," in which he said that server backups had also been deleted to make data recovery impossible and threatened to shut down 40 random servers daily over the next ten days unless the company paid a 20 bitcoin ransom (roughly $750,000 at the time).
"On or about November 25, 2023, at approximately 4:00 p.m. EST, network administrators employed at Victim-1 began receiving password reset notifications for a Victim-1 domain administrator account, as well as hundreds of Victim-1 user accounts," the criminal complaint reads.
"Shortly thereafter, the Victim-1 network administrators discovered that all other Victim-1 domain administrator accounts were deleted, thereby denying domain administrator access to Victim-1's computer networks."
Investigators found that on November 22, while planning his extortion plot, Rhyne used his account on a hidden virtual machine to search the web for information on changing domain user passwords, deleting domain accounts, and clearing Windows logs.
One week earlier, he also searched on his laptop for "command line to change local administrator password," "command line to remotely change local administrator password," and "how to remotely shutdown a computer usign cmd."
Earlier this year, in March, 27-year-old North Carolina data analyst contractor Cameron Curry was also sentenced to two years in prison after being found guilty of extorting his employer, Brightly Software (a Software-as-a-Service company previously known as SchoolDude) for $2.5 million.

articles.title: Canada’s major projects boom is a big opportunity for smaller firms, but hurdles remain | BetaKit
articles.text:
Many of Canada’s small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) are expected to ride the wave of the country’s major projects boom, provided they can overcome some key challenges.
The news: A new report from the Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) and the Transition Accelerator found that Canada’s big infrastructure push could attract more than $670 billion CAD in additional investment and boost the country’s gross domestic product by 4.1 percent over the next four years.
The study, released on Tuesday, surveyed 750 companies that are already supporting such initiatives and 250 other interested firms. It estimates that successfully delivering these large Canadian AI, energy, defence, housing, mining, and gas projects could require the participation of 280,000 Canadian SMBs. This group stands to benefit from as much as $443 billion in economic activity tied to these initiatives. While many such firms are eager to take part, they still face key barriers to reaping the full benefits.
From the source: “This is going to be a major shift for the Canadian economy,” BDC chief economist Pierre Cléroux told BetaKit in an interview. “Many [mid-sized] businesses are ready to be a part of this investment.” But if Canada hopes to fully deliver these projects, it must bring more smaller SMBs along for the ride. “They are also very interested, but it’s more complicated,” he said.
The context: Cléroux was surprised to learn that so many mid-sized businesses—namely, firms with 100 employees or more that already derive 50 percent of their revenue from large projects—were already prepared and positioned to take advantage of this boom. However, he was not taken aback by the survey’s finding that their smaller counterparts, which face greater difficulty building capacity, securing financing, and navigating procurement processes, were not. The solution, BDC argued, is to provide those smaller businesses with better information about upcoming opportunities, smaller contract lots, reduced financial or bonding requirements, more predictable payment terms, and clearer procurement pathways.
Final thought: While construction, mining, and manufacturing SMBs likely stand to benefit most from this push, defence and AI data centres account for approximately $220 billion and $11.2 billion of this major projects pipeline, and Cléroux noted that nearly every initiative will require some degree of technology.
Feature image courtesy Mark Carney via LinkedIn.

articles.title: Bis zu 67 Rabatt auf die eigene Hardware: Diese Echo-Angebote lohnen sich an den Prime Deal Days
articles.text:
Prime Deal Days: Amazon senkt die Preise auf eigene Hardware – ist damit aber nicht allein
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Am 6. und 7. Oktober veranstaltet Amazon erneut seine Prime Deal Days und lockt an beiden Tagen mit zahlreichen Rabatten aus nahezu allen Kategorien. Zwei Tage lang stehen wieder tausende Produkte günstiger im Shop – besonders interessant sind dabei erfahrungsgemäß die Geräte aus dem eigenen Haus. Amazon nutzt solche Aktionstage regelmäßig, um die eigenen Geräte aus dem Echo-Ökosystem deutlich unter den üblichen Preisen anzubieten.
Gerade bei dieser Hardware lohnt sich deshalb ein Vergleich mit den regulären Preisen. Denn Amazon kann bei den eigenen Geräten besonders offensiv rabattieren und kombiniert einzelne Produkte zudem häufig zu Bundles. So werden etwa Türklingeln mit den passenden Kameras und den Echo-Geräten im Paket angeboten.
Trotzdem gilt auch bei den Prime Deal Days: Ein roter Preis allein macht noch kein gutes Angebot. Manche Geräte waren bereits günstiger erhältlich, bei anderen lohnt sich möglicherweise das neuere Modell mehr als der stärker reduzierte Vorgänger, der bestimmte wichtige Funktionen noch nicht bietet. Entscheidend ist deshalb nicht nur die Höhe des Rabatts, sondern auch, was das jeweilige Gerät kann und für wen es gedacht ist.
Wir haben uns die Angebote für Amazons eigene Hardware angesehen und zeigen, welche Echo-Deals am 6. und 7. Oktober besonders interessant sind.
Warum sich die Doppelpackstrategie für Amazon rechnet
Wie schon beim ersten Prime Day in diesem Jahr, der im Juni stattfand, hat das Unternehmen auch dieses Mal wieder eine bewährte Strategie am Start: Die Amazon-Lautsprecher werden gleich im Doppelpack angeboten und sind nur in dieser Kombination nochmal geringfügig günstiger. Das sichert Amazon zusätzliche Umsätze und sorgt für eine breite Durchdringung des Marktes. Denn wer einen braucht, muss das zweite Gerät im Familien- oder Bekanntenkreis unterbringen.
Gut zu wissen: Selbst im Vergleich zum Sommer-Event hat Amazon noch einmal geringfügig die Preise gesenkt. Diese gelten – wie bei vielen Prime-Day-Angeboten – aber eben nur für Kund:innen mit einem gültigen Prime-Abo. Das kann allerdings auch ein Sieben-Tage-Abo für 99 Cent sein oder ein Probe-Abo, das Amazon an bestimmte Kund:innen umsonst vergibt. Wie deine Konditionen bei der Prime-Mitgliedschaft sind, siehst du allerdings erst, wenn du das jeweilige Angebot in den Warenkorb packst.
Die Amazon Echo Lautsprecher
Der Echo Dot ist Amazons kompakter Allround-Smart-Speaker für den Einstieg ins Alexa-Ökosystem. Dabei bietet er für kleinere Räume ausreichenden Klang und zusätzlich einen integrierten Temperatursensor, bleibt aber deutlich kleiner und günstiger als die leistungsstärkeren Echo-Modelle.
- Amazon Echo Dot (Neueste Generation)* für 29,99 Euro statt 89,99 Euro
- Amazon Echo Dot (Neueste Generation)* im Doppelpack für 56,98 Euro statt 179,98 Euro
Der Echo Spot verbindet einen kompakten Alexa-Lautsprecher mit einem kleinen 2,8-Zoll-Display. Darauf zeigt er unter anderem Uhrzeit, Wetter oder Musiktitel an und eignet sich damit vor allem als smarter Wecker für den Nachttisch.
- Amazon Echo Spot (neueste Generation)* für 49,99 Euro statt 119,99 Euro
- Amazon Echo Spot (neueste Generation)* im Doppelpack für 94,98 Euro statt 239,98 Euro
Der Echo Dot Max ist die leistungsfähigere Variante des Dot und bietet mit seinem Zwei-Wege-Lautsprechersystem deutlich mehr Bass und einen volleren Klang. Zudem steckt in ihm neuere Hardware.
- Amazon Echo Dot Max (neueste Generation)* für 64,99 Euro statt 129,99 Euro
- Amazon Echo Dot Max (neueste Generation)* im Doppelpack für 123,48 Euro statt 259,98 Euro
Die Amazon Echo Lautsprecher mit Bildschirm
Der Echo Show 5 ist der kleinste klassische Echo mit Touchscreen. Sein kompaktes Display reicht für Wetterinformationen, Smart-Home-Steuerung, Videoanrufe oder kurze Videos und macht ihn vor allem für Nachttisch oder Schreibtisch interessant.
- Echo Show 5 (neueste Generation)* für 59,99 Euro statt 119,99 Euro
Der Echo Show 8 bietet mit seinem 8-Zoll-Display mehr Platz für Videos, Rezepte, Videoanrufe und die Smart-Home-Steuerung. Gegenüber dem Show 5 bietet er zudem den kräftigeren Klang und eignet sich deshalb eher als zentraler Echo für Küche oder Wohnbereich.
- Amazon Echo Show 8 (neueste Generation)* für 134,99 Euro statt 219,99 Euro
Der Echo Show 11 folgt technisch weitgehend dem neuen Show 8, bietet aber eine größere Bildschirmfläche. Er ist damit vor allem interessant, wenn das Display häufiger für Videos, Informationen oder die Steuerung des Smart Homes genutzt werden soll.
- Amazon Echo Show 11 (neueste Generation)* für 154,99 Euro statt 269,99 Euro
Der Echo Show 15 ist mit seinem 15,6-Zoll-Display eher eine digitale Familienzentrale als ein klassischer Smart Speaker. Er kann an der Wand montiert werden und eignet sich unter anderem für Kalender, Einkaufslisten, Widgets und Videoinhalte.
- Amazon Echo Show 15 (neueste Generation)* für 259,99 Euro statt 379,99 Euro
Keine Lust auf Prime? Kein Problem
Wer sich nicht extra ein Prime-Abo zulegen möchte, um bei einem Echo-Gerät zuzuschlagen, kann auch bei der Konkurrenz zugreifen. Viele große Anbieter, wie etwa Mediamarkt* und Saturn*, haben die Preise auf die Amazon-Hardware ebenfalls gesenkt und bieten viele Lautsprecher und Displays mit derselben Vergünstigung an. Beachten sollte man aber auch: Für den Login in die Alexa-App ist ein Amazon-Konto nötig, für den Betrieb der Geräte ein Prime-Abo zumindest mal von Vorteil.
Bundling-Angebote: Weitere Möglichkeit zum Sparen
Noch attraktiver im Hinblick auf das Sparpotential sind die Bundling-Angebote, etwa mit smarten Steckdosen und Glühbirnen, den passenden Innen- und Außenkameras sowie drahtlosen und netzgebundenen Klingeln aus der Ring-Serie. Hier gibt es allerdings für die jeweiligen Geräte unterschiedliche Kombinationen, die sich jeweils auf der entsprechenden Produktseite finden.
Ebenfalls nicht einzeln führen wir hier die jeweiligen Farbvarianten auf. Dazu ein Tipp: Insbesondere bei weiter fortschreitenden Prime Deal Days können einzelne Farbvarianten zwar nicht ausverkauft sein, wohl aber mit einer langen Lieferfrist versehen – oftmals mehrere Wochen. In diesem Fall lohnt sich oftmals der Wechsel der Farbvariante, um gegebenenfalls das Produkt deutlich schneller zu erhalten.
Zusätzlich zu den hier aufgeführten Echo-Geräten gibt es in einigen Fällen noch spezielle Gerätevarianten für Kinder. Diese sind nicht nur farblich auf die Wünsche des Nachwuchses abgestimmt, sondern bieten insbesondere im Umgang mit den Inhalten und der Alexa-Steuerung die kindgerechte Variante.
Gut zu wissen: Mit Alexa+ hat Amazon seine Sprachassistentin vor einigen Monaten um generative KI erweitert. Der Dienst ist in Deutschland derzeit noch im Early Access verfügbar und läuft auf den meisten aktuellen Echo-Geräten; Käufer neuer Modelleerhalten direkten Zugang. Während der Testphase ist Alexa+ kostenlos, anschließend ist der Dienst für Prime-Mitglieder ohne Aufpreis enthalten. Nutzer ohne Prime-Abo sollen 22,99 Euro pro Monat zahlen.

articles.title: Free Firefox security features to help keep you safe online | The Mozilla Blog
articles.text:
Strengthen your online security for free with Firefox
Every October, Cybersecurity Awareness Month reminds us the importance of protecting our digital lives.
The theme for 2026 is ‘Don’t Make It Easy for Them,’ with the National Cybersecurity Alliance (NCA) and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) providing simple, actionable steps users can take to make it harder for cybercriminals to attack.
Everyone wants to be safe online, but one of the most common excuses we hear is “I don’t have the time or the money to invest in it right now.” Well, we have good news: you can improve your online security easily, for the low price of $0.
Firefox provides several free features designed to make it easier to protect your online life and harder for cybercriminals to target you.  
Password manager: Use a unique password for every account
Reused passwords are one of the easiest ways attackers break into multiple accounts. If one site is breached, your login details could be tested on many others.
Firefox’s free password manager can generate and securely store a strong, unique password per site, which is the single highest-leverage fix against password stuffing. For convenience, Firefox can automatically fill in your saved login information the next time you access a previously visited site. However, you still have the option to turn off password saving for specific websites, or completely if you’re using a shared device or simply prefer to enter it each time.
You can manage your stored logins on a singular device at any time. To get a head start, you also have the option to import passwords saved on several other popular browsers. In addition, you can create a free Mozilla account to safely sync them across your signed-in devices. 
VPN: Privacy built into the browser
Imagine you’re settling into a corner table at a bustling airport cafe, checking some emails on your phone before you board your flight. Or perhaps you took your laptop to the campus library to finally start that research paper you’ve been putting off. Maybe you’re polishing off that last presentation slide between sessions at an out-of-state conference.
While these moments are routine, connecting to public Wi-Fi anywhere can open a small window of risk – as your IP address, approximate location, and browsing activity can be more exposed on networks you don’t control.
That’s where Firefox’s free built-in, browser-based VPN steps in. While Firefox already encrypts your traffic with HTTPS, the built-in VPN feature routes your browsing traffic through a proxy network, hiding your IP address before it reaches a website. This means the sites you visit will see a proxy IP address instead of your own. It offers an industry-leading 50 gigabytes of free VPN-browsing each month, with no extension or extra app to install. Simply sign in, turn it on, and start browsing.
Firefox’s free built-in VPN first launched on desktop in March, later expanding to Android in July. Unlike a standalone or full-service VPN, it’s designed specifically to protect your browsing traffic within Firefox, not your entire device. This means apps, downloads, and other system traffic are not routed through the browser-based VPN. For people who need broader, device-wide VPN protection, Mozilla also offers a separate paid VPN service.
You can check the full list of regions where built-in VPN in Firefox is currently available here, and learn more about the differences between Firefox’s free built-in VPN and Mozilla VPN here. 
Relay: Contain the damage of any one breach
Think about how often you give out your personal email address – for an online purchase, RSVPing to an event, or signing up to a new app. Each time, you trust the site owner will protect your information, but, spam piles up and breaches can still happen – even when you think you’re being careful.
Firefox Relay gives you a smarter way to share. Instead of handing out your real email address, this feature provides secure, random email masks to use any time a website, store, or app asks you for your information. It forwards messages to your real email, while keeping your identity hidden to senders. This means if one service gets compromised, your other accounts stay safe.
You can also use Relay in the U.S. and Canada to shield your phone number, so you can receive calls and texts through masks and reply without exposing your real number.
The best part? To make protecting your privacy even easier, Firefox increased its limit to 50 free email masks earlier this year, allowing you to shield dozens of logins at no cost. 
Browse freely: Firefox protects you by default
Even if you sometimes forget to use Firefox protection tools like password manager, VPN, and Relay, there are multiple always-on features operating within the browser to help keep your session secure and private. These include enhanced tracking protection to block hidden scripts and known trackers that follow you across the web, browser fingerprinting protection to prevent sites from building a unique profile of your device, and warnings about deceptive or malicious websites.
Together, Firefox’s individual and always-on security features work to help keep your browsing safe and your data private. So, this Cybersecurity Awareness Month, take a moment to build new habits, try out our free cybersecurity tools, and make life more difficult for cybercriminals. Small steps add up, and we are here to help. Stay safe, stay smart, and keep exploring the web with confidence on Firefox.

articles.title: Edmonton mayor hints at upcoming support for entrepreneurs as city’s Startup Week kicks off | BetaKit
articles.text:
Downtown Edmonton was abuzz with founders, investors, innovators, and entrepreneurs this evening as the city gathered to officially kick off Edmonton Startup Week.
Spearheaded by Edmonton Unlimited, the annual celebration runs from Oct. 5 to 9. This year’s run of shows includes 30 events at Edmonton Unlimited’s headquarters, and an additional 49 events happening throughout the city.
Events include workshops on the fundamentals of building a startup, panels exploring everything from AI to defence to fundraising, an entire day platforming Edmonton’s burgeoning deep tech ecosystem, and a whole lot of networking.
Opening remarks honed in on the importance of Edmonton’s startups to the growing profile of the city’s entrepreneurial community.
Mayor Andrew Knack, who during his remarks issued an official proclamation from the City denoting this week as Edmonton Startup Week going forward, called the event an opportunity to work on some of the biggest problems facing the world.
“We know the days ahead will feature critical conversations about some of the most complex challenges we’re facing in our world,” he said before adding that the health and vitality of Edmonton’s entrepreneurial class is an indicator of the city’s vitality overall.
RELATED: Edmonton Unlimited unveils 10 companies to watch ahead of Startup Week
“Ninety to 95 percent of businesses in Edmonton are small- and medium-sized businesses. If you’re not thriving, this city is not thriving,” he said.
Knack also teased the City’s upcoming four-year budget, telling a packed auditorium that it was poised to include support for entrepreneurs in the city.
“You will see for the first time in a long time that the city will be heavily invested in not through words, but actions,” Knack said to applause.
13th annual event
This year marks the 13th iteration of Edmonton Startup Week, with the event doubling down on last year’s theme of “step in, step up, step forward.” Over its tenure, Startup Week has grown into a cornerstone gathering for entrepreneurs and investors, with the event routinely drawing attendees from Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and abroad.
This year’s kickoff featured a swath of local leaders, as well as a series of pitches from 10 companies chosen earlier this year as Edmonton Unlimited’s 10 companies to watch in 2026.
Edmonton Unlimited CEO Tom Viinikka touted a “big announcement” on Wednesday, Startup Week’s day showcasing deep tech, adding that there are nearly 80 investment meetings planned, including 66 with out-of-town investors. Viinikka noted that after Edmonton Unlimited’s June deep tech day, meetings led to investment into startups like Zero Point Cryogenics and Aqtiva.
“Investors are coming here, seeing what is being built, and investing,” he said.
Viinikka also cited critical milestones taken by companies moving through Edmonton Unlimited’s programming as indicative of the broader ecosystem’s accelerating momentum. A critical step is, according to Viinikka, a “milestone that must happen for a business to keep moving forward and to achieve specific goals.” Examples include benchmarks like creating a minimum viable product, developing a prototype, completing a first domestic sale, or receiving first patents and investment. Edmonton Unlimited has recorded 461 of those milestones this year.
“Collectively, they’re a measure of the entrepreneurial momentum of our ecosystem,” he said. “Imagine what we could do if we had 10 times those numbers … Startup Week is an opportunity to add to those numbers.”
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.
CORRECTION (10/06/2026): An earlier version of this article stated that nearly 80 investors had connected with founders since last June’s deep tech day. This story has been updated to reflect that nearly 80 investment meetings are happening during Startup Week’s deep tech day, with 66 of those meetings including investors from out of town.

articles.title: Alexa can’t control the aux input on Amazon Echo speakers anymore
articles.text:
If you’ve been using an older Amazon Echo device as a speaker through its 3.5mm aux input, Alexa voice commands to play or pause from line in may stop working. Ars Technica points to this Reddit poster claiming they received a message from Amazon about the change, which the company has confirmed. According to Amazon spokesperson Claudia Chavira Velez, “We recently notified the very small number of customers using voice requests to play or pause audio from the aux audio input on select Echo devices that this functionality will no longer be supported.”
Alexa can’t control the aux input on Amazon Echo speakers anymore
You can still use the 3.5mm port on older Echo devices, but Alexa can’t control your connected device.
The message does not include any explanation for why the feature was removed. It also doesn’t mention any changes to audio output functionality like connecting an external speaker to an Echo Dot. Amazon’s statement notes that the physical connection still works on the devices that have the port: Echo Plus (2nd gen), Echo (3rd gen), Echo (4th gen), and Echo Studio (1st gen). Owners can control it from within the Alexa app, as well as pair Bluetooth speakers.
As Ars Technica points out, it’s been years since Amazon released an Echo speaker with a 3.5mm aux port, and last year, Amazon also removed an Echo feature that allowed users to opt out of sending voice recordings to the cloud.
Update, October 6th: Added comment from Amazon.

WaveSave and its portable rubber dam
articles.text:
WaveSave and its portable rubber dam
The Dutch company has deployed its mobile barrier during floods on three continents to protect farms, hospitals, and water treatment plants.
 As sea levels rise and flood risks worsen due to global warming, WaveSave’s easy-to-erect portable dam offers a quick-response tool. People can use the dam to protect themselves and their property, and it can also store freshwater for later use. Communities in Europe, Africa, and Southeast Asia have deployed it successfully. Now, the company is expanding into other water-related services to help vulnerable places become more resilient.
One in five people globally are at high risk of being exposed to serious floods. Many live in communities without proper protection and can’t afford to evacuate during a flood or relocate permanently. Climate change-driven extreme weather and sea-level rise is only exacerbating the problem.
WaveSave makes a portable rubber dam called SlamDam that customers can quickly install in the early hours of a flood. Anyone can unfurl it on the ground along a riverbank or shoreline and pump it full of water until it swells into place. And there it stands, up to 1.3 meters high, shielding nearby property or structures from damage as waters rise.
Developed in 2013 in the Netherlands, SlamDam was initially tested and is still used today by regional water authorities in that country. WaveSave has since expanded into Africa and Southeast Asia, and customers have now deployed SlamDam in at least a dozen countries.
Key indicators
- Industry: Flood barriers
- Year the company was founded: 2017
- City and country of headquarters: Eindhoven, the Netherlands
- Notable fact: WaveSave is demoing its SlamDam product on New York City’s Governors Island as one of seven winners in a competition for urban climate adaptations. The barrier is installed at a site where high tides and waves from passing ferries often wash ashore.
Potential for impact
Due to both climate change and population growth, nearly 2 billion people will be exposed to floods by 2100—an increase of 300 million from 2020, according to one estimate.
A SlamDam is designed to help protect farmland and personal property as well as critical facilities like hospitals or water treatment plants. It’s cheaper in the short term than more permanent modifications like building levees or rebuilding facilities on higher ground. And its temporary nature means it can be deployed as needed, and then stored away.
To fill the SlamDam, a local installer can use any portable water pump they may have on hand. With a lifespan of more than 40 years, the flood barriers can be used again and again.
This low-tech solution has another important benefit, at least when it comes to freshwater floods: In the weeks and months after a flood, residents can tap the water stored inside the mobile dam to irrigate crops. This is particularly helpful during the dry season or in drought-prone regions. At the rural Mpanda commune in Burundi in East Africa, where a SlamDam was deployed during the 2022 flood season, farmers with access to the water inside produced more crops that year and doubled their incomes, according to a UN report.
Caveats
Companies like AquaFence, MegaSecur, and NOAQ Flood Protection also make mobile flood barriers. WaveSave distinguishes itself in part by focusing on rapid emergency deployment in developing countries, and by emphasizing SlamDam’s ability to store water for later use.
But one research team that analyzed SlamDam’s use in Kenya found a series of challenges to getting communities there to adopt the technology. One was figuring out who should own and deploy the dam.
Another ongoing challenge is the up-front cost. SlamDam is already on par with or more affordable than many alternatives: It costs between €1,000 and €3,000 (about $1,140 and $3,400) per five-meter section, and comes in a range of heights. Protecting a single entrance to a home or facility might require only 10 meters, while surrounding a facility (such as a hospital) or shielding a farm or neighborhood might take 200 to 300 meters. But the price is still too high for many communities or farmers. WaveSave’s managing director Omar Saleh says the company is looking into offering SlamDam as a service and deploying it on demand to make protection more affordable.
Next steps
Right now, an external partner manufactures all SlamDams in the Netherlands; they are then shipped to customers based elsewhere. But WaveSave aims to open a local production facility for SlamDams in Southeast Asia in early 2027, followed by a similar facility in East Africa, which could help lower costs. The company recently won contracts for four new projects totaling about $5.3 million in Burundi, Djibouti, and Guinea, with a “substantial pipeline” developing in Southeast Asia and Latin America, according to Saleh.
The company is currently self-financed and only has seven employees. Saleh says he plans to grow organically by investing profits back into the firm.
Part of that growth will involve offering new services such as advising communities on how to install and operate simple, off-the-shelf rainwater harvesting and irrigation systems, as part of a more comprehensive approach to managing water in climate-stressed regions.
